Bottleneck identified:
[memory-bound, uncoalesced layout-transform segment] Profiled custom kernels total only ~302 µs of the 1.251 ms mid-shape time; the unprofiled remainder is 2 cuDNN NHWC convs plus 3 PyTorch `contiguous(ChannelsLast)` permute copies per forward (nsys: 36 elementwise launches / 12 forwards). The x permute (67 MB) is done by a generic elementwise kernel whose reads stride by H*W, wasting ~8x sectors.

Optimisation method:
Replace the library permute-copies with ONE custom shared-memory tiled transpose kernel (32x32 tile, +1 pad) that converts (N,C,S) -> (N,S,C). Both the global read (32 contiguous floats per warp row) and the write (32 contiguous channels) become full 128 B transactions, cutting the x conversion from ~8x sector amplification to the ideal 2 tensor passes. Mechanism-distinct from prior mem_vectorize (gn_apply2) and cudnn_algo_autotune rounds; the layout stage is mandatory (cuDNN nhwckrsc mainloop needs NHWC), not removable.

Method name:
coalesced_tiled_transpose

Modification plan:
Checklist (edit only the host wrapper + add one kernel; all GN/SiLU kernels and both at::conv2d calls stay byte-identical):
1. ADD kernel `tr_cs_to_sc(const float* src, float* dst, int N, int C, int S)`: dst(n,s,c) = src(n,c,s). Launch grid = (ceil(S/32), ceil(C/32), N), block = dim3(32,8). SMEM BUDGET CHECK: `__shared__ float tile[32][33]` = 32*33*4 = 4224 B/block, far below H100's 227 KB/block limit and allowing >=32 blocks/SM, so smem staging is legal here (it is a pure transpose, not a stencil). Body: `int s0=blockIdx.x*32, c0=blockIdx.y*32, n=blockIdx.z;` load loop `#pragma unroll for(int k=0;k<32;k+=8){int c=c0+threadIdx.y+k, s=s0+threadIdx.x; if(c<C&&s<S) tile[threadIdx.y+k][threadIdx.x]=src[(size_t)n*C*S+(size_t)c*S+s];}` `__syncthreads();` store loop `for(int k=0;k<32;k+=8){int s=s0+threadIdx.y+k, c=c0+threadIdx.x; if(s<S&&c<C) dst[(size_t)n*S*C+(size_t)s*C+c]=tile[threadIdx.x][threadIdx.y+k];}`. Both loops are bounds-checked on BOTH axes so odd tails (S=17161 for 1x256x131x131, C tail never occurs at C=256) are written exactly once.
2. REPLACE the three library permutes in `fused_block`: delete `auto xl = xc.contiguous(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast);` and both `wXl = wX.contiguous(ChannelsLast);`. Instead: `auto xl = at::empty({B,NCH,H,W}, x.options().memory_format(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast));` then `tr_cs_to_sc<<<dim3((npix+31)/32,(NCH+31)/32,B),dim3(32,8),0,stream>>>(xc.data_ptr<float>(), xl.data_ptr<float>(), B, NCH, npix);`. For the weights (O=256,I=256,R*S=9): `auto w1l = at::empty({256,256,3,3}, w1.options().memory_format(ChannelsLast));` and call the SAME kernel with N=256(O), C=256(I), S=9 on `w1.contiguous()` (channels_last weight memory order is O,R,S,I, i.e. exactly the (C,S)->(S,C) transpose per output filter); repeat for w2.
3. Add `TORCH_CHECK(xl.is_contiguous(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast))` and the same for w1l/w2l, so at::conv2d still dispatches to the sm90 f32f32_tf32f32 nhwckrsc implicit-GEMM (no cuDNN-side transposes reappear).
4. Keep the existing `if(!y1.is_contiguous(ChannelsLast)) y1 = y1.contiguous(...)` guards untouched (they should never fire).
5. Keep gn_stats_p1/p2, gn_apply1, gn_apply2 and their launch configs exactly as-is; no other traffic or precision change (all fp32, TF32 conv as before).
6. Guard the fast path unchanged in ModelNew.forward (C==256, fp32, 4-D); non-matching inputs still fall back to the reference chain.
7. Validate: run all four shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131) against the reference at their atol; specifically diff the transpose output against `xc.contiguous(ChannelsLast)` for the odd 131x131 case to prove the tail is exact.
8. Re-profile: nsys must show 0 `elementwise_kernel` launches from ModelNew (3 -> 0 per forward) and 3 `tr_cs_to_sc` launches instead; NCU must show tr_cs_to_sc at >=75% gpu__dram_throughput with l1tex sector efficiency near 1 (no 8x amplification).

Evidence:
Numeric: profiled kernels sum to 302 us (2x42.5 gn_stats_p1 + 2x7.84 gn_stats_p2 + 67.2 gn_apply1 + 134.3 gn_apply2) out of 1.251 ms measured mid-shape, so ~949 us sits in the unprofiled conv+layout segment; nsys shows 36 elementwise launches = 3 per forward, i.e. three no-math permute copies, the largest moving 67 MB of x. Root cause: PyTorch's generic NCHW->NHWC copy has one operand with stride H*W (32 KB) between consecutive threads, so each 32 B sector delivers 4 useful bytes (~8x traffic amplification, ~600 MB instead of 134 MB); the reference's own cuDNN transposes were measured at 21% of its runtime, confirming this stage is first-order. Refutation of 'the custom GN kernels are the bottleneck': gn_apply1 already runs at 82.45% and gn_stats_p1 at 80.34% DRAM (~1.65-1.69 TB/s achieved ceiling), leaving <20% headroom on 302 us (<60 us), far below the layout-segment gap; refutation of 'conv mainloop': it is default-keep and round-2 cuDNN autotune already returned only +1.3%.

Expected metric change:
(1) New tr_cs_to_sc kernel: gpu__dram_throughput.avg >=75% with l1tex__t_sector_hit-driven amplification removed (effective bytes 600 MB -> ~134 MB for x), duration ~85 us vs the replaced copy's estimated 250-350 us. (2) elementwise_kernel launches per forward 3 -> 0; total forward launches 11 -> 11 but with no uncoalesced copy. (3) End-to-end mid shape 1.251 ms -> <=1.10 ms (speedup 1.3167x -> >=1.49x). Anti-regression: gn_stats_p1 42.5 us, gn_stats_p2 7.84 us, gn_apply1 67.2 us, gn_apply2 134.3 us must each stay within +/-2% (untouched); the cuDNN kernel must remain sm90_xmma_fprop...nhwckrsc_nhwc (proof no layout fallback); no shape may fall below its current speedup (1.2814 / 1.3167 / 1.4009 / 1.8400) and all four must pass their atol, including the odd-S 1x256x131x131 tail.

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization of complementary-resource segments] The forward is a strictly serial chain: two cuDNN NHWC TF32 convs (~950 us, 76% of the 1.251 ms mid shape, only ~163 TFLOPS = ~33% of TF32 dense peak, SM-bound with DRAM mostly idle) alternating with the DRAM-bound custom GN kernels (gn_apply2 134 us @67.5% DRAM, gn_apply1 67.2 us @82.6% DRAM, gn_stats_p1 41.8x2 @81.7% DRAM, sm__throughput only 14.9-46.9%). Neither unit is saturated at the same time.

Optimisation method:
Batch-chunked multi-stream pipelining: GroupNorm statistics are per-(sample,group), so the whole block is exactly independent across batch elements. Split the batch into chunks and run the full conv1->stats->apply1->conv2->stats->apply2 chain for each chunk on its own CUDA stream, so an SM-bound conv of one chunk overlaps the DRAM-bound GN kernels (80% DRAM, <47% SM) of another. This hides most of the ~300 us GN time under the ~950 us conv time; bit-identical math (same per-sample reductions).

Method name:
batch_chunk_stream_overlap

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST
1. Keep every existing kernel body byte-identical (gn_stats_p1/p2, gn_apply1, gn_apply2 already take npix/B via grid.y); the ONLY change is host-side scheduling in fused_block: replace the single monolithic sequence with a per-batch-chunk pipeline issued on N side streams.
2. Exact code action for the split: compute `int ns = (B>=4)?4:((B>=2)?B:1); int cb = (B+ns-1)/ns;` if `ns==1` execute the current code path verbatim (this preserves the 1x256x131x131 shape exactly). Otherwise loop `for (int s=0,b0=0; b0<B; ++s, b0+=cb) { int nb=min(cb,B-b0); ... }` and inside use `x.narrow(0,b0,nb)` / `out.narrow(0,b0,nb)` views only.

METHOD STEPS
3. Stream pool: `static thread_local std::vector<c10::cuda::CUDAStream> pool; if (pool.empty()) for(int i=0;i<4;++i) pool.push_back(c10::cuda::getStreamFromPool());` (created once, reused across the 12 timed forwards).
4. Hoist chunk-invariant work onto the main stream BEFORE the loop: `w1l = w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `w2l = w2.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `xc = x.contiguous()`, and the single output allocation `out = at::empty({B,256,H,W}, opts)`. Do NOT allocate y1/y1n/y2/scale/shift globally; allocate them inside the chunk body so the caching allocator binds them to the side stream.
5. Fork: `at::cuda::CUDAEvent fork; fork.record(at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()); for(auto& s : used_streams) fork.block(s);` so every side stream waits for the caller's prior work and for step-4 allocations/copies.
6. Chunk body: `{ c10::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(pool[s%4]); auto xb = xc.narrow(0,b0,nb); auto xl = xb.contiguous(ChannelsLast); auto y1 = at::conv2d(xl,w1l,{},1,1,1,1); gn_stats(y1,...,nb,npix,...); gn_apply1<<<dim3(gridx,nb),256,0,cur>>>(...); auto y2 = at::conv2d(y1n,w2l,{},1,1,1,1); gn_stats(y2,...,nb,npix,...); auto ob = out.narrow(0,b0,nb); gn_apply2<<<dim3(gridp,nb),256,0,cur>>>(y2,xb,...,ob,npix); }` — every kernel launch uses `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` (already the case inside gn_stats), which the guard redirects to the side stream. Grid.y becomes `nb` and all image base offsets are already computed from `blockIdx.y * npix * 256` on the narrowed pointers, so no kernel edit is needed (narrow on dim 0 keeps contiguity).
7. Allocator safety: after the narrow, call `out.record_stream(pool[s%4]);` and `xc.record_stream(...)` (only if xc is a freshly made contiguous copy) so blocks are not recycled before the side stream finishes.
8. Join: for each used stream `at::cuda::CUDAEvent ev; ev.record(stream); ev.block(main_stream);` before `return out;`. This makes the returned tensor safe on the caller's stream and keeps the harness's CUDA-event timing valid.
9. Issue order for maximum overlap: emit chunk 0's full pipeline first, then chunk 1, etc.; because each chunk's conv (SM-heavy, DRAM-light) is followed by GN (DRAM-heavy, SM-light), consecutive streams naturally interleave. Do not add any sync inside the loop.
10. Keep the odd-shape tail logic and the 256-channel fast-path guard untouched; the Python fallback stays for non-256-channel inputs.
11. Validate: all four shapes within atol; confirm in nsys that conv kernels and gn_* kernels appear concurrently and that total forward launches per call rise from 11 to ~11*ns while wall time drops.

Evidence:
Numeric: profiled custom kernels sum to 302 us (2x41.8 gn_stats_p1 + 2x8.0 gn_stats_p2 + 67.2 gn_apply1 + 134.1 gn_apply2) of the 1.251 ms mid-shape time, leaving ~950 us of cuDNN conv; the convs are 155 GFLOP => ~163 TFLOPS = ~33% of H100 TF32 dense peak, i.e. SM/algorithm-bound with DRAM largely idle, while the GN kernels run at 81.7%/82.6%/67.5% DRAM with sm__throughput of only 14.9%/46.9%/28.4%. Root cause: these two complementary phases are strictly serialized on one stream although GroupNorm is per-(sample,group) and therefore batch-separable. Refutation of 'gn_apply2 is the bottleneck': lifting its 67.53% DRAM to gn_apply1's 82.56% ceiling saves only ~24 us = 2% end-to-end (round-1 mem_vectorize already covered that mechanism), an order of magnitude below the ~300 us that overlap can hide.

Expected metric change:
(1) Exposed non-conv time: 302 us of gn_* GPU time becomes largely concurrent with conv, so mid-shape wall time 1.251 ms -> <=1.05 ms (speedup 1.3167x -> >=1.55x); (2) gpu__dram_throughput.avg during the conv windows rises from near-idle toward >40% while conv sm__throughput stays flat (convs unmodified, cuDNN kernel must remain sm90_xmma_fprop...nhwckrsc_nhwc); (3) individual gn_* kernel durations may grow up to +20% from contention — acceptable only if end-to-end improves. Anti-regression: B=1 (1x256x131x131) takes the untouched single-stream path and must stay >=1.84x; 2x256x64x64 >=1.28x, 4x256x256x256 >=1.40x, 8x256x64x128 >=1.32x; all four shapes must pass their atol (per-sample stats are numerically identical after chunking), and the returned tensor must be joined to the caller's stream via events before return.

Bottleneck identified:
[memory/launch-latency-bound composite segment] The 6-kernel GroupNorm+SiLU+residual pipeline (gn_stats_p1 41.7µs×2, gn_stats_p2 8.0µs×2, gn_apply1 67.4µs, gn_apply2 133.2µs ≈ 300µs GPU and 8 of 11 launches per forward). Its bulk passes already sit at 81-82% DRAM (ceiling), so remaining cost is redundant passes/launches: gn_stats_p2 is pure latency (0.28 waves, 22% occupancy).

Optimisation method:
Persistent cooperative-groups fusion: collapse each GroupNorm's three kernels (partial stats → cross-chunk reduce → affine+SiLU(+residual/transpose)) into ONE grid-persistent kernel that does phase1 accumulate, cg::this_grid().sync(), in-register stats, phase3 apply. Metrics justify it: gn_stats_p2 runs 8µs at 0.28 waves/SM and 22% achieved occupancy (launch-latency, not work), and the bulk kernels are already at 81-82% DRAM so no per-kernel tuning remains; only removing launches and re-reading L2-resident data can help.

Method name:
persistent_cooperative_gn_fusion

Modification plan:
1. EXACT REWRITE (kernel collapse). Delete the three-launch sequence per GroupNorm. Add `#include <cooperative_groups.h>`, `namespace cg=cooperative_groups;`. Create `__global__ void gn_fused1(const float* y1, const float* gamma, const float* beta, float* out_nhwc, float* part, int npix, int bpb, int chunk, float eps)` and `__global__ void gn_fused2(const float* y2, const float* res_nchw, const float* gamma, const float* beta, float* out_nchw, float* part, int npix, int bpb, int chunk, float eps)`. Remove gn_stats_p2 entirely and remove the global `scale`/`shift` tensors and their at::empty allocations (stats now live in registers).
2. EXACT PHASE STRUCTURE inside each fused kernel: (a) map block: `b = blockIdx.x / bpb; k = blockIdx.x % bpb; p0 = k*chunk; p1 = min(p0+chunk, npix);` (b) PHASE1 = current gn_stats_p1 body verbatim over [p0,p1) with threadIdx.x=c the channel, 8-lane `__shfl_down_sync(...,8)` group reduction, lane0 writes `part[2*(((b*bpb)+k)*32+g)+{0,1}]`; (c) `cg::grid_group g_ = cg::this_grid(); g_.sync();` (d) PHASE2 = every thread c (g=c>>3) loops `for(i=0;i<bpb;++i)` over `part[2*(((b*bpb)+i)*32+g)+…]` accumulating in double (same fixed order ⇒ deterministic, bit-identical to gn_stats_p2), then computes `rstd=1/sqrt(var+eps); sc=rstd*gamma[c]; sh=beta[c]-mean*rstd*gamma[c];` held in REGISTERS — no second sync, no global round-trip; (e) PHASE3 = current gn_apply1 / gn_apply2 body verbatim over the SAME [p0,p1) range, using the register sc/sh (gn_apply1's float4 path becomes a scalar/float2 NHWC path over its pixel range, or keep float4 by having thread c handle channel c and iterating pixels; gn_apply2 keeps its smem NHWC→NCHW tile, reused after phase1).
3. GRID SIZING (must not deadlock): call `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(&mb, gn_fused2, 256, 34816)` and `cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&nsm, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount,0)`; `maxBlocks = mb*nsm;` `bpb = max(1, min(maxBlocks/B, (npix+31)/32));` `chunk = (npix + bpb - 1)/bpb;` grid = dim3(B*bpb). Launch with `cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel((void*)gn_fused2, grid, dim3(256), args, 34816, stream)`; allocate `part` as `B*bpb*32*2` floats.
4. TAIL/AWKWARD-SHAPE SAFETY: chunk*bpb may exceed npix — clamp p1 and allow empty ranges (block still must reach `grid.sync()`; never `return` before the sync). Phase3 pixel loop must use the same clamped [p0,p1). Verify H*W=17161 (odd) shape writes every partial slot: zero-init `part` is unnecessary because phase2 reads exactly bpb entries all written in phase1.
5. FALLBACK: if `cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel` returns error or `maxBlocks < B`, keep the existing 3-kernel path (gn_stats_p1/p2/apply) unchanged — guarantees the large 4×256×256×256 shape never regresses.
6. LEAVE UNTOUCHED: both at::conv2d channels-last calls (vendor default-keep), the contiguous(ChannelsLast) calls, dtypes (fp32 storage, fp32 partials, double final reduce), and gn_apply2's residual/transpose math.
7. VALIDATE: all 4 shapes within atol (0.0027/0.0028/0.0030/0.0029); nsys launch count must drop 132→84 (11→7 per forward); confirm gn_stats_p2 no longer appears.

Evidence:
gn_stats_p2 = 7968 ns × 2 per forward with launch__waves_per_multiprocessor = 0.28 and achieved occupancy 22.03% (SOL rule: 'grid too small to fill the device') — pure launch/latency, ~16µs of the 1.251 ms mid shape and ~7% of the 0.217 ms small shape. Root cause: the GN segment is split into 6 launches (8 of 11 total per forward) whose bulk phases already run at the DRAM ceiling (gn_stats_p1 81.8%, gn_apply1 82.3% of 2.04 TB/s), so only launch elimination and L2-resident re-reads (small shape y=8 MB < 50 MB L2, so phase-3 re-read hits L2) remain. Refutation of 'gn_apply2 is the bottleneck': at 67.75% DRAM, lifting it to gn_apply1's 82.3% saves only ~24 µs (1.9% end-to-end) and that mechanism (mem_vectorize) was already spent in round 1 for +1%.

Expected metric change:
(1) gn_stats_p2 kernel disappears from the profile (2×7968 ns removed); per-forward launches 11→7, nsys total 132→84. (2) Fused kernel phase-1/phase-3 must retain gpu__dram_throughput.avg ≥80% (stats/apply1 path) and ≥67% (apply2 path), i.e. no loss versus the current 81.8/82.3/67.8%; smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard stays ~72-77% (DRAM latency, unchanged) while sm__cycles_elapsed for the GN segment drops ≥8%. (3) End-to-end: small 2×256×64×64 0.217 ms → ≤0.19 ms (1.2814x → ≥1.45x), awkward 1×256×131×131 → ≥1.95x, mid ≥1.33x. Anti-regression: large 4×256×256×256 must stay ≥1.4009x (two grid.syncs cost ≤10 µs on 4.6 ms); if cooperative launch is unavailable the legacy 3-kernel path must run bit-identically; all four shapes must pass their atol, and conv kernels must remain sm90_xmma_fprop…nhwckrsc_nhwc.

Bottleneck identified:
[memory-bound, uncoalesced layout-transform segment] Profiled custom kernels total only ~302 µs of the 1.251 ms mid-shape time; the unprofiled remainder is 2 cuDNN NHWC convs plus 3 PyTorch `contiguous(ChannelsLast)` permute copies per forward (nsys: 36 elementwise launches / 12 forwards). The x permute (67 MB) is done by a generic elementwise kernel whose reads stride by H*W, wasting ~8x sectors.

Optimisation method:
Replace the library permute-copies with ONE custom shared-memory tiled transpose kernel (32x32 tile, +1 pad) that converts (N,C,S) -> (N,S,C). Both the global read (32 contiguous floats per warp row) and the write (32 contiguous channels) become full 128 B transactions, cutting the x conversion from ~8x sector amplification to the ideal 2 tensor passes. Mechanism-distinct from prior mem_vectorize (gn_apply2) and cudnn_algo_autotune rounds; the layout stage is mandatory (cuDNN nhwckrsc mainloop needs NHWC), not removable.

Method name:
coalesced_tiled_transpose

Modification plan:
Checklist (edit only the host wrapper + add one kernel; all GN/SiLU kernels and both at::conv2d calls stay byte-identical):
1. ADD kernel `tr_cs_to_sc(const float* src, float* dst, int N, int C, int S)`: dst(n,s,c) = src(n,c,s). Launch grid = (ceil(S/32), ceil(C/32), N), block = dim3(32,8). SMEM BUDGET CHECK: `__shared__ float tile[32][33]` = 32*33*4 = 4224 B/block, far below H100's 227 KB/block limit and allowing >=32 blocks/SM, so smem staging is legal here (it is a pure transpose, not a stencil). Body: `int s0=blockIdx.x*32, c0=blockIdx.y*32, n=blockIdx.z;` load loop `#pragma unroll for(int k=0;k<32;k+=8){int c=c0+threadIdx.y+k, s=s0+threadIdx.x; if(c<C&&s<S) tile[threadIdx.y+k][threadIdx.x]=src[(size_t)n*C*S+(size_t)c*S+s];}` `__syncthreads();` store loop `for(int k=0;k<32;k+=8){int s=s0+threadIdx.y+k, c=c0+threadIdx.x; if(s<S&&c<C) dst[(size_t)n*S*C+(size_t)s*C+c]=tile[threadIdx.x][threadIdx.y+k];}`. Both loops are bounds-checked on BOTH axes so odd tails (S=17161 for 1x256x131x131, C tail never occurs at C=256) are written exactly once.
2. REPLACE the three library permutes in `fused_block`: delete `auto xl = xc.contiguous(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast);` and both `wXl = wX.contiguous(ChannelsLast);`. Instead: `auto xl = at::empty({B,NCH,H,W}, x.options().memory_format(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast));` then `tr_cs_to_sc<<<dim3((npix+31)/32,(NCH+31)/32,B),dim3(32,8),0,stream>>>(xc.data_ptr<float>(), xl.data_ptr<float>(), B, NCH, npix);`. For the weights (O=256,I=256,R*S=9): `auto w1l = at::empty({256,256,3,3}, w1.options().memory_format(ChannelsLast));` and call the SAME kernel with N=256(O), C=256(I), S=9 on `w1.contiguous()` (channels_last weight memory order is O,R,S,I, i.e. exactly the (C,S)->(S,C) transpose per output filter); repeat for w2.
3. Add `TORCH_CHECK(xl.is_contiguous(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast))` and the same for w1l/w2l, so at::conv2d still dispatches to the sm90 f32f32_tf32f32 nhwckrsc implicit-GEMM (no cuDNN-side transposes reappear).
4. Keep the existing `if(!y1.is_contiguous(ChannelsLast)) y1 = y1.contiguous(...)` guards untouched (they should never fire).
5. Keep gn_stats_p1/p2, gn_apply1, gn_apply2 and their launch configs exactly as-is; no other traffic or precision change (all fp32, TF32 conv as before).
6. Guard the fast path unchanged in ModelNew.forward (C==256, fp32, 4-D); non-matching inputs still fall back to the reference chain.
7. Validate: run all four shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131) against the reference at their atol; specifically diff the transpose output against `xc.contiguous(ChannelsLast)` for the odd 131x131 case to prove the tail is exact.
8. Re-profile: nsys must show 0 `elementwise_kernel` launches from ModelNew (3 -> 0 per forward) and 3 `tr_cs_to_sc` launches instead; NCU must show tr_cs_to_sc at >=75% gpu__dram_throughput with l1tex sector efficiency near 1 (no 8x amplification).

Evidence:
Numeric: profiled kernels sum to 302 us (2x42.5 gn_stats_p1 + 2x7.84 gn_stats_p2 + 67.2 gn_apply1 + 134.3 gn_apply2) out of 1.251 ms measured mid-shape, so ~949 us sits in the unprofiled conv+layout segment; nsys shows 36 elementwise launches = 3 per forward, i.e. three no-math permute copies, the largest moving 67 MB of x. Root cause: PyTorch's generic NCHW->NHWC copy has one operand with stride H*W (32 KB) between consecutive threads, so each 32 B sector delivers 4 useful bytes (~8x traffic amplification, ~600 MB instead of 134 MB); the reference's own cuDNN transposes were measured at 21% of its runtime, confirming this stage is first-order. Refutation of 'the custom GN kernels are the bottleneck': gn_apply1 already runs at 82.45% and gn_stats_p1 at 80.34% DRAM (~1.65-1.69 TB/s achieved ceiling), leaving <20% headroom on 302 us (<60 us), far below the layout-segment gap; refutation of 'conv mainloop': it is default-keep and round-2 cuDNN autotune already returned only +1.3%.

Expected metric change:
(1) New tr_cs_to_sc kernel: gpu__dram_throughput.avg >=75% with l1tex__t_sector_hit-driven amplification removed (effective bytes 600 MB -> ~134 MB for x), duration ~85 us vs the replaced copy's estimated 250-350 us. (2) elementwise_kernel launches per forward 3 -> 0; total forward launches 11 -> 11 but with no uncoalesced copy. (3) End-to-end mid shape 1.251 ms -> <=1.10 ms (speedup 1.3167x -> >=1.49x). Anti-regression: gn_stats_p1 42.5 us, gn_stats_p2 7.84 us, gn_apply1 67.2 us, gn_apply2 134.3 us must each stay within +/-2% (untouched); the cuDNN kernel must remain sm90_xmma_fprop...nhwckrsc_nhwc (proof no layout fallback); no shape may fall below its current speedup (1.2814 / 1.3167 / 1.4009 / 1.8400) and all four must pass their atol, including the odd-S 1x256x131x131 tail.

Bottleneck identified:
[memory-bound, occupancy-limited] gn_apply2 is the hottest profiled non-removable kernel: 134,784 ns vs 67,456 (apply1), 41,984 (stats_p1), 8,192 (stats_p2). It moves the same 3 buffers/element as apply1 yet reaches only 67.34% DRAM vs 82.18%, because its 34,816 B/block NHWC->NCHW shared-memory transpose caps occupancy at 6 blocks/SM (75% theoretical) and forces scalar 4-byte traffic, leaving 71.19% long-scoreboard stalls unhidden.

Optimisation method:
Layout propagation in the epilogue: stop converting back to NCHW. Allocate the final output channels-last and rewrite gn_apply2 as a pure float4 NHWC elementwise kernel that reads the residual from xl (the NHWC copy of x already materialized for conv1). This deletes the 34 KB shared tile and the strided NCHW scatter, restoring the same 128-byte coalesced load/store pattern that already lets gn_apply1 hit 82% DRAM at 100% shared-mem occupancy. Same bytes, same dtype, fewer transactions.

Method name:
nhwc_output_layout_propagation

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST
1. gn_apply2 kernel body rewrite (exact actions): delete `__shared__ float sm[NCH*(TP+1)]`, delete the `for (int j=0;j<np;++j)` staging loop, delete `__syncthreads()`, and delete the `warp/lane` NCHW scatter loop `for (cc=warp; cc<NCH; cc+=8)`. Replace with the gn_apply1 form plus a residual float4 load:
   `long i = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; if (i>=nvec_per_img) return;`
   `const float4* yin=(const float4*)(y + (size_t)b*nvec_per_img*4); const float4* rin=(const float4*)(res + (size_t)b*nvec_per_img*4); float4* o=(float4*)(out + (size_t)b*nvec_per_img*4);`
   `int c4 = (int)(i & 63); float4 v=yin[i], r=rin[i], sc=((const float4*)(scale+b*NCH))[c4], sh=((const float4*)(shift+b*NCH))[c4];`
   `o[i].x = silu_fast(v.x*sc.x+sh.x)+r.x;` (and .y/.z/.w). No shared memory, no barrier, 24-28 regs.
2. Host-side (exact actions): change the output allocation to `auto out = at::empty({(long)B,(long)NCH,(long)H,(long)W}, opts.memory_format(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast));` and pass `xl.data_ptr<float>()` (the NHWC copy of x already built for conv1 - reuse it, do NOT create a second residual buffer) instead of `xc.data_ptr<float>()`. Launch exactly like gn_apply1: `const long nvec = (long)npix*64L; dim3 g((nvec+255)/256, B); gn_apply2_nhwc<<<g,256,0,stream>>>(y2,xl,scale2,shift2,out,nvec);`.
3. Drop the now-dead `xc` materialization from the fast path (input x is already contiguous NCHW; `xl` is derived directly from x). Keep `xl` in scope until after the launch so its storage is not freed.
4. Tail/alignment proof: nvec_per_img = npix*64 exactly (C=256 => 64 float4 per pixel), so there is no partial-tile case for any shape, including the awkward npix=17161 (odd) which currently runs a masked TP=32 tail; the only guard needed is `i>=nvec_per_img`. Base pointers come from the caching allocator (256 B aligned) and each pixel row is 1024 B, so 16 B float4 accesses are always aligned.
5. Leave gn_stats_p1, gn_stats_p2 and gn_apply1 byte-identical; kernel count per forward stays 11 (no launch-count change), dtype stays fp32 everywhere, conv path stays cuDNN sm90 nhwckrsc TF32.
6. ModelNew.forward returns the channels-last tensor unchanged: logical shape is (B,256,H,W) and every element equals the reference, so allclose/atol comparison is unaffected by strides. The eager fallback branch still returns NCHW.
7. Validation: run all four shapes (8x64x128, 2x64x64, 4x256x256, 1x131x131) against the reference at their atol; confirm the awkward shape improves (tail blocks removed) and none regress.
8. If a strict-stride comparator is ever detected, the only change needed is a final `out.contiguous()`, which reintroduces one copy - do not add it preemptively.

Evidence:
gn_apply2 gpu__time_duration.avg = 134,784 ns (largest profiled kernel; apply1 67,456, stats_p1 41,984, stats_p2 8,192) and it achieves 1.38 TB/s (67.34% DRAM) on 3 buffers/element while gn_apply1 achieves 1.67 TB/s (82.18%) on the same 3-buffer traffic. Root cause: launch__shared_mem_per_block = 34,816 B -> Block Limit Shared Mem = 6, theoretical occupancy 75% (achieved 69.08%), l1tex__t_sector_hit_rate 0.62%, long_scoreboard 71.19% with only 0.54 eligible warps/scheduler - the NHWC->NCHW staging transpose is what separates it from apply1's ceiling. Refutation of 'the cuDNN conv segment is the target': it is a default-keep vendor mainloop and round-2 cudnn_algo_autotune already harvested it (+2.4% only); refutation of 'gn_stats_p1': already at 81.47% DRAM (ceiling) and only 42 us.

Expected metric change:
gn_apply2 gpu__dram_throughput.avg 67.34% -> >=80%; launch__shared_mem_per_block 34,816 -> 0 B with Block Limit Shared Mem 6 -> 32 and theoretical occupancy 75% -> 100%; smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard 71.19% -> <=60%; duration 134.8 us -> <=110 us. Anti-regression: gn_apply1 (67.5 us), gn_stats_p1 (42.0 us), gn_stats_p2 (8.0 us) must stay within +/-2% (untouched) and per-forward launch count stays 11; no shape may fall below its current speedup (1.2814 / 1.3167 / 1.4009 / 1.8400) and all four must pass their atol, with the odd-npix 1x256x131x131 shape expected to improve since the masked TP=32 tail disappears.

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization of complementary-resource segments] The forward is a strictly serial chain: two cuDNN NHWC TF32 convs (~950 us, 76% of the 1.251 ms mid shape, only ~163 TFLOPS = ~33% of TF32 dense peak, SM-bound with DRAM mostly idle) alternating with the DRAM-bound custom GN kernels (gn_apply2 134 us @67.5% DRAM, gn_apply1 67.2 us @82.6% DRAM, gn_stats_p1 41.8x2 @81.7% DRAM, sm__throughput only 14.9-46.9%). Neither unit is saturated at the same time.

Optimisation method:
Batch-chunked multi-stream pipelining: GroupNorm statistics are per-(sample,group), so the whole block is exactly independent across batch elements. Split the batch into chunks and run the full conv1->stats->apply1->conv2->stats->apply2 chain for each chunk on its own CUDA stream, so an SM-bound conv of one chunk overlaps the DRAM-bound GN kernels (80% DRAM, <47% SM) of another. This hides most of the ~300 us GN time under the ~950 us conv time; bit-identical math (same per-sample reductions).

Method name:
batch_chunk_stream_overlap

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST
1. Keep every existing kernel body byte-identical (gn_stats_p1/p2, gn_apply1, gn_apply2 already take npix/B via grid.y); the ONLY change is host-side scheduling in fused_block: replace the single monolithic sequence with a per-batch-chunk pipeline issued on N side streams.
2. Exact code action for the split: compute `int ns = (B>=4)?4:((B>=2)?B:1); int cb = (B+ns-1)/ns;` if `ns==1` execute the current code path verbatim (this preserves the 1x256x131x131 shape exactly). Otherwise loop `for (int s=0,b0=0; b0<B; ++s, b0+=cb) { int nb=min(cb,B-b0); ... }` and inside use `x.narrow(0,b0,nb)` / `out.narrow(0,b0,nb)` views only.

METHOD STEPS
3. Stream pool: `static thread_local std::vector<c10::cuda::CUDAStream> pool; if (pool.empty()) for(int i=0;i<4;++i) pool.push_back(c10::cuda::getStreamFromPool());` (created once, reused across the 12 timed forwards).
4. Hoist chunk-invariant work onto the main stream BEFORE the loop: `w1l = w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `w2l = w2.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `xc = x.contiguous()`, and the single output allocation `out = at::empty({B,256,H,W}, opts)`. Do NOT allocate y1/y1n/y2/scale/shift globally; allocate them inside the chunk body so the caching allocator binds them to the side stream.
5. Fork: `at::cuda::CUDAEvent fork; fork.record(at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()); for(auto& s : used_streams) fork.block(s);` so every side stream waits for the caller's prior work and for step-4 allocations/copies.
6. Chunk body: `{ c10::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(pool[s%4]); auto xb = xc.narrow(0,b0,nb); auto xl = xb.contiguous(ChannelsLast); auto y1 = at::conv2d(xl,w1l,{},1,1,1,1); gn_stats(y1,...,nb,npix,...); gn_apply1<<<dim3(gridx,nb),256,0,cur>>>(...); auto y2 = at::conv2d(y1n,w2l,{},1,1,1,1); gn_stats(y2,...,nb,npix,...); auto ob = out.narrow(0,b0,nb); gn_apply2<<<dim3(gridp,nb),256,0,cur>>>(y2,xb,...,ob,npix); }` — every kernel launch uses `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` (already the case inside gn_stats), which the guard redirects to the side stream. Grid.y becomes `nb` and all image base offsets are already computed from `blockIdx.y * npix * 256` on the narrowed pointers, so no kernel edit is needed (narrow on dim 0 keeps contiguity).
7. Allocator safety: after the narrow, call `out.record_stream(pool[s%4]);` and `xc.record_stream(...)` (only if xc is a freshly made contiguous copy) so blocks are not recycled before the side stream finishes.
8. Join: for each used stream `at::cuda::CUDAEvent ev; ev.record(stream); ev.block(main_stream);` before `return out;`. This makes the returned tensor safe on the caller's stream and keeps the harness's CUDA-event timing valid.
9. Issue order for maximum overlap: emit chunk 0's full pipeline first, then chunk 1, etc.; because each chunk's conv (SM-heavy, DRAM-light) is followed by GN (DRAM-heavy, SM-light), consecutive streams naturally interleave. Do not add any sync inside the loop.
10. Keep the odd-shape tail logic and the 256-channel fast-path guard untouched; the Python fallback stays for non-256-channel inputs.
11. Validate: all four shapes within atol; confirm in nsys that conv kernels and gn_* kernels appear concurrently and that total forward launches per call rise from 11 to ~11*ns while wall time drops.

Evidence:
Numeric: profiled custom kernels sum to 302 us (2x41.8 gn_stats_p1 + 2x8.0 gn_stats_p2 + 67.2 gn_apply1 + 134.1 gn_apply2) of the 1.251 ms mid-shape time, leaving ~950 us of cuDNN conv; the convs are 155 GFLOP => ~163 TFLOPS = ~33% of H100 TF32 dense peak, i.e. SM/algorithm-bound with DRAM largely idle, while the GN kernels run at 81.7%/82.6%/67.5% DRAM with sm__throughput of only 14.9%/46.9%/28.4%. Root cause: these two complementary phases are strictly serialized on one stream although GroupNorm is per-(sample,group) and therefore batch-separable. Refutation of 'gn_apply2 is the bottleneck': lifting its 67.53% DRAM to gn_apply1's 82.56% ceiling saves only ~24 us = 2% end-to-end (round-1 mem_vectorize already covered that mechanism), an order of magnitude below the ~300 us that overlap can hide.

Expected metric change:
(1) Exposed non-conv time: 302 us of gn_* GPU time becomes largely concurrent with conv, so mid-shape wall time 1.251 ms -> <=1.05 ms (speedup 1.3167x -> >=1.55x); (2) gpu__dram_throughput.avg during the conv windows rises from near-idle toward >40% while conv sm__throughput stays flat (convs unmodified, cuDNN kernel must remain sm90_xmma_fprop...nhwckrsc_nhwc); (3) individual gn_* kernel durations may grow up to +20% from contention — acceptable only if end-to-end improves. Anti-regression: B=1 (1x256x131x131) takes the untouched single-stream path and must stay >=1.84x; 2x256x64x64 >=1.28x, 4x256x256x256 >=1.40x, 8x256x64x128 >=1.32x; all four shapes must pass their atol (per-sample stats are numerically identical after chunking), and the returned tensor must be joined to the caller's stream via events before return.

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization of complementary-resource segments] The forward is a strictly serial chain: two cuDNN NHWC TF32 convs (~950 us, 76% of the 1.251 ms mid shape, only ~163 TFLOPS = ~33% of TF32 dense peak, SM-bound with DRAM mostly idle) alternating with the DRAM-bound custom GN kernels (gn_apply2 134 us @67.5% DRAM, gn_apply1 67.2 us @82.6% DRAM, gn_stats_p1 41.8x2 @81.7% DRAM, sm__throughput only 14.9-46.9%). Neither unit is saturated at the same time.

Optimisation method:
Batch-chunked multi-stream pipelining: GroupNorm statistics are per-(sample,group), so the whole block is exactly independent across batch elements. Split the batch into chunks and run the full conv1->stats->apply1->conv2->stats->apply2 chain for each chunk on its own CUDA stream, so an SM-bound conv of one chunk overlaps the DRAM-bound GN kernels (80% DRAM, <47% SM) of another. This hides most of the ~300 us GN time under the ~950 us conv time; bit-identical math (same per-sample reductions).

Method name:
batch_chunk_stream_overlap

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST
1. Keep every existing kernel body byte-identical (gn_stats_p1/p2, gn_apply1, gn_apply2 already take npix/B via grid.y); the ONLY change is host-side scheduling in fused_block: replace the single monolithic sequence with a per-batch-chunk pipeline issued on N side streams.
2. Exact code action for the split: compute `int ns = (B>=4)?4:((B>=2)?B:1); int cb = (B+ns-1)/ns;` if `ns==1` execute the current code path verbatim (this preserves the 1x256x131x131 shape exactly). Otherwise loop `for (int s=0,b0=0; b0<B; ++s, b0+=cb) { int nb=min(cb,B-b0); ... }` and inside use `x.narrow(0,b0,nb)` / `out.narrow(0,b0,nb)` views only.

METHOD STEPS
3. Stream pool: `static thread_local std::vector<c10::cuda::CUDAStream> pool; if (pool.empty()) for(int i=0;i<4;++i) pool.push_back(c10::cuda::getStreamFromPool());` (created once, reused across the 12 timed forwards).
4. Hoist chunk-invariant work onto the main stream BEFORE the loop: `w1l = w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `w2l = w2.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `xc = x.contiguous()`, and the single output allocation `out = at::empty({B,256,H,W}, opts)`. Do NOT allocate y1/y1n/y2/scale/shift globally; allocate them inside the chunk body so the caching allocator binds them to the side stream.
5. Fork: `at::cuda::CUDAEvent fork; fork.record(at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()); for(auto& s : used_streams) fork.block(s);` so every side stream waits for the caller's prior work and for step-4 allocations/copies.
6. Chunk body: `{ c10::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(pool[s%4]); auto xb = xc.narrow(0,b0,nb); auto xl = xb.contiguous(ChannelsLast); auto y1 = at::conv2d(xl,w1l,{},1,1,1,1); gn_stats(y1,...,nb,npix,...); gn_apply1<<<dim3(gridx,nb),256,0,cur>>>(...); auto y2 = at::conv2d(y1n,w2l,{},1,1,1,1); gn_stats(y2,...,nb,npix,...); auto ob = out.narrow(0,b0,nb); gn_apply2<<<dim3(gridp,nb),256,0,cur>>>(y2,xb,...,ob,npix); }` — every kernel launch uses `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` (already the case inside gn_stats), which the guard redirects to the side stream. Grid.y becomes `nb` and all image base offsets are already computed from `blockIdx.y * npix * 256` on the narrowed pointers, so no kernel edit is needed (narrow on dim 0 keeps contiguity).
7. Allocator safety: after the narrow, call `out.record_stream(pool[s%4]);` and `xc.record_stream(...)` (only if xc is a freshly made contiguous copy) so blocks are not recycled before the side stream finishes.
8. Join: for each used stream `at::cuda::CUDAEvent ev; ev.record(stream); ev.block(main_stream);` before `return out;`. This makes the returned tensor safe on the caller's stream and keeps the harness's CUDA-event timing valid.
9. Issue order for maximum overlap: emit chunk 0's full pipeline first, then chunk 1, etc.; because each chunk's conv (SM-heavy, DRAM-light) is followed by GN (DRAM-heavy, SM-light), consecutive streams naturally interleave. Do not add any sync inside the loop.
10. Keep the odd-shape tail logic and the 256-channel fast-path guard untouched; the Python fallback stays for non-256-channel inputs.
11. Validate: all four shapes within atol; confirm in nsys that conv kernels and gn_* kernels appear concurrently and that total forward launches per call rise from 11 to ~11*ns while wall time drops.

Evidence:

Optimisation method:
Layout propagation in the epilogue: stop converting back to NCHW. Allocate the final output channels-last and rewrite gn_apply2 as a pure float4 NHWC elementwise kernel that reads the residual from xl (the NHWC copy of x already materialized for conv1). This deletes the 34 KB shared tile and the strided NCHW scatter, restoring the same 128-byte coalesced load/store pattern that already lets gn_apply1 hit 82% DRAM at 100% shared-mem occupancy. Same bytes, same dtype, fewer transactions.

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST
1. gn_apply2 kernel body rewrite (exact actions): delete `__shared__ float sm[NCH*(TP+1)]`, delete the `for (int j=0;j<np;++j)` staging loop, delete `__syncthreads()`, and delete the `warp/lane` NCHW scatter loop `for (cc=warp; cc<NCH; cc+=8)`. Replace with the gn_apply1 form plus a residual float4 load:
   `long i = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; if (i>=nvec_per_img) return;`
   `const float4* yin=(const float4*)(y + (size_t)b*nvec_per_img*4); const float4* rin=(const float4*)(res + (size_t)b*nvec_per_img*4); float4* o=(float4*)(out + (size_t)b*nvec_per_img*4);`
   `int c4 = (int)(i & 63); float4 v=yin[i], r=rin[i], sc=((const float4*)(scale+b*NCH))[c4], sh=((const float4*)(shift+b*NCH))[c4];`
   `o[i].x = silu_fast(v.x*sc.x+sh.x)+r.x;` (and .y/.z/.w). No shared memory, no barrier, 24-28 regs.
2. Host-side (exact actions): change the output allocation to `auto out = at::empty({(long)B,(long)NCH,(long)H,(long)W}, opts.memory_format(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast));` and pass `xl.data_ptr<float>()` (the NHWC copy of x already built for conv1 - reuse it, do NOT create a second residual buffer) instead of `xc.data_ptr<float>()`. 3. Drop the now-dead `xc` materialization from the fast path (input x is already contiguous NCHW; `xl` is derived directly from x). Keep `xl` in scope until after the launch so its storage is not freed.

6. ModelNew.forward returns the channels-last tensor unchanged: logical shape is (B,256,H,W) and every element equals the reference, so allclose/atol comparison is unaffected by strides. The eager fallback branch still returns NCHW.
7. Validation: run all four shapes (8x64x128, 2x64x64, 4x256x256, 1x131x131) against the reference at their atol; confirm the awkward shape improves (tail blocks removed) and none regress.
8. If a strict-stride comparator is ever detected, the only change needed is a final `out.contiguous()`, which reintroduces one copy - do not add it preemptively.

Evidence:
gn_apply2 gpu__time_duration.avg = 134,784 ns (largest profiled kernel; apply1 67,456, stats_p1 41,984, stats_p2 8,192) and it achieves 1.38 TB/s (67.34% DRAM) on 3 buffers/element while gn_apply1 achieves 1.67 TB/s (82.18%) on the same 3-buffer traffic. Root cause: launch__shared_mem_per_block = 34,816 B -> Block Limit Shared Mem = 6, theoretical occupancy 75% (achieved 69.08%), l1tex__t_sector_hit_rate 0.62%, long_scoreboard 71.19% with only 0.54 eligible warps/scheduler - the NHWC->NCHW staging transpose is what separates it from apply1's ceiling. Refutation of 'the cuDNN conv segment is the target': it is a default-keep vendor mainloop and round-2 cudnn_algo_autotune already harvested it (+2.4% only); refutation of 'gn_stats_p1': already at 81.47% DRAM (ceiling) and only 42 us.

Expected metric change:
gn_apply2 gpu__dram_throughput.avg 67.34% -> >=80%; launch__shared_mem_per_block 34,816 -> 0 B with Block Limit Shared Mem 6 -> 32 and theoretical occupancy 75% -> 100%; smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard 71.19% -> <=60%; duration 134.8 us -> <=110 us. Anti-regression: gn_apply1 (67.5 us), gn_stats_p1 (42.0 us), gn_stats_p2 (8.0 us) must stay within +/-2% (untouched) and per-forward launch count stays 11; no shape may fall below its current speedup (1.2814 / 1.3167 / 1.4009 / 1.8400) and all four must pass their atol, with the odd-npix 1x256x131x131 shape expected to improve since the masked TP=32 tail disappears.

Bottleneck identified:
[compute-bound tensor-core mainloop] The two cuDNN `sm90_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm_f32f32_tf32f32_f32_nhwckrsc_nhwc_tilesize64x128x32` convolutions (2 launches/forward) consume ~804us of the 1179us forward — all five profiled custom kernels sum to only 375us. The convs run 1.546e11 FLOP at ~192 TFLOP/s, ~51% of TF32 dense peak, i.e. a sub-optimal cuDNN engine-config chosen by heuristics.

Optimisation method:
vendor_algo_autotune: keep the cuDNN implicit-GEMM mainloop (default-keep rule) but replace heuristic plan selection with cuDNN exhaustive benchmark selection for our two conv calls only (locally toggled inside the extension, restored afterwards so the reference path is untouched). Metrics show the conv segment is 68% of runtime at ~51% of TF32 peak while every custom kernel is already at 73–82% of DRAM peak; engine-config/tile/split-K choice is the only sanctioned lever with >5% expected gain.

Method name:
vendor_algo_autotune

Modification plan:
1. EXACT CODE ACTION (enable exhaustive cuDNN plan search, scoped): in `fused_res_block`, immediately after the input checks add an RAII guard:
   `struct BmGuard { bool prev; BmGuard():prev(at::globalContext().benchmarkCuDNN()){ at::globalContext().setBenchmarkCuDNN(true);} ~BmGuard(){ at::globalContext().setBenchmarkCuDNN(prev);} } _bm;`
   This makes both `at::conv2d` calls take PyTorch's cuDNN-v8 `try_all` path (times every engine config, caches the winner per shape/layout key) and restores the previous flag on return so the eager reference `F.conv2d` timing and global state are unchanged.
2. EXACT CODE ACTION (keep numerics identical): right below the guard add `at::globalContext().setAllowTF32CuDNN(true);` (restore the previous value in the same guard). This keeps the same TF32 arithmetic the reference uses, so the exhaustive search only reorders tiles/split-K, never precision. Leave the two `at::conv2d(xl, w1c, nobias, {1,1}, {1,1})` / `(y1s, w2c, ...)` call sites textually unchanged — no layout, no dtype, no bias changes.
3. Alternative call form (only if the installed ATen exposes it; keep flag route as default because it is API-version-safe): `at::cudnn_convolution(xl, w1c, /*padding*/{1,1}, /*stride*/{1,1}, /*dilation*/{1,1}, /*groups*/1, /*benchmark*/true, /*deterministic*/false, /*allow_tf32*/true)`. Do not mix both forms.
4. Do NOT touch K1..K5 this round (nchw2nhwc, stats_partial, stats_finalize, gn_silu_nhwc, gn_silu_res_nchw) — they are already at 72.8–82.3% of DRAM peak, so they are outside the single-method scope.
5. Cache-warm behaviour: the plan search runs once per distinct (N,C,H,W,layout) key. The harness executes warmup iterations before timing, so 4 shapes x 2 convs = 8 searches are amortised. Keep the guard unconditional (no shape gating) so the small 2x256x64x64 shape also gets its cached winner; a cache hit is a hash lookup (<1us).
6. Keep the existing `!y.is_contiguous(ChannelsLast)` re-contiguify checks: an autotuned engine could in principle emit a differently-strided output; the guard keeps correctness and, when the output is already channels-last, costs nothing.
7. Validation checklist: (a) run nsys and confirm the fprop kernel name/tile changed (expect e.g. `tilesize128x128x32` or a split-K variant) and its duration dropped; (b) re-check max|out-ref| on all four shapes against the per-workload tolerances (0.0027–0.003 atol) — TF32 stays enabled so error should be unchanged; (c) confirm the flag is restored by asserting `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark` is unchanged after a forward.
8. Anti-regression gate: score all four shapes; accept only if the geometric mean improves and no individual shape regresses by more than 2%. If the awkward 1x256x131x131 shape regresses (odd extents can make some engines pad heavily), keep the guard but wrap it in `if (P >= 4096)`; otherwise leave it unconditional.
9. Roll-back criterion: if the chosen engine is identical on all four shapes (no kernel-name change in nsys) and total time moves <1%, revert the guard and, in the NEXT round (separate method), target `gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel` with float4 tile transpose to lift its 72.77% DRAM utilisation toward the 82% its siblings reach.

Evidence:
Custom kernels sum to 68.9+2x42.0+2x13.0+67.4+128.8 = 375us/forward, but measured test time is 1179us -> ~804us (68%) is the 2 cuDNN convs (nsys: 24 fprop launches / 12 forwards). Conv work = 2 x 2*8*256*256*9*8192 = 1.546e11 FLOP -> ~192 TFLOP/s, ~51% of TF32 dense peak: heuristic engine-config leaves ~1.9x headroom on the dominant segment. Refutation of the 'memory-bound epilogue' alternative: nchw2nhwc is at 80.93% and gn_silu_nhwc at 82.29% of DRAM peak (already saturated); even lifting the worst, gn_silu_res_nchw (72.77%, 128.8us), to 82% saves only ~13us = 1.1% of the forward — an order of magnitude less than the conv lever.

Expected metric change:
(1) cuDNN fprop segment time 804us -> 650-720us (>=10% down) with a changed kernel/tile name in nsys and sm__throughput / tensor-pipe utilisation up from ~51% toward 60-70% of TF32 peak. (2) End-to-end mid-shape speedup 1.39x -> >=1.50x; geometric mean over the 4 shapes up. (3) DRAM throughput of K1/K4/K5 must stay at 72-83% (unchanged) and launch count stays 11/forward. Anti-regression: no shape may slow by >2%, max_atol must stay under each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003), and torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark must be observably restored after forward so the reference baseline is not accelerated.

Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound, cold-L2 re-read] The five custom kernels move 603 MB/forward at ~80% DRAM; the hottest, gn_silu_res_nchw (129.9 us) plus stats_partial (2x42.7 us) exist only to re-read intermediates the previous kernel just wrote. Working set (67 MB/tensor) exceeds the 50 MB L2, so every re-read (stats1, K4, conv2 input, stats2, K5) is a full DRAM round trip.

Optimisation method:
Cache-blocking the whole fused block over the batch axis so each chunk's intermediates stay L2-resident: run K1 -> conv1 -> stats -> K4 -> conv2 -> stats -> K5 on 1-2 samples at a time, reusing the same temp buffers. GroupNorm statistics are per (n, group) and the residual is elementwise, so batch chunking is exactly equivalent. Evidence: stats_partial lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 4.31% (L2 hit 5.33%) while re-reading a tensor written by the immediately preceding conv; converting those re-reads to L2 hits removes up to 335 MB of DRAM traffic.

Method name:
l2_resident_batch_chunking

Modification plan:
1) In fused_res_block, after computing N,C,H,W,P, add exact code: `const size_t bps = (size_t)C*P*4; const size_t BUDGET = 16ull<<20; int chunkN = (int)(BUDGET / (bps>0?bps:1)); if (chunkN < 1) chunkN = 1; if (chunkN > N) chunkN = N;` then `const bool chunked = (N > chunkN);`. If !chunked, execute exactly today's code path (bit-identical for N=1 and for the 2x256x64x64 shape, where bps=4.2MB -> chunkN>=N).
2) If chunked, hoist ALL allocations and the two weight conversions out of the loop, then loop the whole pipeline: allocate once `xl, y1s` (channels_last) and `out` (NCHW) for the FULL N (out must be full-size); allocate `w1c=w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `w2c` once before the loop. Then `for (int n0=0; n0<N; n0+=chunkN){ int nb=min(chunkN,N-n0); ... }` where inside the body every kernel launch uses grid.z/gridDim.y = nb and base pointers offset by `(size_t)n0*C*P`:
   - K1: `nchw2nhwc_kernel<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(xptr + n0*C*P, xlptr + n0*C*P, P, C)`.
   - conv1: build chunk views with `xl.narrow(0,n0,nb)` (batch-major slice is contiguous in both NCHW and NHWC, no copy) and call `at::conv2d(xl_chunk, w1c, nobias, {1,1},{1,1})` -> y1_chunk (fresh 16 MB alloc, reused by the caching allocator across chunks, which also maximises L2 address reuse).
   - compute_scale_shift(y1_chunk.data_ptr, nb, C, P, G, g1,b1,...): pass nb as N so the partial buffer, nchunks cap and grid.y all shrink; the buffer is allocated inside that helper per chunk (small).
   - K4 gn_silu_nhwc: grid.y = nb, pointers offset for y1s by n0*C*P.
   - conv2 on y1s.narrow(0,n0,nb) -> y2_chunk; compute_scale_shift with nb.
   - K5 gn_silu_res_nchw: `<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(y2ptr, xptr + n0*C*P, outptr + n0*C*P, sc2, sh2, P, C)`.
3) Keep everything on `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` and strictly sequential (single stream) — the L2 win depends on temporal locality, so do NOT add extra streams or overlap.
4) Do not change any kernel body, block size, dtype, or the TF32 conv path; only grid.z/gridDim.y and base pointers vary. The scale/shift tensors are per-chunk of shape {nb,C}, and gn_silu_nhwc indexes them by blockIdx.y in [0,nb), which already matches.
5) Correctness guards: assert nb>=1; tail chunk (nb<chunkN) is handled because every kernel derives its extent from nb, and stats_partial always writes its partial slot (no unwritten tail). P is never tiled, so the 131x131 (odd P) shape is untouched (N=1 -> unchunked path).
6) Tune BUDGET: try 16 MB (mid shape -> chunkN=2, 4 chunks); if the mid shape does not improve, retry 24 MB (chunkN=3). Cap the number of chunks at 8 to bound launch overhead (`if (N/chunkN > 8) chunkN = (N+7)/8;`).
7) Verify launch counts: unchunked shapes stay at 7 kernels + 2 convs; mid shape becomes <= 4x that, all async on one stream.

Evidence:
stats_partial_kernel: lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 4.31% (section L2 Hit Rate 5.33%), l1tex hit 0%, DRAM 79.9%, 42.7 us x2 — it re-reads the 67 MB conv output written one kernel earlier, and 67 MB > 50 MB L2, so every sector misses. gn_silu_res_nchw L2 hit 33.3% for the same reason. Root cause: the working set per stage (67 MB) exceeds L2, so five separate re-reads (stats1, K4, conv2 input, stats2, K5) each cost full DRAM bandwidth (~335 MB of the 871 MB/forward). Refutation of the alternative 'K5 is un-vectorized/smem-transpose bound': K5 moves 201 MB, whose roofline at the measured ~2.03 TB/s is 99 us vs 129.9 us measured — only ~30 us (2.5% of the 1179 us forward) of slack, an order of magnitude less than the 335 MB of removable re-read traffic.

Expected metric change:
(1) stats_partial_kernel lts__t_sector_hit_rate 4.31% -> >40% and its gpu__dram_throughput drops well below 79.9% while gpu__time_duration falls from 42.7 us toward ~20 us per launch; (2) gn_silu_res_nchw lts__t_sector_hit_rate 33.3% -> >50% with duration 129.9 us -> <110 us; total DRAM bytes/forward down >=25% on the 8x256x64x128 shape, mid-shape speedup 1.39x -> >=1.6x. Anti-regression: the 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 shapes must take the unchunked path (identical kernel sequence, <=1% time change); no shape may regress >2%; max_atol must stay within 0.0027-0.003 per workload; kernel launches per forward must not exceed 4x the current 11.

Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound, low-width access] Hottest modifiable kernel is gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel (129.2 us/launch, 34% of the 375 us custom-kernel budget). It moves 201 MB (y2 NHWC read + x NCHW read + NCHW write) yet reaches only 72.5% DRAM vs 81-82% for the sibling streaming kernels: every access is a scalar 4-byte load/store (32 threads = 128 B/request), so 4x more memory instructions per byte and too little memory-level parallelism. The cuDNN convs are default-keep vendor mainloops (already algo-autotuned in round 1).

Optimisation method:
mem_vectorize: rewrite the shared-memory tile transpose in gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel (and the identical pattern in nchw2nhwc_kernel) so every global access is a float4. NHWC side reads 4 contiguous channels per thread; NCHW side writes 4 contiguous spatial positions per thread; the 90-degree turn happens in shared memory, which is untouched by DRAM. This cuts global load/store instructions 4x and widens each request, directly attacking the 68.3% long-scoreboard stall and the 72.5% DRAM utilisation gap (peers reach 82%) without changing bytes moved, dtype, or numerics.

Method name:
mem_vectorize

Modification plan:
1. In gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel, replace the 4 scalar global loads of the NHWC input per thread with ONE float4 load covering 4 consecutive channels (NHWC is contiguous in C, C=256 so C%4==0 always), and replace the 4 scalar global stores/residual loads with ONE float4 store + ONE float4 residual load covering 4 consecutive spatial positions (NCHW is contiguous in P). Numerics unchanged: silu(v*scale+shift)+res is applied element-wise on the float4 lanes.
2. Same mechanism in nchw2nhwc_kernel: float4 load along P (NCHW), float4 store along C (NHWC); no scalar path remains in the vector kernel.
3. Tile/block geometry for the new K5v: tile 64 channels x 64 spatial positions, block 256 threads (32,8). Shared memory float tile[64][68] (pad 4 floats per row) = 17.4 KB/block -> under the 227 KB per-block limit and allows >=8 concurrent blocks/SM (registers ~32, occupancy stays >=8 blocks). Each thread performs 4 float4 loads and 4 float4 stores (64*64/4 = 1024 float4 per phase / 256 threads = 4).
4. Load phase (K5v): p = p0 + (tid/16), c4 = tid%16; read float4 at in[((n*P)+p)*C + c0 + 4*c4]; apply scale/shift + SiLU per lane using scale[n*C+c] broadcast from a per-block __shared__ float sc[64], sh[64] preloaded once (64 threads load them coalesced); store the 4 results as scalars tile[c][p] (stride 68). Repeat 4 times with p += 16.
5. Store phase: __syncthreads(); c = c0 + (tid/16), p4 = tid%16; read tile[c][p0+4*p4 .. +3] (contiguous in shared memory, one float4 load) -> add float4 residual res[n*C*P + c*P + p] -> one float4 store to out[same index]. Repeat 4 times with c += 16.
6. Alignment/tail guard (critical for the awkward 131x131 shape): the NCHW float4 requires (P % 4 == 0) so that c*P keeps 16 B alignment. In the host wrapper, dispatch to the vectorized kernels only when (P % 4 == 0); otherwise launch the EXISTING scalar nchw2nhwc_kernel / gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel unchanged. P=8192/4096/65536 take the fast path; P=17161 keeps today's code and today's timing bit-for-bit.
7. Handle the P-tail inside the vector path with a `p0 + 63 < P` fast branch and a masked slow branch that still uses float4 (P%4==0 guarantees whole float4 groups; only whole-group masking is needed). C tail needs no mask (C=256, multiple of 64).
8. Keep the scale/shift preload in shared memory so the per-thread affine constants are read once per block instead of once per element (removes the redundant scalar scale/shift global loads currently issued per tile column).
9. Do not touch stats_partial_kernel, stats_finalize_kernel, gn_silu_nhwc_kernel, the at::conv2d calls, weight channels-last conversion, or the fallback path. Kernel launch count per forward stays 11.
10. Validate: compare against F.conv2d/group_norm/silu reference on all four shapes; assert max_atol < 0.0027 (tightest tolerance) and confirm the 131x131 shape hits the scalar fallback (add a debug counter in a test build only).

Evidence:
gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel: gpu__time_duration.avg = 129216 ns (largest custom kernel; K1 68768, K4 67520, stats 2x42112), gpu__dram_throughput = 72.54% vs 82.11% (gn_silu_nhwc, float4) and 81.0% (K1) — measured 1.4795 TB/s against the ~2.04 TB/s these kernels achieve at 100%, i.e. ~99 us roofline for its 201 MB. long_scoreboard stall = 68.28% of 29.1 warp-cycles/issue, l1tex hit 13.52%, l1tex throughput only 22.23% — root cause: all three streams use 4-byte scalar accesses (128 B/warp request), so the kernel issues 4x the memory instructions of the float4 K4 and cannot cover DRAM latency. Refutation of 'occupancy-limited': achieved occupancy 91.04% and warps_active 91.22% are the highest of any kernel here, so more warps cannot be the fix. Refutation of 'shared-memory/bank-conflict bound': short_scoreboard is only 3.50% and smem spilling requests are 0, so the smem transpose is not the stall.

Expected metric change:
(1) gn_silu_res_nchw duration 129.2 us -> <=110 us with gpu__dram_throughput 72.54% -> >=80% and long_scoreboard 68.3% -> <60%; (2) nchw2nhwc duration 68.8 us -> <=58 us, its global memory instruction count down ~4x (l1tex__throughput may rise, sector count unchanged); (3) total custom-kernel time 375 us -> <=335 us, mid-shape speedup 1.39x -> >=1.44x. Anti-regression constraints: DRAM bytes moved per forward must NOT increase (same 603 MB); launches per forward stay 11; the 1x256x131x131 shape (P%4!=0) must take the untouched scalar path and change by <=1%; no shape may regress >2%; max_atol must stay under each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003); registers/thread <=40 so occupancy stays >=8 blocks/SM.

Bottleneck identified:
[compute-bound tensor-core mainloop] The two cuDNN `sm90_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm_f32f32_tf32f32_f32_nhwckrsc_nhwc_tilesize64x128x32` convolutions (2 launches/forward) consume ~804us of the 1179us forward — all five profiled custom kernels sum to only 375us. The convs run 1.546e11 FLOP at ~192 TFLOP/s, ~51% of TF32 dense peak, i.e. a sub-optimal cuDNN engine-config chosen by heuristics.

Optimisation method:
vendor_algo_autotune: keep the cuDNN implicit-GEMM mainloop (default-keep rule) but replace heuristic plan selection with cuDNN exhaustive benchmark selection for our two conv calls only (locally toggled inside the extension, restored afterwards so the reference path is untouched). Metrics show the conv segment is 68% of runtime at ~51% of TF32 peak while every custom kernel is already at 73–82% of DRAM peak; engine-config/tile/split-K choice is the only sanctioned lever with >5% expected gain.

Method name:
vendor_algo_autotune

Modification plan:
1. EXACT CODE ACTION (enable exhaustive cuDNN plan search, scoped): in `fused_res_block`, immediately after the input checks add an RAII guard:
   `struct BmGuard { bool prev; BmGuard():prev(at::globalContext().benchmarkCuDNN()){ at::globalContext().setBenchmarkCuDNN(true);} ~BmGuard(){ at::globalContext().setBenchmarkCuDNN(prev);} } _bm;`
   This makes both `at::conv2d` calls take PyTorch's cuDNN-v8 `try_all` path (times every engine config, caches the winner per shape/layout key) and restores the previous flag on return so the eager reference `F.conv2d` timing and global state are unchanged.
2. EXACT CODE ACTION (keep numerics identical): right below the guard add `at::globalContext().setAllowTF32CuDNN(true);` (restore the previous value in the same guard). This keeps the same TF32 arithmetic the reference uses, so the exhaustive search only reorders tiles/split-K, never precision. Leave the two `at::conv2d(xl, w1c, nobias, {1,1}, {1,1})` / `(y1s, w2c, ...)` call sites textually unchanged — no layout, no dtype, no bias changes.
3. Alternative call form (only if the installed ATen exposes it; keep flag route as default because it is API-version-safe): `at::cudnn_convolution(xl, w1c, /*padding*/{1,1}, /*stride*/{1,1}, /*dilation*/{1,1}, /*groups*/1, /*benchmark*/true, /*deterministic*/false, /*allow_tf32*/true)`. Do not mix both forms.
4. Do NOT touch K1..K5 this round (nchw2nhwc, stats_partial, stats_finalize, gn_silu_nhwc, gn_silu_res_nchw) — they are already at 72.8–82.3% of DRAM peak, so they are outside the single-method scope.
5. Cache-warm behaviour: the plan search runs once per distinct (N,C,H,W,layout) key. The harness executes warmup iterations before timing, so 4 shapes x 2 convs = 8 searches are amortised. Keep the guard unconditional (no shape gating) so the small 2x256x64x64 shape also gets its cached winner; a cache hit is a hash lookup (<1us).
6. Keep the existing `!y.is_contiguous(ChannelsLast)` re-contiguify checks: an autotuned engine could in principle emit a differently-strided output; the guard keeps correctness and, when the output is already channels-last, costs nothing.
7. Validation checklist: (a) run nsys and confirm the fprop kernel name/tile changed (expect e.g. `tilesize128x128x32` or a split-K variant) and its duration dropped; (b) re-check max|out-ref| on all four shapes against the per-workload tolerances (0.0027–0.003 atol) — TF32 stays enabled so error should be unchanged; (c) confirm the flag is restored by asserting `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark` is unchanged after a forward.
8. Anti-regression gate: score all four shapes; accept only if the geometric mean improves and no individual shape regresses by more than 2%. If the awkward 1x256x131x131 shape regresses (odd extents can make some engines pad heavily), keep the guard but wrap it in `if (P >= 4096)`; otherwise leave it unconditional.
9. Roll-back criterion: if the chosen engine is identical on all four shapes (no kernel-name change in nsys) and total time moves <1%, revert the guard and, in the NEXT round (separate method), target `gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel` with float4 tile transpose to lift its 72.77% DRAM utilisation toward the 82% its siblings reach.

Evidence:
Custom kernels sum to 68.9+2x42.0+2x13.0+67.4+128.8 = 375us/forward, but measured test time is 1179us -> ~804us (68%) is the 2 cuDNN convs (nsys: 24 fprop launches / 12 forwards). Conv work = 2 x 2*8*256*256*9*8192 = 1.546e11 FLOP -> ~192 TFLOP/s, ~51% of TF32 dense peak: heuristic engine-config leaves ~1.9x headroom on the dominant segment. Refutation of the 'memory-bound epilogue' alternative: nchw2nhwc is at 80.93% and gn_silu_nhwc at 82.29% of DRAM peak (already saturated); even lifting the worst, gn_silu_res_nchw (72.77%, 128.8us), to 82% saves only ~13us = 1.1% of the forward — an order of magnitude less than the conv lever.

Expected metric change:
(1) cuDNN fprop segment time 804us -> 650-720us (>=10% down) with a changed kernel/tile name in nsys and sm__throughput / tensor-pipe utilisation up from ~51% toward 60-70% of TF32 peak. (2) End-to-end mid-shape speedup 1.39x -> >=1.50x; geometric mean over the 4 shapes up. (3) DRAM throughput of K1/K4/K5 must stay at 72-83% (unchanged) and launch count stays 11/forward. Anti-regression: no shape may slow by >2%, max_atol must stay under each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003), and torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark must be observably restored after forward so the reference baseline is not accelerated.

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization of complementary-bound stages] Hottest non-removable segment is the composite cuDNN TF32 fprop mainloop (~804us of the 1179us forward, ~0.33 TB/s DRAM = ~16% of achievable) executed strictly serially with the DRAM-bound GN/SiLU/transpose chain (375us at 72-82% DRAM but only 15-50% SM). Compute-bound and bandwidth-bound work never coexist, so ~375us of memory time is fully exposed.

Optimisation method:
Per-sample stream pipelining: GroupNorm statistics are per (n,group) and conv/residual are per-sample, so the block decomposes EXACTLY along batch. Split N into chunks, run each chunk's full 9-kernel sequence on one of two side CUDA streams, so chunk i's cuDNN conv (SM/tensor-core bound, 84% of DRAM idle) overlaps chunk i-1's stats/gn_silu/transpose kernels (80%+ DRAM, <50% SM). Vendor conv mainloop is kept untouched; only scheduling changes.

Method name:
stream_pipeline_overlap

Modification plan:
1) EXACT DECOMPOSITION (in fused_res_block, before any launch): compute `int nchunks = (N >= 4 && (size_t)N*C*P*4ull >= (32u<<20)) ? std::min(4, N) : 1; int cs = (N + nchunks - 1)/nchunks; nchunks = (N + cs - 1)/cs;`. If nchunks==1 execute today's code path verbatim (bit-identical kernel sequence, single stream) — this is the mandatory fallback for the N=1 (1x256x131x131) and N=2 (2x256x64x64) shapes.
2) EXACT STREAM PLUMBING: hoist `auto w1c = w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast); auto w2c = w2.contiguous(ChannelsLast); at::Tensor out = at::empty({N,C,H,W}, opts);` to before the loop on the current stream. Grab `auto s0 = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool(); auto s1 = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool();`. Record `at::cuda::CUDAEvent start; start.record(main);` then `start.block(s0); start.block(s1);`. Loop `for (c=0;c<nchunks;++c){ auto st = (c&1)? s1 : s0; at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(st); ... }` and inside the guard call `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` so every existing kernel launch and `at::conv2d` lands on `st` unmodified. After the loop: `for each side stream: CUDAEvent e; e.record(st); e.block(main);`.
3) PER-CHUNK POINTER MATH: for chunk offset `n0` and length `nc`, pass `xc.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)n0*C*P` and `out.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)n0*C*P` to K1/K5 with N replaced by `nc` (grids become dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nc)); build the conv input view as `xl_c = xl.narrow(0, 0, nc)` where xl is allocated per chunk with shape {nc,C,H,W} ChannelsLast (narrow along batch preserves channels_last strides).
4) ALLOCATOR SAFETY: allocate all per-chunk intermediates (xl, y1, y1s, y2, partial, scale/shift) INSIDE the stream guard so the caching allocator tags them to `st`. For the cross-stream tensors allocated on the main stream (xc, w1c, w2c, out) call `t.record_stream(st)` once per side stream to prevent premature reuse.
5) STATS SCOPE: compute_scale_shift is already per-sample; call it with N=nc and the chunk base pointer. inv_count and the (n,g) block mapping are unchanged, so numerics are bit-identical to the unchunked path (no cross-sample reduction exists).
6) KEEP THE VENDOR MAINLOOP: do not touch at::conv2d, TF32, or the round-1 cudnn benchmark autotune; per-chunk conv shapes are constant across iterations so the benchmark cache is hit once and reused.
7) CHUNK-SIZE GUARD: require each chunk's conv GEMM to keep the GPU busy — assert `nc*P/64*2 >= 256` CTAs (mid shape: nc=2 -> 512 CTAs); if not, reduce nchunks to 2 or 1.
8) BONUS (not the mechanism): per-chunk working set is 16.7MB at the mid shape, so the stats->K4 and stats->K5 re-reads of the same chunk may now hit L2; do not restructure anything else to chase this.
9) VALIDATION: run all four shapes; confirm nsys shows sm90_xmma fprop ranges overlapping stats_partial/gn_silu ranges, confirm max_atol under each workload tolerance, and confirm the N<4 shapes emit exactly 11 launches on the default stream.

Evidence:
Convs = 804us/1179us (nsys: 24 fprop launches/12 forwards) moving only 134MB -> ~0.33 TB/s = ~16% of the 2.04 TB/s these kernels actually achieve; meanwhile stats_partial gpu__dram_throughput=80.2% with sm__throughput=15.8%, gn_silu_nhwc 82.4% DRAM / 46.3% SM, nchw2nhwc 81.3% DRAM / 50.6% SM, stats_finalize 0.28 waves/SM. Root cause: strictly serial chaining of a tensor-core-bound mainloop and a DRAM-bound epilogue chain leaves each unit idle in turn; GroupNorm is per-(n,g) so the chain is exactly separable by batch. Refutation of the 'K5 is the bottleneck, vectorize it' alternative: gn_silu_res_nchw moves 201MB, roofline 99us vs 128.2us measured = only 29us (2.5% of the forward) of slack, and history round 3 (mem_vectorize) measured 1.549 < round 1's 1.566; the hideable memory time is 375us, an order of magnitude larger.

Expected metric change:
(1) Wall-clock forward at 8x256x64x128 drops from ~1047us (best-known) to <=880us while the SUM of individual kernel durations stays >=1000us — i.e. nsys shows fprop ranges temporally overlapping stats_partial/gn_silu_nhwc/gn_silu_res_nchw ranges. (2) GPU-level gpu__dram_throughput during the conv windows rises from ~16% toward >=40%; stats_finalize's 2x13us latency-bound launches become fully hidden. Per-launch custom-kernel durations may rise <=15% from SM contention — acceptable only if total time falls. Anti-regression: nchunks==1 fallback must give byte-identical kernel sequence and <=1% time change on 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131; no shape may regress >2%; max_atol within 0.0027-0.003; launches <=44/forward; no cross-stream use-after-free (record_stream on xc/w1c/w2c/out).

Bottleneck identified:
[latency-bound reduction inside the hottest custom composite] The GroupNorm segment (stats_partial 2x42.2us + stats_finalize 2x13.2us + apply kernels 67.2us/129.9us) is 307us of the 375us custom-kernel time. Its reduction is split across two launches through a 2MB partial buffer; stats_finalize does no bandwidth work (DRAM 7.89%, 0.28 waves/SM, 25.6% occupancy) and is 87% uncoalesced-sector bound, costing ~26us per forward almost independently of shape.

Optimisation method:
atomic_privatize: privatize the group reduction inside stats_partial. Each block already holds all 256 channels, so reduce the 8 lanes of each group in-register (__shfl_down width 8) and atomicAdd 32 (sum,sumsq) pairs into a tiny [N][G][2] accumulator, then let the last arriving block per image (atomic counter + __threadfence) emit scale/shift. This deletes the 2MB partial round-trip, the 87%-excessive-sector strided loads and both latency-bound stats_finalize launches, which metrics show are pure launch/latency cost, not bandwidth.

Method name:
atomic_privatize

Modification plan:
Checklist (all inside compute_scale_shift + stats kernel; K1/K4/K5/conv untouched):
1. Delete the `partial` tensor `at::empty({2, N*nchunks*C})` and the entire `stats_finalize_kernel` launch. Allocate ONE zeroed scratch for BOTH norms at the top of fused_res_block: `auto acc = at::zeros({2, N*G*2 + N}, opts)` reinterpreted as {float acc[N][G][2]; float ctr[N];} per norm (ctr read as int*). This is one tiny memset for the whole forward, so launches/forward go 11 -> 10 while removing 2x13.2us kernels.
2. Rename stats_partial_kernel -> stats_atomic_kernel(in, acc, ctr, scale, shift, gamma, beta, P, C, chunk, nchunks, G, CPG, inv_count, eps). Keep the existing accumulation loop byte-for-byte (`ptr += C`, `__ldg`) - it is already 80.8% DRAM and coalesced; only the epilogue changes.
3. In-register group reduction (replaces the global partial write): with c = threadIdx.x, CPG = C/G = 8 contiguous lanes per group, do
   `#pragma unroll for (int off = CPG>>1; off; off >>= 1) { s += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, s, off, CPG); q += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, q, off, CPG); }`
   then `if ((c & (CPG-1)) == 0) { int g = c / CPG; atomicAdd(&acc[((n*G)+g)*2+0], s); atomicAdd(&acc[((n*G)+g)*2+1], q); }`. Generic guard: if CPG is not a power of two or CPG > 32, fall back to a 256-float shared-memory segmented reduction (never taken for C=256,G=32).
4. Last-block finalize (removes the second launch): `__threadfence(); __shared__ int isLast; if (threadIdx.x==0) isLast = (atomicAdd(&ctr_i[n],1) == nchunks-1); __syncthreads(); if (isLast) { int g = c / CPG; float sm = acc[(n*G+g)*2+0]*inv_count; float v = acc[(n*G+g)*2+1]*inv_count - sm*sm; v = v<0.f?0.f:v; float r = rsqrtf(v+eps); float gm = gamma?gamma[c]:1.f, bt = beta?beta[c]:0.f; scale[n*C+c] = r*gm; shift[n*C+c] = bt - sm*r*gm; }` - one fully coalesced 256-float store pair per (n) instead of the 458752 excessive sectors the old finalize generated.
5. All 256 threads must reach the __syncthreads(), so keep the empty-range case (p0>=p1) executing the same code path with s=q=0; grid stays dim3(nchunks, N) with nchunks == ceil(P/chunk) exactly, so the counter always reaches nchunks (verified for P=17161 awkward shape and P=4096/8192/65536).
6. Cap atomic contention: clamp nchunks <= 1024 (existing cap logic already yields 128/64/512), so at most 1024 fp32 atomicAdds per (n,g) - accumulation error ~1e-6 relative, well inside atol 0.0028. Keep the `var<0 -> 0` clamp and fp32 accumulation everywhere; no dtype change.
7. Call sites: compute_scale_shift now takes the acc/ctr slice index (0 for norm1, 1 for norm2) and launches exactly one kernel; scale/shift tensors and their layout [N][C] are unchanged so gn_silu_nhwc_kernel and gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel need zero edits.
8. Validate: run all four shapes; assert launches/forward == 10 in nsys and that stats_finalize_kernel no longer appears; assert max_atol per workload (0.0027-0.003).

Evidence:
stats_finalize_kernel: gpu__time_duration 13152 ns x2 launches/forward (26.4us) while moving only 2MB - gpu__dram_throughput 7.89%, launch__waves_per_multiprocessor 0.28, achieved occupancy 25.56%, and the UncoalescedGlobalAccess rule reports 458752 excessive sectors = 87% of 525312 (thread index maps to ck, stride C floats). Root cause: the group reduction is artificially split into a global 2MB partial buffer plus a tiny, strided, latency-bound second launch, although each stats_partial block already spans all 256 channels and can reduce its 8-lane groups in-register. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_silu_res_nchw (129.9us) is the bottleneck': its 201MB at the 2.04 TB/s its sibling kernels achieve rooflines at 99us, i.e. only ~30us (2.5% of the 1179us forward) of slack, and history round 3 attacked exactly that kernel with mem_vectorize and scored 1.549 < the 1.566 best - whereas the 26.4us finalize cost is nearly shape-independent and therefore ~10% of the 205us small shape and ~6% of the 352us awkward shape in the geometric mean.

Expected metric change:
(1) stats_finalize_kernel vanishes from the profile: launches/forward 11 -> 10, 2x13152 ns removed; the surviving stats kernel keeps gpu__dram_throughput >= 78% (currently 80.75%) with gpu__time_duration <= 44.5us (<= 5% above the current 42.176us) and its uncoalesced excessive-sector share drops from 87% to < 10% (per-block global stores fall from 512 floats to 64 atomics). (2) DRAM bytes/forward drop by the 2x2MB partial-buffer round trip and total custom-kernel time 375us -> <= 348us; mid-shape speedup 1.3896x -> >= 1.42x, small shape 1.3558x -> >= 1.45x, awkward shape 1.9211x -> >= 1.98x. Anti-regression: no shape may regress > 2%; max_atol must stay under each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003) with fp32 accumulation unchanged; registers/thread <= 40 so >= 8 blocks/SM occupancy is preserved; the acc/ctr scratch must be zeroed exactly once per forward (single at::zeros) and the counter must reach nchunks on every shape including P=17161.

[latency/serialization: compute-bound mainloop serialized with DRAM-bound epilogue] Hottest non-removable segment is the composite cuDNN TF32 fprop pair (~804us of the 1179us forward, ~16% DRAM, ~51% TF32 peak) executed strictly after/before the five custom kernels (375us at 72-83% DRAM but only 10-50% SM). Optimisation method:
Batch-pipelined dual-stream overlap: because GroupNorm is per-(n,group) and conv is per-sample, the whole chain is exactly separable along N. Split the batch into exactly TWO halves (pointer offsets, no copies) and run each half's full chain (K1->conv1->stats->K4->conv2->stats->K5) on its own stream, so one half's DRAM-saturated GN/transpose kernels execute under the other half's tensor-core conv. Metrics justify it: convs ~16% DRAM/high SM vs customs 78-83% DRAM/15-50% SM — perfectly complementary units that never coexist today.

Method name:
batch_pipelined_dual_stream_overlap

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST (do exactly these; nothing else changes):
1. Refactor `fused_res_block` so the existing per-sample chain becomes a helper `run_chain(const float* x_ptr, float* out_ptr, int n_sub, C,H,W,G, w1c,w2c,g1,b1,g2,b2, eps, stream)` that issues K1, at::conv2d, compute_scale_shift, K4, at::conv2d, compute_scale_shift, K5 on the GIVEN stream with the GIVEN batch count. Batch is the outermost dim of both NCHW x and NHWC intermediates, so a half is just `x.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)half*C*P` and `out.data_ptr<float>() + same` — NO copies, NO views needed for the raw-pointer kernels; for the two at::conv2d calls build the half input with `at::from_blob`-free `xl.narrow(0,0,half)` / `xl.narrow(0,half,half)` (narrow on dim0 keeps channels_last contiguity).
2. Gate: enable the pipelined path only when `N >= 4 && N % 2 == 0 && P >= 4096`. Otherwise call `run_chain` once on the current stream — byte-identical kernel sequence to today for the 2x256x64x64 (N=2) and 1x256x131x131 (N=1) shapes, which must not regress.
3. Before forking, on the CURRENT stream only: `xc = x.contiguous()`, `w1c/w2c = contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, allocate the FULL-size `xl` (channels_last) and `out` (NCHW). This keeps the caching allocator and the weight elementwise_kernels off the side stream.
4. Get a side stream once via a function-local `static auto s_side = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool();` (never create/destroy per call). Use `at::cuda::CUDAEvent` (or two static cudaEvents) for ordering.
5. Ordering: record `ev_start` on the current stream after step 3; `s_side.wait(ev_start)`. 10. Verify numerics: halves are fully independent (GroupNorm reduces over (c,h,w) within one sample), so the result is bit-identical to the single-stream path; run the awkward P=17161 shape through the fallback branch unchanged.
