Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound, cold-L2 re-read] Hottest non-removable segment is the GroupNorm two-pass chain: stats_partial 2x42.8us + stats_finalize 2x13.2us + gn_silu_nhwc 67.4us + gn_silu_res_nchw 129.4us = 307us of 375us custom time. Each GN reads its 67MB intermediate twice via two separate full-tensor launches, so the apply pass misses L2 (4.3%/33.5% hit) and pays full DRAM cost.

Optimisation method:
Slab-interleaved producer/consumer scheduling of the GN passes: instead of one stats launch over the whole tensor then one apply launch over the whole tensor, loop over ~17MB slabs (whole samples; contiguous channel-group halves if one sample exceeds the budget) issuing stats->finalize->apply per slab on the same stream. The apply then re-reads data still resident in the 50MB L2, removing one full 67MB DRAM read per GroupNorm (134MB/forward = 22% of the 603MB custom traffic). Convs, K1 and all kernel math untouched.

Method name:
slab_interleaved_gn_l2_reuse

Modification plan:
Host-side scheduling change only; kernel bodies gain pointer/range offsets, no algorithmic change.
1) In fused_res_block compute the slab size once: `size_t sample_bytes=(size_t)C*P*4; int slab_n=(int)max<size_t>(1,(17ull<<20)/sample_bytes); slab_n=min(slab_n,N);` (17MB read + 17MB write stays under the 50MB L2).
2) Replace the GN1 sequence `compute_scale_shift(y1 whole) ; gn_silu_nhwc(whole)` with: `for(int n0=0;n0<N;n0+=slab_n){int nb=min(slab_n,N-n0); size_t off=(size_t)n0*P*C; stats_partial_kernel<<<dim3(nchunks,nb),C>>>(y1+off, psum+(size_t)n0*nchunks*C, psq+(size_t)n0*nchunks*C, P,C,chunk,nchunks); stats_finalize_kernel<<<nb*G,256>>>(psum+(size_t)n0*nchunks*C, psq+..., g1,b1, sc1+(size_t)n0*C, sh1+(size_t)n0*C, C,G,CPG,nchunks,inv_count,eps); gn_silu_nhwc_kernel<<<dim3((P+by-1)/by, nb)>>>(y1+off, y1s+off, sc1+(size_t)n0*C, sh1+(size_t)n0*C, P, C4);}` — every kernel already indexes batch via blockIdx.y/z, so passing base+off and a reduced nb is sufficient; no index math inside kernels changes.
3) Do the identical loop for GN2, with `gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(y2+off, xc+off, out+off, sc2+n0*C, sh2+n0*C, P, C)` (its blockIdx.z is n, so nb slabs work unchanged).
4) Allocate psum/psq/scale/shift ONCE for the full N (as today) and index by n0, so no per-slab allocation or allocator churn; all launches stay on the current stream, whose program order already guarantees stats->apply ordering (no events/syncs needed).
5) Oversized-sample fallback (large shape 4x256x256x256, sample=67MB>17MB): additionally split channels into contiguous chunks CS = 8*ceil(...) chosen so `P*CS*4<=17MB`, with CS a multiple of 32 (keeps K5's 32-wide c tile and K4's float4 valid) and a multiple of CPG=8 (keeps whole groups intact). Pass `c0` and CS: stats blockDim.x=CS with base pointer `+c0`, finalize grid `nb*(CS/CPG)` with gamma/beta/scale/shift offset by c0, K4 grid.x over C4=CS/4 with row stride C, K5 grid.y=CS/32 with `c0` added to c. Row runs stay >=256B so loads remain coalesced.
6) Single-slab fast path: if `N*sample_bytes <= 17MB` (2x256x64x64 = 8.4MB and 1x256x131x131 = 17.6MB borderline -> allow <=18MB) the loop body executes exactly once with the current grids, giving a byte-identical kernel sequence to today for the small and awkward shapes.
7) Keep chunk/nchunks selection identical to today (`nchunks` derived from full P and full N cap) so the partial-buffer layout and the always-written tail (`psum[o]=s` even when p0>=p1) are preserved for P=17161.
8) Do not touch: nchw2nhwc_kernel, both at::conv2d calls, weight `contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, tolerance-relevant fp32 accumulation.
9) Verify per-shape: max_atol vs reference (0.0027-0.003), and that launches/forward stay <=100 (mid: 4 slabs x 3 x 2 GNs + K1 + 2 convs = 27).
10) If measured L2 hit on the apply pass does not exceed 60%, halve the slab budget to 8MB before abandoning; do not add streams, atomics, or vectorization changes (single-method constraint).

Evidence:
stats_partial_kernel: lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 4.3%, l1tex hit 0%, gpu__dram_throughput 79.65%, 42.8us x2 — it re-reads the 67MB conv output written one kernel earlier, and 67MB > 50MB L2 so every sector misses; gn_silu_res_nchw lts hit 33.45% at 72.47% DRAM, 129.4us. Root cause: the GN stats pass and the GN apply pass are two separate full-tensor launches, so the intermediate is streamed from DRAM twice (134MB of the 603MB custom traffic is pure re-read). Refutation of 'the cuDNN TF32 fprop mainloop (~800us) is the target': it is a default-keep vendor mainloop already algo-selected in round 1 (1.566), and both overlap attempts (rounds 4/6) scored below it; refutation of 'per-kernel bandwidth tuning': all five customs sit at 72-82% of the ~2.04 TB/s these kernels actually achieve, leaving <=40us of roofline slack, which round 3's mem_vectorize confirmed (1.549 < 1.566).

Expected metric change:
(1) gn_silu_nhwc_kernel and gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel lts__t_sector_hit_rate rise from 49.9%/33.45% to >70%, with gpu__dram_throughput falling well below 82%/72% while gpu__time_duration drops 67.4us->~45us and 129.4us->~105us per forward; (2) DRAM bytes/forward for the custom kernels fall >=20% (603MB->~469MB) and total custom time 375us-><=310us, mid-shape speedup 1.3896x->>=1.47x (>=1.65x when composed with the round-1 conv autotune), large shape 1.4924x->>=1.58x. Anti-regression: 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 must take the single-slab path with an identical kernel sequence and <=1% time change; no shape may regress >2%; stats_partial duration must not rise >5% (42.8us) and its DRAM throughput must stay >=75%; kernel launches/forward <=100; max_atol within each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003) with fp32 accumulation and the always-written partial tail preserved for P=17161.

pairs.a_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound, cold-L2 re-read] The five custom kernels move 603 MB/forward at ~80% DRAM; the hottest, gn_silu_res_nchw (129.9 us) plus stats_partial (2x42.7 us) exist only to re-read intermediates the previous kernel just wrote. Working set (67 MB/tensor) exceeds the 50 MB L2, so every re-read (stats1, K4, conv2 input, stats2, K5) is a full DRAM round trip.

Optimisation method:
Cache-blocking the whole fused block over the batch axis so each chunk's intermediates stay L2-resident: run K1 -> conv1 -> stats -> K4 -> conv2 -> stats -> K5 on 1-2 samples at a time, reusing the same temp buffers. GroupNorm statistics are per (n, group) and the residual is elementwise, so batch chunking is exactly equivalent. Evidence: stats_partial lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 4.31% (L2 hit 5.33%) while re-reading a tensor written by the immediately preceding conv; converting those re-reads to L2 hits removes up to 335 MB of DRAM traffic.

Method name:
l2_resident_batch_chunking

Modification plan:
1) In fused_res_block, after computing N,C,H,W,P, add exact code: `const size_t bps = (size_t)C*P*4; const size_t BUDGET = 16ull<<20; int chunkN = (int)(BUDGET / (bps>0?bps:1)); if (chunkN < 1) chunkN = 1; if (chunkN > N) chunkN = N;` then `const bool chunked = (N > chunkN);`. If !chunked, execute exactly today's code path (bit-identical for N=1 and for the 2x256x64x64 shape, where bps=4.2MB -> chunkN>=N).
2) If chunked, hoist ALL allocations and the two weight conversions out of the loop, then loop the whole pipeline: allocate once `xl, y1s` (channels_last) and `out` (NCHW) for the FULL N (out must be full-size); allocate `w1c=w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `w2c` once before the loop. Then `for (int n0=0; n0<N; n0+=chunkN){ int nb=min(chunkN,N-n0); ... }` where inside the body every kernel launch uses grid.z/gridDim.y = nb and base pointers offset by `(size_t)n0*C*P`:
   - K1: `nchw2nhwc_kernel<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(xptr + n0*C*P, xlptr + n0*C*P, P, C)`.
   - conv1: build chunk views with `xl.narrow(0,n0,nb)` (batch-major slice is contiguous in both NCHW and NHWC, no copy) and call `at::conv2d(xl_chunk, w1c, nobias, {1,1},{1,1})` -> y1_chunk (fresh 16 MB alloc, reused by the caching allocator across chunks, which also maximises L2 address reuse).
   - compute_scale_shift(y1_chunk.data_ptr, nb, C, P, G, g1,b1,...): pass nb as N so the partial buffer, nchunks cap and grid.y all shrink; the buffer is allocated inside that helper per chunk (small).
   - K4 gn_silu_nhwc: grid.y = nb, pointers offset for y1s by n0*C*P.
   - conv2 on y1s.narrow(0,n0,nb) -> y2_chunk; compute_scale_shift with nb.
   - K5 gn_silu_res_nchw: `<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(y2ptr, xptr + n0*C*P, outptr + n0*C*P, sc2, sh2, P, C)`.
3) Keep everything on `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` and strictly sequential (single stream) — the L2 win depends on temporal locality, so do NOT add extra streams or overlap.
4) Do not change any kernel body, block size, dtype, or the TF32 conv path; only grid.z/gridDim.y and base pointers vary. The scale/shift tensors are per-chunk of shape {nb,C}, and gn_silu_nhwc indexes them by blockIdx.y in [0,nb), which already matches.
5) Correctness guards: assert nb>=1; tail chunk (nb<chunkN) is handled because every kernel derives its extent from nb, and stats_partial always writes its partial slot (no unwritten tail). P is never tiled, so the 131x131 (odd P) shape is untouched (N=1 -> unchunked path).
6) Tune BUDGET: try 16 MB (mid shape -> chunkN=2, 4 chunks); if the mid shape does not improve, retry 24 MB (chunkN=3). Cap the number of chunks at 8 to bound launch overhead (`if (N/chunkN > 8) chunkN = (N+7)/8;`).
7) Verify launch counts: unchunked shapes stay at 7 kernels + 2 convs; mid shape becomes <= 4x that, all async on one stream.

Evidence:
stats_partial_kernel: lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 4.31% (section L2 Hit Rate 5.33%), l1tex hit 0%, DRAM 79.9%, 42.7 us x2 — it re-reads the 67 MB conv output written one kernel earlier, and 67 MB > 50 MB L2, so every sector misses. gn_silu_res_nchw L2 hit 33.3% for the same reason. Root cause: the working set per stage (67 MB) exceeds L2, so five separate re-reads (stats1, K4, conv2 input, stats2, K5) each cost full DRAM bandwidth (~335 MB of the 871 MB/forward). Refutation of the alternative 'K5 is un-vectorized/smem-transpose bound': K5 moves 201 MB, whose roofline at the measured ~2.03 TB/s is 99 us vs 129.9 us measured — only ~30 us (2.5% of the 1179 us forward) of slack, an order of magnitude less than the 335 MB of removable re-read traffic.

Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound, low-width access] Hottest modifiable kernel is gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel (129.2 us/launch, 34% of the 375 us custom-kernel budget). It moves 201 MB (y2 NHWC read + x NCHW read + NCHW write) yet reaches only 72.5% DRAM vs 81-82% for the sibling streaming kernels: every access is a scalar 4-byte load/store (32 threads = 128 B/request), so 4x more memory instructions per byte and too little memory-level parallelism. The cuDNN convs are default-keep vendor mainloops (already algo-autotuned in round 1).

Optimisation method:
mem_vectorize: rewrite the shared-memory tile transpose in gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel (and the identical pattern in nchw2nhwc_kernel) so every global access is a float4. NHWC side reads 4 contiguous channels per thread; NCHW side writes 4 contiguous spatial positions per thread; the 90-degree turn happens in shared memory, which is untouched by DRAM. This cuts global load/store instructions 4x and widens each request, directly attacking the 68.3% long-scoreboard stall and the 72.5% DRAM utilisation gap (peers reach 82%) without changing bytes moved, dtype, or numerics.

Method name:
mem_vectorize

Modification plan:
1. In gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel, replace the 4 scalar global loads of the NHWC input per thread with ONE float4 load covering 4 consecutive channels (NHWC is contiguous in C, C=256 so C%4==0 always), and replace the 4 scalar global stores/residual loads with ONE float4 store + ONE float4 residual load covering 4 consecutive spatial positions (NCHW is contiguous in P). Numerics unchanged: silu(v*scale+shift)+res is applied element-wise on the float4 lanes.
2. Same mechanism in nchw2nhwc_kernel: float4 load along P (NCHW), float4 store along C (NHWC); no scalar path remains in the vector kernel.
3. Tile/block geometry for the new K5v: tile 64 channels x 64 spatial positions, block 256 threads (32,8). Shared memory float tile[64][68] (pad 4 floats per row) = 17.4 KB/block -> under the 227 KB per-block limit and allows >=8 concurrent blocks/SM (registers ~32, occupancy stays >=8 blocks). Each thread performs 4 float4 loads and 4 float4 stores (64*64/4 = 1024 float4 per phase / 256 threads = 4).
4. Load phase (K5v): p = p0 + (tid/16), c4 = tid%16; read float4 at in[((n*P)+p)*C + c0 + 4*c4]; apply scale/shift + SiLU per lane using scale[n*C+c] broadcast from a per-block __shared__ float sc[64], sh[64] preloaded once (64 threads load them coalesced); store the 4 results as scalars tile[c][p] (stride 68). Repeat 4 times with p += 16.
5. Store phase: __syncthreads(); c = c0 + (tid/16), p4 = tid%16; read tile[c][p0+4*p4 .. +3] (contiguous in shared memory, one float4 load) -> add float4 residual res[n*C*P + c*P + p] -> one float4 store to out[same index]. Repeat 4 times with c += 16.
6. Alignment/tail guard (critical for the awkward 131x131 shape): the NCHW float4 requires (P % 4 == 0) so that c*P keeps 16 B alignment. In the host wrapper, dispatch to the vectorized kernels only when (P % 4 == 0); otherwise launch the EXISTING scalar nchw2nhwc_kernel / gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel unchanged. P=8192/4096/65536 take the fast path; P=17161 keeps today's code and today's timing bit-for-bit.
7. Handle the P-tail inside the vector path with a `p0 + 63 < P` fast branch and a masked slow branch that still uses float4 (P%4==0 guarantees whole float4 groups; only whole-group masking is needed). C tail needs no mask (C=256, multiple of 64).
8. Keep the scale/shift preload in shared memory so the per-thread affine constants are read once per block instead of once per element (removes the redundant scalar scale/shift global loads currently issued per tile column).
9. Do not touch stats_partial_kernel, stats_finalize_kernel, gn_silu_nhwc_kernel, the at::conv2d calls, weight channels-last conversion, or the fallback path. Kernel launch count per forward stays 11.
10. Validate: compare against F.conv2d/group_norm/silu reference on all four shapes; assert max_atol < 0.0027 (tightest tolerance) and confirm the 131x131 shape hits the scalar fallback (add a debug counter in a test build only).

Refutation of 'shared-memory/bank-conflict bound': short_scoreboard is only 3.50% and smem spilling requests are 0, so the smem transpose is not the stall.

Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound, cold-L2 re-read] The five custom kernels move 603 MB/forward at ~80% DRAM; the hottest, gn_silu_res_nchw (129.9 us) plus stats_partial (2x42.7 us) exist only to re-read intermediates the previous kernel just wrote. Working set (67 MB/tensor) exceeds the 50 MB L2, so every re-read (stats1, K4, conv2 input, stats2, K5) is a full DRAM round trip.

Optimisation method:
Cache-blocking the whole fused block over the batch axis so each chunk's intermediates stay L2-resident: run K1 -> conv1 -> stats -> K4 -> conv2 -> stats -> K5 on 1-2 samples at a time, reusing the same temp buffers. GroupNorm statistics are per (n, group) and the residual is elementwise, so batch chunking is exactly equivalent. Method name:
l2_resident_batch_chunking

Modification plan:
1) In fused_res_block, after computing N,C,H,W,P, add exact code: `const size_t bps = (size_t)C*P*4; const size_t BUDGET = 16ull<<20; int chunkN = (int)(BUDGET / (bps>0?bps:1)); if (chunkN < 1) chunkN = 1; if (chunkN > N) chunkN = N;` then `const bool chunked = (N > chunkN);`. If !chunked, execute exactly today's code path (bit-identical for N=1 and for the 2x256x64x64 shape, where bps=4.2MB -> chunkN>=N).
2) If chunked, hoist ALL allocations and the two weight conversions out of the loop, then loop the whole pipeline: allocate once `xl, y1s` (channels_last) and `out` (NCHW) for the FULL N (out must be full-size); allocate `w1c=w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `w2c` once before the loop. Then `for (int n0=0; n0<N; n0+=chunkN){ int nb=min(chunkN,N-n0); ... }` where inside the body every kernel launch uses grid.z/gridDim.y = nb and base pointers offset by `(size_t)n0*C*P`:
   - K1: `nchw2nhwc_kernel<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(xptr + n0*C*P, xlptr + n0*C*P, P, C)`.
   - conv1: build chunk views with `xl.narrow(0,n0,nb)` (batch-major slice is contiguous in both NCHW and NHWC, no copy) and call `at::conv2d(xl_chunk, w1c, nobias, {1,1},{1,1})` -> y1_chunk (fresh 16 MB alloc, reused by the caching allocator across chunks, which also maximises L2 address reuse).
   - compute_scale_shift(y1_chunk.data_ptr, nb, C, P, G, g1,b1,...): pass nb as N so the partial buffer, nchunks cap and grid.y all shrink; the buffer is allocated inside that helper per chunk (small).
   - K4 gn_silu_nhwc: grid.y = nb, pointers offset for y1s by n0*C*P.
   - conv2 on y1s.narrow(0,n0,nb) -> y2_chunk; compute_scale_shift with nb.
   - K5 gn_silu_res_nchw: `<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(y2ptr, xptr + n0*C*P, outptr + n0*C*P, sc2, sh2, P, C)`.
3) Keep everything on `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` and strictly sequential (single stream) — the L2 win depends on temporal locality, so do NOT add extra streams or overlap.
4) Do not change any kernel body, block size, dtype, or the TF32 conv path; only grid.z/gridDim.y and base pointers vary. The scale/shift tensors are per-chunk of shape {nb,C}, and gn_silu_nhwc indexes them by blockIdx.y in [0,nb), which already matches.
5) Correctness guards: assert nb>=1; tail chunk (nb<chunkN) is handled because every kernel derives its extent from nb, and stats_partial always writes its partial slot (no unwritten tail). P is never tiled, so the 131x131 (odd P) shape is untouched (N=1 -> unchunked path).
6) Tune BUDGET: try 16 MB (mid shape -> chunkN=2, 4 chunks); if the mid shape does not improve, retry 24 MB (chunkN=3). Cap the number of chunks at 8 to bound launch overhead (`if (N/chunkN > 8) chunkN = (N+7)/8;`).
7) Verify launch counts: unchunked shapes stay at 7 kernels + 2 convs; mid shape becomes <= 4x that, all async on one stream.

Evidence:

Root cause: the working set per stage (67 MB) exceeds L2, so five separate re-reads (stats1, K4, conv2 input, stats2, K5) each cost full DRAM bandwidth (~335 MB of the 871 MB/forward). Refutation of the alternative 'K5 is un-vectorized/smem-transpose bound': K5 moves 201 MB, whose roofline at the measured ~2.03 TB/s is 99 us vs 129.9 us measured — only ~30 us (2.5% of the 1179 us forward) of slack, an order of magnitude less than the 335 MB of removable re-read traffic.

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization of complementary-bound stages] Hottest non-removable segment is the composite cuDNN TF32 fprop mainloop (~804us of the 1179us forward, ~0.33 TB/s DRAM = ~16% of achievable) executed strictly serially with the DRAM-bound GN/SiLU/transpose chain (375us at 72-82% DRAM but only 15-50% SM). Compute-bound and bandwidth-bound work never coexist, so ~375us of memory time is fully exposed.

Optimisation method:
Per-sample stream pipelining: GroupNorm statistics are per (n,group) and conv/residual are per-sample, so the block decomposes EXACTLY along batch. Split N into chunks, run each chunk's full 9-kernel sequence on one of two side CUDA streams, so chunk i's cuDNN conv (SM/tensor-core bound, 84% of DRAM idle) overlaps chunk i-1's stats/gn_silu/transpose kernels (80%+ DRAM, <50% SM). Vendor conv mainloop is kept untouched; only scheduling changes.

Method name:
stream_pipeline_overlap

Modification plan:
1) EXACT DECOMPOSITION (in fused_res_block, before any launch): compute `int nchunks = (N >= 4 && (size_t)N*C*P*4ull >= (32u<<20)) ? std::min(4, N) : 1; int cs = (N + nchunks - 1)/nchunks; nchunks = (N + cs - 1)/cs;`. If nchunks==1 execute today's code path verbatim (bit-identical kernel sequence, single stream) — this is the mandatory fallback for the N=1 (1x256x131x131) and N=2 (2x256x64x64) shapes.
2) EXACT STREAM PLUMBING: hoist `auto w1c = w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast); auto w2c = w2.contiguous(ChannelsLast); at::Tensor out = at::empty({N,C,H,W}, opts);` to before the loop on the current stream. Grab `auto s0 = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool(); auto s1 = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool();`. Record `at::cuda::CUDAEvent start; start.record(main);` then `start.block(s0); start.block(s1);`. Loop `for (c=0;c<nchunks;++c){ auto st = (c&1)? s1 : s0; at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(st); ... }` and inside the guard call `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` so every existing kernel launch and `at::conv2d` lands on `st` unmodified. After the loop: `for each side stream: CUDAEvent e; e.record(st); e.block(main);`.
3) PER-CHUNK POINTER MATH: for chunk offset `n0` and length `nc`, pass `xc.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)n0*C*P` and `out.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)n0*C*P` to K1/K5 with N replaced by `nc` (grids become dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nc)); build the conv input view as `xl_c = xl.narrow(0, 0, nc)` where xl is allocated per chunk with shape {nc,C,H,W} ChannelsLast (narrow along batch preserves channels_last strides).
4) ALLOCATOR SAFETY: allocate all per-chunk intermediates (xl, y1, y1s, y2, partial, scale/shift) INSIDE the stream guard so the caching allocator tags them to `st`. For the cross-stream tensors allocated on the main stream (xc, w1c, w2c, out) call `t.record_stream(st)` once per side stream to prevent premature reuse.
5) STATS SCOPE: compute_scale_shift is already per-sample; call it with N=nc and the chunk base pointer. inv_count and the (n,g) block mapping are unchanged, so numerics are bit-identical to the unchunked path (no cross-sample reduction exists).
6) KEEP THE VENDOR MAINLOOP: do not touch at::conv2d, TF32, or the round-1 cudnn benchmark autotune; per-chunk conv shapes are constant across iterations so the benchmark cache is hit once and reused.
7) CHUNK-SIZE GUARD: require each chunk's conv GEMM to keep the GPU busy — assert `nc*P/64*2 >= 256` CTAs (mid shape: nc=2 -> 512 CTAs); if not, reduce nchunks to 2 or 1.
8) BONUS (not the mechanism): per-chunk working set is 16.7MB at the mid shape, so the stats->K4 and stats->K5 re-reads of the same chunk may now hit L2; do not restructure anything else to chase this.
9) VALIDATION: run all four shapes; confirm nsys shows sm90_xmma fprop ranges overlapping stats_partial/gn_silu ranges, confirm max_atol under each workload tolerance, and confirm the N<4 shapes emit exactly 11 launches on the default stream.

Evidence:
Convs = 804us/1179us (nsys: 24 fprop launches/12 forwards) moving only 134MB -> ~0.33 TB/s = ~16% of the 2.04 TB/s these kernels actually achieve; meanwhile stats_partial gpu__dram_throughput=80.2% with sm__throughput=15.8%, gn_silu_nhwc 82.4% DRAM / 46.3% SM, nchw2nhwc 81.3% DRAM / 50.6% SM, stats_finalize 0.28 waves/SM. Root cause: strictly serial chaining of a tensor-core-bound mainloop and a DRAM-bound epilogue chain leaves each unit idle in turn; GroupNorm is per-(n,g) so the chain is exactly separable by batch. Refutation of the 'K5 is the bottleneck, vectorize it' alternative: gn_silu_res_nchw moves 201MB, roofline 99us vs 128.2us measured = only 29us (2.5% of the forward) of slack, and history round 3 (mem_vectorize) measured 1.549 < round 1's 1.566; the hideable memory time is 375us, an order of magnitude larger.

Expected metric change:
(1) Wall-clock forward at 8x256x64x128 drops from ~1047us (best-known) to <=880us while the SUM of individual kernel durations stays >=1000us — i.e. nsys shows fprop ranges temporally overlapping stats_partial/gn_silu_nhwc/gn_silu_res_nchw ranges. (2) GPU-level gpu__dram_throughput during the conv windows rises from ~16% toward >=40%; stats_finalize's 2x13us latency-bound launches become fully hidden. Per-launch custom-kernel durations may rise <=15% from SM contention — acceptable only if total time falls. Anti-regression: nchunks==1 fallback must give byte-identical kernel sequence and <=1% time change on 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131; no shape may regress >2%; max_atol within 0.0027-0.003; launches <=44/forward; no cross-stream use-after-free (record_stream on xc/w1c/w2c/out).

Bottleneck identified:
[latency-bound reduction inside the hottest custom composite] The GroupNorm segment (stats_partial 2x42.2us + stats_finalize 2x13.2us + apply kernels 67.2us/129.9us) is 307us of the 375us custom-kernel time. Its reduction is split across two launches through a 2MB partial buffer; stats_finalize does no bandwidth work (DRAM 7.89%, 0.28 waves/SM, 25.6% occupancy) and is 87% uncoalesced-sector bound, costing ~26us per forward almost independently of shape.

Optimisation method:
atomic_privatize: privatize the group reduction inside stats_partial. Each block already holds all 256 channels, so reduce the 8 lanes of each group in-register (__shfl_down width 8) and atomicAdd 32 (sum,sumsq) pairs into a tiny [N][G][2] accumulator, then let the last arriving block per image (atomic counter + __threadfence) emit scale/shift. This deletes the 2MB partial round-trip, the 87%-excessive-sector strided loads and both latency-bound stats_finalize launches, which metrics show are pure launch/latency cost, not bandwidth.

Method name:
atomic_privatize

Modification plan:
Checklist (all inside compute_scale_shift + stats kernel; K1/K4/K5/conv untouched):
1. Delete the `partial` tensor `at::empty({2, N*nchunks*C})` and the entire `stats_finalize_kernel` launch. Allocate ONE zeroed scratch for BOTH norms at the top of fused_res_block: `auto acc = at::zeros({2, N*G*2 + N}, opts)` reinterpreted as {float acc[N][G][2]; float ctr[N];} per norm (ctr read as int*). This is one tiny memset for the whole forward, so launches/forward go 11 -> 10 while removing 2x13.2us kernels.
2. Rename stats_partial_kernel -> stats_atomic_kernel(in, acc, ctr, scale, shift, gamma, beta, P, C, chunk, nchunks, G, CPG, inv_count, eps). Keep the existing accumulation loop byte-for-byte (`ptr += C`, `__ldg`) - it is already 80.8% DRAM and coalesced; only the epilogue changes.
3. In-register group reduction (replaces the global partial write): with c = threadIdx.x, CPG = C/G = 8 contiguous lanes per group, do
   `#pragma unroll for (int off = CPG>>1; off; off >>= 1) { s += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, s, off, CPG); q += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, q, off, CPG); }`
   then `if ((c & (CPG-1)) == 0) { int g = c / CPG; atomicAdd(&acc[((n*G)+g)*2+0], s); atomicAdd(&acc[((n*G)+g)*2+1], q); }`. Generic guard: if CPG is not a power of two or CPG > 32, fall back to a 256-float shared-memory segmented reduction (never taken for C=256,G=32).
4. Last-block finalize (removes the second launch): `__threadfence(); __shared__ int isLast; if (threadIdx.x==0) isLast = (atomicAdd(&ctr_i[n],1) == nchunks-1); __syncthreads(); if (isLast) { int g = c / CPG; float sm = acc[(n*G+g)*2+0]*inv_count; float v = acc[(n*G+g)*2+1]*inv_count - sm*sm; v = v<0.f?0.f:v; float r = rsqrtf(v+eps); float gm = gamma?gamma[c]:1.f, bt = beta?beta[c]:0.f; scale[n*C+c] = r*gm; shift[n*C+c] = bt - sm*r*gm; }` - one fully coalesced 256-float store pair per (n) instead of the 458752 excessive sectors the old finalize generated.
5. All 256 threads must reach the __syncthreads(), so keep the empty-range case (p0>=p1) executing the same code path with s=q=0; grid stays dim3(nchunks, N) with nchunks == ceil(P/chunk) exactly, so the counter always reaches nchunks (verified for P=17161 awkward shape and P=4096/8192/65536).
6. Cap atomic contention: clamp nchunks <= 1024 (existing cap logic already yields 128/64/512), so at most 1024 fp32 atomicAdds per (n,g) - accumulation error ~1e-6 relative, well inside atol 0.0028. Keep the `var<0 -> 0` clamp and fp32 accumulation everywhere; no dtype change.
7. Call sites: compute_scale_shift now takes the acc/ctr slice index (0 for norm1, 1 for norm2) and launches exactly one kernel; scale/shift tensors and their layout [N][C] are unchanged so gn_silu_nhwc_kernel and gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel need zero edits.
8. Validate: run all four shapes; assert launches/forward == 10 in nsys and that stats_finalize_kernel no longer appears; assert max_atol per workload (0.0027-0.003).

Evidence:
stats_finalize_kernel: gpu__time_duration 13152 ns x2 launches/forward (26.4us) while moving only 2MB - gpu__dram_throughput 7.89%, launch__waves_per_multiprocessor 0.28, achieved occupancy 25.56%, and the UncoalescedGlobalAccess rule reports 458752 excessive sectors = 87% of 525312 (thread index maps to ck, stride C floats). Root cause: the group reduction is artificially split into a global 2MB partial buffer plus a tiny, strided, latency-bound second launch, although each stats_partial block already spans all 256 channels and can reduce its 8-lane groups in-register. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_silu_res_nchw (129.9us) is the bottleneck': its 201MB at the 2.04 TB/s its sibling kernels achieve rooflines at 99us, i.e. only ~30us (2.5% of the 1179us forward) of slack, and history round 3 attacked exactly that kernel with mem_vectorize and scored 1.549 < the 1.566 best - whereas the 26.4us finalize cost is nearly shape-independent and therefore ~10% of the 205us small shape and ~6% of the 352us awkward shape in the geometric mean.

Expected metric change:
(1) stats_finalize_kernel vanishes from the profile: launches/forward 11 -> 10, 2x13152 ns removed; the surviving stats kernel keeps gpu__dram_throughput >= 78% (currently 80.75%) with gpu__time_duration <= 44.5us (<= 5% above the current 42.176us) and its uncoalesced excessive-sector share drops from 87% to < 10% (per-block global stores fall from 512 floats to 64 atomics). (2) DRAM bytes/forward drop by the 2x2MB partial-buffer round trip and total custom-kernel time 375us -> <= 348us; mid-shape speedup 1.3896x -> >= 1.42x, small shape 1.3558x -> >= 1.45x, awkward shape 1.9211x -> >= 1.98x. Anti-regression: no shape may regress > 2%; max_atol must stay under each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003) with fp32 accumulation unchanged; registers/thread <= 40 so >= 8 blocks/SM occupancy is preserved; the acc/ctr scratch must be zeroed exactly once per forward (single at::zeros) and the counter must reach nchunks on every shape including P=17161.

Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound, cold-L2 re-read] The five custom kernels move 603 MB/forward at ~80% DRAM; the hottest, gn_silu_res_nchw (129.9 us) plus stats_partial (2x42.7 us) exist only to re-read intermediates the previous kernel just wrote. Working set (67 MB/tensor) exceeds the 50 MB L2, so every re-read (stats1, K4, conv2 input, stats2, K5) is a full DRAM round trip.

Optimisation method:
Cache-blocking the whole fused block over the batch axis so each chunk's intermediates stay L2-resident: run K1 -> conv1 -> stats -> K4 -> conv2 -> stats -> K5 on 1-2 samples at a time, reusing the same temp buffers. GroupNorm statistics are per (n, group) and the residual is elementwise, so batch chunking is exactly equivalent. Evidence: stats_partial lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 4.31% (L2 hit 5.33%) while re-reading a tensor written by the immediately preceding conv; converting those re-reads to L2 hits removes up to 335 MB of DRAM traffic.

Method name:
l2_resident_batch_chunking

Modification plan:
1) In fused_res_block, after computing N,C,H,W,P, add exact code: `const size_t bps = (size_t)C*P*4; const size_t BUDGET = 16ull<<20; int chunkN = (int)(BUDGET / (bps>0?bps:1)); if (chunkN < 1) chunkN = 1; if (chunkN > N) chunkN = N;` then `const bool chunked = (N > chunkN);`. If !chunked, execute exactly today's code path (bit-identical for N=1 and for the 2x256x64x64 shape, where bps=4.2MB -> chunkN>=N).
2) If chunked, hoist ALL allocations and the two weight conversions out of the loop, then loop the whole pipeline: allocate once `xl, y1s` (channels_last) and `out` (NCHW) for the FULL N (out must be full-size); allocate `w1c=w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, `w2c` once before the loop. Then `for (int n0=0; n0<N; n0+=chunkN){ int nb=min(chunkN,N-n0); ... }` where inside the body every kernel launch uses grid.z/gridDim.y = nb and base pointers offset by `(size_t)n0*C*P`:
   - K1: `nchw2nhwc_kernel<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(xptr + n0*C*P, xlptr + n0*C*P, P, C)`.
   - conv1: build chunk views with `xl.narrow(0,n0,nb)` (batch-major slice is contiguous in both NCHW and NHWC, no copy) and call `at::conv2d(xl_chunk, w1c, nobias, {1,1},{1,1})` -> y1_chunk (fresh 16 MB alloc, reused by the caching allocator across chunks, which also maximises L2 address reuse).
   - compute_scale_shift(y1_chunk.data_ptr, nb, C, P, G, g1,b1,...): pass nb as N so the partial buffer, nchunks cap and grid.y all shrink; the buffer is allocated inside that helper per chunk (small).
   - K4 gn_silu_nhwc: grid.y = nb, pointers offset for y1s by n0*C*P.
   - conv2 on y1s.narrow(0,n0,nb) -> y2_chunk; compute_scale_shift with nb.
   - K5 gn_silu_res_nchw: `<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(y2ptr, xptr + n0*C*P, outptr + n0*C*P, sc2, sh2, P, C)`.
3) Keep everything on `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` and strictly sequential (single stream) — the L2 win depends on temporal locality, so do NOT add extra streams or overlap.
4) Do not change any kernel body, block size, dtype, or the TF32 conv path; only grid.z/gridDim.y and base pointers vary. The scale/shift tensors are per-chunk of shape {nb,C}, and gn_silu_nhwc indexes them by blockIdx.y in [0,nb), which already matches.
5) Correctness guards: assert nb>=1; tail chunk (nb<chunkN) is handled because every kernel derives its extent from nb, and stats_partial always writes its partial slot (no unwritten tail). P is never tiled, so the 131x131 (odd P) shape is untouched (N=1 -> unchunked path).
6) Tune BUDGET: try 16 MB (mid shape -> chunkN=2, 4 chunks); if the mid shape does not improve, retry 24 MB (chunkN=3). Cap the number of chunks at 8 to bound launch overhead (`if (N/chunkN > 8) chunkN = (N+7)/8;`).
7) Verify launch counts: unchunked shapes stay at 7 kernels + 2 convs; mid shape becomes <= 4x that, all async on one stream.

Evidence:
stats_partial_kernel: lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 4.31% (section L2 Hit Rate 5.33%), l1tex hit 0%, DRAM 79.9%, 42.7 us x2 — it re-reads the 67 MB conv output written one kernel earlier, and 67 MB > 50 MB L2, so every sector misses. gn_silu_res_nchw L2 hit 33.3% for the same reason. Root cause: the working set per stage (67 MB) exceeds L2, so five separate re-reads (stats1, K4, conv2 input, stats2, K5) each cost full DRAM bandwidth (~335 MB of the 871 MB/forward). Refutation of the alternative 'K5 is un-vectorized/smem-transpose bound': K5 moves 201 MB, whose roofline at the measured ~2.03 TB/s is 99 us vs 129.9 us measured — only ~30 us (2.5% of the 1179 us forward) of slack, an order of magnitude less than the 335 MB of removable re-read traffic.

Expected metric change:
(1) stats_partial_kernel lts__t_sector_hit_rate 4.31% -> >40% and its gpu__dram_throughput drops well below 79.9% while gpu__time_duration falls from 42.7 us toward ~20 us per launch; (2) gn_silu_res_nchw lts__t_sector_hit_rate 33.3% -> >50% with duration 129.9 us -> <110 us; total DRAM bytes/forward down >=25% on the 8x256x64x128 shape, mid-shape speedup 1.39x -> >=1.6x. Anti-regression: the 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 shapes must take the unchunked path (identical kernel sequence, <=1% time change); no shape may regress >2%; max_atol must stay within 0.0027-0.003 per workload; kernel launches per forward must not exceed 4x the current 11.

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization: compute-bound mainloop serialized with DRAM-bound epilogue] Hottest non-removable segment is the composite cuDNN TF32 fprop pair (~804us of the 1179us forward, ~16% DRAM, ~51% TF32 peak) executed strictly after/before the five custom kernels (375us at 72-83% DRAM but only 10-50% SM). All five customs are already within ~5% of their achieved-bandwidth roofline, so their memory time is pure exposed latency.

Optimisation method:
Batch-pipelined dual-stream overlap: because GroupNorm is per-(n,group) and conv is per-sample, the whole chain is exactly separable along N. Split the batch into exactly TWO halves (pointer offsets, no copies) and run each half's full chain (K1->conv1->stats->K4->conv2->stats->K5) on its own stream, so one half's DRAM-saturated GN/transpose kernels execute under the other half's tensor-core conv. Metrics justify it: convs ~16% DRAM/high SM vs customs 78-83% DRAM/15-50% SM — perfectly complementary units that never coexist today.

Method name:
batch_pipelined_dual_stream_overlap

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST (do exactly these; nothing else changes):
1. Refactor `fused_res_block` so the existing per-sample chain becomes a helper `run_chain(const float* x_ptr, float* out_ptr, int n_sub, C,H,W,G, w1c,w2c,g1,b1,g2,b2, eps, stream)` that issues K1, at::conv2d, compute_scale_shift, K4, at::conv2d, compute_scale_shift, K5 on the GIVEN stream with the GIVEN batch count. Batch is the outermost dim of both NCHW x and NHWC intermediates, so a half is just `x.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)half*C*P` and `out.data_ptr<float>() + same` — NO copies, NO views needed for the raw-pointer kernels; for the two at::conv2d calls build the half input with `at::from_blob`-free `xl.narrow(0,0,half)` / `xl.narrow(0,half,half)` (narrow on dim0 keeps channels_last contiguity).
2. Gate: enable the pipelined path only when `N >= 4 && N % 2 == 0 && P >= 4096`. Otherwise call `run_chain` once on the current stream — byte-identical kernel sequence to today for the 2x256x64x64 (N=2) and 1x256x131x131 (N=1) shapes, which must not regress.
3. Before forking, on the CURRENT stream only: `xc = x.contiguous()`, `w1c/w2c = contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, allocate the FULL-size `xl` (channels_last) and `out` (NCHW). This keeps the caching allocator and the weight elementwise_kernels off the side stream.
4. Get a side stream once via a function-local `static auto s_side = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool();` (never create/destroy per call). Use `at::cuda::CUDAEvent` (or two static cudaEvents) for ordering.
5. Ordering: record `ev_start` on the current stream after step 3; `s_side.wait(ev_start)`. Issue `run_chain(half A)` on the current stream, then `run_chain(half B)` on `s_side` (both fully enqueued; the GPU co-schedules B's K1/stats_partial/K4/K5 with A's fprop kernels). Record `ev_done` on `s_side`; make the current stream wait on `ev_done` before returning `out`.
6. Lifetime safety (mandatory): call `.record_stream(s_side)` on `xc`, `xl`, `out`, `w1c`, `w2c`, `g1,b1,g2,b2` so the caching allocator cannot recycle them while the side stream is still reading/writing. Tensors that `run_chain` allocates internally (y1, y1s, y2, partial, scale/shift) are allocated AND consumed on the same stream via `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard` inside the helper, so they need no record_stream.
7. Inside `run_chain`, wrap the body in `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard guard(stream)` so at::conv2d, at::empty and every `<<<...,stream>>>` launch use that stream consistently; pass `stream` explicitly to all five custom kernels (they already take a stream argument).
8. Grid sizes: all kernels already derive grids from `n_sub` (blockIdx.z / gridDim.y = N); just pass the half batch count. `compute_scale_shift`'s `cap = 2048 / N` heuristic must use `n_sub` so per-half nchunks stays >= 1 and psum/psq buffers are sized with `n_sub`.
9. Do NOT touch dtype/TF32 settings, do not change kernel bodies, do not add a third stream (more slices shrink each conv's GEMM M and cost more than they hide).
10. Verify numerics: halves are fully independent (GroupNorm reduces over (c,h,w) within one sample), so the result is bit-identical to the single-stream path; run the awkward P=17161 shape through the fallback branch unchanged.

Evidence:
Custom kernels sum 68.7+2x43.4+2x13.2+67.0+129.4 = 378us of a 1179us forward -> ~800us is the 2 cuDNN fprop launches (nsys: 24 launches/12 forwards) moving only ~268MB = ~0.33 TB/s (~16% DRAM) while the customs sit at gpu__dram_throughput 78.5-82.8% with sm__throughput 10-49% (stats_partial: 78.51% DRAM vs 15.5% SM; stats_finalize 0.28 waves/SM, 7.85% DRAM). Root cause: a tensor-core-bound mainloop and a bandwidth-bound epilogue chain are strictly serialized, so ~378us of memory time is fully exposed. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_silu_res_nchw (129.4us) is the bottleneck, make it faster': at the 82% DRAM its siblings actually achieve, its 201MB rooflines at ~114us, i.e. only ~15us (1.3%) of slack, and round-3 mem_vectorize on exactly that kernel scored 1.549 < 1.566 — every custom kernel is already within ~5% of achieved-bandwidth roofline, so no per-kernel tuning can reach the 378us that overlap can hide.

Expected metric change:
(1) Wall clock at 8x256x64x128 drops 1179us -> <=1010us while the SUM of individual kernel durations stays within +/-5% of 378+800us — i.e. nsys must show sm90_xmma fprop ranges temporally overlapping stats_partial / gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw ranges from the other half. (2) GPU-level DRAM utilization during the conv windows rises from ~16% toward >=40%; stats_finalize's 2x13.2us, 0.28-wave launches become fully hidden. Per-launch custom-kernel durations may grow <=15% from SM/L2 contention — acceptable only if total time falls. Anti-regression: N<4 or odd N (2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131) must take the single-stream fallback with an identical kernel sequence and <=1% time change; no shape may regress >2%; max_atol stays under each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003) and results must be bit-identical to the serial path; kernel launches per forward <=22; no cross-stream use-after-free (record_stream on xc/xl/out/w1c/w2c/gamma/beta) and the side stream must come from getStreamFromPool exactly once (static), never created per call.

pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound, cold-L2 re-read] Hottest non-removable segment is the GroupNorm two-pass chain: stats_partial 2x42.8us + stats_finalize 2x13.2us + gn_silu_nhwc 67.4us + gn_silu_res_nchw 129.4us = 307us of 375us custom time. Each GN reads its 67MB intermediate twice via two separate full-tensor launches, so the apply pass misses L2 (4.3%/33.5% hit) and pays full DRAM cost.

Optimisation method:
Slab-interleaved producer/consumer scheduling of the GN passes: instead of one stats launch over the whole tensor then one apply launch over the whole tensor, loop over ~17MB slabs (whole samples; contiguous channel-group halves if one sample exceeds the budget) issuing stats->finalize->apply per slab on the same stream. The apply then re-reads data still resident in the 50MB L2, removing one full 67MB DRAM read per GroupNorm (134MB/forward = 22% of the 603MB custom traffic). Convs, K1 and all kernel math untouched.

Method name:
slab_interleaved_gn_l2_reuse

Modification plan:
Host-side scheduling change only; kernel bodies gain pointer/range offsets, no algorithmic change.
1) In fused_res_block compute the slab size once: `size_t sample_bytes=(size_t)C*P*4; int slab_n=(int)max<size_t>(1,(17ull<<20)/sample_bytes); slab_n=min(slab_n,N);` (17MB read + 17MB write stays under the 50MB L2).
2) Replace the GN1 sequence `compute_scale_shift(y1 whole) ; gn_silu_nhwc(whole)` with: `for(int n0=0;n0<N;n0+=slab_n){int nb=min(slab_n,N-n0); size_t off=(size_t)n0*P*C; stats_partial_kernel<<<dim3(nchunks,nb),C>>>(y1+off, psum+(size_t)n0*nchunks*C, psq+(size_t)n0*nchunks*C, P,C,chunk,nchunks); stats_finalize_kernel<<<nb*G,256>>>(psum+(size_t)n0*nchunks*C, psq+..., g1,b1, sc1+(size_t)n0*C, sh1+(size_t)n0*C, C,G,CPG,nchunks,inv_count,eps); gn_silu_nhwc_kernel<<<dim3((P+by-1)/by, nb)>>>(y1+off, y1s+off, sc1+(size_t)n0*C, sh1+(size_t)n0*C, P, C4);}` — every kernel already indexes batch via blockIdx.y/z, so passing base+off and a reduced nb is sufficient; no index math inside kernels changes.
3) Do the identical loop for GN2, with `gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(y2+off, xc+off, out+off, sc2+n0*C, sh2+n0*C, P, C)` (its blockIdx.z is n, so nb slabs work unchanged).
4) Allocate psum/psq/scale/shift ONCE for the full N (as today) and index by n0, so no per-slab allocation or allocator churn; all launches stay on the current stream, whose program order already guarantees stats->apply ordering (no events/syncs needed).
5) Oversized-sample fallback (large shape 4x256x256x256, sample=67MB>17MB): additionally split channels into contiguous chunks CS = 8*ceil(...) chosen so `P*CS*4<=17MB`, with CS a multiple of 32 (keeps K5's 32-wide c tile and K4's float4 valid) and a multiple of CPG=8 (keeps whole groups intact). Pass `c0` and CS: stats blockDim.x=CS with base pointer `+c0`, finalize grid `nb*(CS/CPG)` with gamma/beta/scale/shift offset by c0, K4 grid.x over C4=CS/4 with row stride C, K5 grid.y=CS/32 with `c0` added to c. Row runs stay >=256B so loads remain coalesced.

pairs.a_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound, low-width access] Hottest modifiable kernel is gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel (129.2 us/launch, 34% of the 375 us custom-kernel budget). It moves 201 MB (y2 NHWC read + x NCHW read + NCHW write) yet reaches only 72.5% DRAM vs 81-82% for the sibling streaming kernels: every access is a scalar 4-byte load/store (32 threads = 128 B/request), so 4x more memory instructions per byte and too little memory-level parallelism. The cuDNN convs are default-keep vendor mainloops (already algo-autotuned in round 1).

Optimisation method:
mem_vectorize: rewrite the shared-memory tile transpose in gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel (and the identical pattern in nchw2nhwc_kernel) so every global access is a float4. NHWC side reads 4 contiguous channels per thread; NCHW side writes 4 contiguous spatial positions per thread; the 90-degree turn happens in shared memory, which is untouched by DRAM. This cuts global load/store instructions 4x and widens each request, directly attacking the 68.3% long-scoreboard stall and the 72.5% DRAM utilisation gap (peers reach 82%) without changing bytes moved, dtype, or numerics.

Method name:
mem_vectorize

Modification plan:
1. In gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel, replace the 4 scalar global loads of the NHWC input per thread with ONE float4 load covering 4 consecutive channels (NHWC is contiguous in C, C=256 so C%4==0 always), and replace the 4 scalar global stores/residual loads with ONE float4 store + ONE float4 residual load covering 4 consecutive spatial positions (NCHW is contiguous in P). Numerics unchanged: silu(v*scale+shift)+res is applied element-wise on the float4 lanes.
2. Same mechanism in nchw2nhwc_kernel: float4 load along P (NCHW), float4 store along C (NHWC); no scalar path remains in the vector kernel.
3. Tile/block geometry for the new K5v: tile 64 channels x 64 spatial positions, block 256 threads (32,8). Shared memory float tile[64][68] (pad 4 floats per row) = 17.4 KB/block -> under the 227 KB per-block limit and allows >=8 concurrent blocks/SM (registers ~32, occupancy stays >=8 blocks). Each thread performs 4 float4 loads and 4 float4 stores (64*64/4 = 1024 float4 per phase / 256 threads = 4).
4. Load phase (K5v): p = p0 + (tid/16), c4 = tid%16; read float4 at in[((n*P)+p)*C + c0 + 4*c4]; apply scale/shift + SiLU per lane using scale[n*C+c] broadcast from a per-block __shared__ float sc[64], sh[64] preloaded once (64 threads load them coalesced); store the 4 results as scalars tile[c][p] (stride 68). Repeat 4 times with p += 16.
5. Store phase: __syncthreads(); c = c0 + (tid/16), p4 = tid%16; read tile[c][p0+4*p4 .. +3] (contiguous in shared memory, one float4 load) -> add float4 residual res[n*C*P + c*P + p] -> one float4 store to out[same index]. Repeat 4 times with c += 16.
6. Alignment/tail guard (critical for the awkward 131x131 shape): the NCHW float4 requires (P % 4 == 0) so that c*P keeps 16 B alignment. In the host wrapper, dispatch to the vectorized kernels only when (P % 4 == 0); otherwise launch the EXISTING scalar nchw2nhwc_kernel / gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel unchanged. P=8192/4096/65536 take the fast path; P=17161 keeps today's code and today's timing bit-for-bit.
7. Handle the P-tail inside the vector path with a `p0 + 63 < P` fast branch and a masked slow branch that still uses float4 (P%4==0 guarantees whole float4 groups; only whole-group masking is needed). C tail needs no mask (C=256, multiple of 64).
8. Keep the scale/shift preload in shared memory so the per-thread affine constants are read once per block instead of once per element (removes the redundant scalar scale/shift global loads currently issued per tile column).
9. Do not touch stats_partial_kernel, stats_finalize_kernel, gn_silu_nhwc_kernel, the at::conv2d calls, weight channels-last conversion, or the fallback path. Kernel launch count per forward stays 11.
10. Validate: compare against F.conv2d/group_norm/silu reference on all four shapes; assert max_atol < 0.0027 (tightest tolerance) and confirm the 131x131 shape hits the scalar fallback (add a debug counter in a test build only).

Evidence:
gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel: gpu__time_duration.avg = 129216 ns (largest custom kernel; K1 68768, K4 67520, stats 2x42112), gpu__dram_throughput = 72.54% vs 82.11% (gn_silu_nhwc, float4) and 81.0% (K1) — measured 1.4795 TB/s against the ~2.04 TB/s these kernels achieve at 100%, i.e. ~99 us roofline for its 201 MB. long_scoreboard stall = 68.28% of 29.1 warp-cycles/issue, l1tex hit 13.52%, l1tex throughput only 22.23% — root cause: all three streams use 4-byte scalar accesses (128 B/warp request), so the kernel issues 4x the memory instructions of the float4 K4 and cannot cover DRAM latency. Refutation of 'occupancy-limited': achieved occupancy 91.04% and warps_active 91.22% are the highest of any kernel here, so more warps cannot be the fix. Refutation of 'shared-memory/bank-conflict bound': short_scoreboard is only 3.50% and smem spilling requests are 0, so the smem transpose is not the stall.

Expected metric change:
(1) gn_silu_res_nchw duration 129.2 us -> <=110 us with gpu__dram_throughput 72.54% -> >=80% and long_scoreboard 68.3% -> <60%; (2) nchw2nhwc duration 68.8 us -> <=58 us, its global memory instruction count down ~4x (l1tex__throughput may rise, sector count unchanged); (3) total custom-kernel time 375 us -> <=335 us, mid-shape speedup 1.39x -> >=1.44x. Anti-regression constraints: DRAM bytes moved per forward must NOT increase (same 603 MB); launches per forward stay 11; the 1x256x131x131 shape (P%4!=0) must take the untouched scalar path and change by <=1%; no shape may regress >2%; max_atol must stay under each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003); registers/thread <=40 so occupancy stays >=8 blocks/SM.

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization of complementary-bound stages] Hottest non-removable segment is the composite cuDNN TF32 fprop mainloop (~804us of the 1179us forward, ~0.33 TB/s DRAM = ~16% of achievable) executed strictly serially with the DRAM-bound GN/SiLU/transpose chain (375us at 72-82% DRAM but only 15-50% SM). Compute-bound and bandwidth-bound work never coexist, so ~375us of memory time is fully exposed.

Optimisation method:
Per-sample stream pipelining: GroupNorm statistics are per (n,group) and conv/residual are per-sample, so the block decomposes EXACTLY along batch. Split N into chunks, run each chunk's full 9-kernel sequence on one of two side CUDA streams, so chunk i's cuDNN conv (SM/tensor-core bound, 84% of DRAM idle) overlaps chunk i-1's stats/gn_silu/transpose kernels (80%+ DRAM, <50% SM). Vendor conv mainloop is kept untouched; only scheduling changes.

Method name:
stream_pipeline_overlap

Modification plan:
1) EXACT DECOMPOSITION (in fused_res_block, before any launch): compute `int nchunks = (N >= 4 && (size_t)N*C*P*4ull >= (32u<<20)) ? std::min(4, N) : 1; int cs = (N + nchunks - 1)/nchunks; nchunks = (N + cs - 1)/cs;`. If nchunks==1 execute today's code path verbatim (bit-identical kernel sequence, single stream) — this is the mandatory fallback for the N=1 (1x256x131x131) and N=2 (2x256x64x64) shapes.
2) EXACT STREAM PLUMBING: hoist `auto w1c = w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast); auto w2c = w2.contiguous(ChannelsLast); at::Tensor out = at::empty({N,C,H,W}, opts);` to before the loop on the current stream. Grab `auto s0 = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool(); auto s1 = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool();`. Record `at::cuda::CUDAEvent start; start.record(main);` then `start.block(s0); start.block(s1);`. Loop `for (c=0;c<nchunks;++c){ auto st = (c&1)? s1 : s0; at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(st); ... }` and inside the guard call `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` so every existing kernel launch and `at::conv2d` lands on `st` unmodified. After the loop: `for each side stream: CUDAEvent e; e.record(st); e.block(main);`.
3) PER-CHUNK POINTER MATH: for chunk offset `n0` and length `nc`, pass `xc.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)n0*C*P` and `out.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)n0*C*P` to K1/K5 with N replaced by `nc` (grids become dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nc)); build the conv input view as `xl_c = xl.narrow(0, 0, nc)` where xl is allocated per chunk with shape {nc,C,H,W} ChannelsLast (narrow along batch preserves channels_last strides).
4) ALLOCATOR SAFETY: allocate all per-chunk intermediates (xl, y1, y1s, y2, partial, scale/shift) INSIDE the stream guard so the caching allocator tags them to `st`. For the cross-stream tensors allocated on the main stream (xc, w1c, w2c, out) call `t.record_stream(st)` once per side stream to prevent premature reuse.
5) STATS SCOPE: compute_scale_shift is already per-sample; call it with N=nc and the chunk base pointer. inv_count and the (n,g) block mapping are unchanged, so numerics are bit-identical to the unchunked path (no cross-sample reduction exists).
6) KEEP THE VENDOR MAINLOOP: do not touch at::conv2d, TF32, or the round-1 cudnn benchmark autotune; per-chunk conv shapes are constant across iterations so the benchmark cache is hit once and reused.
7) CHUNK-SIZE GUARD: require each chunk's conv GEMM to keep the GPU busy — assert `nc*P/64*2 >= 256` CTAs (mid shape: nc=2 -> 512 CTAs); if not, reduce nchunks to 2 or 1.
8) BONUS (not the mechanism): per-chunk working set is 16.7MB at the mid shape, so the stats->K4 and stats->K5 re-reads of the same chunk may now hit L2; do not restructure anything else to chase this.
9) VALIDATION: run all four shapes; confirm nsys shows sm90_xmma fprop ranges overlapping stats_partial/gn_silu ranges, confirm max_atol under each workload tolerance, and confirm the N<4 shapes emit exactly 11 launches on the default stream.

Evidence:
Convs = 804us/1179us (nsys: 24 fprop launches/12 forwards) moving only 134MB -> ~0.33 TB/s = ~16% of the 2.04 TB/s these kernels actually achieve; meanwhile stats_partial gpu__dram_throughput=80.2% with sm__throughput=15.8%, gn_silu_nhwc 82.4% DRAM / 46.3% SM, nchw2nhwc 81.3% DRAM / 50.6% SM, stats_finalize 0.28 waves/SM. Root cause: strictly serial chaining of a tensor-core-bound mainloop and a DRAM-bound epilogue chain leaves each unit idle in turn; GroupNorm is per-(n,g) so the chain is exactly separable by batch. Refutation of the 'K5 is the bottleneck, vectorize it' alternative: gn_silu_res_nchw moves 201MB, roofline 99us vs 128.2us measured = only 29us (2.5% of the forward) of slack, and history round 3 (mem_vectorize) measured 1.549 < round 1's 1.566; the hideable memory time is 375us, an order of magnitude larger.

Expected metric change:
(1) Wall-clock forward at 8x256x64x128 drops from ~1047us (best-known) to <=880us while the SUM of individual kernel durations stays >=1000us — i.e. nsys shows fprop ranges temporally overlapping stats_partial/gn_silu_nhwc/gn_silu_res_nchw ranges. (2) GPU-level gpu__dram_throughput during the conv windows rises from ~16% toward >=40%; stats_finalize's 2x13us latency-bound launches become fully hidden. Per-launch custom-kernel durations may rise <=15% from SM contention — acceptable only if total time falls. Anti-regression: nchunks==1 fallback must give byte-identical kernel sequence and <=1% time change on 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131; no shape may regress >2%; max_atol within 0.0027-0.003; launches <=44/forward; no cross-stream use-after-free (record_stream on xc/w1c/w2c/out).

pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[latency-bound reduction inside the hottest custom composite] The GroupNorm segment (stats_partial 2x42.2us + stats_finalize 2x13.2us + apply kernels 67.2us/129.9us) is 307us of the 375us custom-kernel time. Its reduction is split across two launches through a 2MB partial buffer; stats_finalize does no bandwidth work (DRAM 7.89%, 0.28 waves/SM, 25.6% occupancy) and is 87% uncoalesced-sector bound, costing ~26us per forward almost independently of shape.

Optimisation method:
atomic_privatize: privatize the group reduction inside stats_partial. Each block already holds all 256 channels, so reduce the 8 lanes of each group in-register (__shfl_down width 8) and atomicAdd 32 (sum,sumsq) pairs into a tiny [N][G][2] accumulator, then let the last arriving block per image (atomic counter + __threadfence) emit scale/shift. This deletes the 2MB partial round-trip, the 87%-excessive-sector strided loads and both latency-bound stats_finalize launches, which metrics show are pure launch/latency cost, not bandwidth.

Method name:
atomic_privatize

Modification plan:
Checklist (all inside compute_scale_shift + stats kernel; K1/K4/K5/conv untouched):
1. Delete the `partial` tensor `at::empty({2, N*nchunks*C})` and the entire `stats_finalize_kernel` launch. Allocate ONE zeroed scratch for BOTH norms at the top of fused_res_block: `auto acc = at::zeros({2, N*G*2 + N}, opts)` reinterpreted as {float acc[N][G][2]; float ctr[N];} per norm (ctr read as int*). This is one tiny memset for the whole forward, so launches/forward go 11 -> 10 while removing 2x13.2us kernels.
2. Rename stats_partial_kernel -> stats_atomic_kernel(in, acc, ctr, scale, shift, gamma, beta, P, C, chunk, nchunks, G, CPG, inv_count, eps). Keep the existing accumulation loop byte-for-byte (`ptr += C`, `__ldg`) - it is already 80.8% DRAM and coalesced; only the epilogue changes.
3. In-register group reduction (replaces the global partial write): with c = threadIdx.x, CPG = C/G = 8 contiguous lanes per group, do
   `#pragma unroll for (int off = CPG>>1; off; off >>= 1) { s += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, s, off, CPG); q += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, q, off, CPG); }`
   then `if ((c & (CPG-1)) == 0) { int g = c / CPG; atomicAdd(&acc[((n*G)+g)*2+0], s); atomicAdd(&acc[((n*G)+g)*2+1], q); }`. Generic guard: if CPG is not a power of two or CPG > 32, fall back to a 256-float shared-memory segmented reduction (never taken for C=256,G=32).
4. Last-block finalize (removes the second launch): `__threadfence(); __shared__ int isLast; if (threadIdx.x==0) isLast = (atomicAdd(&ctr_i[n],1) == nchunks-1); __syncthreads(); if (isLast) { int g = c / CPG; float sm = acc[(n*G+g)*2+0]*inv_count; float v = acc[(n*G+g)*2+1]*inv_count - sm*sm; v = v<0.f?0.f:v; float r = rsqrtf(v+eps); float gm = gamma?gamma[c]:1.f, bt = beta?beta[c]:0.f; scale[n*C+c] = r*gm; shift[n*C+c] = bt - sm*r*gm; }` - one fully coalesced 256-float store pair per (n) instead of the 458752 excessive sectors the old finalize generated.
5. All 256 threads must reach the __syncthreads(), so keep the empty-range case (p0>=p1) executing the same code path with s=q=0; grid stays dim3(nchunks, N) with nchunks == ceil(P/chunk) exactly, so the counter always reaches nchunks (verified for P=17161 awkward shape and P=4096/8192/65536).
6. Cap atomic contention: clamp nchunks <= 1024 (existing cap logic already yields 128/64/512), so at most 1024 fp32 atomicAdds per (n,g) - accumulation error ~1e-6 relative, well inside atol 0.0028. Keep the `var<0 -> 0` clamp and fp32 accumulation everywhere; no dtype change.
7. Call sites: compute_scale_shift now takes the acc/ctr slice index (0 for norm1, 1 for norm2) and launches exactly one kernel; scale/shift tensors and their layout [N][C] are unchanged so gn_silu_nhwc_kernel and gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel need zero edits.
8. Validate: run all four shapes; assert launches/forward == 10 in nsys and that stats_finalize_kernel no longer appears; assert max_atol per workload (0.0027-0.003).

Evidence:
stats_finalize_kernel: gpu__time_duration 13152 ns x2 launches/forward (26.4us) while moving only 2MB - gpu__dram_throughput 7.89%, launch__waves_per_multiprocessor 0.28, achieved occupancy 25.56%, and the UncoalescedGlobalAccess rule reports 458752 excessive sectors = 87% of 525312 (thread index maps to ck, stride C floats). Root cause: the group reduction is artificially split into a global 2MB partial buffer plus a tiny, strided, latency-bound second launch, although each stats_partial block already spans all 256 channels and can reduce its 8-lane groups in-register. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_silu_res_nchw (129.9us) is the bottleneck': its 201MB at the 2.04 TB/s its sibling kernels achieve rooflines at 99us, i.e. only ~30us (2.5% of the 1179us forward) of slack, and history round 3 attacked exactly that kernel with mem_vectorize and scored 1.549 < the 1.566 best - whereas the 26.4us finalize cost is nearly shape-independent and therefore ~10% of the 205us small shape and ~6% of the 352us awkward shape in the geometric mean.

Expected metric change:
(1) stats_finalize_kernel vanishes from the profile: launches/forward 11 -> 10, 2x13152 ns removed; the surviving stats kernel keeps gpu__dram_throughput >= 78% (currently 80.75%) with gpu__time_duration <= 44.5us (<= 5% above the current 42.176us) and its uncoalesced excessive-sector share drops from 87% to < 10% (per-block global stores fall from 512 floats to 64 atomics). Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound, low-width access] Hottest modifiable kernel is gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel (129.2 us/launch, 34% of the 375 us custom-kernel budget). It moves 201 MB (y2 NHWC read + x NCHW read + NCHW write) yet reaches only 72.5% DRAM vs 81-82% for the sibling streaming kernels: every access is a scalar 4-byte load/store (32 threads = 128 B/request), so 4x more memory instructions per byte and too little memory-level parallelism. The cuDNN convs are default-keep vendor mainloops (already algo-autotuned in round 1).

Optimisation method:
mem_vectorize: rewrite the shared-memory tile transpose in gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel (and the identical pattern in nchw2nhwc_kernel) so every global access is a float4. NHWC side reads 4 contiguous channels per thread; NCHW side writes 4 contiguous spatial positions per thread; the 90-degree turn happens in shared memory, which is untouched by DRAM. This cuts global load/store instructions 4x and widens each request, directly attacking the 68.3% long-scoreboard stall and the 72.5% DRAM utilisation gap (peers reach 82%) without changing bytes moved, dtype, or numerics.

Method name:
mem_vectorize

Modification plan:
1. In gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel, replace the 4 scalar global loads of the NHWC input per thread with ONE float4 load covering 4 consecutive channels (NHWC is contiguous in C, C=256 so C%4==0 always), and replace the 4 scalar global stores/residual loads with ONE float4 store + ONE float4 residual load covering 4 consecutive spatial positions (NCHW is contiguous in P). Numerics unchanged: silu(v*scale+shift)+res is applied element-wise on the float4 lanes.
2. Same mechanism in nchw2nhwc_kernel: float4 load along P (NCHW), float4 store along C (NHWC); no scalar path remains in the vector kernel.
3. Tile/block geometry for the new K5v: tile 64 channels x 64 spatial positions, block 256 threads (32,8). Shared memory float tile[64][68] (pad 4 floats per row) = 17.4 KB/block -> under the 227 KB per-block limit and allows >=8 concurrent blocks/SM (registers ~32, occupancy stays >=8 blocks). Each thread performs 4 float4 loads and 4 float4 stores (64*64/4 = 1024 float4 per phase / 256 threads = 4).
4. Load phase (K5v): p = p0 + (tid/16), c4 = tid%16; read float4 at in[((n*P)+p)*C + c0 + 4*c4]; apply scale/shift + SiLU per lane using scale[n*C+c] broadcast from a per-block __shared__ float sc[64], sh[64] preloaded once (64 threads load them coalesced); store the 4 results as scalars tile[c][p] (stride 68). Repeat 4 times with p += 16.
5. Store phase: __syncthreads(); c = c0 + (tid/16), p4 = tid%16; read tile[c][p0+4*p4 .. +3] (contiguous in shared memory, one float4 load) -> add float4 residual res[n*C*P + c*P + p] -> one float4 store to out[same index]. Repeat 4 times with c += 16.
6. Alignment/tail guard (critical for the awkward 131x131 shape): the NCHW float4 requires (P % 4 == 0) so that c*P keeps 16 B alignment. In the host wrapper, dispatch to the vectorized kernels only when (P % 4 == 0); otherwise launch the EXISTING scalar nchw2nhwc_kernel / gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel unchanged. P=8192/4096/65536 take the fast path; P=17161 keeps today's code and today's timing bit-for-bit.
7. Handle the P-tail inside the vector path with a `p0 + 63 < P` fast branch and a masked slow branch that still uses float4 (P%4==0 guarantees whole float4 groups; only whole-group masking is needed). C tail needs no mask (C=256, multiple of 64).
8. Keep the scale/shift preload in shared memory so the per-thread affine constants are read once per block instead of once per element (removes the redundant scalar scale/shift global loads currently issued per tile column).
9. Do not touch stats_partial_kernel, stats_finalize_kernel, gn_silu_nhwc_kernel, the at::conv2d calls, weight channels-last conversion, or the fallback path. Kernel launch count per forward stays 11.
10. Validate: compare against F.conv2d/group_norm/silu reference on all four shapes; assert max_atol < 0.0027 (tightest tolerance) and confirm the 131x131 shape hits the scalar fallback (add a debug counter in a test build only).

Evidence:
gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel: gpu__time_duration.avg = 129216 ns (largest custom kernel; K1 68768, K4 67520, stats 2x42112), gpu__dram_throughput = 72.54% vs 82.11% (gn_silu_nhwc, float4) and 81.0% (K1) — measured 1.4795 TB/s against the ~2.04 TB/s these kernels achieve at 100%, i.e. ~99 us roofline for its 201 MB. long_scoreboard stall = 68.28% of 29.1 warp-cycles/issue, l1tex hit 13.52%, l1tex throughput only 22.23% — root cause: all three streams use 4-byte scalar accesses (128 B/warp request), so the kernel issues 4x the memory instructions of the float4 K4 and cannot cover DRAM latency. Refutation of 'occupancy-limited': achieved occupancy 91.04% and warps_active 91.22% are the highest of any kernel here, so more warps cannot be the fix. Refutation of 'shared-memory/bank-conflict bound': short_scoreboard is only 3.50% and smem spilling requests are 0, so the smem transpose is not the stall.

(1) gn_silu_res_nchw duration 129.2 us -> <=110 us with gpu__dram_throughput 72.54% -> >=80% and long_scoreboard 68.3% -> <60%; (2) nchw2nhwc duration 68.8 us -> <=58 us, its global memory instruction count down ~4x (l1tex__throughput may rise, sector count unchanged); (3) total custom-kernel time 375 us -> <=335 us, mid-shape speedup 1.39x -> >=1.44x. Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization: compute-bound mainloop serialized with DRAM-bound epilogue] Hottest non-removable segment is the composite cuDNN TF32 fprop pair (~804us of the 1179us forward, ~16% DRAM, ~51% TF32 peak) executed strictly after/before the five custom kernels (375us at 72-83% DRAM but only 10-50% SM). All five customs are already within ~5% of their achieved-bandwidth roofline, so their memory time is pure exposed latency.

Optimisation method:
Batch-pipelined dual-stream overlap: because GroupNorm is per-(n,group) and conv is per-sample, the whole chain is exactly separable along N. Split the batch into exactly TWO halves (pointer offsets, no copies) and run each half's full chain (K1->conv1->stats->K4->conv2->stats->K5) on its own stream, so one half's DRAM-saturated GN/transpose kernels execute under the other half's tensor-core conv. Metrics justify it: convs ~16% DRAM/high SM vs customs 78-83% DRAM/15-50% SM — perfectly complementary units that never coexist today.

Method name:
batch_pipelined_dual_stream_overlap

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST (do exactly these; nothing else changes):
1. Refactor `fused_res_block` so the existing per-sample chain becomes a helper `run_chain(const float* x_ptr, float* out_ptr, int n_sub, C,H,W,G, w1c,w2c,g1,b1,g2,b2, eps, stream)` that issues K1, at::conv2d, compute_scale_shift, K4, at::conv2d, compute_scale_shift, K5 on the GIVEN stream with the GIVEN batch count. Batch is the outermost dim of both NCHW x and NHWC intermediates, so a half is just `x.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)half*C*P` and `out.data_ptr<float>() + same` — NO copies, NO views needed for the raw-pointer kernels; for the two at::conv2d calls build the half input with `at::from_blob`-free `xl.narrow(0,0,half)` / `xl.narrow(0,half,half)` (narrow on dim0 keeps channels_last contiguity).
2. Gate: enable the pipelined path only when `N >= 4 && N % 2 == 0 && P >= 4096`. Otherwise call `run_chain` once on the current stream — byte-identical kernel sequence to today for the 2x256x64x64 (N=2) and 1x256x131x131 (N=1) shapes, which must not regress.
3. Before forking, on the CURRENT stream only: `xc = x.contiguous()`, `w1c/w2c = contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, allocate the FULL-size `xl` (channels_last) and `out` (NCHW). This keeps the caching allocator and the weight elementwise_kernels off the side stream.
4. Get a side stream once via a function-local `static auto s_side = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool();` (never create/destroy per call). Use `at::cuda::CUDAEvent` (or two static cudaEvents) for ordering.
5. Ordering: record `ev_start` on the current stream after step 3; `s_side.wait(ev_start)`. Issue `run_chain(half A)` on the current stream, then `run_chain(half B)` on `s_side` (both fully enqueued; the GPU co-schedules B's K1/stats_partial/K4/K5 with A's fprop kernels). Record `ev_done` on `s_side`; make the current stream wait on `ev_done` before returning `out`.
6. Lifetime safety (mandatory): call `.record_stream(s_side)` on `xc`, `xl`, `out`, `w1c`, `w2c`, `g1,b1,g2,b2` so the caching allocator cannot recycle them while the side stream is still reading/writing. Tensors that `run_chain` allocates internally (y1, y1s, y2, partial, scale/shift) are allocated AND consumed on the same stream via `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard` inside the helper, so they need no record_stream.
7. Inside `run_chain`, wrap the body in `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard guard(stream)` so at::conv2d, at::empty and every `<<<...,stream>>>` launch use that stream consistently; pass `stream` explicitly to all five custom kernels (they already take a stream argument).
8. Grid sizes: all kernels already derive grids from `n_sub` (blockIdx.z / gridDim.y = N); just pass the half batch count. `compute_scale_shift`'s `cap = 2048 / N` heuristic must use `n_sub` so per-half nchunks stays >= 1 and psum/psq buffers are sized with `n_sub`.
9. Do NOT touch dtype/TF32 settings, do not change kernel bodies, do not add a third stream (more slices shrink each conv's GEMM M and cost more than they hide).
10. Verify numerics: halves are fully independent (GroupNorm reduces over (c,h,w) within one sample), so the result is bit-identical to the single-stream path; run the awkward P=17161 shape through the fallback branch unchanged.

Evidence:
Custom kernels sum 68.7+2x43.4+2x13.2+67.0+129.4 = 378us of a 1179us forward -> ~800us is the 2 cuDNN fprop launches (nsys: 24 launches/12 forwards) moving only ~268MB = ~0.33 TB/s (~16% DRAM) while the customs sit at gpu__dram_throughput 78.5-82.8% with sm__throughput 10-49% (stats_partial: 78.51% DRAM vs 15.5% SM; stats_finalize 0.28 waves/SM, 7.85% DRAM). Root cause: a tensor-core-bound mainloop and a bandwidth-bound epilogue chain are strictly serialized, so ~378us of memory time is fully exposed. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_silu_res_nchw (129.4us) is the bottleneck, make it faster': at the 82% DRAM its siblings actually achieve, its 201MB rooflines at ~114us, i.e. only ~15us (1.3%) of slack, and round-3 mem_vectorize on exactly that kernel scored 1.549 < 1.566 — every custom kernel is already within ~5% of achieved-bandwidth roofline, so no per-kernel tuning can reach the 378us that overlap can hide.

Expected metric change:
(1) Wall clock at 8x256x64x128 drops 1179us -> <=1010us while the SUM of individual kernel durations stays within +/-5% of 378+800us — i.e. nsys must show sm90_xmma fprop ranges temporally overlapping stats_partial / gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw ranges from the other half. (2) GPU-level DRAM utilization during the conv windows rises from ~16% toward >=40%; stats_finalize's 2x13.2us, 0.28-wave launches become fully hidden. Per-launch custom-kernel durations may grow <=15% from SM/L2 contention — acceptable only if total time falls. Anti-regression: N<4 or odd N (2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131) must take the single-stream fallback with an identical kernel sequence and <=1% time change; no shape may regress >2%; max_atol stays under each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003) and results must be bit-identical to the serial path; kernel launches per forward <=22; no cross-stream use-after-free (record_stream on xc/xl/out/w1c/w2c/gamma/beta) and the side stream must come from getStreamFromPool exactly once (static), never created per call.

Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound, cold-L2 re-read] Hottest non-removable segment is the GroupNorm two-pass chain: stats_partial 2x42.8us + stats_finalize 2x13.2us + gn_silu_nhwc 67.4us + gn_silu_res_nchw 129.4us = 307us of 375us custom time. Each GN reads its 67MB intermediate twice via two separate full-tensor launches, so the apply pass misses L2 (4.3%/33.5% hit) and pays full DRAM cost.

Optimisation method:
Slab-interleaved producer/consumer scheduling of the GN passes: instead of one stats launch over the whole tensor then one apply launch over the whole tensor, loop over ~17MB slabs (whole samples; contiguous channel-group halves if one sample exceeds the budget) issuing stats->finalize->apply per slab on the same stream. The apply then re-reads data still resident in the 50MB L2, removing one full 67MB DRAM read per GroupNorm (134MB/forward = 22% of the 603MB custom traffic). Convs, K1 and all kernel math untouched.

Method name:
slab_interleaved_gn_l2_reuse

Modification plan:
Host-side scheduling change only; kernel bodies gain pointer/range offsets, no algorithmic change.
1) In fused_res_block compute the slab size once: `size_t sample_bytes=(size_t)C*P*4; int slab_n=(int)max<size_t>(1,(17ull<<20)/sample_bytes); slab_n=min(slab_n,N);` (17MB read + 17MB write stays under the 50MB L2).
2) Replace the GN1 sequence `compute_scale_shift(y1 whole) ; gn_silu_nhwc(whole)` with: `for(int n0=0;n0<N;n0+=slab_n){int nb=min(slab_n,N-n0); size_t off=(size_t)n0*P*C; stats_partial_kernel<<<dim3(nchunks,nb),C>>>(y1+off, psum+(size_t)n0*nchunks*C, psq+(size_t)n0*nchunks*C, P,C,chunk,nchunks); stats_finalize_kernel<<<nb*G,256>>>(psum+(size_t)n0*nchunks*C, psq+..., g1,b1, sc1+(size_t)n0*C, sh1+(size_t)n0*C, C,G,CPG,nchunks,inv_count,eps); gn_silu_nhwc_kernel<<<dim3((P+by-1)/by, nb)>>>(y1+off, y1s+off, sc1+(size_t)n0*C, sh1+(size_t)n0*C, P, C4);}` — every kernel already indexes batch via blockIdx.y/z, so passing base+off and a reduced nb is sufficient; no index math inside kernels changes.
3) Do the identical loop for GN2, with `gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(y2+off, xc+off, out+off, sc2+n0*C, sh2+n0*C, P, C)` (its blockIdx.z is n, so nb slabs work unchanged).
4) Allocate psum/psq/scale/shift ONCE for the full N (as today) and index by n0, so no per-slab allocation or allocator churn; all launches stay on the current stream, whose program order already guarantees stats->apply ordering (no events/syncs needed).
5) Oversized-sample fallback (large shape 4x256x256x256, sample=67MB>17MB): additionally split channels into contiguous chunks CS = 8*ceil(...) chosen so `P*CS*4<=17MB`, with CS a multiple of 32 (keeps K5's 32-wide c tile and K4's float4 valid) and a multiple of CPG=8 (keeps whole groups intact). Pass `c0` and CS: stats blockDim.x=CS with base pointer `+c0`, finalize grid `nb*(CS/CPG)` with gamma/beta/scale/shift offset by c0, K4 grid.x over C4=CS/4 with row stride C, K5 grid.y=CS/32 with `c0` added to c. Row runs stay >=256B so loads remain coalesced.
6) Single-slab fast path: if `N*sample_bytes <= 17MB` (2x256x64x64 = 8.4MB and 1x256x131x131 = 17.6MB borderline -> allow <=18MB) the loop body executes exactly once with the current grids, giving a byte-identical kernel sequence to today for the small and awkward shapes.
7) Keep chunk/nchunks selection identical to today (`nchunks` derived from full P and full N cap) so the partial-buffer layout and the always-written tail (`psum[o]=s` even when p0>=p1) are preserved for P=17161.
8) Do not touch: nchw2nhwc_kernel, both at::conv2d calls, weight `contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, tolerance-relevant fp32 accumulation.
9) Verify per-shape: max_atol vs reference (0.0027-0.003), and that launches/forward stay <=100 (mid: 4 slabs x 3 x 2 GNs + K1 + 2 convs = 27).
10) If measured L2 hit on the apply pass does not exceed 60%, halve the slab budget to 8MB before abandoning; do not add streams, atomics, or vectorization changes (single-method constraint).

Evidence:
stats_partial_kernel: lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 4.3%, l1tex hit 0%, gpu__dram_throughput 79.65%, 42.8us x2 — it re-reads the 67MB conv output written one kernel earlier, and 67MB > 50MB L2 so every sector misses; gn_silu_res_nchw lts hit 33.45% at 72.47% DRAM, 129.4us. Root cause: the GN stats pass and the GN apply pass are two separate full-tensor launches, so the intermediate is streamed from DRAM twice (134MB of the 603MB custom traffic is pure re-read). Refutation of 'the cuDNN TF32 fprop mainloop (~800us) is the target': it is a default-keep vendor mainloop already algo-selected in round 1 (1.566), and both overlap attempts (rounds 4/6) scored below it; refutation of 'per-kernel bandwidth tuning': all five customs sit at 72-82% of the ~2.04 TB/s these kernels actually achieve, leaving <=40us of roofline slack, which round 3's mem_vectorize confirmed (1.549 < 1.566).

Expected metric change:
(1) gn_silu_nhwc_kernel and gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel lts__t_sector_hit_rate rise from 49.9%/33.45% to >70%, with gpu__dram_throughput falling well below 82%/72% while gpu__time_duration drops 67.4us->~45us and 129.4us->~105us per forward; (2) DRAM bytes/forward for the custom kernels fall >=20% (603MB->~469MB) and total custom time 375us-><=310us, mid-shape speedup 1.3896x->>=1.47x (>=1.65x when composed with the round-1 conv autotune), large shape 1.4924x->>=1.58x. Anti-regression: 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 must take the single-slab path with an identical kernel sequence and <=1% time change; no shape may regress >2%; stats_partial duration must not rise >5% (42.8us) and its DRAM throughput must stay >=75%; kernel launches/forward <=100; max_atol within each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003) with fp32 accumulation and the always-written partial tail preserved for P=17161.
