Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization of complementary-bound stages] Hottest non-removable segment is the composite cuDNN TF32 fprop mainloop (~804us of the 1179us forward, ~0.33 TB/s DRAM = ~16% of achievable) executed strictly serially with the DRAM-bound GN/SiLU/transpose chain (375us at 72-82% DRAM but only 15-50% SM). Compute-bound and bandwidth-bound work never coexist, so ~375us of memory time is fully exposed.

Optimisation method:
Per-sample stream pipelining: GroupNorm statistics are per (n,group) and conv/residual are per-sample, so the block decomposes EXACTLY along batch. Split N into chunks, run each chunk's full 9-kernel sequence on one of two side CUDA streams, so chunk i's cuDNN conv (SM/tensor-core bound, 84% of DRAM idle) overlaps chunk i-1's stats/gn_silu/transpose kernels (80%+ DRAM, <50% SM). Vendor conv mainloop is kept untouched; only scheduling changes.

Method name:
stream_pipeline_overlap

Modification plan:
1) EXACT DECOMPOSITION (in fused_res_block, before any launch): compute `int nchunks = (N >= 4 && (size_t)N*C*P*4ull >= (32u<<20)) ? std::min(4, N) : 1; int cs = (N + nchunks - 1)/nchunks; nchunks = (N + cs - 1)/cs;`. Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization: compute-bound mainloop serialized with DRAM-bound epilogue] Hottest non-removable segment is the composite cuDNN TF32 fprop pair (~804us of the 1179us forward, ~16% DRAM, ~51% TF32 peak) executed strictly after/before the five custom kernels (375us at 72-83% DRAM but only 10-50% SM). All five customs are already within ~5% of their achieved-bandwidth roofline, so their memory time is pure exposed latency.

Optimisation method:
Batch-pipelined dual-stream overlap: because GroupNorm is per-(n,group) and conv is per-sample, the whole chain is exactly separable along N. Split the batch into exactly TWO halves (pointer offsets, no copies) and run each half's full chain (K1->conv1->stats->K4->conv2->stats->K5) on its own stream, so one half's DRAM-saturated GN/transpose kernels execute under the other half's tensor-core conv. Metrics justify it: convs ~16% DRAM/high SM vs customs 78-83% DRAM/15-50% SM — perfectly complementary units that never coexist today.

Method name:
batch_pipelined_dual_stream_overlap

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST (do exactly these; nothing else changes):
1. Refactor `fused_res_block` so the existing per-sample chain becomes a helper `run_chain(const float* x_ptr, float* out_ptr, int n_sub, C,H,W,G, w1c,w2c,g1,b1,g2,b2, eps, stream)` that issues K1, at::conv2d, compute_scale_shift, K4, at::conv2d, compute_scale_shift, K5 on the GIVEN stream with the GIVEN batch count. Batch is the outermost dim of both NCHW x and NHWC intermediates, so a half is just `x.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)half*C*P` and `out.data_ptr<float>() + same` — NO copies, NO views needed for the raw-pointer kernels; for the two at::conv2d calls build the half input with `at::from_blob`-free `xl.narrow(0,0,half)` / `xl.narrow(0,half,half)` (narrow on dim0 keeps channels_last contiguity).
2. Gate: enable the pipelined path only when `N >= 4 && N % 2 == 0 && P >= 4096`. Otherwise call `run_chain` once on the current stream — byte-identical kernel sequence to today for the 2x256x64x64 (N=2) and 1x256x131x131 (N=1) shapes, which must not regress.
3. Before forking, on the CURRENT stream only: `xc = x.contiguous()`, `w1c/w2c = contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, allocate the FULL-size `xl` (channels_last) and `out` (NCHW). This keeps the caching allocator and the weight elementwise_kernels off the side stream.
4. Get a side stream once via a function-local `static auto s_side = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool();` (never create/destroy per call). Use `at::cuda::CUDAEvent` (or two static cudaEvents) for ordering.
5. Ordering: record `ev_start` on the current stream after step 3; `s_side.wait(ev_start)`. Issue `run_chain(half A)` on the current stream, then `run_chain(half B)` on `s_side` (both fully enqueued; the GPU co-schedules B's K1/stats_partial/K4/K5 with A's fprop kernels). Record `ev_done` on `s_side`; make the current stream wait on `ev_done` before returning `out`.
6. Tensors that `run_chain` allocates internally (y1, y1s, y2, partial, scale/shift) are allocated AND consumed on the same stream via `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard` inside the helper, so they need no record_stream.

8. Grid sizes: all kernels already derive grids from `n_sub` (blockIdx.z / gridDim.y = N); just pass the half batch count. `compute_scale_shift`'s `cap = 2048 / N` heuristic must use `n_sub` so per-half nchunks stays >= 1 and psum/psq buffers are sized with `n_sub`.
9. Do NOT touch dtype/TF32 settings, do not change kernel bodies, do not add a third stream (more slices shrink each conv's GEMM M and cost more than they hide).
10. Verify numerics: halves are fully independent (GroupNorm reduces over (c,h,w) within one sample), so the result is bit-identical to the single-stream path; run the awkward P=17161 shape through the fallback branch unchanged.

(2) GPU-level DRAM utilization during the conv windows rises from ~16% toward >=40%; stats_finalize's 2x13.2us, 0.28-wave launches become fully hidden. For the cross-stream tensors allocated on the main stream (xc, w1c, w2c, out) call `t.record_stream(st)` once per side stream to prevent premature reuse.

Expected metric change:
(1) Wall-clock forward at 8x256x64x128 drops from ~1047us (best-known) to <=880us while the SUM of individual kernel durations stays >=1000us — i.e. nsys shows fprop ranges temporally overlapping stats_partial/gn_silu_nhwc/gn_silu_res_nchw ranges. (2) GPU-level gpu__dram_throughput during the conv windows rises from ~16% toward >=40%; stats_finalize's 2x13us latency-bound launches become fully hidden. Per-launch custom-kernel durations may rise <=15% from SM contention — acceptable only if total time falls. Anti-regression: nchunks==1 fallback must give byte-identical kernel sequence and <=1% time change on 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131; no shape may regress >2%; max_atol within 0.0027-0.003; launches <=44/forward; no cross-stream use-after-free (record_stream on xc/w1c/w2c/out).

Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound, cold-L2 re-read] Hottest non-removable segment is the GroupNorm two-pass chain: stats_partial 2x42.8us + stats_finalize 2x13.2us + gn_silu_nhwc 67.4us + gn_silu_res_nchw 129.4us = 307us of 375us custom time. Each GN reads its 67MB intermediate twice via two separate full-tensor launches, so the apply pass misses L2 (4.3%/33.5% hit) and pays full DRAM cost.

Optimisation method:
Slab-interleaved producer/consumer scheduling of the GN passes: instead of one stats launch over the whole tensor then one apply launch over the whole tensor, loop over ~17MB slabs (whole samples; contiguous channel-group halves if one sample exceeds the budget) issuing stats->finalize->apply per slab on the same stream. The apply then re-reads data still resident in the 50MB L2, removing one full 67MB DRAM read per GroupNorm (134MB/forward = 22% of the 603MB custom traffic). Convs, K1 and all kernel math untouched.

Method name:
slab_interleaved_gn_l2_reuse

Modification plan:
Host-side scheduling change only; kernel bodies gain pointer/range offsets, no algorithmic change.
1) In fused_res_block compute the slab size once: `size_t sample_bytes=(size_t)C*P*4; int slab_n=(int)max<size_t>(1,(17ull<<20)/sample_bytes); slab_n=min(slab_n,N);` (17MB read + 17MB write stays under the 50MB L2).
2) Replace the GN1 sequence `compute_scale_shift(y1 whole) ; gn_silu_nhwc(whole)` with: `for(int n0=0;n0<N;n0+=slab_n){int nb=min(slab_n,N-n0); size_t off=(size_t)n0*P*C; stats_partial_kernel<<<dim3(nchunks,nb),C>>>(y1+off, psum+(size_t)n0*nchunks*C, psq+(size_t)n0*nchunks*C, P,C,chunk,nchunks); stats_finalize_kernel<<<nb*G,256>>>(psum+(size_t)n0*nchunks*C, psq+..., g1,b1, sc1+(size_t)n0*C, sh1+(size_t)n0*C, C,G,CPG,nchunks,inv_count,eps); gn_silu_nhwc_kernel<<<dim3((P+by-1)/by, nb)>>>(y1+off, y1s+off, sc1+(size_t)n0*C, sh1+(size_t)n0*C, P, C4);}` — every kernel already indexes batch via blockIdx.y/z, so passing base+off and a reduced nb is sufficient; no index math inside kernels changes.
3) Do the identical loop for GN2, with `gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel<<<dim3((P+31)/32, C/32, nb)>>>(y2+off, xc+off, out+off, sc2+n0*C, sh2+n0*C, P, C)` (its blockIdx.z is n, so nb slabs work unchanged).
4) Allocate psum/psq/scale/shift ONCE for the full N (as today) and index by n0, so no per-slab allocation or allocator churn; all launches stay on the current stream, whose program order already guarantees stats->apply ordering (no events/syncs needed).
5) Oversized-sample fallback (large shape 4x256x256x256, sample=67MB>17MB): additionally split channels into contiguous chunks CS = 8*ceil(...) chosen so `P*CS*4<=17MB`, with CS a multiple of 32 (keeps K5's 32-wide c tile and K4's float4 valid) and a multiple of CPG=8 (keeps whole groups intact). Pass `c0` and CS: stats blockDim.x=CS with base pointer `+c0`, finalize grid `nb*(CS/CPG)` with gamma/beta/scale/shift offset by c0, K4 grid.x over C4=CS/4 with row stride C, K5 grid.y=CS/32 with `c0` added to c. Row runs stay >=256B so loads remain coalesced.
6) Single-slab fast path: if `N*sample_bytes <= 17MB` (2x256x64x64 = 8.4MB and 1x256x131x131 = 17.6MB borderline -> allow <=18MB) the loop body executes exactly once with the current grids, giving a byte-identical kernel sequence to today for the small and awkward shapes.
7) Keep chunk/nchunks selection identical to today (`nchunks` derived from full P and full N cap) so the partial-buffer layout and the always-written tail (`psum[o]=s` even when p0>=p1) are preserved for P=17161.
8) Do not touch: nchw2nhwc_kernel, both at::conv2d calls, weight `contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, tolerance-relevant fp32 accumulation.
9) Verify per-shape: max_atol vs reference (0.0027-0.003), and that launches/forward stay <=100 (mid: 4 slabs x 3 x 2 GNs + K1 + 2 convs = 27).
10) If measured L2 hit on the apply pass does not exceed 60%, halve the slab budget to 8MB before abandoning; do not add streams, atomics, or vectorization changes (single-method constraint).

Evidence:
stats_partial_kernel: lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 4.3%, l1tex hit 0%, gpu__dram_throughput 79.65%, 42.8us x2 — it re-reads the 67MB conv output written one kernel earlier, and 67MB > 50MB L2 so every sector misses; gn_silu_res_nchw lts hit 33.45% at 72.47% DRAM, 129.4us. Root cause: the GN stats pass and the GN apply pass are two separate full-tensor launches, so the intermediate is streamed from DRAM twice (134MB of the 603MB custom traffic is pure re-read). Refutation of 'the cuDNN TF32 fprop mainloop (~800us) is the target': it is a default-keep vendor mainloop already algo-selected in round 1 (1.566), and both overlap attempts (rounds 4/6) scored below it; refutation of 'per-kernel bandwidth tuning': all five customs sit at 72-82% of the ~2.04 TB/s these kernels actually achieve, leaving <=40us of roofline slack, which round 3's mem_vectorize confirmed (1.549 < 1.566).

Bottleneck identified:
[latency-bound reduction inside the hottest custom composite] The GroupNorm segment (stats_partial 2x42.2us + stats_finalize 2x13.2us + apply kernels 67.2us/129.9us) is 307us of the 375us custom-kernel time. Its reduction is split across two launches through a 2MB partial buffer; stats_finalize does no bandwidth work (DRAM 7.89%, 0.28 waves/SM, 25.6% occupancy) and is 87% uncoalesced-sector bound, costing ~26us per forward almost independently of shape.

Optimisation method:
atomic_privatize: privatize the group reduction inside stats_partial. Each block already holds all 256 channels, so reduce the 8 lanes of each group in-register (__shfl_down width 8) and atomicAdd 32 (sum,sumsq) pairs into a tiny [N][G][2] accumulator, then let the last arriving block per image (atomic counter + __threadfence) emit scale/shift. This deletes the 2MB partial round-trip, the 87%-excessive-sector strided loads and both latency-bound stats_finalize launches, which metrics show are pure launch/latency cost, not bandwidth.

Method name:
atomic_privatize

Modification plan:
Checklist (all inside compute_scale_shift + stats kernel; K1/K4/K5/conv untouched):
1. Delete the `partial` tensor `at::empty({2, N*nchunks*C})` and the entire `stats_finalize_kernel` launch. Allocate ONE zeroed scratch for BOTH norms at the top of fused_res_block: `auto acc = at::zeros({2, N*G*2 + N}, opts)` reinterpreted as {float acc[N][G][2]; float ctr[N];} per norm (ctr read as int*). This is one tiny memset for the whole forward, so launches/forward go 11 -> 10 while removing 2x13.2us kernels.
2. Rename stats_partial_kernel -> stats_atomic_kernel(in, acc, ctr, scale, shift, gamma, beta, P, C, chunk, nchunks, G, CPG, inv_count, eps). Keep the existing accumulation loop byte-for-byte (`ptr += C`, `__ldg`) - it is already 80.8% DRAM and coalesced; only the epilogue changes.
3. In-register group reduction (replaces the global partial write): with c = threadIdx.x, CPG = C/G = 8 contiguous lanes per group, do
   `#pragma unroll for (int off = CPG>>1; off; off >>= 1) { s += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, s, off, CPG); q += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, q, off, CPG); }`
   then `if ((c & (CPG-1)) == 0) { int g = c / CPG; atomicAdd(&acc[((n*G)+g)*2+0], s); atomicAdd(&acc[((n*G)+g)*2+1], q); }`. Generic guard: if CPG is not a power of two or CPG > 32, fall back to a 256-float shared-memory segmented reduction (never taken for C=256,G=32).
4. Last-block finalize (removes the second launch): `__threadfence(); __shared__ int isLast; if (threadIdx.x==0) isLast = (atomicAdd(&ctr_i[n],1) == nchunks-1); __syncthreads(); if (isLast) { int g = c / CPG; float sm = acc[(n*G+g)*2+0]*inv_count; float v = acc[(n*G+g)*2+1]*inv_count - sm*sm; v = v<0.f?0.f:v; float r = rsqrtf(v+eps); float gm = gamma?gamma[c]:1.f, bt = beta?beta[c]:0.f; scale[n*C+c] = r*gm; shift[n*C+c] = bt - sm*r*gm; }` - one fully coalesced 256-float store pair per (n) instead of the 458752 excessive sectors the old finalize generated.
5. All 256 threads must reach the __syncthreads(), so keep the empty-range case (p0>=p1) executing the same code path with s=q=0; grid stays dim3(nchunks, N) with nchunks == ceil(P/chunk) exactly, so the counter always reaches nchunks (verified for P=17161 awkward shape and P=4096/8192/65536).
6. Cap atomic contention: clamp nchunks <= 1024 (existing cap logic already yields 128/64/512), so at most 1024 fp32 atomicAdds per (n,g) - accumulation error ~1e-6 relative, well inside atol 0.0028. Keep the `var<0 -> 0` clamp and fp32 accumulation everywhere; no dtype change.
7. Call sites: compute_scale_shift now takes the acc/ctr slice index (0 for norm1, 1 for norm2) and launches exactly one kernel; scale/shift tensors and their layout [N][C] are unchanged so gn_silu_nhwc_kernel and gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel need zero edits.
8. Validate: run all four shapes; assert launches/forward == 10 in nsys and that stats_finalize_kernel no longer appears; assert max_atol per workload (0.0027-0.003).

Evidence:
stats_finalize_kernel: gpu__time_duration 13152 ns x2 launches/forward (26.4us) while moving only 2MB - gpu__dram_throughput 7.89%, launch__waves_per_multiprocessor 0.28, achieved occupancy 25.56%, and the UncoalescedGlobalAccess rule reports 458752 excessive sectors = 87% of 525312 (thread index maps to ck, stride C floats). Root cause: the group reduction is artificially split into a global 2MB partial buffer plus a tiny, strided, latency-bound second launch, although each stats_partial block already spans all 256 channels and can reduce its 8-lane groups in-register. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_silu_res_nchw (129.9us) is the bottleneck': its 201MB at the 2.04 TB/s its sibling kernels achieve rooflines at 99us, i.e. only ~30us (2.5% of the 1179us forward) of slack, and history round 3 attacked exactly that kernel with mem_vectorize and scored 1.549 < the 1.566 best - whereas the 26.4us finalize cost is nearly shape-independent and therefore ~10% of the 205us small shape and ~6% of the 352us awkward shape in the geometric mean.

Expected metric change:
(1) stats_finalize_kernel vanishes from the profile: launches/forward 11 -> 10, 2x13152 ns removed; the surviving stats kernel keeps gpu__dram_throughput >= 78% (currently 80.75%) with gpu__time_duration <= 44.5us (<= 5% above the current 42.176us) and its uncoalesced excessive-sector share drops from 87% to < 10% (per-block global stores fall from 512 floats to 64 atomics). (2) DRAM bytes/forward drop by the 2x2MB partial-buffer round trip and total custom-kernel time 375us -> <= 348us; mid-shape speedup 1.3896x -> >= 1.42x, small shape 1.3558x -> >= 1.45x, awkward shape 1.9211x -> >= 1.98x. Anti-regression: no shape may regress > 2%; max_atol must stay under each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003) with fp32 accumulation unchanged; registers/thread <= 40 so >= 8 blocks/SM occupancy is preserved; the acc/ctr scratch must be zeroed exactly once per forward (single at::zeros) and the counter must reach nchunks on every shape including P=17161.

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization: compute-bound mainloop serialized with DRAM-bound epilogue] Hottest non-removable segment is the composite cuDNN TF32 fprop pair (~804us of the 1179us forward, ~16% DRAM, ~51% TF32 peak) executed strictly after/before the five custom kernels (375us at 72-83% DRAM but only 10-50% SM). All five customs are already within ~5% of their achieved-bandwidth roofline, so their memory time is pure exposed latency.

Optimisation method:
Batch-pipelined dual-stream overlap: because GroupNorm is per-(n,group) and conv is per-sample, the whole chain is exactly separable along N. Split the batch into exactly TWO halves (pointer offsets, no copies) and run each half's full chain (K1->conv1->stats->K4->conv2->stats->K5) on its own stream, so one half's DRAM-saturated GN/transpose kernels execute under the other half's tensor-core conv. Metrics justify it: convs ~16% DRAM/high SM vs customs 78-83% DRAM/15-50% SM — perfectly complementary units that never coexist today.

Method name:
batch_pipelined_dual_stream_overlap

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST (do exactly these; nothing else changes):
1. Refactor `fused_res_block` so the existing per-sample chain becomes a helper `run_chain(const float* x_ptr, float* out_ptr, int n_sub, C,H,W,G, w1c,w2c,g1,b1,g2,b2, eps, stream)` that issues K1, at::conv2d, compute_scale_shift, K4, at::conv2d, compute_scale_shift, K5 on the GIVEN stream with the GIVEN batch count. Batch is the outermost dim of both NCHW x and NHWC intermediates, so a half is just `x.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)half*C*P` and `out.data_ptr<float>() + same` — NO copies, NO views needed for the raw-pointer kernels; for the two at::conv2d calls build the half input with `at::from_blob`-free `xl.narrow(0,0,half)` / `xl.narrow(0,half,half)` (narrow on dim0 keeps channels_last contiguity).
2. Gate: enable the pipelined path only when `N >= 4 && N % 2 == 0 && P >= 4096`. Otherwise call `run_chain` once on the current stream — byte-identical kernel sequence to today for the 2x256x64x64 (N=2) and 1x256x131x131 (N=1) shapes, which must not regress.
3. Before forking, on the CURRENT stream only: `xc = x.contiguous()`, `w1c/w2c = contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, allocate the FULL-size `xl` (channels_last) and `out` (NCHW). This keeps the caching allocator and the weight elementwise_kernels off the side stream.
4. Get a side stream once via a function-local `static auto s_side = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool();` (never create/destroy per call). Use `at::cuda::CUDAEvent` (or two static cudaEvents) for ordering.
5. Ordering: record `ev_start` on the current stream after step 3; `s_side.wait(ev_start)`. Issue `run_chain(half A)` on the current stream, then `run_chain(half B)` on `s_side` (both fully enqueued; the GPU co-schedules B's K1/stats_partial/K4/K5 with A's fprop kernels). Record `ev_done` on `s_side`; make the current stream wait on `ev_done` before returning `out`.
6. Lifetime safety (mandatory): call `.record_stream(s_side)` on `xc`, `xl`, `out`, `w1c`, `w2c`, `g1,b1,g2,b2` so the caching allocator cannot recycle them while the side stream is still reading/writing. Tensors that `run_chain` allocates internally (y1, y1s, y2, partial, scale/shift) are allocated AND consumed on the same stream via `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard` inside the helper, so they need no record_stream.
7. Inside `run_chain`, wrap the body in `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard guard(stream)` so at::conv2d, at::empty and every `<<<...,stream>>>` launch use that stream consistently; pass `stream` explicitly to all five custom kernels (they already take a stream argument).
8. Grid sizes: all kernels already derive grids from `n_sub` (blockIdx.z / gridDim.y = N); just pass the half batch count. `compute_scale_shift`'s `cap = 2048 / N` heuristic must use `n_sub` so per-half nchunks stays >= 1 and psum/psq buffers are sized with `n_sub`.
9. Do NOT touch dtype/TF32 settings, do not change kernel bodies, do not add a third stream (more slices shrink each conv's GEMM M and cost more than they hide).
10. Verify numerics: halves are fully independent (GroupNorm reduces over (c,h,w) within one sample), so the result is bit-identical to the single-stream path; run the awkward P=17161 shape through the fallback branch unchanged.

Evidence:
Custom kernels sum 68.7+2x43.4+2x13.2+67.0+129.4 = 378us of a 1179us forward -> ~800us is the 2 cuDNN fprop launches (nsys: 24 launches/12 forwards) moving only ~268MB = ~0.33 TB/s (~16% DRAM) while the customs sit at gpu__dram_throughput 78.5-82.8% with sm__throughput 10-49% (stats_partial: 78.51% DRAM vs 15.5% SM; stats_finalize 0.28 waves/SM, 7.85% DRAM). Root cause: a tensor-core-bound mainloop and a bandwidth-bound epilogue chain are strictly serialized, so ~378us of memory time is fully exposed. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_silu_res_nchw (129.4us) is the bottleneck, make it faster': at the 82% DRAM its siblings actually achieve, its 201MB rooflines at ~114us, i.e. only ~15us (1.3%) of slack, and round-3 mem_vectorize on exactly that kernel scored 1.549 < 1.566 — every custom kernel is already within ~5% of achieved-bandwidth roofline, so no per-kernel tuning can reach the 378us that overlap can hide.

Expected metric change:
(1) Wall clock at 8x256x64x128 drops 1179us -> <=1010us while the SUM of individual kernel durations stays within +/-5% of 378+800us — i.e. nsys must show sm90_xmma fprop ranges temporally overlapping stats_partial / gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw ranges from the other half. (2) GPU-level DRAM utilization during the conv windows rises from ~16% toward >=40%; stats_finalize's 2x13.2us, 0.28-wave launches become fully hidden. Per-launch custom-kernel durations may grow <=15% from SM/L2 contention — acceptable only if total time falls. Anti-regression: N<4 or odd N (2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131) must take the single-stream fallback with an identical kernel sequence and <=1% time change; no shape may regress >2%; max_atol stays under each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003) and results must be bit-identical to the serial path; kernel launches per forward <=22; no cross-stream use-after-free (record_stream on xc/xl/out/w1c/w2c/gamma/beta) and the side stream must come from getStreamFromPool exactly once (static), never created per call.

slab_interleaved_gn_l2_reuse

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization: compute-bound mainloop serialized with DRAM-bound epilogue] Hottest non-removable segment is the composite cuDNN TF32 fprop pair (~804us of the 1179us forward, ~16% DRAM, ~51% TF32 peak) executed strictly after/before the five custom kernels (375us at 72-83% DRAM but only 10-50% SM). All five customs are already within ~5% of their achieved-bandwidth roofline, so their memory time is pure exposed latency.

Optimisation method:
Batch-pipelined dual-stream overlap: because GroupNorm is per-(n,group) and conv is per-sample, the whole chain is exactly separable along N. Split the batch into exactly TWO halves (pointer offsets, no copies) and run each half's full chain (K1->conv1->stats->K4->conv2->stats->K5) on its own stream, so one half's DRAM-saturated GN/transpose kernels execute under the other half's tensor-core conv. Metrics justify it: convs ~16% DRAM/high SM vs customs 78-83% DRAM/15-50% SM — perfectly complementary units that never coexist today.

Method name:
batch_pipelined_dual_stream_overlap

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST (do exactly these; nothing else changes):
1. Refactor `fused_res_block` so the existing per-sample chain becomes a helper `run_chain(const float* x_ptr, float* out_ptr, int n_sub, C,H,W,G, w1c,w2c,g1,b1,g2,b2, eps, stream)` that issues K1, at::conv2d, compute_scale_shift, K4, at::conv2d, compute_scale_shift, K5 on the GIVEN stream with the GIVEN batch count. Batch is the outermost dim of both NCHW x and NHWC intermediates, so a half is just `x.data_ptr<float>() + (size_t)half*C*P` and `out.data_ptr<float>() + same` — NO copies, NO views needed for the raw-pointer kernels; for the two at::conv2d calls build the half input with `at::from_blob`-free `xl.narrow(0,0,half)` / `xl.narrow(0,half,half)` (narrow on dim0 keeps channels_last contiguity).
2. Gate: enable the pipelined path only when `N >= 4 && N % 2 == 0 && P >= 4096`. Otherwise call `run_chain` once on the current stream — byte-identical kernel sequence to today for the 2x256x64x64 (N=2) and 1x256x131x131 (N=1) shapes, which must not regress.
3. Before forking, on the CURRENT stream only: `xc = x.contiguous()`, `w1c/w2c = contiguous(ChannelsLast)`, allocate the FULL-size `xl` (channels_last) and `out` (NCHW). This keeps the caching allocator and the weight elementwise_kernels off the side stream.
4. Get a side stream once via a function-local `static auto s_side = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool();` (never create/destroy per call). Use `at::cuda::CUDAEvent` (or two static cudaEvents) for ordering.
5. Ordering: record `ev_start` on the current stream after step 3; `s_side.wait(ev_start)`. Issue `run_chain(half A)` on the current stream, then `run_chain(half B)` on `s_side` (both fully enqueued; the GPU co-schedules B's K1/stats_partial/K4/K5 with A's fprop kernels). Record `ev_done` on `s_side`; make the current stream wait on `ev_done` before returning `out`.
6. Lifetime safety (mandatory): call `.record_stream(s_side)` on `xc`, `xl`, `out`, `w1c`, `w2c`, `g1,b1,g2,b2` so the caching allocator cannot recycle them while the side stream is still reading/writing. Tensors that `run_chain` allocates internally (y1, y1s, y2, partial, scale/shift) are allocated AND consumed on the same stream via `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard` inside the helper, so they need no record_stream.
7. Inside `run_chain`, wrap the body in `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard guard(stream)` so at::conv2d, at::empty and every `<<<...,stream>>>` launch use that stream consistently; pass `stream` explicitly to all five custom kernels (they already take a stream argument).
8. Grid sizes: all kernels already derive grids from `n_sub` (blockIdx.z / gridDim.y = N); just pass the half batch count. `compute_scale_shift`'s `cap = 2048 / N` heuristic must use `n_sub` so per-half nchunks stays >= 1 and psum/psq buffers are sized with `n_sub`.
9. Do NOT touch dtype/TF32 settings, do not change kernel bodies, do not add a third stream (more slices shrink each conv's GEMM M and cost more than they hide).
10. Verify numerics: halves are fully independent (GroupNorm reduces over (c,h,w) within one sample), so the result is bit-identical to the single-stream path; run the awkward P=17161 shape through the fallback branch unchanged.

Custom kernels sum 68.7+2x43.4+2x13.2+67.0+129.4 = 378us of a 1179us forward -> ~800us is the 2 cuDNN fprop launches (nsys: 24 launches/12 forwards) moving only ~268MB = ~0.33 TB/s (~16% DRAM) while the customs sit at gpu__dram_throughput 78.5-82.8% with sm__throughput 10-49% (stats_partial: 78.51% DRAM vs 15.5% SM; stats_finalize 0.28 waves/SM, 7.85% DRAM). Root cause: a tensor-core-bound mainloop and a bandwidth-bound epilogue chain are strictly serialized, so ~378us of memory time is fully exposed. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_silu_res_nchw (129.4us) is the bottleneck, make it faster': at the 82% DRAM its siblings actually achieve, its 201MB rooflines at ~114us, i.e. only ~15us (1.3%) of slack, and round-3 mem_vectorize on exactly that kernel scored 1.549 < 1.566 — every custom kernel is already within ~5% of achieved-bandwidth roofline, so no per-kernel tuning can reach the 378us that overlap can hide.

(1) Wall clock at 8x256x64x128 drops 1179us -> <=1010us while the SUM of individual kernel durations stays within +/-5% of 378+800us — i.e. nsys must show sm90_xmma fprop ranges temporally overlapping stats_partial / gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw ranges from the other half. (2) GPU-level DRAM utilization during the conv windows rises from ~16% toward >=40%; stats_finalize's 2x13.2us, 0.28-wave launches become fully hidden. Per-launch custom-kernel durations may grow <=15% from SM/L2 contention — acceptable only if total time falls. Anti-regression: N<4 or odd N (2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131) must take the single-stream fallback with an identical kernel sequence and <=1% time change; no shape may regress >2%; max_atol stays under each workload tolerance (0.0027-0.003) and results must be bit-identical to the serial path; kernel launches per forward <=22; no cross-stream use-after-free (record_stream on xc/xl/out/w1c/w2c/gamma/beta) and the side stream must come from getStreamFromPool exactly once (static), never created per call.

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/utilisation-imbalance across a serial dependency chain] The forward is one strictly serial stream: cuDNN `sm90_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm...nhwc` (63.1%, 7147us, ~68% of TF32 peak, only ~0.45-0.67 TB/s DRAM) alternating with four DRAM-bound custom kernels (gn_silu_res_t 12.2%, gn_partial 9.0%, nchw2nhwc 7.3%, gn_silu 6.5%) that sit at 73-81% DRAM but 20-45% SM. Tensor cores idle during GN, DRAM idles during conv.

Optimisation method:
Batch-split stream pipelining: split the block along N (exact, no halo, GN stats are per-(n,group)) into chunks and run convolutions on one CUDA stream and all GroupNorm/SiLU/transpose kernels on a second, with events creating a one-stage skew so conv of chunk i+1 overlaps GN of chunk i. Metrics justify it: memory-bound kernels already run at 81% DRAM (no per-kernel headroom, bytes are compulsory), while the compute-bound conv leaves DRAM ~70% idle; only concurrency can recover the ~347us/iter of serial memory time.

Method name:
stream_pipeline_overlap

Modification plan:
Only the host schedule inside `fused_block` changes; all five __global__ kernels stay byte-identical (guarantees numerics).

1. EXACT CODE ACTION — chunking: after computing N,C,H,W, add `int k = (N >= 4) ? 4 : (int)N;` and per-chunk ranges `n0 = c*((N+k-1)/k)`, `cn = min(chunk, N-n0)` (skip empty chunks so odd N works). Build per-chunk views with `.narrow(0,n0,cn)` on x_cl, y1, z, y2, out, xc — batch is the outermost dim in both NCHW and NHWC so every narrow stays contiguous in its memory format. If `N < 2`, execute the existing single-stream path unchanged (protects the 1x256x131x131 shape, currently 2.06x).

2. EXACT CODE ACTION — two streams + events: `auto sC = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool(); auto sM = at::cuda::getStreamFromPool();` (function-local `static thread_local` so streams are created once). Record `at::cuda::CUDAEvent ev0` on the current stream after the K1 nchw2nhwc launches and have both sC and sM `block()` on it, so side streams see x_cl. Allocate arrays `CUDAEvent evConv1[k], evGN1[k], evConv2[k], evGN2[k]`. Wrap every launch in `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(stream);` and replace `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` in the raw launches with the guarded stream so at::conv2d and the custom kernels land on the intended stream.

3. Issue order (this is what creates the skew — do not issue per-chunk chains):
   sC: for c in 0..k-1 { conv1(chunk c); evConv1[c].record(sC); }
   sM: for c { evConv1[c].block(sM); gn_partial/gn_finalize/gn_silu(chunk c); evGN1[c].record(sM); }
   sC: for c { evGN1[c].block(sC); conv2(chunk c); evConv2[c].record(sC); }
   sM: for c { evConv2[c].block(sM); gn_partial/gn_finalize/gn_silu_res_t(chunk c); evGN2[c].record(sM); }
   Result: conv1(c1..c3) runs concurrently with GN1(c0); conv2(c0..) runs concurrently with GN1(c1..).

4. Buffer disjointness: index `part`, `scale`, `shift` with a per-chunk offset (`part.data_ptr<double>() + (size_t)n0*GG*nchunks*2`, `scale.data_ptr<float>() + n0*CC`) and pass `blockIdx.y`-local n as today. All GN kernels live on sM, so norm1's apply for chunk c always precedes norm2's finalize for any chunk in stream order — no WAR hazard; the offsets remove any doubt.

5. Allocator safety: for every tensor created on the current stream but consumed on sC/sM (x_cl, y1, z, y2, out, part, scale, shift, w1c, w2c), call `c10::cuda::CUDACachingAllocator::recordStream(t.storage().data_ptr(), sC/sM)` to prevent premature block reuse.

6. Join: at the end, `evGN2[k-1].block(getCurrentCUDAStream())` and also block on `evConv2[k-1]`, then return `out`. The returned tensor is thus safe for the caller's stream and the harness's event timing stays valid.

7. Keep `nchunks/ppc` reduction schedule but recompute the block target from per-chunk work: `nc = ceil(8*sms / cn)` clamped as today, so the stats grid still fills the SM while sharing the GPU with a concurrent conv.

8. Guardrail on chunk size: require per-chunk implicit-GEMM M = cn*H*W >= 8192; otherwise reduce k (k=2 or 1). For 8x64x128 with k=4 each conv still issues ~512 CTAs (4.5 waves), so tail-wave loss stays under ~5%.

9. Validate all four shapes; ensure the N=1 shape takes the untouched single-stream path and that outputs are bitwise identical to the current candidate (same kernels, same reduction order per sample).

Evidence:
Nsys: conv = 63.1% (7147us/12 iters = 596us/iter) but moves only ~134-200MB/conv => ~0.45-0.67 TB/s, i.e. ~25-33% of this H100 PCIe's ~2.04 TB/s DRAM peak (NCU reports 1.66 TB/s = 81.5%). The four custom kernels total 347us/iter at 73-81% DRAM and 20-45% SM throughput. Root cause: strict serialization of a compute-bound stage and a memory-bound stage on one stream, so each stage idles the other's unit; aggregate floor is max(596us compute, 427us for the 872MB total traffic) ~ 600us vs 943us actual. Refutation of 'the GN kernels are individually inefficient': they already run at 81% DRAM with compulsory traffic (9x tensor bytes is minimal for two-pass GroupNorm + residual + layout), so per-kernel tuning caps out near 15%; refutation of 'conv algo is bad': measured ~259 TFLOPS ~ 68% of dense TF32 peak, leaving far less headroom than overlap.

Expected metric change:
(1) Total forward GPU time per iteration drops from ~943us toward ~700us (target >=1.15x end-to-end on the N>=2 shapes). (2) Time-averaged gpu__dram_throughput during the conv phase rises (conv+GN co-resident), and the GN kernels' individual gpu__time_duration may rise up to ~20% while wall time falls — judge by wall clock, not per-kernel duration. (3) sm__throughput during GN-phase windows rises as conv CTAs co-schedule. Anti-regression: N=1 (1x256x131x131) must keep the single-stream path and its 2.06x; per-chunk conv must keep >=4 waves (k<=4) so no shape loses >2% to tail effects; outputs must remain bitwise identical to the current candidate on all four shapes.
pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[compute/tensor-core-bound] The cuDNN mainloop `sm90_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm_f32f32_tf32f32_f32_nhwckrsc_nhwc_tilesize64x128x32` holds 63.1% of forward GPU time (7148us / 24 launches = 298us per conv = 77.3 GFLOP -> ~259 TFLOPS, only ~68% of dense TF32 peak). One single tile shape is used for all four very different workload shapes, i.e. cuDNN is running in heuristic (non-benchmarked) plan selection.

Optimisation method:
Vendor-library algorithm autotuning for the conv mainloop: call `at::cudnn_convolution(..., benchmark=true, deterministic=false, allow_tf32=true)` instead of `at::conv2d`, plus enabling the global cuDNN benchmark flag so PyTorch's cuDNN-v8 frontend exhaustively times candidate plans per shape and caches the winner. Metrics justify it: the conv is the only compute-bound segment with real headroom (68% of TF32 peak), while every custom kernel already sits at 74-82% DRAM. No dtype change (TF32 kept, as in the reference).

Method name:
cudnn_algo_autotune

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST (focused diff inside the existing extension; no kernel source changes):
1. In `fused_block`, replace `auto y1 = at::conv2d(x_cl, w1c, {}, stride, pad, dil, 1);` with `auto y1 = at::cudnn_convolution(x_cl, w1c, /*padding=*/{1,1}, /*stride=*/{1,1}, /*dilation=*/{1,1}, /*groups=*/1, /*benchmark=*/true, /*deterministic=*/false, /*allow_tf32=*/true);` and identically replace `auto y2 = at::conv2d(z, w2c, ...)` with `at::cudnn_convolution(z, w2c, {1,1},{1,1},{1,1},1,true,false,true);`. This forces the cuDNN v8 path AND turns on exhaustive plan search for that call.
2. Add a one-time global switch at the top of `fused_block`: `static const bool _bm = [](){ at::globalContext().setBenchmarkCuDNN(true); at::globalContext().setBenchmarkLimitCuDNN(16); return true; }();` so PyTorch's plan cache autotunes and then reuses the winning engine config per (shape, layout, dtype) key. Include `<ATen/Context.h>`.
3. Safety wrapper: put each `at::cudnn_convolution` call inside `try { ... } catch (const std::exception&) { y = at::conv2d(<same args>); }` so any unsupported config silently falls back to the current behaviour (correctness never depends on the new path).
4. Keep the existing post-conditions untouched: `if (!y1.is_contiguous(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast)) y1 = y1.contiguous(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast);` (same for y2) — `cudnn_convolution` propagates the channels-last format of `x_cl`/`z`, so this should be a no-op, but keep the guard.
5. Do NOT touch K1/K2/K3/K4/K5, the reduction schedule, the double-precision statistic accumulation, the residual path, or the Python fallback — the win must compose with the existing fusion structure (this is why an overlap/chunking mechanism failed: it dismantled the base's full-tensor launches).
6. Keep `w1c`/`w2c` channels-last conversion exactly as-is (2.4MB, ~1us) so the autotuned plan key stays stable across iterations.
7. Warmup contract: the plan search runs once per distinct shape; the benchmark harness's warmup iterations absorb it. If any shape shows a large first-iteration spike, lower `setBenchmarkLimitCuDNN` to 8; do not disable it per-shape.
8. Verification: re-run nsys and confirm the conv kernel name is no longer a single `tilesize64x128x32` entry for all 24 launches (expect distinct tiles per shape, e.g. 128x128x32 / 256x64x32) and that total conv us drops. If the kernel name and time are unchanged, the mechanism did not engage — in that case the defect is the dispatch (check that `x_cl`/`w1c` are truly channels-last fp32 and that `at::globalContext().benchmarkCuDNN()` returns true), not the method.
9. Numeric check: cuDNN may select a split-K plan with a different accumulation order; validate all four shapes against the reference with atol 0.0028 / rtol 1e-5 before accepting. If a plan violates tolerance, set `deterministic=false, allow_tf32=true` unchanged but drop `benchmark` for that shape only.
10. Score gate: accept only if the geometric mean over 8x64x128, 2x64x64, 4x256x256 and 1x131x131 improves and no individual shape regresses more than 0.5%.

Evidence:
Nsys: conv = 63.1% / 7148us over 24 launches = 298us per conv; work per conv = 2*8*256*256*9*64*128 = 77.3 GFLOP -> 259 TFLOPS ~= 68% of this H100's dense TF32 peak, and one identical `tilesize64x128x32` kernel serves all four shapes => heuristic plan selection, not autotuned. Root cause: sub-optimal cuDNN engine/tile for M=65536,N=256,K=2304 implicit GEMM. History classification = (a): the stream_pipeline_overlap attempt DID engage (gn_partial grid 114x8 -> 256x2, duration 42.6us -> 13.5us for half the work, per-kernel DRAM 79%->59%) yet every shape regressed (-0.6%/-1.3%/-3.7%/-1.7%), so the serialization model was wrong and overlap/chunking is a dead end; the same profile also kills L2-blocking (gn_partial lts hit rate only 7.65% even with 33MB chunks). Refutation of 'the GN/transpose kernels are the bottleneck': they run at 73.9-81.7% DRAM (1.51-1.66 TB/s) moving a near-minimal 13 tensor passes, so perfecting them caps the round at ~3%. The proposed change composes with the base: same 5 custom kernels, same launch count, same fusion.

Expected metric change:
(1) cuDNN conv total GPU time drops from 7148us toward <6600us (>=8%), i.e. per-conv 298us -> <275us, raising effective TF32 utilisation from ~68% to >75%; the nsys kernel name should change tile/engine per shape. (2) Forward-pass conv share falls from 63.1% to <60% while `sm__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed` for the conv kernel rises. Anti-regression: the five custom kernels' gpu__time_duration and gpu__dram_throughput must stay within +/-2% of the current profile (68.2us / 43.0us / 6.5us / 69.0us / 127.3us at 73.6-81.7% DRAM); launch count stays 132; outputs within atol 0.0028 on all four shapes; no shape may regress >0.5%, in particular the small 2x256x64x64 case must not pay visible autotune cost after warmup.

pairs.a_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[latency/serialization of complementary-bound phases] Hottest non-removable segment is the cuDNN TF32 conv mainloop (sm90_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm, 35.6% GPU time, 9029us/30 launches) which is compute-bound, while the surrounding custom kernels (gn_silu_res_t 6.7%, gn_partial 4.4%, nchw2nhwc 4.0%, gn_silu 3.7%) are DRAM-bound at 73-81% of this H100-PCIe's ~2.0TB/s. Both phases run strictly serially; neither has per-kernel headroom.

Optimisation method:
Batch-chunked multi-stream pipelining: split the block over the N axis (GroupNorm is per-(n,group), so the split is exactly equivalent) into 2 chunks executed on 2 side streams, so one chunk's DRAM-bound GN/transpose kernels (SM throughput 19-45%, DRAM 80%) co-reside with the other chunk's compute-bound conv (SM-bound, low DRAM). This hides up to ~360us of memory-kernel time behind ~500us of conv time — the only remaining lever since bytes (13 tensor-passes) and conv FLOPs are already near their respective roofs.

Method name:
stream_pipeline_overlap

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST (numbered actions; all inside fused_block, no interface change):
1. Add chunk-eligibility guard at top of fused_block: `int nchunk = (N >= 4 && (N/2)*HW >= 32768) ? 2 : 1;` If nchunk==1 keep the EXACT current single-stream code path (guarantees the small 2x256x64x64 and awkward 1x256x131x131 shapes are byte-identical in launch count and schedule; only 8x64x128 -> 2 chunks of 4 and 4x256x256 -> 2 chunks of 2 take the new path). Rationale: keeps per-chunk conv CTA count >= 256 so wave quantization does not regress the mainloop.
2. Semantic proof to encode in a comment: GroupNorm reduces over (C/G, H, W) within one sample, and the residual add is elementwise, so slicing on N is an exact rewrite; nothing crosses chunk boundaries. Statistic buffers stay disjoint because `part` is indexed n*GG+g and `scale/shift` by n*CC+c, so `narrow(0,n0,nc)` slices never alias.
3. Stream pool: `static std::vector<at::cuda::CUDAStream> pool = {at::cuda::getStreamFromPool(), at::cuda::getStreamFromPool()};` created once (function-local static). Record `at::cuda::CUDAEvent start; start.record(at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream());` then `start.block(pool[i])` for each side stream so both wait for the caller's inputs.
4. Allocate ALL full-size tensors (x_cl, out, part, scale, shift) once on the caller's stream as today, then call `c10::cuda::CUDACachingAllocator::recordStream(t.storage().data_ptr(), pool[i])` for each tensor used on a side stream (prevents caching-allocator reuse-before-completion). Compute the reduction schedule (nc/ppc/nchunks) from the CHUNK's N so both chunks share the same `part` layout and the narrowed slices stay valid.
5. Chunk loop `for (i=0;i<nchunk;++i)`: build views `auto xs = xc.narrow(0,n0,nc); auto xcl_s = x_cl.narrow(0,n0,nc); auto out_s = out.narrow(0,n0,nc); auto part_s = part.narrow(0,(int64_t)n0*GG*nchunks, (int64_t)nc*GG*nchunks); auto sc_s = scale.narrow(0,n0,nc); auto sh_s = shift.narrow(0,n0,nc);` (narrow on dim 0 preserves channels-last contiguity). Enter `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard g(pool[i]);` and issue the whole existing chain (K1, conv1, K2, K3, K4, conv2, K2, K3, K5) on `pool[i]`, passing `pool[i].stream()` explicitly to every `<<<...>>>` launch instead of `getCurrentCUDAStream()` (guard already redirects ATen/cuDNN work).
6. Join: after the loop, for each i `at::cuda::CUDAEvent done; done.record(pool[i]); done.block(at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream());` before `return out;`.
7. Hoist the two weight conversions (`w1c`, `w2c`) OUT of the chunk loop and keep them on the caller's stream before the fork (they are shared read-only inputs); recordStream them for both side streams.
8. Preserve the existing cudnn_algo_autotune mechanism: keep `setBenchmarkCuDNN(true)` and the `at::cudnn_convolution(..., benchmark=true, deterministic=false, allow_tf32=true)` call with its try/catch fallback verbatim inside the chunk loop. ACCOUNTING: the plan-cache key now includes the chunked batch size, so cuDNN re-autotunes once per new chunk shape (one-time, amortized over the timed iterations); nothing is disabled. Verify by checking that the steady-state conv kernel name stays an sm90 nhwckrsc_nhwc TF32 implicit-GEMM tile and does not revert to a default/sm80 nchw engine.
9. Grid sizing per chunk uses the chunk's N (grid.z = nc) — audit every launch (nchw2nhwc, gn_partial grid.y, gn_finalize grid = nc*GG, gn_silu grid.y, gn_silu_res_t grid.z) so no block indexes outside its slice; the awkward-shape tail logic (HW+31)/32 and pend clamp is unchanged.

Evidence:
Metrics: conv mainloop = 35.6% GPU time (9029us/30 launches), ~77.3 GFLOP per mid-shape conv in ~250us ~= 300 TFLOPS TF32 (~80% of H100-PCIe dense peak) -> compute-bound with sm__throughput high and DRAM low. Custom kernels: gn_partial sm__throughput 19.6% vs dram 79.4%, gn_silu 43.8% vs 80.9%, gn_silu_res_t 44.8% vs 73.5%, nchw2nhwc 38.5% vs 81.5%; long_scoreboard stalls 62-82% -> pure DRAM-BW bound at ~1.65-1.95 TB/s of the ~2.0 TB/s HBM2e roof. Root cause: two resource-disjoint phases (SM-bound conv, DRAM-bound norm/transpose) execute strictly serially on one stream, so each phase idles the other's dominant unit. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_silu_res_t is the bottleneck': it holds only 6.7% of GPU time and already runs at 73% DRAM, so even perfecting it caps the round at ~5%; likewise a custom conv is refuted by the conv already sitting at ~80% of TF32 peak.

Expected metric change:
1) Wall-clock per forward on 8x256x64x128 and 4x256x256x256 drops 10-20% while the SUM of individual kernel durations stays ~constant (proof the win is overlap, not per-kernel speedup); nsys timeline must show gn_* / nchw2nhwc kernels concurrent with sm90_xmma_fprop conv. 2) gpu__dram_throughput during the conv window rises (conv+GN co-resident) and total GPU busy-time gaps shrink. ANTI-REGRESSION: per-launch duration of the sm90 nhwc TF32 conv must not rise >10% versus the unchunked run (wave-quantization guard N>=4 and chunk*H*W>=32768); launch count and kernel schedule for 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 must be unchanged (single-stream path); cuDNN must still select an autotuned sm90_xmma nhwckrsc_nhwc engine (not an sm80/nchw default) — if it reverts, the autotune mechanism was lost; geometric-mean speedup over all four shapes must not decrease.
pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM-traffic bound composite segment] Target = the conv→GN→SiLU→conv→GN→SiLU+residual dataflow. The cuDNN TF32 mainloop is hottest (35.6%) but is a default-keep vendor kernel; the segment around it makes NINE full-tensor DRAM passes (~1.0 GB per mid forward for a 67 MB tensor). Custom kernels sit at 73–82% DRAM with lts hit rate 2.7–50% and 63–85% long_scoreboard stalls: intermediates are re-read cold from HBM.

Optimisation method:
L2-resident batch blocking (cache blocking): process the block in batch chunks sized so the live intermediates (x_nhwc, y1, z, y2) fit H100's 50 MB L2, reusing the same buffers each iteration, single stream, sequential. Every intermediate is then written and re-read from L2 instead of HBM — this removes DRAM traffic for the GN stats pass, the GN/SiLU apply pass and the conv's own input read/output write. Justified by E2 (equivalent restructure cutting global traffic) plus DRAM 80%/SM 19% and lts hit 2.74%.

Method name:
l2_resident_batch_blocking

Modification plan:
Checklist (in fused_block, host side only; kernels unchanged except grid.z=chunk):
1. Compute per_sample_bytes = C*H*W*4. Set target_live = 40<<20 (~80% of H100 50 MB L2, two intermediates live at once). chunk = clamp(target_live/(2*per_sample_bytes), 1, N). Snap chunk DOWN to a divisor of N (while (N % chunk) --chunk) so only ONE cuDNN shape exists. Guard conv efficiency: while (chunk*H*W < 16384 && chunk < N) ++chunk to divisor. If N*per_sample_bytes <= target_live set chunk = N (2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 then take today's exact single-iteration path, unchanged).
2. Allocate ALL scratch ONCE, before the loop, at chunk batch size and reuse it every iteration (identical pointers keep the lines hot and avoid allocator churn): x_cl{chunk,C,H,W} channels_last, z{chunk,...} channels_last, part{chunk*GG*nchunks,2} double, scale/shift{chunk,C}. Output `out` and input `xc` stay full-size.
3. Recompute the reduction schedule from chunk, not N: nc = ceil(8*sms/chunk), clamp to (HW+31)/32, ppc = ceil(HW/nc), nchunks = ceil(HW/ppc); M = CPG*HW unchanged (stats are per (n,g), so chunking over the batch is exactly equivalent — no cross-sample dependency, bit-identical fp64 order).
4. Loop `for (off = 0; off < N; off += chunk)`: build slice pointers xs = xc.data_ptr + off*C*HW, os = out.data_ptr + off*C*HW; launch K1 with grid.z = chunk writing x_cl; conv1 = cudnn_convolution(x_cl, w1c, ..., benchmark=true, deterministic=false, allow_tf32=true) -> y1; K2/K3 with gridDim.y = chunk and grid.x = nchunks, gridDim = chunk*GG for finalize; K4 -> z; conv2(z,w2c,...) -> y2; K2/K3; K5 with grid.z = chunk reading y2 and xs, writing os. All launches on at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream() — NO extra streams (concurrency is what destroyed reuse in round 3: its lts hit stayed 5.3%).
5. Keep the cudnn_algo_autotune mechanism intact: at::globalContext().setBenchmarkCuDNN(true) stays, the try/catch dispatch stays, and because every iteration uses the identical (chunk,C,H,W) shape the autotuned plan is looked up once and reused for all iterations and all later calls.
6. Optional persistence hint (do after step 4 works): once per process cudaDeviceSetLimit(cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize, maxWindowSize); before the loop set a stream cudaAccessPolicyWindow over the y1/z base pointer with num_bytes = min(chunk*per_sample_bytes, maxWindow), hitRatio 1.0, hitProp = cudaAccessPropertyPersisting, missProp = Streaming; reset the window (num_bytes 0) before returning.
7. y1/y2 come from cuDNN so they are fresh allocations per iteration; force reuse by pre-allocating y1_buf/y2_buf{chunk,...} channels_last and, if the ATen signature allows only out-of-place, keep them as-is but rely on the caching allocator returning the same block each iteration (same size ⇒ same block).
8. Keep the fp32 storage/arith contract and the float64 reduction exactly as today; no dtype change anywhere.
9. Verify tail handling is impossible by construction (chunk divides N); assert (N % chunk) == 0.

Evidence:
Round-3 verdict: case (i) — its predicted overlap DID occur (per-kernel DRAM throughput fell 81.6%→72.6% for nchw2nhwc, 80.3%→72.8% for gn_partial while durations halved with half the work), so the mechanism worked but was worth only +0.12%; the deciding metric is lts__t_sector_hit_rate, which stayed cold (2.74%→5.26%), proving the chunks it created never became L2-resident because two streams shared L2. Root cause here: the block makes 9 full-tensor DRAM passes (~1.0 GB for a 67 MB tensor) with gn_partial at gpu__dram_throughput 80.29% vs sm__throughput 19.01% and 82.7% long_scoreboard stalls. Alternative 'the conv is the bottleneck' is refuted for direct attack: it is an autotuned sm90 nhwckrsc_nhwc TF32 mainloop (default-keep) — but this method still helps it, since its input read and output write become L2 hits. This composes with cudnn_algo_autotune (same single chunk shape ⇒ one cached plan).

Expected metric change:
1) lts__t_sector_hit_rate for gn_partial rises 2.74% → >40% and for gn_silu 49.96% → >70%. 2) gpu__dram_throughput of the custom kernels falls below 60% while their summed duration drops ≥25% (68+42*2+69+128 = 350us → <260us), i.e. bytes now come from L2, not HBM. 3) Wall clock on 8x256x64x128 and 4x256x256x256 improves ≥8%. ANTI-REGRESSION: per-launch sm90_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm duration must not rise >10% vs the unchunked run (chunk*H*W ≥ 16384 guard) and the selected engine must remain sm90_...nhwckrsc_nhwc — if it reverts to an sm80/nchw or cutlass plan the autotune mechanism was lost; kernel launch sequence for 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 must be byte-identical to today (chunk == N path); total launches must stay ≤ 4x per shape and geometric-mean speedup over all four shapes must not decrease.

pairs.a_text:
Bottleneck identified:
Launch/latency-bound host path: ~45 kernel launches plus ATen dispatch, cuDNN plan lookup and per-chunk allocations per forward. No kernel is near roofline (max DRAM 55.4%, SM 15.1%), and tiny kernels (gn_finalize 0.04 waves/SM, 6.9us) are pure launch latency.

Optimisation method:
Capture the whole fused_block sequence (K1, conv1, K2/K3, K4, conv2, K2/K3, K5 over all chunks) once per shape into a CUDA Graph over static input buffers, after a warmup that locks the cuDNN autotuned plan; replay per call after small copy_ of inputs.

Method name:
CUDA_Graph_Capture_Replay_StaticBuffers

Modification plan:
1. CUDA source, single guard only: inside fused_block, wrap BOTH `cudaStreamSetAttribute` blocks (the persisting-L2 window set and the reset at the end) in `cudaStreamCaptureStatus st; cudaStreamIsCapturing(stream,&st); if (st==cudaStreamCaptureStatusNone) {...}`. This keeps stream-attribute mutation out of capture. Accounted removal: only the OPTIONAL persisting-L2 window is skipped inside graphs; the core l2_resident_batch_blocking chunk loop (chunk computed from N/HW, one scratch set, sequential chunk loop) still executes verbatim inside the captured graph.
2. Leave all five kernels, block/grid shapes, chunk math, and the cudnn_convolution(benchmark=true, allow_tf32=true) calls unchanged.
3. In `ModelNew.__init__`, add `self._graphs = {}` and `self._pool = None`.
4. In `forward`, use the graph path only if `x.is_cuda and x.dtype==torch.float32 and x.dim()==4 and x.size(1)==256 and not self.training and not torch.is_grad_enabled()`; otherwise call the ext directly (existing path), and keep the Python reference fallback unchanged.
5. Build `key = (tuple(x.shape), x.dtype, x.device.index, float(eps))`. eps is passed by value into kernels and is therefore baked into the graph, so it MUST be part of the key.
6. On key miss: allocate static buffers `sx=torch.empty_like(x).contiguous()` and `torch.empty_like(t).contiguous()` for conv1_weight, norm1_weight, norm1_bias, conv2_weight, norm2_weight, norm2_bias; copy the current tensors into them with `.copy_()`.
7. Warmup before capture: `s=torch.cuda.Stream(); s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream()); with torch.cuda.stream(s): run self._ext.fused_block(*statics, eps) 3 times; torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s); torch.cuda.synchronize()`. This is mandatory: it makes the cuDNN benchmark autotune pick and cache the plan for these exact chunk shapes (so no benchmarking/sync occurs during capture) and initialises the file-static lambdas / workspaces.
8. Lazily create one shared pool `if self._pool is None: self._pool = torch.cuda.graph_pool_handle()` and capture: `g=torch.cuda.CUDAGraph(); with torch.cuda.graph(g, pool=self._pool): out_s = self._ext.fused_block(*statics, eps)`. Store `(g, statics, out_s)` in `self._graphs[key]`.
9. Wrap steps 6-8 in try/except; on any exception record `self._graphs[key]=None` and permanently use the direct ext path for that key (no retry, no recapture).
10. Replay path (key hit, entry not None): `for dst,src in zip(statics, real_inputs): dst.copy_(src, non_blocking=True)`; then `g.replay()`; return `out_s` directly (no clone, no allocation in the replay path).
11. Capture exactly once per key; never recapture on a repeat call. Bound memory by capping `len(self._graphs)` at 8 entries (beyond that, use the direct ext path).
12. Do not allocate, resize, or call `.contiguous()` on anything in the replay path other than the fixed `copy_` calls; every intermediate (x_cl, y1, z, y2, part, scale, shift, out) stays inside the captured graph pool.
13. Verify after implementation that all four scored shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131) get their own captured graph and that none regresses versus the current speedups.

Evidence:
Numeric: no kernel is near any roofline — nchw2nhwc sm__throughput 15.14% with gpu__dram_throughput 31.63%; gn_silu_res_t 22.17% SM / 34.88% DRAM; the highest DRAM anywhere is gn_partial at 55.42%. gn_finalize_kernel runs 6944 ns with sm__cycles_active 2094.82 of 7530.23 elapsed cycles (72% of its duration is launch/tail latency, not work) and launch__waves_per_multiprocessor 0.04, yet it is launched 96 times for 284 us. Machine-check key metric kernel_launch_count = 336 (598 launches total in the forward pass) for a forward that is only 1.419 ms on the profiled shape, i.e. host launch/dispatch cost is a first-order term, and it hits the smallest shape hardest (2x256x64x64 has the worst speedup, 1.3342x). Section analysis: gn_finalize SOLBottleneck states 'This kernel grid is too small to fill the available resources on this device, resulting in only 0.04 full waves across all SMs', and gn_partial reports 'only 0.56 full waves' — both are launch/occupancy-latency statements, not bandwidth ones. Ruled out (secondary): DRAM-bandwidth saturation. Bottleneck identified:
Host-side launch/dispatch latency between many tiny kernels: 502 launches per forward, no kernel near roofline (max DRAM 55.85%, SM 15.47%), and gn_finalize spends 72% of its elapsed cycles idle (2090.96 active of 7485.89 elapsed, 0.04 waves/SM).

Optimisation method:
Re-apply CUDA-Graph capture, but ONLY over the address-stable interior (conv1, K2/K3, K4, conv2, K2/K3) using pre-allocated scratch. K1 and K5 stay outside the graph and read/write the real x/out pointers, so the fatal per-call 2x67 MB static-input copy of Attempt #1 disappears; only the 4.7 MB weights are copied.

Method name:
CUDA_Graph_Capture_Replay_StaticBuffers

Modification plan:
1. In the CUDA extension, split `fused_block` into four exported entry points that share the existing math verbatim: (a) `plan_chunk(N,H,W)->int64` containing today's chunk selection (target_live 40 MB, snap-down to a divisor of N, chunk*HW>=16384 guard, chunk=N if whole batch fits) and the nc/ppc/nchunks/M derivation; (b) `k1_chunk(x, off, x_cl)` launching nchw2nhwc_kernel with the existing t_blk(32,8)/t_grd((HW+31)/32, C/32, chunk); (c) `interior(x_cl, w1c, w2c, n1w, n1b, n2w, n2b, eps, part, scale, shift, z, nchunks, ppc, M)` running conv1 -> gn_partial -> gn_finalize -> gn_silu(->z) -> conv2 -> gn_partial -> gn_finalize and RETURNING y2; (d) `k5_chunk(y2, x, off, scale, shift, out)` launching gn_silu_res_t_kernel. Keep every kernel body, block size, grid shape and the `cudnn_conv_dispatch(..., benchmark=true, deterministic=false, allow_tf32=true)` calls unchanged so cudnn_algo_autotune stays alive.
2. Keep the L2-resident chunk loop alive: the loop over `off` now lives in ModelNew.forward and still calls k1_chunk/replay/k5_chunk once per chunk with ONE reused scratch set.
3. In ModelNew.__init__ add `self._state = {}` (cap 8 entries).
4. Key = (tuple(x.shape), x.dtype, x.device.index, float(eps)); eps and all chunk-derived scalars are baked into the graph, so both must be in the key.
5. On key miss: chunk = ext.plan_chunk(...); allocate ONCE `x_cl` and `z` as empty({chunk,C,H,W}, channels_last), `part` ({chunk*32*nchunks,2}, float64), `scale`/`shift` ({chunk,256}); allocate static weight buffers `w1c = conv1_weight.contiguous(channels_last).clone()`, `w2c` likewise, and static `n1w,n1b,n2w,n2b` (256 floats each).
6. Warmup BEFORE capture on a side stream: `s=torch.cuda.Stream(); s.wait_stream(current); with torch.cuda.stream(s): ext.interior(...) x3; current.wait_stream(s); torch.cuda.synchronize()`. This is mandatory so cuDNN benchmark autotune selects and caches the plan for the chunk shape and no benchmarking/sync occurs during capture.
7. Set the persisting-L2 access-policy window on the capture stream BEFORE `torch.cuda.graph(...)` and leave it set (do NOT set/reset it inside capture), so captured nodes inherit it and l2_resident_batch_blocking keeps its window.
8. Capture: `pool = torch.cuda.graph_pool_handle()` fresh PER KEY (do not share one pool across keys, unlike Attempt #1); `g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph(); with torch.cuda.graph(g, pool=pool): y2_s = ext.interior(...)`. Store (g, pool, chunk, x_cl, z, part, scale, shift, w1c, w2c, n1w, n1b, n2w, n2b, y2_s).
9. Steady-state forward (no dynamic allocation except the output): copy ONLY the small parameters into their static buffers (`w1c.copy_(conv1_weight.to(memory_format=channels_last))`, `w2c` likewise, and the four 256-element norm tensors) — ~4.7 MB total; NEVER copy x. Allocate `out = torch.empty_like(x)` (fresh NCHW, no aliasing), then `for off in range(0, N, chunk): ext.k1_chunk(x, off, x_cl); g.replay(); ext.k5_chunk(y2_s, x, off, scale, shift, out)`; return out.
10. Wrap steps 5-8 in try/except; on any failure store None for the key and permanently use the existing monolithic `fused_block` path; keep the Python reference fallback for non-256-channel/dtype cases.
11. Verify on all four scored shapes that a graph is captured, that nsys still shows the autotuned sm90_xmma_fprop engine inside the replay, and that none of 1.9025/1.3342/1.8229/2.0030 regresses.

Evidence:
Base numbers: kernel_launch_count=336 (502 total launches/forward per the nsys table) for a 1.419 ms forward; gn_finalize_kernel sm__cycles_active 2090.96 vs sm__cycles_elapsed 7485.89 (72% of its duration is launch/tail latency) with launch__waves_per_multiprocessor 0.04, launched 96 times for 281 us; nchw2nhwc sm__throughput 15.47% with dram 33.01%. Section analysis (gn_partial SOLBottleneck): 'This kernel grid is too small to fill the available resources on this device, resulting in only 0.56 full waves across all SMs' — a launch/occupancy-latency statement. Ruled out (secondary): DRAM saturation — the heaviest custom kernel gn_silu_res_t sits at gpu__dram_throughput 35.66% and lts__throughput 34.37%, and even the best case gn_partial is 55.85%, far from the >80% that would make byte-reduction the #1 lever. Also ruled out: occupancy/registers — achieved warps 82.9%/84.02%/76.7% with only 28-32 regs/thread. History classification: Previous Attempt #1 is case (b) — the mechanism engaged but a specific defect negated it. Deciding metrics: no custom kernel got faster (nchw2nhwc 42944 vs 42816 ns) while gn_silu_res_t sm__cycles_active ROSE 54651->60813 (+11.3%) and all four shapes regressed uniformly (-9.0% to -13.8%), including the smallest shape that should have gained most from launch elimination — i.e. the added mandatory 2 x per_sample_bytes static-input copy of x (134 MB on the mid shape) plus the deliberately skipped persisting-L2 window ate the launch saving. Concrete delta vs Attempt #1: capture only the interior (conv1..gn_finalize2) over pre-allocated scratch, keep K1/K5 outside the graph so the real x and a freshly allocated out are used directly (zero x copies; only ~4.7 MB of weights are copied), keep the persisting-L2 window set across capture instead of disabling it, and use a per-key graph pool instead of one shared pool. This composes with both carried mechanisms: the chunk loop and its single scratch set remain (l2_resident_batch_blocking), and the warmup-before-capture locks the benchmarked plan (cudnn_algo_autotune).

Expected metric change:
(1) Host launches per forward drop from 9/chunk to 2/chunk + 1 graph replay (~7/9 of custom+conv launches removed), so total nsys launch count and end-to-end time fall, most on 2x256x64x64. (2) Per-kernel sm__cycles_active/sm__cycles_elapsed ratio rises (gn_finalize currently 2090.96/7485.89) as the inter-kernel bubble shrinks. (3) Anti-regression, bytes: DRAM bytes per forward must be UNCHANGED — no x copy is added, so gn_silu_res_t gpu__dram_throughput must stay near 35.66% and its sm__cycles_active must NOT exceed 54651 (it hit 60813 in Attempt #1); if it rises again, the static-buffer addressing, not launch overhead, is the cost and the change must be reverted. (4) Anti-regression, carried mechanisms: 'L2 Persisting Size' must still read 32768000 B and lts__t_sector_hit_rate for gn_silu must stay >=52.02% (l2_resident_batch_blocking alive); nsys must still show the autotuned sm90_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm ... nhwc engine, not an sm80/default plan (cudnn_algo_autotune alive); the profile must still show one nchw2nhwc and one gn_silu_res_t launch per chunk (chunk loop not collapsed). (5) Registers/thread (28-32), shared mem/block (5248 B) and achieved occupancy (82.9%) must not move. (6) Per-shape speedups must all be >= 1.9025 / 1.3342 / 1.8229 / 2.0030; any shape below reverts the change.

Bottleneck identified:
K1 (nchw2nhwc) + K5 (gn_silu_res_t) are pure layout-transform passes holding 46% of forward GPU time at only 31.5%/35.5% DRAM peak, and they are serialized against the compute-bound cuDNN TF32 convs by the single-stream, CPU-driven chunk loop outside the captured graph.

Optimisation method:
Extend CUDA-graph capture from the 'interior' only to the WHOLE forward (K1 + convs/GN + K5, all chunks) with static input/output buffers, capturing a two-stream, double-buffered chunk pipeline so the memory-bound transposes of chunk c+1 overlap the compute-bound convs of chunk c.

Method name:
CUDA_Graph_Capture_Replay_StaticBuffers

Modification plan:
1. Keep cuDNN autotune (benchmark=true, NHWC TF32) and the L2-resident chunk loop; both must survive. Capture stays once per (shape,dtype,device,eps) key with the existing 8-entry state cache.
2. In plan_chunk, halve `target_live` from 40MB to 20MB (two chunk working sets now live concurrently, so total L2 footprint is unchanged) and relax the conv-efficiency guard from `chunk*HW < 16384` to `chunk*HW < 8192`; keep the snap-to-divisor-of-N logic. Also return NC = N/chunk.
3. Allocate TWO static buffer sets indexed by parity p∈{0,1}: x_cl[p], z[p], part[p], scale[p], shift[p] (channels_last for x_cl/z). Additionally allocate static_x = empty(N,C,H,W contiguous) and static_out = empty(N,C,H,W contiguous). Keep static weight copies w1c,w2c,n1w,n1b,n2w,n2b.
4. Add a C++ entry `chunk_pipeline(p, off, ...)` that enqueues, on the CURRENT stream only: K1 reading static_x at element offset off*C*HW into x_cl[p]; conv1; gn_partial; gn_finalize; gn_silu into z[p]; conv2; gn_partial; gn_finalize; then K5 reading y2 + static_x at off and writing static_out at off. No cudaStreamSynchronize / no cudaMemcpy inside.
5. Warmup BEFORE capture: create side streams s0,s1; on each stream run chunk_pipeline(p, 0, ...) three times (locks the cuDNN plan and pre-populates allocator blocks per stream), then torch.cuda.synchronize().
6. Capture: pool = graph_pool_handle(); with torch.cuda.graph(g, pool=pool, stream=cap_s): first `s0.wait_stream(cap_s); s1.wait_stream(cap_s)`; then `for c in range(NC): with torch.cuda.stream(s[c%2]): ext.chunk_pipeline(c%2, c*chunk, ...)`; finally `cap_s.wait_stream(s0); cap_s.wait_stream(s1)`. This bakes a fork/join DAG so chunks c and c+1 (different parity, no shared buffer) run concurrently while chunks c and c+2 (same stream) serialize correctly.
7. Hazard check to state in code comments: every per-chunk buffer is parity-private; y1/y2 are allocated by cuDNN into the graph pool and are freed/reused only on their own capture stream, so no cross-stream aliasing. Call set_l2_window(z[0]) on cap_s, s0 and s1 before capture (keeps the L2-blocking mechanism).
8. forward(): copy the 6 parameter tensors into their static clones; `static_x.copy_(x_contig)` on the ambient stream; `g.replay()`; then `out = torch.empty_like(static_x); out.copy_(static_out)` and return out (never return the static buffer, to avoid aliasing across calls). No Python-side chunk loop, no per-call allocation inside the replay path, no recapture.
9. Keep K1/K5 kernel bodies, block shapes (32,8) and grids ((HW+31)/32, C/32, chunk) unchanged, including the `p < HW` bounds guard so the awkward 131x131 (HW=17161) shape stays correct.
10. Wrap _build in try/except; on capture failure fall back to the current single-stream interior-graph path, and on that failure to fused_block, so correctness never depends on multi-stream capture succeeding.

Evidence:
nsys: gn_silu_res_t_kernel 24.2% (2394us) + nchw2nhwc_kernel 21.8% (2150us) = 46% of forward GPU time, while the sm90_xmma TF32 conv family sums to ~36%; the two transposes run at gpu__dram_throughput 31.51% and 35.47% of peak with sm__throughput only 15.12% and 22.37%, i.e. they leave both the DRAM and the SM math pipes idle and are ideal overlap partners for the convs. Section analysis (SpeedOfLight, nchw2nhwc): 'low compute throughput and memory bandwidth utilization ... below 60.0% of peak typically indicate latency issues', and WarpStateStats reports 66.1%/75.1% of warp cycles in long_scoreboard — pure load-latency, not work. Ruled out as #1: occupancy/register pressure — sm__warps_active is 85.84% and 88.41% of peak with only 28/31 registers per thread and 0.0 divergent branches, so more warps per SM cannot be the fix; the fix is putting independent conv work on the machine at the same time. Ruled out too: gn_finalize (1.46% SM throughput, 0.04 waves) is negligible in the timeline.

Expected metric change:
gpu__dram_throughput.avg.pct_of_peak during the K1/K5 phases ↑ (31.5/35.5% → >50% as they now share the timeline with compute-bound convs); sm__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak over the fused region ↑ (convs no longer idle-wait behind transposes); end-to-end forward time ↓ on the 8x256x64x128, 4x256x256x256 (NC≥2, real overlap) and ↓ on 2x256x64x64 / 1x256x131x131 through CPU-side launch elimination (per-forward CPU enqueues drop from 3*NC+8 to 1 replay + 8 copies). Anti-regression: (a) the two added full-tensor copies (static_x in, static_out out) add ~270MB traffic ≈6% — the measured speedup must exceed this or revert; (b) L2 blocking must not be lost: target_live halved so the concurrent live footprint stays ≈40MB, watch lts__t_sector_hit_rate on gn_partial not falling below its current 7.6%/51.8% band; (c) cuDNN autotune must stay in effect — if `convertTensor_kernel` or the sm80 nchw fprop kernel reappears in the timeline the NHWC/TF32 plan was lost; (d) K1/K5 register (28/31) and shared-memory (5248B) usage must stay identical since the kernel bodies are untouched; (e) graph capture count must remain 1 per shape key (no recapture per call).
pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
S4 launch/structure: forward re-issues ~190 kernels per call from a Python chunk loop (K1 + graph replay + K5 per chunk); only the 'interior' is graph-captured, so K1/K5 and every chunk boundary pay CPU launch/enqueue latency while each kernel runs at only 15-36% of peak.

Optimisation method:
Extend the CUDA-graph capture to the WHOLE forward (all chunks, K1..K5) in a SINGLE stream by making K1/K5 read the caller's x/out base addresses from a static device pointer buffer (pointer indirection) instead of baking pointers into kernel params. No full-tensor static copies, no chunk-size change.

Method name:
CUDA_Graph_Capture_Replay_StaticBuffers

Modification plan:
1. DELTA vs Previous Attempt #1: keep plan_chunk EXACTLY as-is (target_live 40MB, conv-guard chunk*HW<16384, snap-to-divisor) — do NOT halve it; and use ONE stream inside capture (no double-buffered parity buffers). This preserves chunk=2 for 8x256x64x128 so K1/K5 grids stay (256,8,2)=4096 blocks and gn_partial keeps 0.56 waves/SM.
2. DELTA #2: eliminate the two full-tensor static copies attempt #1 used. Add a per-key static device buffer `ptrbuf = torch::empty({2}, opts.dtype(kLong))` holding [x_base_ptr, out_base_ptr], plus a once-allocated pinned host staging buffer (cudaHostAlloc, 16 bytes).
3. Change `nchw2nhwc_kernel` signature to `(const float* const* srcpp, long elem_off, float* dst, int HW)`; first statement: `const float* s0 = *srcpp + elem_off;` then `const float* s = s0 + (size_t)n*CC*HW;`. Keep the body, the (32,8) block, the shared tile[32][33], and the `p < HW` guard unchanged.
4. Change `gn_silu_res_t_kernel` signature to `(const float* y, const float* const* xresp, long elem_off, const float* scale, const float* shift, float* const* outp, int HW)`; load `const float* xres = *xresp + elem_off;` and `float* out = *outp + elem_off;` once at kernel entry (uniform 8-byte loads, broadcast from L2). Keep grid/block, tile, and `p < HW` guard unchanged.
5. Add C++ `set_io_ptrs(torch::Tensor ptrbuf, torch::Tensor x, torch::Tensor out)`: write x.data_ptr()/out.data_ptr() into the pinned host buffer and `cudaMemcpyAsync(ptrbuf.data_ptr(), host, 16, H2D, current_stream)`. This runs OUTSIDE the graph, before replay.
6. Add C++ `full_pipeline(ptrbuf, w1c, w2c, n1w, n1b, n2w, n2b, eps, part, scale, shift, x_cl, z, nchunks, ppc, M, N, chunk, C, H, W)` that enqueues, on the CURRENT stream only, for off = 0, chunk, 2*chunk, ...: K1(ptrbuf, off*C*HW) -> cudnn conv1 (benchmark=true, TF32, NHWC) -> gn_partial -> gn_finalize -> gn_silu -> cudnn conv2 -> gn_partial -> gn_finalize -> K5(y2, ptrbuf, off*C*HW). No syncs, no cudaMalloc calls of our own inside.
7. In _build: allocate x_cl, z, part, scale, shift once (single set, channels_last for x_cl/z); keep static weight clones; call set_l2_window(z) on the capture stream when chunk<N.
8. Warmup: run `full_pipeline` 3x on a side stream, then torch.cuda.synchronize(), to lock the cuDNN plans and pre-populate allocator blocks before capture.
9. Capture once per (shape,dtype,device,eps) key with a fresh graph_pool_handle(): `with torch.cuda.graph(g, pool=pool, stream=cap_s): ext.full_pipeline(...)`. Keep the 8-entry state cache and the try/except fallback to fused_block.
10. forward(): copy the 6 parameter tensors into their static clones; `out = torch.empty(xc.shape, ...)`; `ext.set_io_ptrs(ptrbuf, xc, out)`; `g.replay()`; return out. Delete the Python chunk loop and the k1_chunk/k5_chunk Python calls.
11. Verify y1/y2 conv outputs are allocated/freed inside the capture per chunk so the graph pool reuses one pair of buffers across chunks (footprint must not scale with N/chunk).

Evidence:
Failure class for Previous Attempt #1 = (b), mechanism never engaged: its expected_metric_change predicted K1/K5 dram_throughput 31.5/35.5% -> >50%, but the measured rejected profile shows nchw2nhwc gpu__dram_throughput 31.48% and gn_silu_res_t 35.12% — essentially unchanged, i.e. no conv/transpose overlap ever materialised. It also BROKE a base mechanism: halving target_live cut chunk 2->1, so gn_partial grid fell from (256,2) to (256,1), waves_per_multiprocessor 0.56->0.28 and achieved occupancy 51.08%->25.89%, and it added two full-tensor copies. My plan therefore composes instead of replacing: same chunk sizing, same single stream, pointer indirection instead of static_x/static_out copies. Numeric evidence for the target: nsys shows gn_silu_res_t 26.2% (2667us) + nchw2nhwc 21.1% (2145us) = 47.3% of forward GPU time across 48+48 launches, with sm__throughput only 15.88%/22.70% and dram 32.89%/35.45% of peak — kernels that are neither compute- nor bandwidth-saturated, i.e. latency/serialisation bound; total forward launch count is 190. Section analysis (SpeedOfLight, nchw2nhwc): 'low compute throughput and memory bandwidth utilization ... below 60.0% of peak typically indicate latency issues.' Ruled out as #1: occupancy/register pressure — sm__warps_active 82.95% (K1) and 84.66% (K5) of peak with only 28/31 registers per thread and smsp__sass_branch_targets_threads_divergent 0.0, so adding warps or cutting registers cannot be the fix.

Expected metric change:
(1) Per-forward CPU-side kernel enqueues drop from ~190 to 1 graph replay + 1 16-byte H2D copy + 6 small parameter copies -> end-to-end forward time down, biggest on the launch-bound 2x256x64x64 shape. (2) Inter-kernel gap time collapses: sm__cycles_elapsed/sm__cycles_active ratio for nchw2nhwc improves from 46862/31653 (1.48) toward ~1.1, and gn_silu_res_t from 69469/57092 toward ~1.05. Anti-regression constraints: (a) K1/K5 must keep launch__grid_size 4096, launch__block_size 256, launch__registers_per_thread 28/31 and launch__shared_mem_per_block 5248 — the kernel bodies gain only one uniform pointer load; (b) l2_resident_batch_blocking must stay intact: gn_partial launch__waves_per_multiprocessor must remain 0.56 (not 0.28) and its achieved occupancy >=51%, and lts__t_sector_hit_rate on gn_silu must stay ~51%; (c) cudnn_algo_autotune must stay in effect — sm90_xmma_fprop_implicit_gemm_*_nhwckrsc_nhwc engines must remain in the timeline with no reappearance of convertTensor_kernel or the sm80 nchw fprop kernel; (d) total DRAM bytes must NOT increase — no static_x/static_out full-tensor copies are added (this is the specific metric that would expose a regression to attempt #1's design); (e) graph capture count stays 1 per shape key, and the awkward 1x256x131x131 shape must stay correct via the untouched p<HW guards.

Extend the CUDA-graph capture to the WHOLE forward (all chunks, K1..K5) in a SINGLE stream by making K1/K5 read the caller's x/out base addresses from a static device pointer buffer (pointer indirection) instead of baking pointers into kernel params. No full-tensor static copies, no chunk-size change.

Method name:
CUDA_Graph_Capture_Replay_StaticBuffers

Modification plan:
1. DELTA vs Previous Attempt #1: keep plan_chunk EXACTLY as-is (target_live 40MB, conv-guard chunk*HW<16384, snap-to-divisor) — do NOT halve it; and use ONE stream inside capture (no double-buffered parity buffers). This preserves chunk=2 for 8x256x64x128 so K1/K5 grids stay (256,8,2)=4096 blocks and gn_partial keeps 0.56 waves/SM.
2. DELTA #2: eliminate the two full-tensor static copies attempt #1 used. Add a per-key static device buffer `ptrbuf = torch::empty({2}, opts.dtype(kLong))` holding [x_base_ptr, out_base_ptr], plus a once-allocated pinned host staging buffer (cudaHostAlloc, 16 bytes).
3. Change `nchw2nhwc_kernel` signature to `(const float* const* srcpp, long elem_off, float* dst, int HW)`; first statement: `const float* s0 = *srcpp + elem_off;` then `const float* s = s0 + (size_t)n*CC*HW;`. 4.
