Bottleneck identified:
Not per-kernel bandwidth: the forward issues 688 kernel launches (336 custom + cuDNN/convertTensor) per call, many microscopic (gn_finalize 3.2us, 0.03 waves/SM, 1.79% DRAM). Launch/dispatch gaps and CPU-side scheduling dominate the non-conv 30% of time, worst on the small shapes.

Optimisation method:
Capture the entire ModelNew.forward (weight relayout + 5 custom kernels + both cuDNN convs, incl. the two-stream fork/join) once per input shape into a torch.cuda.CUDAGraph over static input/output buffers, then replay: one graph launch replaces ~172 launches per call, removing per-launch dispatch and inter-kernel gaps.

Method name:
CUDA_Graph_Capture_Replay_StaticBuffers

Modification plan:
1. In ModelNew.__init__ add: self._graphs = {} (cache), self._pool = None (shared torch.cuda.graph_pool_handle(), created lazily), self._graph_ok = True (sticky disable on failure).
2. Build a cache key in forward: (tuple(x.shape), x.dtype, x.device.index, tuple(conv1_weight.shape), tuple(conv2_weight.shape), eps_f). This keys all four benchmark shapes separately so each gets its own graph; no recapture for a repeated shape.
3. On cache miss and self._graph_ok and x.is_cuda and use_fast: call self._capture(key, x, w1, g1, b1, w2, g2, b2, eps_f) inside try/except; on any exception set self._graph_ok=False and fall through to today's eager `self._ext.fused_resblock(...)` path.
4. _capture: allocate static buffers with fixed addresses — static_x = torch.empty_like(x).contiguous(); static_w1, static_g1, static_b1, static_w2, static_g2, static_b2 = torch.empty_like(t).contiguous() for each parameter tensor; copy the current values into all of them with .copy_() BEFORE warmup.
5. Warmup (mandatory, outside capture) on a dedicated side stream: s = torch.cuda.Stream(); s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream()); with torch.cuda.stream(s): run self._cl_weight(static_w1/static_w2) and self._ext.fused_resblock(static_x, w1c, static_g1, static_b1, w2c, static_g2, static_b2, eps_f) three times; torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s); torch.cuda.synchronize(). This forces cuDNN benchmark autotuning, workspace allocation, the channels_last weight relayout into self._cl_cache (keyed by id(static_w*), which is now stable), and the one-time init_cudnn_flags — so the capture region performs NO algorithm search.
6. Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound epilogue chain]. The cutlass TF32 fprop mainloop holds 69.1% but is already at vendor SOL (~103 TFLOPS on 4x256x256x256 vs 104.8 TF32 peak) → default-keep. The addressable 31% is the GN/layout chain (nchw2nhwc, gn_partial x2, gn_silu_inplace, gn_silu_res), all DRAM-bound with ~77-95% long-scoreboard stalls and near-zero L2 reuse although each chunk buffer is touched 3-4 times.

Optimisation method:
L2 cache-residency control (reuse, not new math): pin the per-chunk activation buffer (conv output y / y2, 8-17 MB on three of four shapes) in L2 with a cudaAccessPolicyWindow (hitProp=persisting, missProp=streaming) on the owning stream, plus persist-aware chunk sizing. The stats pass, the normalize+SiLU pass and conv2's input read then hit L2 instead of DRAM. Justified by E1: gn_partial lts__t_sector_hit_rate=1.59% and gn_silu_res=1.96% while both sit at 73-87% DRAM peak with 94.9%/78.0% long-scoreboard stalls.

Method name:

1. 2. EXACT CODE ACTION (window helpers): add `static void set_persist(cudaStream_t s, const void* p, size_t bytes, int nact){ if(!g_persist_max) return; size_t budget=g_persist_max/(size_t)std::max(1,nact); size_t win=std::min(bytes, g_win_max?g_win_max:bytes); float r=(float)budget/(float)win; if(r>1.f) r=1.f; if(r<0.25f){ clear_persist(s); return;} cudaStreamAttrValue v{}; v.accessPolicyWindow.base_ptr=(void*)p; v.accessPolicyWindow.num_bytes=win; v.accessPolicyWindow.hitRatio=r; v.accessPolicyWindow.hitProp=cudaAccessPropertyPersisting; v.accessPolicyWindow.missProp=cudaAccessPropertyStreaming; cudaStreamSetAttribute(s, cudaStreamAttributeAccessPolicyWindow, &v);} ` and `clear_persist(s)` identical but with `num_bytes=0, hitProp=missProp=cudaAccessPropertyNormal`. 3. In `run_chunk`, add parameter `int nact` (1 when nchunk==1, else 2). 9. Keep the residual tensor x, xn and out outside any window (normal policy) so they cannot evict the pinned activation.
10. Do not add CUDA-graph capture (history shows it regressed to 1.156x vs the 1.25 geomean baseline); this round is a single mechanism: L2 residency for the activation buffer.

pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[vendor-conv segment, launch/format-overhead bound] Hottest non-removable target is the cuDNN 3x3 conv segment (68% cutlass s1688fprop + ~13% other fprop engines) and its attached no-math companion `cudnn::engines_precompiled::convertTensor_kernel` (4.8%, 1470us, 232 launches ≈ 2 per conv, ~6.3us each ≈ filter-sized 2.36MB re-transform). The filter transform is loop-invariant yet re-executed every forward call.

Optimisation method:
Vendor conv invocation-plan caching + filter prepack: pick, once per input shape and cache, the (filter layout, cuDNN entry point, conv invocations per forward) combination by real cudaEvent timing, then reuse a pre-packed filter tensor on every subsequent call. This removes the per-call loop-invariant filter conversion (232 convertTensor launches, 4.8% of GPU time doing zero math) and lets cuDNN benchmark a wider engine set on larger per-call M, addressing the ~15% gap between measured conv time (9.38ms/iter) and TF32 roofline (7.94ms/iter).

Method name:
vendor_conv_plan_filter_prepack_cache

Modification plan:
1. HOT-PATH PREPACK (removes the loop-invariant work): in `run_conv`, delete the per-call `w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast)` / `w2.contiguous(ChannelsLast)` calls in `fused_resblock`; instead keep a static filter cache in the extension: `static std::unordered_map<const void*, std::pair<at::Tensor,at::Tensor>> g_wcache;` mapping the caller weight `data_ptr()` -> {w_channels_last, w_kcrs_contiguous}, both built ONCE and held alive. Pass a `const at::Tensor&` chosen by the cached plan into `at::cudnn_convolution`, so no filter re-materialisation or re-transform is requested per call.
2. PLAN STRUCT + CACHE: add `struct ConvPlan { int filt; /*0=CL,1=KCRS*/ int api; /*0=at::cudnn_convolution,1=at::conv2d*/ int nchunk; };` and `static std::map<std::array<int,5>, ConvPlan> g_plan;` keyed by (B,C,H,W,1). Guard with `std::mutex`. `run_conv(in,w,plan)` selects filter tensor and entry point from the plan; keep the existing try/catch fallback intact.
3. ONE-TIME AUTOTUNE (`pick_plan`): on cache miss, before any output is produced, allocate a scratch NHWC input `at::empty({cb,C,H,W}, opts.memory_format(ChannelsLast))` for each candidate `nchunk in {1,2,4}` (cb=B/nchunk, only when B%nchunk==0), and for each (filt,api) pair run 2 warmups + 5 timed iterations of the two convolutions back-to-back on a private stream with `at::cuda::CUDAEvent` start/stop; score = min elapsed * nchunk (total per-forward conv cost). Store the argmin in `g_plan`. Free scratch buffers. Cost is a few ms once per shape and is amortised over all benchmark iterations.
4. WIDEN ENGINE SEARCH (same mechanism, plan selection): in `init_cudnn_flags`, raise `setBenchmarkLimitCuDNN(10)` to 32 so cuDNN's benchmark mode evaluates more engines (e.g. 128x128/128x64 tiles) before the plan is frozen; keep `setBenchmarkCuDNN(true)` and `setAllowTF32CuDNN(true)`.
5. WIRE nchunk: replace the current hand-rolled chunk heuristic (`cb = B/4` loop) with `plan.nchunk`; keep `cb = B/plan.nchunk`, the two side streams, the event fork/join and `recordStream` bookkeeping exactly as today. Fewer, larger conv invocations => proportionally fewer per-call cuDNN fixed overheads (filter transforms scale with invocation count: 8/call -> 4 or 2/call).
6. NUMERICS INVARIANCE: keep `ppb`/`P` computed from the FULL batch (`calc_pix_per_block(HW,B)`) exactly as now, so GN reduction order is unchanged for any chosen nchunk; do not touch any custom kernel body, block size or grid shape.
7. SAFETY: the currently-shipped configuration (filt=CL, api=cudnn_convolution, nchunk=4 for B>=2 && B*HW>=32768, else 1) MUST be one of the autotune candidates, and selection is by measured time, so no shape can be slower than today. If the scratch allocation or timing throws, fall back to today's heuristic and mark the shape as `plan_ok=false`.
8. PYTHON SIDE: `_cl_weight` cache stays but only builds the channels_last copy once; do not add per-call `.contiguous()`; pass the raw weights plus the cached CL copies straight through.
9. VALIDATION: assert output equality vs the eager fallback on all four shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131); note H*W=17161 (odd) must still work since ppb/P logic is untouched.

Evidence:
nsys: `convertTensor_kernel` = 4.8% / 1470us / 232 launches, i.e. ~2 per conv at ~6.3us each — consistent with a 2.36MB filter read+write (4.7MB / 1.79TB/s = 2.6us), not with activation-sized traffic (a 67MB chunk would cost ~75us), so it is a per-call, loop-invariant filter re-transform performing no math. Root cause: the conv is re-invoked 2*nchunk (=8) times per forward and each invocation re-runs cuDNN's filter conversion; the transformed filter is identical every call. Refutation of the alternative 'the custom GN/layout chain is the bottleneck': that chain is only 11.3% of forward GPU time and already at DRAM SOL (gn_silu_res 86.61%, nchw2nhwc 84.02%, gn_silu_inplace 83.50% of peak DRAM), so even perfect optimisation there caps the round near 2%.

Expected metric change:
(1) `convertTensor_kernel` GPU time share 4.8% -> <1.5% and its launch count 232 -> <=1 per conv invocation (invocations themselves drop 8->4 or 2 per forward); (2) total forward kernel launches 688 -> <500, and cutlass fprop average per-launch efficiency rises (measured conv time per iteration 9.38ms -> <8.8ms vs 7.94ms TF32 roofline). Anti-regression: the shipped configuration is a candidate in the autotune and the winner is chosen by measured cudaEvent time, so per-shape speedup must not drop on any of the four shapes; all custom kernels keep identical grids/registers (gn_silu_res 27 regs, 86.6% DRAM) and identical numerics (ppb/P still derived from the full batch), so outputs stay bit-identical to the current candidate.

Section analysis (gn_finalize SOLBottleneck OPT) states 'This kernel grid is too small to fill the available resources on this device, resulting in only 0.03 full waves across all SMs.' Ruled-out secondary bottleneck: DRAM bandwidth of the big custom kernels — gn_silu_res_nchw already reaches 86.36% of peak DRAM and nchw2nhwc 75.42%, i.e. they are within ~15% of SOL and together are only 3.5%+3.0% of forward GPU time, so squeezing them caps the round at ~1%. Ruled out compute: sm__throughput.avg is 20.24% / 19.22% / 5.63%, far from any compute limit. The convolutions (69.3%) are vendor cuTLASS kernels we cannot beat, but a graph still removes their per-launch dispatch cost and all inter-kernel gaps across 688 launches, which is exactly where the small shape (2x256x64x64, only 1.12x today, ref 0.302 ms for 688 launches) loses.

Expected metric change:
End-to-end forward wall time ↓ (largest on the launch-bound 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 shapes); effective per-call kernel launch/dispatch count ↓ from ~688 to 1 graph launch; inter-kernel gap time ↓ so gn_finalize's elapsed/active cycle ratio (7,712/1,700) shrinks toward 1 and gpu busy% ↑. Anti-regression: per-kernel metrics must be unchanged (gn_silu_res_nchw DRAM 86.36%, registers/thread 27, occupancy 87.19% must not drop) since no kernel body or launch shape changes; replay must contain zero dynamic allocation and zero cuDNN autotuning (all moved to warmup); the shared graph pool must not blow up memory for the 4x256x256x256 shape (use one pool handle for all graphs); numerics must stay bit-identical (same reduction order, ppb/P computed from the full batch); any capture failure must silently fall back to today's eager path so no shape can regress.
pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM/latency-bound epilogue chain] Hottest non-removable *addressable* segment is the GroupNorm chain around the (already TF32-SOL) cuDNN conv: gn_partial (13.3us, 96 launches, DRAM 72%, L2 hit 1.5%, 92% long-scoreboard) re-reads the whole conv output that the apply kernel reads again microseconds later, and gn_finalize (3.3us, 0.03 waves/SM, DRAM 2%) is pure launch/latency on the critical path.

Optimisation method:
epilogue_fusion via one cooperative (grid-synchronised) persistent GroupNorm kernel per stage: phase1 partial moments -> grid.sync -> finalize (A,B) -> grid.sync -> apply(affine+SiLU[+residual+NHWC->NCHW]). This collapses gn_partial+gn_finalize+apply into a single launch, so the phase-2 re-read of the chunk (16-67MB) hits L2 instead of DRAM (current lts hit 1.5%), removes the 3.3us near-empty finalize from the dependency chain, and cuts custom launches per forward from 28 to 12.

Method name:
coop_gridsync_gn_fusion

Modification plan:
1. Add `#include <cooperative_groups.h>`; write ONE kernel `gn_fused_kernel(const float* y, const float* res, float* out, const float* gamma, const float* beta, float* partial, float* A, float* Bs, int HW, int C, int P, int ppb, int Bc, float eps, float invCount, int mode)` where mode=0 -> in-place apply on y (stage1), mode=1 -> apply+residual+NHWC->NCHW into out (stage2). It replaces the launch triple {gn_partial, gn_finalize, gn_silu_inplace|gn_silu_res_nchw}; the exact code action is: move the three existing kernel bodies into three phases of this kernel separated by `cg::this_grid().sync()`, and delete the two intermediate kernel launches from run_chunk.
2. Phase A (stats): grid-stride over work items w = n*P + pb (n<Bc, pb<P) using EXACTLY today's pixel ranges (pstart = pb*ppb, pend = min(pstart+ppb,HW)) and today's 256-thread/one-channel-per-thread accumulation + 8-lane shfl reduction, writing partial[n][pb][g][2]. Keeping P/ppb derived from the full batch preserves bit-identical reduction order.
3. `cg::this_grid().sync()`.
4. Phase B (finalize): grid-stride over ng = 0..Bc*G-1, one block per ng (128 threads), identical loop `for i=tid; i<P; i+=blockDim` + block_reduce2 -> mean/rstd -> A[n*C+c]=gamma*rstd, Bs=beta-mean*A. Deterministic (no float atomics), so stats match today exactly.
5. `cg::this_grid().sync()`.
6. Phase C (apply): mode 0 -> today's float4 in-place normalize+SiLU body, grid-stride over i in [0, Bc*HW*C/4). mode 1 -> today's 32x32 tiled body (shared 32x33 floats = 4.2KB, well under the 99KB/block limit), grid-stride over tile index t in [0, Bc * ceil(HW/32) * (C/32)), decoding n, p0, c0 from t so any HW (incl. odd 17161) is covered by the existing `if (p<HW)` guards.
7. Launch with cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel. Size the grid: query `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(&occ, gn_fused_kernel, 256, 0)` once (static), maxCoop = numSMs*occ; when nchunk>1 use maxCoop/2 so the two stream-chunks and the concurrent cuDNN conv can coexist without the driver having to serialise; grid = min(maxCoop_eff, max(P*Bc, Bc*G, tilesNeeded)). Block size 256 for both phases (finalize uses only the first 128 threads, guarded).
8. Fallback: if cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel returns any error (or occ==0), set a sticky `g_coop_ok=false` and call today's three-kernel path (keep gn_partial/gn_finalize/gn_silu_inplace/gn_silu_res_nchw kernels in the file untouched). Never spin-wait on a hand-rolled atomic barrier — co-residency must come from the cooperative launch API only.
9. Keep K1 nchw2nhwc, both cuDNN conv calls, the channels_last weight cache, the chunk planner and the two-stream fork/join exactly as today; only the two GN triples inside run_chunk change.
10. Register pressure: cap with `__launch_bounds__(256, 4)` so occupancy (and therefore the legal cooperative grid) stays >=4 blocks/SM; verify no local spills.
11. Correctness guards: partial buffer sized Bc*P*G*2 as today and fully written before the first sync (all P chunks covered by the grid-stride loop, so no unwritten tail for odd HW); A/Bs sized Bc*C.
12. Validate all four shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131) against the reference within atol 2.8e-3; if any shape regresses vs the current candidate, disable the fused path for that (B,HW) via the same sticky flag.

Evidence:
gn_partial: gpu__time_duration 13312ns, gpu__dram_throughput 72.06%, lts__t_sector_hit_rate 1.54%, l1tex hit 0.89%, long_scoreboard 91.71%, achieved occupancy 33% — it streams the whole conv output from DRAM with ~zero L2 reuse, then gn_silu_inplace (13664ns, DRAM 83.89%) streams the very same bytes again; gn_finalize adds 3296ns at 0.03 waves/SM and 2% DRAM purely as a launch bubble between them, 96 times. Root cause: the two-pass GroupNorm is split across three launches, so the second pass's reuse distance spans a full kernel boundary and the data is evicted. Refuted alternative — 'the conv mainloop is the target': mid shape needs 2*2*(8*8192)*256*2304 = 154.6 GFLOP, i.e. 1.48ms at the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak versus 1.761ms measured end-to-end, so the cutlass s1688fprop kernel is already at ~100% of vendor SOL and is default-keep.

Expected metric change:
lts__t_sector_hit_rate of the fused kernel's apply phase 1.5% -> >40% and its gpu__dram_throughput share falls while total non-conv GPU time drops (gn_partial 13.3us + gn_finalize 3.3us + apply 13.7us -> one kernel <20us); custom kernel launches per forward 28 -> 12 and total forward launches 688 -> <500, shrinking gn_finalize-style elapsed/active cycle gaps. Anti-regression: apply-phase DRAM throughput must stay >=80% of peak (no coalescing loss from the grid-stride remap); registers/thread <=40 with zero local spills; stats must stay bit-identical (same ppb/P, same partial ordering, no float atomics); if cooperative launch fails or occupancy <4 blocks/SM, fall back to today's three-kernel path so no shape (esp. B=1 131x131 and 2x64x64) can regress.

Bottleneck identified:
Not per-kernel bandwidth: the forward issues 688 kernel launches (336 custom + cuDNN/convertTensor) per call, many microscopic (gn_finalize 3.2us, 0.03 waves/SM, 1.79% DRAM). Launch/dispatch gaps and CPU-side scheduling dominate the non-conv 30% of time, worst on the small shapes.

Optimisation method:
Capture the entire ModelNew.forward (weight relayout + 5 custom kernels + both cuDNN convs, incl. the two-stream fork/join) once per input shape into a torch.cuda.CUDAGraph over static input/output buffers, then replay: one graph launch replaces ~172 launches per call, removing per-launch dispatch and inter-kernel gaps.

Method name:
CUDA_Graph_Capture_Replay_StaticBuffers

Modification plan:
1. In ModelNew.__init__ add: self._graphs = {} (cache), self._pool = None (shared torch.cuda.graph_pool_handle(), created lazily), self._graph_ok = True (sticky disable on failure).
2. Build a cache key in forward: (tuple(x.shape), x.dtype, x.device.index, tuple(conv1_weight.shape), tuple(conv2_weight.shape), eps_f). This keys all four benchmark shapes separately so each gets its own graph; no recapture for a repeated shape.
3. On cache miss and self._graph_ok and x.is_cuda and use_fast: call self._capture(key, x, w1, g1, b1, w2, g2, b2, eps_f) inside try/except; on any exception set self._graph_ok=False and fall through to today's eager `self._ext.fused_resblock(...)` path.
4. _capture: allocate static buffers with fixed addresses — static_x = torch.empty_like(x).contiguous(); static_w1, static_g1, static_b1, static_w2, static_g2, static_b2 = torch.empty_like(t).contiguous() for each parameter tensor; copy the current values into all of them with .copy_() BEFORE warmup.
5. Warmup (mandatory, outside capture) on a dedicated side stream: s = torch.cuda.Stream(); s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream()); with torch.cuda.stream(s): run self._cl_weight(static_w1/static_w2) and self._ext.fused_resblock(static_x, w1c, static_g1, static_b1, w2c, static_g2, static_b2, eps_f) three times; torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(s); torch.cuda.synchronize(). This forces cuDNN benchmark autotuning, workspace allocation, the channels_last weight relayout into self._cl_cache (keyed by id(static_w*), which is now stable), and the one-time init_cudnn_flags — so the capture region performs NO algorithm search.
6. Capture: if self._pool is None: self._pool = torch.cuda.graph_pool_handle(); g = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph(); with torch.cuda.graph(g, pool=self._pool): static_out = self._ext.fused_resblock(static_x, self._cl_weight(static_w1), static_g1, static_b1, self._cl_weight(static_w2), static_g2, static_b2, eps_f). Keep the returned static_out tensor alive in the cache entry (its storage lives in the graph pool and is address-stable across replays). Sharing one pool across the four shape-graphs bounds extra memory.
7. Multi-stream safety: the extension's fork/join (CUDAEvent record on main stream, block on the two pool side streams, events back to main) is capture-legal, but add a defensive retry — extend fused_resblock with a trailing `bool force_single_stream=false` argument that forces nchunk=1/cb=B; if the first capture throws, delete the graph and retry capture once with force_single_stream=true; if that also throws, set self._graph_ok=False.
8. Replay path (cache hit): static_x.copy_(x, non_blocking=True) and .copy_() the six parameter tensors into their static buffers (cheap: weights are 2.36 MB each, x-copy is the only sizeable one), then graph.replay(), then return static_out. No allocation, no .item(), no device query, no stream switch on this path.
9. eps handling stays as today (float(eps.item()) once per call before the key is built); eps is baked into the captured kernels, and since it is part of the cache key a different eps forces a fresh capture.
10. Keep every kernel body, block size, grid shape and numerics unchanged — this round only removes launch/dispatch overhead. Keep the existing fallback branches (non-CUDA, non-fp32, C!=256) routed to the eager PyTorch path untouched.
11. Do not modify get_inputs/get_init_inputs, do not move tensors across devices, and allocate static buffers on x.device.

Evidence:
Numerics: gn_finalize_kernel runs 3,200 ns with sm__cycles_active 1,700 vs sm__cycles_elapsed 7,712 (77% of the kernel window is ramp/idle), launch__waves_per_multiprocessor 0.03, dram_throughput 1.79%, achieved occupancy 7.54% — pure launch overhead, and it is launched 96 times. machine_check reports kernel_launch_count 336 and case LAUNCH_S4_CUDAGRAPH_FALLBACK; nsys shows 688 launches per forward. Section analysis (gn_finalize SOLBottleneck OPT) states 'This kernel grid is too small to fill the available resources on this device, resulting in only 0.03 full waves across all SMs.' Ruled-out secondary bottleneck: DRAM bandwidth of the big custom kernels — gn_silu_res_nchw already reaches 86.36% of peak DRAM and nchw2nhwc 75.42%, i.e. they are within ~15% of SOL and together are only 3.5%+3.0% of forward GPU time, so squeezing them caps the round at ~1%. Ruled out compute: sm__throughput.avg is 20.24% / 19.22% / 5.63%, far from any compute limit. The convolutions (69.3%) are vendor cuTLASS kernels we cannot beat, but a graph still removes their per-launch dispatch cost and all inter-kernel gaps across 688 launches, which is exactly where the small shape (2x256x64x64, only 1.12x today, ref 0.302 ms for 688 launches) loses.

Expected metric change:
End-to-end forward wall time ↓ (largest on the launch-bound 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 shapes); effective per-call kernel launch/dispatch count ↓ from ~688 to 1 graph launch; inter-kernel gap time ↓ so gn_finalize's elapsed/active cycle ratio (7,712/1,700) shrinks toward 1 and gpu busy% ↑. Anti-regression: per-kernel metrics must be unchanged (gn_silu_res_nchw DRAM 86.36%, registers/thread 27, occupancy 87.19% must not drop) since no kernel body or launch shape changes; replay must contain zero dynamic allocation and zero cuDNN autotuning (all moved to warmup); the shared graph pool must not blow up memory for the 4x256x256x256 shape (use one pool handle for all graphs); numerics must stay bit-identical (same reduction order, ppb/P computed from the full batch); any capture failure must silently fall back to today's eager path so no shape can regress.
pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[vendor-call/fixed-overhead bound] The conv segment dominates (cutlass s1688fprop 68.7%), but its attached no-math companion `cudnn::engines_precompiled::convertTensor_kernel` costs 4.9% / 1,453us over 232 launches (~2.4 per conv call, ~6.3us ≈ one 4.7MB filter re-transform). Because the batch is split into 4 chunks, every forward issues 8 conv calls, multiplying this loop-invariant per-call overhead 4x.

Optimisation method:
Vendor-call coalescing: halve the pipeline chunk count (nchunk 4 -> 2, cb = B/2) so each forward issues 4 instead of 8 cuDNN conv invocations, cutting the per-call convertTensor filter re-transforms ~2x and doubling the M dimension per conv (fewer tail waves), while still keeping two chunks on two streams so the DRAM-bound GN/layout kernels of one chunk overlap the conv of the other. No kernel body, grid or numeric change.

Method name:
conv_call_coalescing_chunk2

Modification plan:
1. (Exact code action) In `fused_resblock`, delete the current chunk planner block (`cb = std::max(1, B/4); while ((B % cb) != 0) --cb; nchunk = B/cb; if (nchunk > 4) {...}`) and replace it with a fixed 2-way split: `int nchunk = 1, cb = B; if (B >= 2 && (B % 2 == 0) && (long)B * (long)HW >= 32768L) { nchunk = 2; cb = B / 2; }`. This makes each forward issue exactly 2 conv calls per stage instead of 2*4, removing ~half of the 232 convertTensor launches.
2. (Exact code action) Leave `calc_pix_per_block(HW, B)` and `P = (HW+ppb-1)/ppb` computed from the FULL batch B exactly as today, so the GN reduction partitioning/order is bit-identical to the current candidate; only the per-chunk grid z-extent changes from cb=B/4 to cb=B/2 in `run_chunk` (grids already derive from the passed `Bc`).
3. Keep every kernel body unchanged: nchw2nhwc_kernel, gn_partial_kernel, gn_finalize_kernel, gn_silu_inplace_kernel, gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel keep identical block sizes (256/128), shared memory, register counts and math.
4. Keep the two-stream fork/join intact: with nchunk=2 the loop still alternates `side_streams[ci & 1]`, so chunk0 and chunk1 chains run concurrently and the DRAM-bound custom kernels of one chunk still hide behind the other chunk's cutlass conv.
5. Odd/awkward batches: if `B % 2 != 0` (B=1 for the 131x131 shape) or `B*HW < 32768` (B=2,64x64 shape) keep nchunk=1 — those shapes already run a single chunk today, so they are untouched (no regression path).
6. Keep the existing guard `if (nchunk > 1) { if (!xc.narrow(...).is_contiguous() || !out.narrow(...).is_contiguous()) { nchunk = 1; cb = B; } }` unchanged after the new planner.
7. Per-chunk temporaries (`xn`, `partial`, `A`, `Bs`, conv outputs) are now 2x larger each but there are half as many live chunks, so peak memory is unchanged; no allocator changes needed. Keep `rec_stream()` bookkeeping for `out`, `xc`, weights on both side streams.
8. cuDNN autotune: `benchmark=true` caches per (N,C,H,W) key; the new chunk batch (B/2) is a new key, so the first call re-benchmarks once per shape. Keep `init_cudnn_flags()` and the `at::cudnn_convolution` fast path with the existing try/catch fallback to `at::conv2d` untouched.
9. Optional safety valve (no extra mechanism): read env `VAE_NCHUNK` once (static) and, if set to 1/2/4, override the planner value; default 2. This makes A/B verification of the chunk granularity trivial without touching kernels.
10. Verification checklist before shipping: (a) outputs match reference within max_atol per shape on all four shapes; (b) nsys shows nchw2nhwc_kernel launches per forward drop 4 -> 2 and convertTensor_kernel launches per forward roughly halve; (c) cutlass s1688fprop launch count per forward drops 8 -> 4 with ~2x longer per-launch duration and no drop in achieved FLOP rate; (d) wall time must not regress on the 4x256x256x256 shape (B=4 -> cb=2) or the 8x256x64x128 shape (B=8 -> cb=4); if either regresses, set the default override to the previous 4-way split for that shape class via the `B*HW` threshold only (no other code change).
11. Do not touch get_inputs/get_init_inputs, do not move tensors across devices, keep the Python `_cl_weight` cache and the eager fallback branch exactly as-is.

Evidence:
convertTensor_kernel: 4.9% of forward GPU time, 1,453us over 232 launches, ~6.3us each; at ~1.5TB/s that is ~9.4MB moved per launch = filter-sized (2.36MB read + write) — i.e. no-math, loop-invariant work whose count scales with conv invocations. nchw2nhwc_kernel shows 48 launches for 12 profiled forwards => nchunk=4 => 8 conv calls/forward => ~19 convertTensor launches/forward. Root cause: batch chunking multiplies cuDNN's fixed per-call filter/format overhead by nchunk. Refutation of the alternative 'the custom GN/layout chain is the bottleneck': gn_silu_res_nchw is at 86.63% of peak DRAM, nchw2nhwc 84.22%, gn_silu_inplace 82.10% — <15% headroom on kernels holding only 9.9% of forward time (<1.5% total), and the cutlass mainloop itself is at ~100% of the TF32 roofline (154.6 GFLOP / 104.8 TFLOPS = 1.48ms vs 1.761ms measured end-to-end), so it is default-keep.

Expected metric change:
convertTensor_kernel GPU-time share 4.9% -> ~2.5% and its launch count per forward ~19 -> ~10; cutlass s1688fprop launches per forward 8 -> 4 with ~2x M per call (fewer tail waves, per-launch duration ~2x, aggregate conv time flat or slightly lower); total forward launches 688 -> ~450. Anti-regression: all custom kernels keep identical grids/registers/occupancy (gn_silu_res 27 regs, 86.6% DRAM; nchw2nhwc 26 regs, 84.2% DRAM) and identical numerics (ppb/P still from full batch, same reduction order); two-stream overlap must be preserved (nchunk stays >=2 whenever B is even and B*HW>=32768) so mid/large shapes must not lose the current conv/epilogue overlap; B=1 and B=2 small shapes stay on the untouched single-chunk path, so 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 speedups must be unchanged.

pairs.a_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound epilogue chain]. The cutlass TF32 fprop mainloop holds 69.1% but is already at vendor SOL (~103 TFLOPS on 4x256x256x256 vs 104.8 TF32 peak) → default-keep. The addressable 31% is the GN/layout chain (nchw2nhwc, gn_partial x2, gn_silu_inplace, gn_silu_res), all DRAM-bound with ~77-95% long-scoreboard stalls and near-zero L2 reuse although each chunk buffer is touched 3-4 times.

Optimisation method:
L2 cache-residency control (reuse, not new math): pin the per-chunk activation buffer (conv output y / y2, 8-17 MB on three of four shapes) in L2 with a cudaAccessPolicyWindow (hitProp=persisting, missProp=streaming) on the owning stream, plus persist-aware chunk sizing. The stats pass, the normalize+SiLU pass and conv2's input read then hit L2 instead of DRAM. Justified by E1: gn_partial lts__t_sector_hit_rate=1.59% and gn_silu_res=1.96% while both sit at 73-87% DRAM peak with 94.9%/78.0% long-scoreboard stalls.

Method name:
l2_persist_window_reuse

Modification plan:
1. EXACT CODE ACTION (setup): add `static size_t g_persist_max=0, g_win_max=0;` and `static void init_l2_persist(){ cudaDeviceProp p; int d; cudaGetDevice(&d); if(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&p,d)==cudaSuccess){ g_persist_max=p.persistingL2CacheMaxSize; g_win_max=p.accessPolicyMaxWindowSize; if(g_persist_max) cudaDeviceSetLimit(cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize, g_persist_max);} }` and call it inside the existing `init_cudnn_flags()` once-lambda (single global init, no per-call cost).
2. EXACT CODE ACTION (window helpers): add `static void set_persist(cudaStream_t s, const void* p, size_t bytes, int nact){ if(!g_persist_max) return; size_t budget=g_persist_max/(size_t)std::max(1,nact); size_t win=std::min(bytes, g_win_max?g_win_max:bytes); float r=(float)budget/(float)win; if(r>1.f) r=1.f; if(r<0.25f){ clear_persist(s); return;} cudaStreamAttrValue v{}; v.accessPolicyWindow.base_ptr=(void*)p; v.accessPolicyWindow.num_bytes=win; v.accessPolicyWindow.hitRatio=r; v.accessPolicyWindow.hitProp=cudaAccessPropertyPersisting; v.accessPolicyWindow.missProp=cudaAccessPropertyStreaming; cudaStreamSetAttribute(s, cudaStreamAttributeAccessPolicyWindow, &v);} ` and `clear_persist(s)` identical but with `num_bytes=0, hitProp=missProp=cudaAccessPropertyNormal`. Ignore returned errors (feature optional).
3. In `run_chunk`, add parameter `int nact` (1 when nchunk==1, else 2). Immediately after conv1 and its channels_last check: `set_persist(stream, y.data_ptr<float>(), (size_t)Bc*C*HW*4, nact);` and leave the window installed across gn_partial/gn_finalize/gn_silu_inplace AND conv2, so conv2's read of y is also served from L2.
4. After conv2 returns y2 (and its contiguity fix): `set_persist(stream, y2.data_ptr<float>(), (size_t)Bc*C*HW*4, nact);` (this replaces the y window) before the second `run_group_norm_stats` + `gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel`.
5. At the end of `run_chunk` call `clear_persist(stream)` only — never `cudaCtxResetPersistingL2Cache()` mid-run, since that would flush the sibling stream's pinned lines. Optionally call it once after the join in `fused_resblock`.
6. Persist-aware chunk planner: in the existing chunk block, after computing candidate `cb`, shrink it while `(size_t)cb*C*HW*4 > g_persist_max/2 && cb>1 && (B%(cb/2)==0)` → `cb/=2`, recompute `nchunk=B/cb`, cap `nchunk<=8`. This makes the mid shape (16.8 MB/chunk) and awkward shape fully resident; the small shape already is; the large shape keeps hitRatio-scaled partial residency.
7. Do NOT touch any kernel body, block/grid shape, ppb/P computation or reduction order — numerics stay bit-identical; only stream attributes and chunk count change.
8. Guard rails: if `g_persist_max==0` or any cuda API call fails, every helper is a no-op and behaviour is exactly today's; keep the existing eager/PyTorch fallbacks untouched.
9. Keep the residual tensor x, xn and out outside any window (normal policy) so they cannot evict the pinned activation.
10. Do not add CUDA-graph capture (history shows it regressed to 1.156x vs the 1.25 geomean baseline); this round is a single mechanism: L2 residency for the activation buffer.
11. Validate on all four shapes; if the large shape (4x256x256x256) regresses, tighten the `r<0.25f` skip threshold to 0.4f so it silently disables there.

Evidence:
gn_partial_kernel: lts__t_sector_hit_rate=1.59%, l1tex hit 0.89%, DRAM 73.31%, long_scoreboard 94.85% — it re-reads a 16.8 MB buffer conv1 wrote microseconds earlier and misses L2 almost entirely; gn_silu_res_nchw: lts hit 1.96%, DRAM 86.64%, 28.3 us (2.2%); gn_silu_inplace already shows 51.26% L2 hit, proving partial residency exists and is capacity/eviction limited. Root cause: two concurrent stream chains stream ~70-84 MB through L2, evicting the just-written activation before its 2-3 subsequent readers touch it. Refuted alternative: the conv mainloop (69.1%) is not fixable — 2*4*65536*256*2304*2 FLOP / ~6.0 ms ≈ 103 TFLOPS ≈ 100% of the 104.8 TF32 peak, and compute SM throughput of the custom kernels (5.8-23.6%) rules out a compute bound.

Expected metric change:
lts__t_sector_hit_rate: gn_partial 1.59% → >50%, gn_silu_res 1.96% → >40%; gpu__dram_throughput.avg for these kernels falls (traffic served by L2) while gpu__time_duration.avg drops (gn_partial 13.3 us → <9 us, gn_silu_res 28.3 us → <22 us) and smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard drops below 85%/70%. Anti-regression: conv (cutlass s1688fprop) per-launch duration must not rise >2% (missProp=streaming applies only inside the window); launch count, registers/thread, occupancy and output values must be unchanged (bit-identical, same ppb/P and reduction order); if the persist window cannot cover ≥25% of the chunk (large shape) the helper disables itself so no shape regresses.
pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[vendor-conv segment, launch/format-overhead bound] Hottest non-removable target is the cuDNN 3x3 conv segment (68% cutlass s1688fprop + ~13% other fprop engines) and its attached no-math companion `cudnn::engines_precompiled::convertTensor_kernel` (4.8%, 1470us, 232 launches ≈ 2 per conv, ~6.3us each ≈ filter-sized 2.36MB re-transform). The filter transform is loop-invariant yet re-executed every forward call.

Optimisation method:
Vendor conv invocation-plan caching + filter prepack: pick, once per input shape and cache, the (filter layout, cuDNN entry point, conv invocations per forward) combination by real cudaEvent timing, then reuse a pre-packed filter tensor on every subsequent call. This removes the per-call loop-invariant filter conversion (232 convertTensor launches, 4.8% of GPU time doing zero math) and lets cuDNN benchmark a wider engine set on larger per-call M, addressing the ~15% gap between measured conv time (9.38ms/iter) and TF32 roofline (7.94ms/iter).

Method name:
vendor_conv_plan_filter_prepack_cache

Modification plan:
1. HOT-PATH PREPACK (removes the loop-invariant work): in `run_conv`, delete the per-call `w1.contiguous(ChannelsLast)` / `w2.contiguous(ChannelsLast)` calls in `fused_resblock`; instead keep a static filter cache in the extension: `static std::unordered_map<const void*, std::pair<at::Tensor,at::Tensor>> g_wcache;` mapping the caller weight `data_ptr()` -> {w_channels_last, w_kcrs_contiguous}, both built ONCE and held alive. Pass a `const at::Tensor&` chosen by the cached plan into `at::cudnn_convolution`, so no filter re-materialisation or re-transform is requested per call.
2. PLAN STRUCT + CACHE: add `struct ConvPlan { int filt; /*0=CL,1=KCRS*/ int api; /*0=at::cudnn_convolution,1=at::conv2d*/ int nchunk; };` and `static std::map<std::array<int,5>, ConvPlan> g_plan;` keyed by (B,C,H,W,1). Guard with `std::mutex`. `run_conv(in,w,plan)` selects filter tensor and entry point from the plan; keep the existing try/catch fallback intact.
3. ONE-TIME AUTOTUNE (`pick_plan`): on cache miss, before any output is produced, allocate a scratch NHWC input `at::empty({cb,C,H,W}, opts.memory_format(ChannelsLast))` for each candidate `nchunk in {1,2,4}` (cb=B/nchunk, only when B%nchunk==0), and for each (filt,api) pair run 2 warmups + 5 timed iterations of the two convolutions back-to-back on a private stream with `at::cuda::CUDAEvent` start/stop; score = min elapsed * nchunk (total per-forward conv cost). Store the argmin in `g_plan`. Free scratch buffers. Cost is a few ms once per shape and is amortised over all benchmark iterations.
4. WIDEN ENGINE SEARCH (same mechanism, plan selection): in `init_cudnn_flags`, raise `setBenchmarkLimitCuDNN(10)` to 32 so cuDNN's benchmark mode evaluates more engines (e.g. 128x128/128x64 tiles) before the plan is frozen; keep `setBenchmarkCuDNN(true)` and `setAllowTF32CuDNN(true)`.
5. WIRE nchunk: replace the current hand-rolled chunk heuristic (`cb = B/4` loop) with `plan.nchunk`; keep `cb = B/plan.nchunk`, the two side streams, the event fork/join and `recordStream` bookkeeping exactly as today. Fewer, larger conv invocations => proportionally fewer per-call cuDNN fixed overheads (filter transforms scale with invocation count: 8/call -> 4 or 2/call).
6. NUMERICS INVARIANCE: keep `ppb`/`P` computed from the FULL batch (`calc_pix_per_block(HW,B)`) exactly as now, so GN reduction order is unchanged for any chosen nchunk; do not touch any custom kernel body, block size or grid shape.
7. SAFETY: the currently-shipped configuration (filt=CL, api=cudnn_convolution, nchunk=4 for B>=2 && B*HW>=32768, else 1) MUST be one of the autotune candidates, and selection is by measured time, so no shape can be slower than today. If the scratch allocation or timing throws, fall back to today's heuristic and mark the shape as `plan_ok=false`.
8. PYTHON SIDE: `_cl_weight` cache stays but only builds the channels_last copy once; do not add per-call `.contiguous()`; pass the raw weights plus the cached CL copies straight through.
9. VALIDATION: assert output equality vs the eager fallback on all four shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131); note H*W=17161 (odd) must still work since ppb/P logic is untouched.

Evidence:
nsys: `convertTensor_kernel` = 4.8% / 1470us / 232 launches, i.e. ~2 per conv at ~6.3us each — consistent with a 2.36MB filter read+write (4.7MB / 1.79TB/s = 2.6us), not with activation-sized traffic (a 67MB chunk would cost ~75us), so it is a per-call, loop-invariant filter re-transform performing no math. Root cause: the conv is re-invoked 2*nchunk (=8) times per forward and each invocation re-runs cuDNN's filter conversion; the transformed filter is identical every call. Refutation of the alternative 'the custom GN/layout chain is the bottleneck': that chain is only 11.3% of forward GPU time and already at DRAM SOL (gn_silu_res 86.61%, nchw2nhwc 84.02%, gn_silu_inplace 83.50% of peak DRAM), so even perfect optimisation there caps the round near 2%.

Expected metric change:
(1) `convertTensor_kernel` GPU time share 4.8% -> <1.5% and its launch count 232 -> <=1 per conv invocation (invocations themselves drop 8->4 or 2 per forward); (2) total forward kernel launches 688 -> <500, and cutlass fprop average per-launch efficiency rises (measured conv time per iteration 9.38ms -> <8.8ms vs 7.94ms TF32 roofline). Anti-regression: the shipped configuration is a candidate in the autotune and the winner is chosen by measured cudaEvent time, so per-shape speedup must not drop on any of the four shapes; all custom kernels keep identical grids/registers (gn_silu_res 27 regs, 86.6% DRAM) and identical numerics (ppb/P still derived from the full batch), so outputs stay bit-identical to the current candidate.

pairs.a_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[memory/DRAM-bound epilogue chain]. The cutlass TF32 fprop mainloop holds 69.1% but is already at vendor SOL (~103 TFLOPS on 4x256x256x256 vs 104.8 TF32 peak) → default-keep. The addressable 31% is the GN/layout chain (nchw2nhwc, gn_partial x2, gn_silu_inplace, gn_silu_res), all DRAM-bound with ~77-95% long-scoreboard stalls and near-zero L2 reuse although each chunk buffer is touched 3-4 times.

Optimisation method:
L2 cache-residency control (reuse, not new math): pin the per-chunk activation buffer (conv output y / y2, 8-17 MB on three of four shapes) in L2 with a cudaAccessPolicyWindow (hitProp=persisting, missProp=streaming) on the owning stream, plus persist-aware chunk sizing. The stats pass, the normalize+SiLU pass and conv2's input read then hit L2 instead of DRAM. Justified by E1: gn_partial lts__t_sector_hit_rate=1.59% and gn_silu_res=1.96% while both sit at 73-87% DRAM peak with 94.9%/78.0% long-scoreboard stalls.

Method name:
l2_persist_window_reuse

Modification plan:
1. EXACT CODE ACTION (setup): add `static size_t g_persist_max=0, g_win_max=0;` and `static void init_l2_persist(){ cudaDeviceProp p; int d; cudaGetDevice(&d); if(cudaGetDeviceProperties(&p,d)==cudaSuccess){ g_persist_max=p.persistingL2CacheMaxSize; g_win_max=p.accessPolicyMaxWindowSize; if(g_persist_max) cudaDeviceSetLimit(cudaLimitPersistingL2CacheSize, g_persist_max);} }` and call it inside the existing `init_cudnn_flags()` once-lambda (single global init, no per-call cost).
2. EXACT CODE ACTION (window helpers): add `static void set_persist(cudaStream_t s, const void* p, size_t bytes, int nact){ if(!g_persist_max) return; size_t budget=g_persist_max/(size_t)std::max(1,nact); size_t win=std::min(bytes, g_win_max?g_win_max:bytes); float r=(float)budget/(float)win; if(r>1.f) r=1.f; if(r<0.25f){ clear_persist(s); return;} cudaStreamAttrValue v{}; v.accessPolicyWindow.base_ptr=(void*)p; v.accessPolicyWindow.num_bytes=win; v.accessPolicyWindow.hitRatio=r; v.accessPolicyWindow.hitProp=cudaAccessPropertyPersisting; v.accessPolicyWindow.missProp=cudaAccessPropertyStreaming; cudaStreamSetAttribute(s, cudaStreamAttributeAccessPolicyWindow, &v);} ` and `clear_persist(s)` identical but with `num_bytes=0, hitProp=missProp=cudaAccessPropertyNormal`. Ignore returned errors (feature optional).
3. In `run_chunk`, add parameter `int nact` (1 when nchunk==1, else 2). Immediately after conv1 and its channels_last check: `set_persist(stream, y.data_ptr<float>(), (size_t)Bc*C*HW*4, nact);` and leave the window installed across gn_partial/gn_finalize/gn_silu_inplace AND conv2, so conv2's read of y is also served from L2.
4. After conv2 returns y2 (and its contiguity fix): `set_persist(stream, y2.data_ptr<float>(), (size_t)Bc*C*HW*4, nact);` (this replaces the y window) before the second `run_group_norm_stats` + `gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel`.
5. At the end of `run_chunk` call `clear_persist(stream)` only — never `cudaCtxResetPersistingL2Cache()` mid-run, since that would flush the sibling stream's pinned lines. Optionally call it once after the join in `fused_resblock`.
6. Persist-aware chunk planner: in the existing chunk block, after computing candidate `cb`, shrink it while `(size_t)cb*C*HW*4 > g_persist_max/2 && cb>1 && (B%(cb/2)==0)` → `cb/=2`, recompute `nchunk=B/cb`, cap `nchunk<=8`. This makes the mid shape (16.8 MB/chunk) and awkward shape fully resident; the small shape already is; the large shape keeps hitRatio-scaled partial residency.
7. Do NOT touch any kernel body, block/grid shape, ppb/P computation or reduction order — numerics stay bit-identical; only stream attributes and chunk count change.
8. Guard rails: if `g_persist_max==0` or any cuda API call fails, every helper is a no-op and behaviour is exactly today's; keep the existing eager/PyTorch fallbacks untouched.
9. Keep the residual tensor x, xn and out outside any window (normal policy) so they cannot evict the pinned activation.
10. Do not add CUDA-graph capture (history shows it regressed to 1.156x vs the 1.25 geomean baseline); this round is a single mechanism: L2 residency for the activation buffer.
11. Validate on all four shapes; if the large shape (4x256x256x256) regresses, tighten the `r<0.25f` skip threshold to 0.4f so it silently disables there.

Evidence:
gn_partial_kernel: lts__t_sector_hit_rate=1.59%, l1tex hit 0.89%, DRAM 73.31%, long_scoreboard 94.85% — it re-reads a 16.8 MB buffer conv1 wrote microseconds earlier and misses L2 almost entirely; gn_silu_res_nchw: lts hit 1.96%, DRAM 86.64%, 28.3 us (2.2%); gn_silu_inplace already shows 51.26% L2 hit, proving partial residency exists and is capacity/eviction limited. Root cause: two concurrent stream chains stream ~70-84 MB through L2, evicting the just-written activation before its 2-3 subsequent readers touch it. Refuted alternative: the conv mainloop (69.1%) is not fixable — 2*4*65536*256*2304*2 FLOP / ~6.0 ms ≈ 103 TFLOPS ≈ 100% of the 104.8 TF32 peak, and compute SM throughput of the custom kernels (5.8-23.6%) rules out a compute bound.

Expected metric change:
lts__t_sector_hit_rate: gn_partial 1.59% → >50%, gn_silu_res 1.96% → >40%; gpu__dram_throughput.avg for these kernels falls (traffic served by L2) while gpu__time_duration.avg drops (gn_partial 13.3 us → <9 us, gn_silu_res 28.3 us → <22 us) and smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard drops below 85%/70%. Anti-regression: conv (cutlass s1688fprop) per-launch duration must not rise >2% (missProp=streaming applies only inside the window); launch count, registers/thread, occupancy and output values must be unchanged (bit-identical, same ppb/P and reduction order); if the persist window cannot cover ≥25% of the chunk (large shape) the helper disables itself so no shape regresses.

Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM/latency-bound epilogue chain] Hottest non-removable *addressable* segment is the GroupNorm chain around the (already TF32-SOL) cuDNN conv: gn_partial (13.3us, 96 launches, DRAM 72%, L2 hit 1.5%, 92% long-scoreboard) re-reads the whole conv output that the apply kernel reads again microseconds later, and gn_finalize (3.3us, 0.03 waves/SM, DRAM 2%) is pure launch/latency on the critical path.

Optimisation method:
epilogue_fusion via one cooperative (grid-synchronised) persistent GroupNorm kernel per stage: phase1 partial moments -> grid.sync -> finalize (A,B) -> grid.sync -> apply(affine+SiLU[+residual+NHWC->NCHW]). This collapses gn_partial+gn_finalize+apply into a single launch, so the phase-2 re-read of the chunk (16-67MB) hits L2 instead of DRAM (current lts hit 1.5%), removes the 3.3us near-empty finalize from the dependency chain, and cuts custom launches per forward from 28 to 12.

Method name:
coop_gridsync_gn_fusion

Modification plan:
1. Add `#include <cooperative_groups.h>`; write ONE kernel `gn_fused_kernel(const float* y, const float* res, float* out, const float* gamma, const float* beta, float* partial, float* A, float* Bs, int HW, int C, int P, int ppb, int Bc, float eps, float invCount, int mode)` where mode=0 -> in-place apply on y (stage1), mode=1 -> apply+residual+NHWC->NCHW into out (stage2). It replaces the launch triple {gn_partial, gn_finalize, gn_silu_inplace|gn_silu_res_nchw}; the exact code action is: move the three existing kernel bodies into three phases of this kernel separated by `cg::this_grid().sync()`, and delete the two intermediate kernel launches from run_chunk.
2. Phase A (stats): grid-stride over work items w = n*P + pb (n<Bc, pb<P) using EXACTLY today's pixel ranges (pstart = pb*ppb, pend = min(pstart+ppb,HW)) and today's 256-thread/one-channel-per-thread accumulation + 8-lane shfl reduction, writing partial[n][pb][g][2]. Keeping P/ppb derived from the full batch preserves bit-identical reduction order.
3. `cg::this_grid().sync()`.
4. Phase B (finalize): grid-stride over ng = 0..Bc*G-1, one block per ng (128 threads), identical loop `for i=tid; i<P; i+=blockDim` + block_reduce2 -> mean/rstd -> A[n*C+c]=gamma*rstd, Bs=beta-mean*A. Deterministic (no float atomics), so stats match today exactly.
5. `cg::this_grid().sync()`.
6. Phase C (apply): mode 0 -> today's float4 in-place normalize+SiLU body, grid-stride over i in [0, Bc*HW*C/4). mode 1 -> today's 32x32 tiled body (shared 32x33 floats = 4.2KB, well under the 99KB/block limit), grid-stride over tile index t in [0, Bc * ceil(HW/32) * (C/32)), decoding n, p0, c0 from t so any HW (incl. odd 17161) is covered by the existing `if (p<HW)` guards.
7. Launch with cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel. Size the grid: query `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(&occ, gn_fused_kernel, 256, 0)` once (static), maxCoop = numSMs*occ; when nchunk>1 use maxCoop/2 so the two stream-chunks and the concurrent cuDNN conv can coexist without the driver having to serialise; grid = min(maxCoop_eff, max(P*Bc, Bc*G, tilesNeeded)). Block size 256 for both phases (finalize uses only the first 128 threads, guarded).
8. Fallback: if cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel returns any error (or occ==0), set a sticky `g_coop_ok=false` and call today's three-kernel path (keep gn_partial/gn_finalize/gn_silu_inplace/gn_silu_res_nchw kernels in the file untouched). Never spin-wait on a hand-rolled atomic barrier — co-residency must come from the cooperative launch API only.
9. Keep K1 nchw2nhwc, both cuDNN conv calls, the channels_last weight cache, the chunk planner and the two-stream fork/join exactly as today; only the two GN triples inside run_chunk change.
10. Register pressure: cap with `__launch_bounds__(256, 4)` so occupancy (and therefore the legal cooperative grid) stays >=4 blocks/SM; verify no local spills.
11. Correctness guards: partial buffer sized Bc*P*G*2 as today and fully written before the first sync (all P chunks covered by the grid-stride loop, so no unwritten tail for odd HW); A/Bs sized Bc*C.
12. Validate all four shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131) against the reference within atol 2.8e-3; if any shape regresses vs the current candidate, disable the fused path for that (B,HW) via the same sticky flag.

Evidence:
gn_partial: gpu__time_duration 13312ns, gpu__dram_throughput 72.06%, lts__t_sector_hit_rate 1.54%, l1tex hit 0.89%, long_scoreboard 91.71%, achieved occupancy 33% — it streams the whole conv output from DRAM with ~zero L2 reuse, then gn_silu_inplace (13664ns, DRAM 83.89%) streams the very same bytes again; gn_finalize adds 3296ns at 0.03 waves/SM and 2% DRAM purely as a launch bubble between them, 96 times. Root cause: the two-pass GroupNorm is split across three launches, so the second pass's reuse distance spans a full kernel boundary and the data is evicted. Refuted alternative — 'the conv mainloop is the target': mid shape needs 2*2*(8*8192)*256*2304 = 154.6 GFLOP, i.e. 1.48ms at the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak versus 1.761ms measured end-to-end, so the cutlass s1688fprop kernel is already at ~100% of vendor SOL and is default-keep.

Expected metric change:
lts__t_sector_hit_rate of the fused kernel's apply phase 1.5% -> >40% and its gpu__dram_throughput share falls while total non-conv GPU time drops (gn_partial 13.3us + gn_finalize 3.3us + apply 13.7us -> one kernel <20us); custom kernel launches per forward 28 -> 12 and total forward launches 688 -> <500, shrinking gn_finalize-style elapsed/active cycle gaps. Anti-regression: apply-phase DRAM throughput must stay >=80% of peak (no coalescing loss from the grid-stride remap); registers/thread <=40 with zero local spills; stats must stay bit-identical (same ppb/P, same partial ordering, no float atomics); if cooperative launch fails or occupancy <4 blocks/SM, fall back to today's three-kernel path so no shape (esp. B=1 131x131 and 2x64x64) can regress.

pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[vendor-call/fixed-overhead bound] The conv segment dominates (cutlass s1688fprop 68.7%), but its attached no-math companion `cudnn::engines_precompiled::convertTensor_kernel` costs 4.9% / 1,453us over 232 launches (~2.4 per conv call, ~6.3us ≈ one 4.7MB filter re-transform). Because the batch is split into 4 chunks, every forward issues 8 conv calls, multiplying this loop-invariant per-call overhead 4x.

Optimisation method:
Vendor-call coalescing: halve the pipeline chunk count (nchunk 4 -> 2, cb = B/2) so each forward issues 4 instead of 8 cuDNN conv invocations, cutting the per-call convertTensor filter re-transforms ~2x and doubling the M dimension per conv (fewer tail waves), while still keeping two chunks on two streams so the DRAM-bound GN/layout kernels of one chunk overlap the conv of the other. No kernel body, grid or numeric change.

Method name:
conv_call_coalescing_chunk2

Modification plan:
1. (Exact code action) In `fused_resblock`, delete the current chunk planner block (`cb = std::max(1, B/4); while ((B % cb) != 0) --cb; nchunk = B/cb; if (nchunk > 4) {...}`) and replace it with a fixed 2-way split: `int nchunk = 1, cb = B; if (B >= 2 && (B % 2 == 0) && (long)B * (long)HW >= 32768L) { nchunk = 2; cb = B / 2; }`. This makes each forward issue exactly 2 conv calls per stage instead of 2*4, removing ~half of the 232 convertTensor launches.
2. (Exact code action) Leave `calc_pix_per_block(HW, B)` and `P = (HW+ppb-1)/ppb` computed from the FULL batch B exactly as today, so the GN reduction partitioning/order is bit-identical to the current candidate; only the per-chunk grid z-extent changes from cb=B/4 to cb=B/2 in `run_chunk` (grids already derive from the passed `Bc`).
3. Keep every kernel body unchanged: nchw2nhwc_kernel, gn_partial_kernel, gn_finalize_kernel, gn_silu_inplace_kernel, gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel keep identical block sizes (256/128), shared memory, register counts and math.

Bottleneck identified:
[vendor-conv segment, launch/format-overhead bound] Hottest non-removable target is the cuDNN 3x3 conv segment (68% cutlass s1688fprop + ~13% other fprop engines) and its attached no-math companion `cudnn::engines_precompiled::convertTensor_kernel` (4.8%, 1470us, 232 launches ≈ 2 per conv, ~6.3us each ≈ filter-sized 2.36MB re-transform). Optimisation method:

2. SAFETY: the currently-shipped configuration (filt=CL, api=cudnn_convolution, nchunk=4 for B>=2 && B*HW>=32768, else 1) MUST be one of the autotune candidates, and selection is by measured time, so no shape can be slower than today. Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM/latency-bound epilogue chain] Hottest non-removable *addressable* segment is the GroupNorm chain around the (already TF32-SOL) cuDNN conv: gn_partial (13.3us, 96 launches, DRAM 72%, L2 hit 1.5%, 92% long-scoreboard) re-reads the whole conv output that the apply kernel reads again microseconds later, and gn_finalize (3.3us, 0.03 waves/SM, DRAM 2%) is pure launch/latency on the critical path.

Optimisation method:
epilogue_fusion via one cooperative (grid-synchronised) persistent GroupNorm kernel per stage: phase1 partial moments -> grid.sync -> finalize (A,B) -> grid.sync -> apply(affine+SiLU[+residual+NHWC->NCHW]). This collapses gn_partial+gn_finalize+apply into a single launch, so the phase-2 re-read of the chunk (16-67MB) hits L2 instead of DRAM (current lts hit 1.5%), removes the 3.3us near-empty finalize from the dependency chain, and cuts custom launches per forward from 28 to 12.

Method name:
coop_gridsync_gn_fusion

Modification plan:
1. Add `#include <cooperative_groups.h>`; write ONE kernel `gn_fused_kernel(const float* y, const float* res, float* out, const float* gamma, const float* beta, float* partial, float* A, float* Bs, int HW, int C, int P, int ppb, int Bc, float eps, float invCount, int mode)` where mode=0 -> in-place apply on y (stage1), mode=1 -> apply+residual+NHWC->NCHW into out (stage2). It replaces the launch triple {gn_partial, gn_finalize, gn_silu_inplace|gn_silu_res_nchw}; the exact code action is: move the three existing kernel bodies into three phases of this kernel separated by `cg::this_grid().sync()`, and delete the two intermediate kernel launches from run_chunk.
2. Phase A (stats): grid-stride over work items w = n*P + pb (n<Bc, pb<P) using EXACTLY today's pixel ranges (pstart = pb*ppb, pend = min(pstart+ppb,HW)) and today's 256-thread/one-channel-per-thread accumulation + 8-lane shfl reduction, writing partial[n][pb][g][2]. Keeping P/ppb derived from the full batch preserves bit-identical reduction order.
3. `cg::this_grid().sync()`.
4. Phase B (finalize): grid-stride over ng = 0..Bc*G-1, one block per ng (128 threads), identical loop `for i=tid; i<P; i+=blockDim` + block_reduce2 -> mean/rstd -> A[n*C+c]=gamma*rstd, Bs=beta-mean*A. Deterministic (no float atomics), so stats match today exactly.
5. `cg::this_grid().sync()`.
6. Phase C (apply): mode 0 -> today's float4 in-place normalize+SiLU body, grid-stride over i in [0, Bc*HW*C/4). mode 1 -> today's 32x32 tiled body (shared 32x33 floats = 4.2KB, well under the 99KB/block limit), grid-stride over tile index t in [0, Bc * ceil(HW/32) * (C/32)), decoding n, p0, c0 from t so any HW (incl. odd 17161) is covered by the existing `if (p<HW)` guards.
7. Launch with cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel. Size the grid: query `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(&occ, gn_fused_kernel, 256, 0)` once (static), maxCoop = numSMs*occ; when nchunk>1 use maxCoop/2 so the two stream-chunks and the concurrent cuDNN conv can coexist without the driver having to serialise; grid = min(maxCoop_eff, max(P*Bc, Bc*G, tilesNeeded)). Block size 256 for both phases (finalize uses only the first 128 threads, guarded).
8. Fallback: if cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel returns any error (or occ==0), set a sticky `g_coop_ok=false` and call today's three-kernel path (keep gn_partial/gn_finalize/gn_silu_inplace/gn_silu_res_nchw kernels in the file untouched). Never spin-wait on a hand-rolled atomic barrier — co-residency must come from the cooperative launch API only.
9. Keep K1 nchw2nhwc, both cuDNN conv calls, the channels_last weight cache, the chunk planner and the two-stream fork/join exactly as today; only the two GN triples inside run_chunk change.
10. Register pressure: cap with `__launch_bounds__(256, 4)` so occupancy (and therefore the legal cooperative grid) stays >=4 blocks/SM; verify no local spills.
11. Correctness guards: partial buffer sized Bc*P*G*2 as today and fully written before the first sync (all P chunks covered by the grid-stride loop, so no unwritten tail for odd HW); A/Bs sized Bc*C.
12. Validate all four shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131) against the reference within atol 2.8e-3; if any shape regresses vs the current candidate, disable the fused path for that (B,HW) via the same sticky flag.

Evidence:
gn_partial: gpu__time_duration 13312ns, gpu__dram_throughput 72.06%, lts__t_sector_hit_rate 1.54%, l1tex hit 0.89%, long_scoreboard 91.71%, achieved occupancy 33% — it streams the whole conv output from DRAM with ~zero L2 reuse, then gn_silu_inplace (13664ns, DRAM 83.89%) streams the very same bytes again; gn_finalize adds 3296ns at 0.03 waves/SM and 2% DRAM purely as a launch bubble between them, 96 times. Root cause: the two-pass GroupNorm is split across three launches, so the second pass's reuse distance spans a full kernel boundary and the data is evicted. Refuted alternative — 'the conv mainloop is the target': mid shape needs 2*2*(8*8192)*256*2304 = 154.6 GFLOP, i.e. 1.48ms at the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak versus 1.761ms measured end-to-end, so the cutlass s1688fprop kernel is already at ~100% of vendor SOL and is default-keep.

Expected metric change:
lts__t_sector_hit_rate of the fused kernel's apply phase 1.5% -> >40% and its gpu__dram_throughput share falls while total non-conv GPU time drops (gn_partial 13.3us + gn_finalize 3.3us + apply 13.7us -> one kernel <20us); custom kernel launches per forward 28 -> 12 and total forward launches 688 -> <500, shrinking gn_finalize-style elapsed/active cycle gaps. Anti-regression: apply-phase DRAM throughput must stay >=80% of peak (no coalescing loss from the grid-stride remap); registers/thread <=40 with zero local spills; stats must stay bit-identical (same ppb/P, same partial ordering, no float atomics); if cooperative launch fails or occupancy <4 blocks/SM, fall back to today's three-kernel path so no shape (esp. B=1 131x131 and 2x64x64) can regress.

Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM/latency-bound epilogue chain] Hottest non-removable *addressable* segment is the GroupNorm chain around the (already TF32-SOL) cuDNN conv: gn_partial (13.3us, 96 launches, DRAM 72%, L2 hit 1.5%, 92% long-scoreboard) re-reads the whole conv output that the apply kernel reads again microseconds later, and gn_finalize (3.3us, 0.03 waves/SM, DRAM 2%) is pure launch/latency on the critical path.

Optimisation method:
epilogue_fusion via one cooperative (grid-synchronised) persistent GroupNorm kernel per stage: phase1 partial moments -> grid.sync -> finalize (A,B) -> grid.sync -> apply(affine+SiLU[+residual+NHWC->NCHW]). This collapses gn_partial+gn_finalize+apply into a single launch, so the phase-2 re-read of the chunk (16-67MB) hits L2 instead of DRAM (current lts hit 1.5%), removes the 3.3us near-empty finalize from the dependency chain, and cuts custom launches per forward from 28 to 12.

Method name:
coop_gridsync_gn_fusion

Modification plan:
1. Add `#include <cooperative_groups.h>`; write ONE kernel `gn_fused_kernel(const float* y, const float* res, float* out, const float* gamma, const float* beta, float* partial, float* A, float* Bs, int HW, int C, int P, int ppb, int Bc, float eps, float invCount, int mode)` where mode=0 -> in-place apply on y (stage1), mode=1 -> apply+residual+NHWC->NCHW into out (stage2). It replaces the launch triple {gn_partial, gn_finalize, gn_silu_inplace|gn_silu_res_nchw}; the exact code action is: move the three existing kernel bodies into three phases of this kernel separated by `cg::this_grid().sync()`, and delete the two intermediate kernel launches from run_chunk.
2. Phase A (stats): grid-stride over work items w = n*P + pb (n<Bc, pb<P) using EXACTLY today's pixel ranges (pstart = pb*ppb, pend = min(pstart+ppb,HW)) and today's 256-thread/one-channel-per-thread accumulation + 8-lane shfl reduction, writing partial[n][pb][g][2]. Keeping P/ppb derived from the full batch preserves bit-identical reduction order.
3. `cg::this_grid().sync()`.
4. Phase B (finalize): grid-stride over ng = 0..Bc*G-1, one block per ng (128 threads), identical loop `for i=tid; i<P; i+=blockDim` + block_reduce2 -> mean/rstd -> A[n*C+c]=gamma*rstd, Bs=beta-mean*A. Deterministic (no float atomics), so stats match today exactly.
5. `cg::this_grid().sync()`.
6. Phase C (apply): mode 0 -> today's float4 in-place normalize+SiLU body, grid-stride over i in [0, Bc*HW*C/4). mode 1 -> today's 32x32 tiled body (shared 32x33 floats = 4.2KB, well under the 99KB/block limit), grid-stride over tile index t in [0, Bc * ceil(HW/32) * (C/32)), decoding n, p0, c0 from t so any HW (incl. odd 17161) is covered by the existing `if (p<HW)` guards.
7. Launch with cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel. Size the grid: query `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(&occ, gn_fused_kernel, 256, 0)` once (static), maxCoop = numSMs*occ; when nchunk>1 use maxCoop/2 so the two stream-chunks and the concurrent cuDNN conv can coexist without the driver having to serialise; grid = min(maxCoop_eff, max(P*Bc, Bc*G, tilesNeeded)). Block size 256 for both phases (finalize uses only the first 128 threads, guarded).
8. Fallback: if cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel returns any error (or occ==0), set a sticky `g_coop_ok=false` and call today's three-kernel path (keep gn_partial/gn_finalize/gn_silu_inplace/gn_silu_res_nchw kernels in the file untouched). Never spin-wait on a hand-rolled atomic barrier — co-residency must come from the cooperative launch API only.
9. Keep K1 nchw2nhwc, both cuDNN conv calls, the channels_last weight cache, the chunk planner and the two-stream fork/join exactly as today; only the two GN triples inside run_chunk change.
10. Register pressure: cap with `__launch_bounds__(256, 4)` so occupancy (and therefore the legal cooperative grid) stays >=4 blocks/SM; verify no local spills.
11. Correctness guards: partial buffer sized Bc*P*G*2 as today and fully written before the first sync (all P chunks covered by the grid-stride loop, so no unwritten tail for odd HW); A/Bs sized Bc*C.
12. Validate all four shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131) against the reference within atol 2.8e-3; if any shape regresses vs the current candidate, disable the fused path for that (B,HW) via the same sticky flag.

Evidence:
gn_partial: gpu__time_duration 13312ns, gpu__dram_throughput 72.06%, lts__t_sector_hit_rate 1.54%, l1tex hit 0.89%, long_scoreboard 91.71%, achieved occupancy 33% — it streams the whole conv output from DRAM with ~zero L2 reuse, then gn_silu_inplace (13664ns, DRAM 83.89%) streams the very same bytes again; gn_finalize adds 3296ns at 0.03 waves/SM and 2% DRAM purely as a launch bubble between them, 96 times. Root cause: the two-pass GroupNorm is split across three launches, so the second pass's reuse distance spans a full kernel boundary and the data is evicted. Refuted alternative — 'the conv mainloop is the target': mid shape needs 2*2*(8*8192)*256*2304 = 154.6 GFLOP, i.e. 1.48ms at the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak versus 1.761ms measured end-to-end, so the cutlass s1688fprop kernel is already at ~100% of vendor SOL and is default-keep.

Expected metric change:
lts__t_sector_hit_rate of the fused kernel's apply phase 1.5% -> >40% and its gpu__dram_throughput share falls while total non-conv GPU time drops (gn_partial 13.3us + gn_finalize 3.3us + apply 13.7us -> one kernel <20us); custom kernel launches per forward 28 -> 12 and total forward launches 688 -> <500, shrinking gn_finalize-style elapsed/active cycle gaps. Anti-regression: apply-phase DRAM throughput must stay >=80% of peak (no coalescing loss from the grid-stride remap); registers/thread <=40 with zero local spills; stats must stay bit-identical (same ppb/P, same partial ordering, no float atomics); if cooperative launch fails or occupancy <4 blocks/SM, fall back to today's three-kernel path so no shape (esp. B=1 131x131 and 2x64x64) can regress.

Bottleneck identified:
[vendor-call/fixed-overhead bound] The conv segment dominates (cutlass s1688fprop 68.7%), but its attached no-math companion `cudnn::engines_precompiled::convertTensor_kernel` costs 4.9% / 1,453us over 232 launches (~2.4 per conv call, ~6.3us ≈ one 4.7MB filter re-transform). Optimisation method:
Vendor-call coalescing: halve the pipeline chunk count (nchunk 4 -> 2, cb = B/2) so each forward issues 4 instead of 8 cuDNN conv invocations, cutting the per-call convertTensor filter re-transforms ~2x and doubling the M dimension per conv (fewer tail waves), while still keeping two chunks on two streams so the DRAM-bound GN/layout kernels of one chunk overlap the conv of the other. No kernel body, grid or numeric change.

Method name:
conv_call_coalescing_chunk2

Modification plan:
1. (Exact code action) In `fused_resblock`, delete the current chunk planner block (`cb = std::max(1, B/4); while ((B % cb) != 0) --cb; nchunk = B/cb; if (nchunk > 4) {...}`) and replace it with a fixed 2-way split: `int nchunk = 1, cb = B; if (B >= 2 && (B % 2 == 0) && (long)B * (long)HW >= 32768L) { nchunk = 2; cb = B / 2; }`. 2. (Exact code action) Leave `calc_pix_per_block(HW, B)` and `P = (HW+ppb-1)/ppb` computed from the FULL batch B exactly as today, so the GN reduction partitioning/order is bit-identical to the current candidate; only the per-chunk grid z-extent changes from cb=B/4 to cb=B/2 in `run_chunk` (grids already derive from the passed `Bc`).
3. Keep every kernel body unchanged: nchw2nhwc_kernel, gn_partial_kernel, gn_finalize_kernel, gn_silu_inplace_kernel, gn_silu_res_nchw_kernel keep identical block sizes (256/128), shared memory, register counts and math.
4. Keep the two-stream fork/join intact: with nchunk=2 the loop still alternates `side_streams[ci & 1]`, so chunk0 and chunk1 chains run concurrently and the DRAM-bound custom kernels of one chunk still hide behind the other chunk's cutlass conv.
5. Odd/awkward batches: if `B % 2 != 0` (B=1 for the 131x131 shape) or `B*HW < 32768` (B=2,64x64 shape) keep nchunk=1 — those shapes already run a single chunk today, so they are untouched (no regression path).
6. Keep the existing guard `if (nchunk > 1) { if (!xc.narrow(...).is_contiguous() || !out.narrow(...).is_contiguous()) { nchunk = 1; cb = B; } }` unchanged after the new planner.
7. Per-chunk temporaries (`xn`, `partial`, `A`, `Bs`, conv outputs) are now 2x larger each but there are half as many live chunks, so peak memory is unchanged; no allocator changes needed. Keep `rec_stream()` bookkeeping for `out`, `xc`, weights on both side streams.
8. cuDNN autotune: `benchmark=true` caches per (N,C,H,W) key; the new chunk batch (B/2) is a new key, so the first call re-benchmarks once per shape. Keep `init_cudnn_flags()` and the `at::cudnn_convolution` fast path with the existing try/catch fallback to `at::conv2d` untouched.
9. Optional safety valve (no extra mechanism): read env `VAE_NCHUNK` once (static) and, if set to 1/2/4, override the planner value; default 2. This makes A/B verification of the chunk granularity trivial without touching kernels.
10. Verification checklist before shipping: (a) outputs match reference within max_atol per shape on all four shapes; (b) nsys shows nchw2nhwc_kernel launches per forward drop 4 -> 2 and convertTensor_kernel launches per forward roughly halve; (c) cutlass s1688fprop launch count per forward drops 8 -> 4 with ~2x longer per-launch duration and no drop in achieved FLOP rate; (d) wall time must not regress on the 4x256x256x256 shape (B=4 -> cb=2) or the 8x256x64x128 shape (B=8 -> cb=4); if either regresses, set the default override to the previous 4-way split for that shape class via the `B*HW` threshold only (no other code change).
11. Do not touch get_inputs/get_init_inputs, do not move tensors across devices, keep the Python `_cl_weight` cache and the eager fallback branch exactly as-is.

Refutation of the alternative 'the custom GN/layout chain is the bottleneck': gn_silu_res_nchw is at 86.63% of peak DRAM, nchw2nhwc 84.22%, gn_silu_inplace 82.10% — <15% headroom on kernels holding only 9.9% of forward time (<1.5% total), and the cutlass mainloop itself is at ~100% of the TF32 roofline (154.6 GFLOP / 104.8 TFLOPS = 1.48ms vs 1.761ms measured end-to-end), so it is default-keep.
