pairs.a_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[memory-bound, vendor-inserted copies] The conv segment: `cutlass...s1688fprop_tf32_nhwc` is 78.2% (758us/conv) but runs 77.3 GFLOP/758us = 102 TFLOPS ≈ 97% of the 104.8 TF32 peak, so it is untouchable. Attached to it, cuDNN emits 2 `convertTensor_kernel` passes per conv (48 launches, 1831us, 7.9%), pure fp32→fp32 copies (~134MB, ~76us each) doing zero math.

Optimisation method:
Bypass PyTorch's cuDNN-v8 plan selection and call cuDNN directly inside the extension (`cudnnConvolutionForward`, NHWC fp32 descriptors, `CUDNN_TENSOR_OP_MATH`, algo cached per shape). The ALLOW_CONVERSION-style plan PyTorch currently gets stages tf32-rounded copies of x and w before the mainloop; selecting a plan that consumes fp32 NHWC directly deletes both convertTensor passes per conv (7.9% of forward, ~268MB/iter of copy traffic) while keeping the identical cutlass tf32 mainloop and identical numerics.

Method name:
cudnn_plan_select

Modification plan:
Checklist (all custom kernels stay byte-identical; only the conv invocation changes):
1. EXACT CODE ACTION — add cuDNN to the extension: in `_CUDA_SRC` add `#include <cudnn.h>` and `#include <ATen/cudnn/Handle.h>`; in `load_inline(...)` add `extra_ldflags=["-lcudnn"]`. Add `#define CUDNN_CK(x) TORCH_CHECK((x)==CUDNN_STATUS_SUCCESS)`.
2. EXACT CODE ACTION — new host function `torch::Tensor conv3x3_nhwc(torch::Tensor x, torch::Tensor w)`: allocate `y = torch::empty({B,256,H,W}, x.options().memory_format(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast))`; create `cudnnTensorDescriptor_t` xd/yd with `cudnnSetTensor4dDescriptor(.., CUDNN_TENSOR_NHWC, CUDNN_DATA_FLOAT, B,256,H,W)`; `cudnnFilterDescriptor_t` wd with `cudnnSetFilter4dDescriptor(wd, CUDNN_DATA_FLOAT, CUDNN_TENSOR_NHWC, 256,256,3,3)`; `cudnnSetConvolution2dDescriptor(cd, 1,1, 1,1, 1,1, CUDNN_CROSS_CORRELATION, CUDNN_DATA_FLOAT)`; then `cudnnSetConvolutionMathType(cd, CUDNN_TENSOR_OP_MATH)` (NOT `..._ALLOW_CONVERSION`, which is what forces the fp32→tf32 staging copies of x and w seen as the 48 convertTensor launches). Then replace both `F.conv2d(...)` calls in `ModelNew.forward` with `self.ext.conv3x3_nhwc(xl, w1)` / `(y, w2)`; delete nothing else.
3. Algo selection, cached: static `std::unordered_map<uint64_t, Plan>` keyed by `((uint64_t)B<<40)|(H<<20)|W`, holding descriptors, `cudnnConvolutionFwdAlgo_t`, workspace bytes. On miss, call `cudnnGetConvolutionForwardAlgorithm_v7(handle, xd, wd, cd, yd, 8, &n, perf[])` and pick the first entry with `status==SUCCESS`, `mathType==CUDNN_TENSOR_OP_MATH`, and `memory <= 256MB` (normally `IMPLICIT_PRECOMP_GEMM`). Store it; descriptors are destroyed only at process exit.
4. Workspace: `auto ws = torch::empty({(int64_t)ws_bytes}, x.options().dtype(torch::kUInt8));` (PyTorch caching allocator → no cudaMalloc in steady state).
5. Launch: `handle = at::native::getCudnnHandle()` (already bound to the current stream); `alpha=1.f, beta=0.f`; `cudnnConvolutionForward(handle, &alpha, xd, x.data_ptr(), wd, w.data_ptr(), cd, algo, ws.data_ptr(), ws_bytes, &beta, yd, y.data_ptr())`.
6. Anti-regression guard: if `cudnnGetConvolutionForwardAlgorithm_v7` yields no usable entry, or `cudnnConvolutionForward` returns non-SUCCESS, set a per-shape `use_fallback=true` in the cached Plan and return an empty tensor sentinel; Python side then calls `F.conv2d(x, w, None, 1, 1)` exactly as today. This keeps all four benchmark shapes (2x64x64, 8x64x128, 4x256x256, 1x131x131) correct and never slower than the current path.
7. Optional one-time A/B (first call per shape only, outside steady state): time the cuDNN plan vs `F.conv2d` with cudaEvents and latch the faster into the Plan. Guarantees geomean cannot regress on the awkward 131x131 shape where a different engine may win.
8. Keep `conv*_weight.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)` as-is (0.6%); keep `nchw2nhwc_kernel`, `gn_stats/gn_final`, `gn_silu_apply`, `gn_silu_res_t` untouched — they already run at 80–89% DRAM SOL.
9. Numerics: math stays TF32 tensor-core fp32-accumulate, exactly what the reference `F.conv2d` uses under `allow_tf32`; GN reductions unchanged (fp32 partials, fp64 final). Validate against atol 2.8e-3 / rtol 1e-5 on all four shapes.
10. Sanity: assert `x.is_contiguous(ChannelsLast)` and `C==256`, `H,W>=1`; no shape divisibility assumptions (131x131 safe).

Evidence:
convertTensor_kernel: 1831us total / 48 launches = 7.9% of forward GPU time, 2 per conv, ~76us for the activation-sized pass = 134MB @ ~1.76TB/s → pure DRAM-bound copy with zero FLOPs. Root cause: PyTorch's cuDNN-v8 plan for fp32+TF32 stages tf32-rounded copies of x and w before the cutlass mainloop. Refutation of 'the conv mainloop is the bottleneck to fix': 77.3 GFLOP/758us = 102 TFLOPS = 97% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 roofline; a 9-GEMM cuBLASLt rewrite would move 9x3 tensor passes (~1.8GB → ≥1.0ms) vs 758us, strictly worse.

Expected metric change:
convertTensor_kernel launches 48→0 and its 1831us → 0 (forward GPU time -7.9%); DRAM bytes moved per iteration drops ~268MB (~15% of total traffic); total launches 180→132. Anti-regression constraint: the cutlass s1688fprop kernel duration must stay ≤758us/launch (±2%) and output must satisfy atol 2.8e-3 on all four shapes; if either fails, the per-shape fallback latches back to F.conv2d so no shape regresses.
pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM-bandwidth-bound working-set overflow] Hottest non-removable segment = the GN2+SiLU+residual epilogue (gn_silu_res_t, 4.7%, 89us/call) plus its stats pass, and the whole non-conv pipeline (263us/call). Every one of these kernels already runs at 86-89% of DRAM peak; the 5 live 67MB tensors (335MB) blow past L2, so x and each intermediate round-trip to DRAM instead of staying cached.

Optimisation method:
L2 cache blocking: execute the entire residual block in batch chunks (GroupNorm stats are per-(image,group), so per-image chunking is exactly equivalent) sized so {x_chunk, z, y2} stay resident in the 96MB L2. This converts the transpose write, conv in/out, both stats re-reads and the final residual read from DRAM traffic into L2 hits. Justified by evidence that the 67MB stats read already serves from L2 at 4.27TB/s while cold passes cap at 1.57TB/s. Gated on working-set size so other shapes are untouched.

Method name:
l2_cache_blocking

Modification plan:
Checklist (host-side only; no kernel math changes):
1. In ModelNew.forward, hoist the per-call invariants OUT of any loop: parse `eps` once; compute `w1 = conv1_weight.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)` and `w2 = ...` ONCE (this also deletes the 24 at::native::elementwise_kernel weight-copy launches, 152us, from being repeated per chunk).
2. Add an out-tensor variant so chunks write in place: change `gn_silu_res_nchw(y,res,w,b,eps)` to `gn_silu_res_nchw(y,res,w,b,eps,out)` where `out` is a pre-allocated NCHW tensor (keep `TORCH_CHECK(out.is_contiguous())`, drop the internal `torch::empty`); export the new signature in _CPP_SRC. Kernel body unchanged.
3. Compute the chunk size in Python:
   `S = C*H*W*4` (bytes per image, C=256);
   `BUDGET = 56*1024*1024`;
   `bc = min(B, max(1, BUDGET // (3*S)))`;
   if `3*S > BUDGET` or `bc >= B`: take the EXISTING single-shot path unchanged (this is the gate: small 2x256x64x64 (3S=50MB, B=2 -> bc>=B), large 4x256x256x256 (3S=201MB > budget) and awkward 1x256x131x131 (B=1) all fall through to today's byte-identical code, so they cannot regress).
4. Chunked path (mid shape 8x256x64x128 -> S=8.4MB, bc=2, 4 chunks): allocate `out = torch.empty_like(x)` once, then `for i in range(0, B, bc):` with `n = min(bc, B-i)`:
   a. `xc = x.narrow(0, i, n)` (dim-0 narrow of a contiguous NCHW tensor is contiguous, so the extension's `is_contiguous` check passes; no copy).
   b. `xl = ext.nchw_to_nhwc(xc)`
   c. `y = F.conv2d(xl, w1, None, 1, 1)`
   d. `y = ext.gn_silu_nhwc(y, nw1, nb1, eps)`
   e. `y = F.conv2d(y, w2, None, 1, 1)`
   f. `ext.gn_silu_res_nchw(y, xc, nw2, nb2, eps, out.narrow(0, i, n))`
   All on the current stream, in order; the chunk's x/intermediates (~50MB live) stay in L2 across steps b-f, so step f's residual read of `xc` and the stats re-reads hit L2 instead of DRAM.
5. Keep every CUDA kernel and `pick_P` untouched: with B=n=2, `pick_P` returns min((HW+31)/32, 512)=256, grid (256,2)=512 blocks, and every psum/psq entry is still fully written (tail-safe for odd HW).
6. Return `out`.

Method steps / rationale for the sizing: live set during conv2 is x_chunk + z + y2 = 3 x n x S. With n=2 that is 50MB inside the ~96MB L2 (plus 2.4MB weights), leaving headroom for the streaming write-back of dead y1 lines. Do NOT choose n=1 for this shape: n=2 keeps the cutlass 128x64 tile at 16384/128 x 256/64 = 512 CTAs (3 waves over 170 SMs) so conv efficiency is preserved; n=1 would give only 256 CTAs.
7. Anti-regression guard in code: if `B % bc != 0` the last chunk is simply smaller (handled by `n = min(bc, B-i)`), and if `bc < 1` the gate forces the single-shot path.
8. Do not touch conv engine selection, dtypes, or the convertTensor path; the mechanism composes with (and benefits) them because their copies also become L2-served.

Evidence:
Nsight Systems: gn_stats_kernel = 377us/24 launches = 15.7us for a 67MB read = 4.27 TB/s, i.e. 2.4x DRAM peak (1.792 TB/s) -> that read is already served by L2, proving L2 holds a 67MB tensor. By contrast nchw2nhwc = 1026us/12 = 85.5us for 134MB = 1.57 TB/s (88% of DRAM peak) and gn_silu_res_t shows gpu__dram_throughput 89.32% with lts__t_sector_hit_rate 1.63% -> cold DRAM traffic because the full-batch live set (5 x 67MB) evicts x. Root cause: working set > L2, not access pattern (both kernels are fully coalesced, smsp divergent branches = 0, achieved occupancy 89-94%). Refutation of 'the cutlass conv is the bottleneck': 77.3 GFLOP / 730us = 105.9 TFLOPS = 101% of the 104.8 TF32 roofline, zero headroom. Refutation of 'fuse stats into apply (single-pass GN)': the whole GPU register file (170x64K x4B = 43.5MB) plus shared memory (17MB) cannot hold the 67MB activation, so a second read is mandatory; only cache residency can make it cheap. Previous attempt classification: (b) - it predicted convertTensor 2176us -> 0 yet all four shapes moved by only -1.0/-0.9/+0.3/-0.5%, far below the 9.5% the removal would have produced, so the plan-select never engaged; its NCU profile still shows the base's 5 fused kernels intact, so the base structure was not broken. Regardless, convertTensor is a copy-only/removable kernel and is excluded as a primary target here; l2_cache_blocking composes with it.

Expected metric change:

Optimisation method:
Bypass PyTorch's cuDNN-v8 plan selection and call cuDNN directly inside the extension (`cudnnConvolutionForward`, NHWC fp32 descriptors, `CUDNN_TENSOR_OP_MATH`, algo cached per shape). Method name:
cudnn_plan_select

Modification plan:
Checklist (all custom kernels stay byte-identical; only the conv invocation changes):
1. EXACT CODE ACTION — add cuDNN to the extension: in `_CUDA_SRC` add `#include <cudnn.h>` and `#include <ATen/cudnn/Handle.h>`; in `load_inline(...)` add `extra_ldflags=["-lcudnn"]`. Add `#define CUDNN_CK(x) TORCH_CHECK((x)==CUDNN_STATUS_SUCCESS)`.
2. EXACT CODE ACTION — new host function `torch::Tensor conv3x3_nhwc(torch::Tensor x, torch::Tensor w)`: allocate `y = torch::empty({B,256,H,W}, x.options().memory_format(at::MemoryFormat::ChannelsLast))`; create `cudnnTensorDescriptor_t` xd/yd with `cudnnSetTensor4dDescriptor(.., CUDNN_TENSOR_NHWC, CUDNN_DATA_FLOAT, B,256,H,W)`; `cudnnFilterDescriptor_t` wd with `cudnnSetFilter4dDescriptor(wd, CUDNN_DATA_FLOAT, CUDNN_TENSOR_NHWC, 256,256,3,3)`; `cudnnSetConvolution2dDescriptor(cd, 1,1, 1,1, 1,1, CUDNN_CROSS_CORRELATION, CUDNN_DATA_FLOAT)`; then `cudnnSetConvolutionMathType(cd, CUDNN_TENSOR_OP_MATH)` (NOT `..._ALLOW_CONVERSION`, which is what forces the fp32→tf32 staging copies of x and w seen as the 48 convertTensor launches). [serialization of complementary-resource kernels] Hottest non-removable segment is the cutlass_tensorop_s1688fprop conv pair (76.8%, 1489us/forward) which is compute-saturated (~104 TFLOPS TF32) but uses only ~0.18 TB/s (10%) of DRAM. Optimisation method:
Multi-stream pipelined batch chunking: split the batch into 2 per-sample-independent halves and run the two identical pipelines on two CUDA streams, staggered by one stage with an event so a chunk's memory-bound transpose/GroupNorm kernels execute concurrently with the other chunk's compute-bound cuDNN conv. Metrics justify it: conv leaves ~90% of DRAM idle, GN/transpose kernels leave ~85% of SM issue idle — perfectly complementary. GroupNorm stats are per-(batch,group), so chunking is numerically per-sample exact. Gated to B>=4.

Method name:
multistream_pipeline

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST
1. Add an out-parameter entry point `gn_silu_res_nchw_out(y,res,w,b,eps,out)` to the extension: identical body to `gn_silu_res_nchw` but writes into the caller-supplied contiguous NCHW tensor instead of allocating (TORCH_CHECK out.is_contiguous(), same sizes). Keep the existing function for the fallback path. No kernel code, grid, block, or pick_P heuristic is changed.
2. In `ModelNew.__init__` set `self._streams=None`; on first forward lazily create `sA, sB = torch.cuda.Stream(), torch.cuda.Stream()` plus `ev0, evStage, evA, evB = [torch.cuda.Event() for _ in range(4)]` and cache them.
3. In forward, compute `B = x.size(0)`. If `B < 4`: run the EXISTING single-stream code path verbatim and return (freezes 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 behavior).
4. Else set `s0 = B//2`, chunks `[0:s0]`, `[s0:B]` (batch slices of a contiguous NCHW tensor are themselves contiguous — no copies).
5. On the current stream: normalize params once (`nw1/nb1/nw2/nb2`), build `w1c = conv1_weight.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)`, `w2c` likewise, allocate `out = torch.empty_like(x)` (NCHW contiguous), then `ev0.record()`.
METHOD STEPS
6. `sA.wait_event(ev0)`; `sB.wait_event(ev0)` so both side streams observe x, out and the converted weights.
7. Under `with torch.cuda.stream(sA):` call `x.record_stream(sA); out.record_stream(sA); w1c.record_stream(sA); w2c.record_stream(sA)` then run chunk0 exactly as today: `xl = ext.nchw_to_nhwc(x[0:s0])`; immediately `evStage.record(sA)`; `y = F.conv2d(xl, w1c, None,1,1)`; `y = ext.gn_silu_nhwc(y, nw1, nb1, eps)`; `y = F.conv2d(y, w2c, None,1,1)`; `ext.gn_silu_res_nchw_out(y, x[0:s0], nw2, nb2, eps, out[0:s0])`; `evA.record(sA)`.
8. Under `with torch.cuda.stream(sB):` FIRST `sB.wait_event(evStage)` — this is the stagger that creates the overlap: chunk1's memory-bound `nchw2nhwc` starts only when chunk0's compute-bound conv1 starts, after which the two pipelines stay one stage out of phase (A's GN pass overlaps B's conv, B's GN pass overlaps A's next conv). Then record_stream the shared tensors on sB and run the identical 5-call sequence for `x[s0:B]` writing `out[s0:B]`; `evB.record(sB)`.
9. Back on the current stream: `torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_event(evA); ...wait_event(evB)`; return `out`.
10. Allocation safety: all per-chunk temporaries (xl, conv outputs, mean/rstd, psum/psq) are allocated inside the `torch.cuda.stream()` context, so the caching allocator and `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` inside the extension both bind to that side stream; only x/out/weights cross streams and they are bracketed by ev0 and evA/evB plus explicit `record_stream`.
11. Numerics: conv, GroupNorm moments (per batch,group) and the residual add are all per-sample independent, so the chunked result equals the unchunked result up to the partial-sum ordering inside `gn_final_kernel` (already accumulated in double); `pick_P` is recomputed from the chunk's B so every partial-buffer entry is still written — the H*W%tile tail bug class cannot reappear.
12. Anti-regression guard: if `B < 4` (small and awkward shapes) or `x` is not 4-D/fp32/CUDA, take the untouched legacy path; keep a single-stream fallback if stream creation fails.

Nsight Systems: cutlass s1688fprop = 17,872us/12 iters = 1489us/forward (76.8%) moving only ~268MB => ~0.18 TB/s = 10% of the 1.792 TB/s peak, while nchw2nhwc (86.8% DRAM, 15.2% SM), gn_silu_res_t (87.6% DRAM, 13.8% SM) and gn_silu_apply (78.3% DRAM, 12.6% SM) total 293us plus 157us of cuDNN converts — 450us/forward that occupies almost no compute. (1) nsys timeline: cutlass s1688fprop instances become concurrent with nchw2nhwc/gn_stats/gn_silu_* instances (currently 0 overlap); exposed non-conv time per forward drops from ~450us toward <200us, mid-shape forward 1.917ms -> ~1.65-1.75ms. Every one of these kernels already runs at 86-89% of DRAM peak; the 5 live 67MB tensors (335MB) blow past L2, so x and each intermediate round-trip to DRAM instead of staying cached.

Optimisation method:
L2 cache blocking: execute the entire residual block in batch chunks (GroupNorm stats are per-(image,group), so per-image chunking is exactly equivalent) sized so {x_chunk, z, y2} stay resident in the 96MB L2. This converts the transpose write, conv in/out, both stats re-reads and the final residual read from DRAM traffic into L2 hits. Justified by evidence that the 67MB stats read already serves from L2 at 4.27TB/s while cold passes cap at 1.57TB/s. Gated on working-set size so other shapes are untouched.

Method name:
l2_cache_blocking

Modification plan:
Checklist (host-side only; no kernel math changes):
1. In ModelNew.forward, hoist the per-call invariants OUT of any loop: parse `eps` once; compute `w1 = conv1_weight.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last)` and `w2 = ...` ONCE (this also deletes the 24 at::native::elementwise_kernel weight-copy launches, 152us, from being repeated per chunk).
2. Add an out-tensor variant so chunks write in place: change `gn_silu_res_nchw(y,res,w,b,eps)` to `gn_silu_res_nchw(y,res,w,b,eps,out)` where `out` is a pre-allocated NCHW tensor (keep `TORCH_CHECK(out.is_contiguous())`, drop the internal `torch::empty`); export the new signature in _CPP_SRC. Kernel body unchanged.
3. Compute the chunk size in Python:
   `S = C*H*W*4` (bytes per image, C=256);
   `BUDGET = 56*1024*1024`;
   `bc = min(B, max(1, BUDGET // (3*S)))`;
   if `3*S > BUDGET` or `bc >= B`: take the EXISTING single-shot path unchanged (this is the gate: small 2x256x64x64 (3S=50MB, B=2 -> bc>=B), large 4x256x256x256 (3S=201MB > budget) and awkward 1x256x131x131 (B=1) all fall through to today's byte-identical code, so they cannot regress).
4. Chunked path (mid shape 8x256x64x128 -> S=8.4MB, bc=2, 4 chunks): allocate `out = torch.empty_like(x)` once, then `for i in range(0, B, bc):` with `n = min(bc, B-i)`:
   a. `xc = x.narrow(0, i, n)` (dim-0 narrow of a contiguous NCHW tensor is contiguous, so the extension's `is_contiguous` check passes; no copy).
   b. `xl = ext.nchw_to_nhwc(xc)`
   c. `y = F.conv2d(xl, w1, None, 1, 1)`
   d. `y = ext.gn_silu_nhwc(y, nw1, nb1, eps)`
   e. `y = F.conv2d(y, w2, None, 1, 1)`
   f. `ext.gn_silu_res_nchw(y, xc, nw2, nb2, eps, out.narrow(0, i, n))`
   All on the current stream, in order; the chunk's x/intermediates (~50MB live) stay in L2 across steps b-f, so step f's residual read of `xc` and the stats re-reads hit L2 instead of DRAM.
5. Keep every CUDA kernel and `pick_P` untouched: with B=n=2, `pick_P` returns min((HW+31)/32, 512)=256, grid (256,2)=512 blocks, and every psum/psq entry is still fully written (tail-safe for odd HW).
6. Return `out`.

With n=2 that is 50MB inside the ~96MB L2 (plus 2.4MB weights), leaving headroom for the streaming write-back of dead y1 lines. Do NOT choose n=1 for this shape: n=2 keeps the cutlass 128x64 tile at 16384/128 x 256/64 = 512 CTAs (3 waves over 170 SMs) so conv efficiency is preserved; n=1 would give only 256 CTAs.
7. Anti-regression guard in code: if `B % bc != 0` the last chunk is simply smaller (handled by `n = min(bc, B-i)`), and if `bc < 1` the gate forces the single-shot path.
8. Do not touch conv engine selection, dtypes, or the convertTensor path; the mechanism composes with (and benefits) them because their copies also become L2-served.

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/launch-overhead-bound sub-segment inside the DRAM-bound GN epilogue] gn_final_kernel + gn_stats_kernel. gn_final runs 4.96us at 0.03 waves/SM, 5.3% achieved occupancy, 1.8% DRAM, 87% excessive sectors — pure launch/tail latency, 8 launches/forward (~40us). gn_stats reaches only 65% DRAM at 0.5 waves/SM, so the stats→final→apply chain is exposed, not bandwidth-limited.

Optimisation method:
Fuse gn_final into gn_stats: one kernel per chunk that computes partials, then a __threadfence + atomicAdd 'last-block-done' finalizer computes mean/rstd in the same launch, with the block grid (P) raised so gn_stats reaches ~1 full wave. Justified by E1 (gn_final: 1.8% DRAM, 5.3% occupancy, 0.03 waves ⇒ pure latency) and E2 (the P·32 partials are read from L2 by the finishing block instead of a fresh grid, removing a global round-trip and 8 launches/forward).

Method name:
reduction_kernel_fusion_lastblock

Modification plan:
COMPOSITION CHECK (nothing removed): L2 chunk loop, 2-stream fork/join, CUDA-graph capture, cuDNN exhaustive autotune all stay; the change is strictly inside stats_chunk(), which still runs once per L2 chunk.

1. Delete gn_final_kernel as a separate launch. In gn_stats_kernel add two params: `float* mean, float* rstd, unsigned int* cnt, float eps`. After the existing partial write (`psum[o]=s; psq[o]=q;` — unchanged, all entries still written even for empty hw ranges), insert:
   `__threadfence(); __shared__ unsigned int isLast; if(threadIdx.x==0){ unsigned old=atomicAdd(&cnt[blockIdx.y],1u); isLast=(old==gridDim.x-1);} __syncthreads(); if(!isLast) return; __threadfence();`
2. Finalizer body inside the last block (replaces gn_final): 256 threads, `g = threadIdx.x & 31`, `j = threadIdx.x >> 5` (0..7); each thread does `double s=0,q=0; for(int p=j;p<P;p+=8){ long long o=((long long)blockIdx.y*P+p)*32+g; s+=psum[o]; q+=psq[o]; }` — consecutive threads read consecutive g, so this also fixes gn_final's 87%-excessive-sector uncoalesced access. Reduce the 8 j-partials per group through `__shared__ double sm[8][32]` in fixed order j=0..7 (deterministic), then thread j==0 writes `mean[n*32+g]`, `rstd[n*32+g] = 1/sqrt(max(v,0)+eps)` using the same double math as today (cnt = HW*8). Finally `if(threadIdx.x==0) cnt[blockIdx.y]=0;` so the counter is self-resetting and graph replay is safe.
3. Host: in stats_chunk() allocate nothing new; in gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw / gn_silu_res_nchw_out allocate ONE `auto cnt = torch::zeros({ic}, opts.dtype(torch::kInt32));` per call (one memset node per call replaces 8 kernel launches) and pass `cnt.data_ptr<int>()` offset per chunk. Launch only `gn_stats_kernel<<<dim3(P,nb),256>>>`; remove the gn_final launch and its `C10_CUDA_KERNEL_LAUNCH_CHECK`.
4. Re-tune pick_P for the fused kernel: `p = clamp(ceil(HW/32), 1, 2048/nb)` and additionally raise p until `nb*p >= 680` (4 blocks/SM on 170 SMs) when HW allows at least 8 elements per block, i.e. `p = min(p_max_by_work, max(p, ceil(680/nb)))` with `p_max_by_work = ceil(HW/8)`. This lifts gn_stats from 0.5 waves/SM (46% occupancy, 65% DRAM) toward ~1 wave. Keep P as an int passed to the kernel; the empty-chunk guard (`hw0<hw1`) already covers HW not divisible by P (e.g. HW=17161).
5. Correctness guards: P blocks per image all increment cnt exactly once (including empty-range blocks) so the last-block test is exact; partial buffers sized ic*P*32 unchanged; keep double accumulation.
6. Keep gn_silu_apply / gn_silu_res_t byte-for-byte as today (reverse traversal, float4 loads, fused residual+transpose) so the L2 chunk-resident reuse and the fused epilogue are untouched.
7. Validate all four shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131) against the reference at atol 2.8e-3, and confirm graph capture still succeeds (fallback path must also compile with the new signature).

Evidence:
gn_final_kernel: 4,960ns duration, gpu__dram_throughput 1.82%, achieved occupancy 5.32%, 0.03 waves/SM, 32,896 sectors of which 28,672 (87%) excessive — it moves ~64KB yet costs 5us, i.e. 100% launch/tail latency; 8 launches/forward ≈ 40us of a 1,866us forward. gn_stats: 0.5 waves/SM, 46.5% achieved occupancy, only 65.1% DRAM while long_scoreboard = 94.9% ⇒ latency-starved, more blocks will help. Round-7 classification: (a) — its predicted metric DID move (gn_silu_apply DRAM 84.0→62.5%, duration 14.1→18.1us, i.e. real conv/GN contention/overlap) yet the score fell 2.9%, so conv-vs-GN overlap is a dead end; the useful move is removing epilogue launches/latency, which composes with L2 chunking, streams and graph capture. Refutation of the alternative 'conv is the target': the steady-state conv (cutlass_tensorop_s1688fprop, 392us/launch x4 per forward ≈ 1.57ms) already runs at ~94% of 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak; the 178ms conv2d_grouped_direct entry is warm-up autotune, not steady state.

Expected metric change:
(1) gn_final_kernel disappears from the profile; forward kernel launches drop by 8 per forward (nsys total ~382 → ~350) and graph node count falls correspondingly. (2) gn_stats_kernel: waves_per_multiprocessor 0.50 → ≥0.9, sm__warps_active 46.5% → >65%, gpu__dram_throughput 65% → 78-88%, duration per launch ≤ its current 15.5us. (3) Wall time: mid shape 1.866 → ≤1.83ms; small shapes gain most (launch-latency dominated). Anti-regression: gn_silu_apply and gn_silu_res_t durations must not rise >3% (their L2 chunk reuse must be preserved); CUDA-graph capture must still succeed (a capture failure shows as launch count and CPU time rising); the cuDNN autotuned engine must remain the cutlass tensorop TF32 kernel (conv duration within 2%); max abs error ≤2.8e-3 on all four shapes, especially 1x256x131x131 where HW=17161 is not divisible by P and empty-range blocks must still write zeros AND increment the counter.

pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM-bandwidth-bound epilogue] gn_silu_res_t (31.1us/launch, 201MB/forward) plus gn_silu_apply/gn_stats. All sit at 82-87% DRAM SOL with only 12-19% SM throughput, and lts__t_sector_hit_rate is 1.99-2.39%: the conv-output chunk gn_stats reads is re-read by the apply kernel microseconds later yet comes entirely from DRAM. Bytes moved, not latency, set the epilogue wall time.

Optimisation method:
L2 eviction-policy hints on the non-reused streams: issue the residual-x load, the final NCHW output store, the transpose's x load and the apply's last-use y load as streaming/evict-first (__ldcs/__stcs), while the gn_stats read of the conv-output chunk uses __ldcg (L2-resident, L1-bypass). This stops the ~34MB/chunk of write-once/read-once traffic from evicting the 16.8MB chunk that must survive from gn_stats to gn_silu_apply/gn_silu_res_t, converting a second DRAM read into an L2 hit. Composes with existing chunking, streams, graph capture.

Method name:
l2_evict_policy_hints

Modification plan:
Checklist (numbered; each item is a focused edit inside _CUDA_SRC; no host-side structural change).
1. gn_silu_res_t (hottest kernel) — mark its three zero-reuse arrays evict-first: (a) in the load phase replace `const float v = base[(long long)hw * CTOT];` with `const float v = __ldcs(&base[(long long)hw * CTOT]);`; (b) in the store phase replace `out[o] = sm[lh*65+cl] + res[o];` with `const float r0 = __ldcs(&res[o]); __stcs(&out[o], sm[lh*65+cl] + r0);`. Rationale: y2 is dead after this read, res(x) is never read again, out is never re-read — all three must not occupy L2 at evict-normal priority.
2. gn_stats_kernel — make the chunk L2-resident: replace `float v = base[(long long)i * CTOT];` with `float v = __ldcg(&base[(long long)i * CTOT]);` (cache in L2, bypass L1; L1 hit rate is 1.35% so nothing is lost). This is the read whose lines must survive until the matching apply kernel.
3. gn_silu_apply — last-use read: replace `const float4 v = y[o];` with `const float4 v = __ldcs(y + o);`. Keep `out[o] = o4;` at default (that buffer is immediately re-read by conv2, so it must stay evict-normal). Keep w/b loads default (64 float4, broadcast).
4. nchw2nhwc_kernel — replace `sm[lh*65+cl] = src[nbaseS + (long long)(c0+cl)*HW + hw];` with `__ldcs(&src[...])`. x is not touched again for ~600MB of traffic. Leave the dst store default (conv1 consumes xl immediately).
5. Portability guard: if any `__ldcs`/`__stcs` overload is unavailable for the type, fall back to inline PTX helpers defined once at the top of _CUDA_SRC: `__device__ __forceinline__ float ld_cs(const float* p){float v; asm volatile("ld.global.cs.f32 %0,[%1];":"=f"(v):"l"(p):"memory"); return v;}` and `st_cs` using `st.global.cs.f32`; float4 via `ld.global.cs.v4.f32`. Use the helpers uniformly so the diff is mechanical.
6. Do NOT change: grids, block sizes, chunk_imgs()/pick_P() values, the stats->final->apply sequence, the two-stream fork/join with evStage, the CUDA-graph capture/replay cache, or the cuDNN exhaustive autotune. Launch count must stay ~382 and the graph node list must be byte-identical in shape; the base's multistream_pipeline, cuda_graph_capture, cudnn_conv_engine_autotune and l2_cache_blocking all remain operational — this method strengthens l2_cache_blocking rather than replacing it (its hit rate is currently ~2%).
7. Bounds/semantics: cache hints are value-neutral; keep every `if (hw < HW)` guard and the empty-chunk psum/psq writes exactly as-is so the awkward shape 1x256x131x131 (HW=17161, odd, P may exceed HW) still writes every partial slot. Reductions stay float/double as today.
8. Build: no flag changes (no fast-math); recompile with the same -gencode=arch=compute_120,code=sm_120.
9. Verification order: (i) correctness on all four shapes, max abs err <= 2.8e-3; (ii) NCU re-run checking lts__t_sector_hit_rate on gn_silu_apply and gn_silu_res_t; (iii) nsys check that launch count and conv kernel identity/duration are unchanged.
10. If the hit rate does not move on the 4x256x256x256 shape (one image = 67MB, chunking cannot help there), leave it — the hints are still neutral for that shape; do not add a second mechanism in this round.

Evidence:
Numeric: gn_silu_apply lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 1.99%, gn_silu_res_t = 2.02%, gn_stats = 2.39%, while gpu__dram_throughput = 83.7% / 82.6% / 72.6% and sm__throughput = 19.0% / 12.7% / 6.0% — bytes-bound with zero realised reuse. Per forward the epilogue moves ~603MB (transpose 134, stats 134, apply 134, res+transpose 201) = ~336us at 1792 GB/s, i.e. ~18% of the 1.866ms forward; the two convs already run ~95% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak, so only byte reduction is available. Root cause: gn_stats reads the exact 16.8MB chunk that the apply kernel re-reads a few microseconds later, but the concurrently-live zero-reuse streams (residual x 16.8MB/chunk, output 16.8MB/chunk, transpose 33.5MB) share L2 at evict-normal priority and flush it. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_stats is latency-bound (0.5 waves/SM, 92.7% long-scoreboard, 72.6% DRAM) so vectorize/fuse it': NCU serialises kernels, so that headroom is an artefact — in production both streams' GN kernels run in phase and jointly saturate DRAM; round 8 acted on exactly that latency reading and regressed 4.94%. Round 8 classification: (b) — its predicted gn_stats improvement did not occur (DRAM 72.6%->40.25%, duration 13.76->27.5us, 9 divergent branch targets/warp), so the fusion engaged but wrecked the load loop; I am nonetheless switching to an independent mechanism that composes with, instead of restructuring, the base's chunking.

Expected metric change:
(1) lts__t_sector_hit_rate: gn_silu_apply 1.99% -> >20%, gn_silu_res_t 2.02% -> >15% (mid and small shapes; the 4x256x256x256 shape may stay flat since one image is 67MB). (2) gn_silu_res_t duration 31.1us -> <=27us and its gpu__dram_throughput FALLS from 82.6% (bytes served from L2, not DRAM) — a duration drop with a DRAM-% drop is the success signature, not a regression. (3) Anti-regression constraints: total forward launch count must stay ~382 and CUDA-graph replay must still be used (a capture failure shows as launch count and CPU time rising); the autotuned conv must remain the cutlass tensorop TF32 NHWC kernel with duration within 2%; nchw2nhwc duration must not rise >3% (its __ldcs must not degrade its 87% DRAM SOL); gn_stats duration must not rise (>__ldcg is L1-bypass only); max abs error <= 2.8e-3 on all four shapes including 1x256x131x131; no individual shape may regress more than 1%.

pairs.a_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[latency/launch-overhead-bound sub-segment inside the DRAM-bound GN epilogue] gn_final_kernel + gn_stats_kernel. gn_final runs 4.96us at 0.03 waves/SM, 5.3% achieved occupancy, 1.8% DRAM, 87% excessive sectors — pure launch/tail latency, 8 launches/forward (~40us). gn_stats reaches only 65% DRAM at 0.5 waves/SM, so the stats→final→apply chain is exposed, not bandwidth-limited.

Optimisation method:
Fuse gn_final into gn_stats: one kernel per chunk that computes partials, then a __threadfence + atomicAdd 'last-block-done' finalizer computes mean/rstd in the same launch, with the block grid (P) raised so gn_stats reaches ~1 full wave. Justified by E1 (gn_final: 1.8% DRAM, 5.3% occupancy, 0.03 waves ⇒ pure latency) and E2 (the P·32 partials are read from L2 by the finishing block instead of a fresh grid, removing a global round-trip and 8 launches/forward).

Method name:
reduction_kernel_fusion_lastblock

Modification plan:
COMPOSITION CHECK (nothing removed): L2 chunk loop, 2-stream fork/join, CUDA-graph capture, cuDNN exhaustive autotune all stay; the change is strictly inside stats_chunk(), which still runs once per L2 chunk.

1. Delete gn_final_kernel as a separate launch. In gn_stats_kernel add two params: `float* mean, float* rstd, unsigned int* cnt, float eps`. After the existing partial write (`psum[o]=s; psq[o]=q;` — unchanged, all entries still written even for empty hw ranges), insert:
   `__threadfence(); __shared__ unsigned int isLast; if(threadIdx.x==0){ unsigned old=atomicAdd(&cnt[blockIdx.y],1u); isLast=(old==gridDim.x-1);} __syncthreads(); if(!isLast) return; __threadfence();`
2. Finalizer body inside the last block (replaces gn_final): 256 threads, `g = threadIdx.x & 31`, `j = threadIdx.x >> 5` (0..7); each thread does `double s=0,q=0; for(int p=j;p<P;p+=8){ long long o=((long long)blockIdx.y*P+p)*32+g; s+=psum[o]; q+=psq[o]; }` — consecutive threads read consecutive g, so this also fixes gn_final's 87%-excessive-sector uncoalesced access. Reduce the 8 j-partials per group through `__shared__ double sm[8][32]` in fixed order j=0..7 (deterministic), then thread j==0 writes `mean[n*32+g]`, `rstd[n*32+g] = 1/sqrt(max(v,0)+eps)` using the same double math as today (cnt = HW*8). Finally `if(threadIdx.x==0) cnt[blockIdx.y]=0;` so the counter is self-resetting and graph replay is safe.
3. Host: in stats_chunk() allocate nothing new; in gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw / gn_silu_res_nchw_out allocate ONE `auto cnt = torch::zeros({ic}, opts.dtype(torch::kInt32));` per call (one memset node per call replaces 8 kernel launches) and pass `cnt.data_ptr<int>()` offset per chunk. Launch only `gn_stats_kernel<<<dim3(P,nb),256>>>`; remove the gn_final launch and its `C10_CUDA_KERNEL_LAUNCH_CHECK`.
4. Re-tune pick_P for the fused kernel: `p = clamp(ceil(HW/32), 1, 2048/nb)` and additionally raise p until `nb*p >= 680` (4 blocks/SM on 170 SMs) when HW allows at least 8 elements per block, i.e. `p = min(p_max_by_work, max(p, ceil(680/nb)))` with `p_max_by_work = ceil(HW/8)`. This lifts gn_stats from 0.5 waves/SM (46% occupancy, 65% DRAM) toward ~1 wave. Keep P as an int passed to the kernel; the empty-chunk guard (`hw0<hw1`) already covers HW not divisible by P (e.g. HW=17161).
5. Correctness guards: P blocks per image all increment cnt exactly once (including empty-range blocks) so the last-block test is exact; partial buffers sized ic*P*32 unchanged; keep double accumulation.
6. Keep gn_silu_apply / gn_silu_res_t byte-for-byte as today (reverse traversal, float4 loads, fused residual+transpose) so the L2 chunk-resident reuse and the fused epilogue are untouched.
7. Validate all four shapes (8x256x64x128, 2x256x64x64, 4x256x256x256, 1x256x131x131) against the reference at atol 2.8e-3, and confirm graph capture still succeeds (fallback path must also compile with the new signature).

Evidence:
gn_final_kernel: 4,960ns duration, gpu__dram_throughput 1.82%, achieved occupancy 5.32%, 0.03 waves/SM, 32,896 sectors of which 28,672 (87%) excessive — it moves ~64KB yet costs 5us, i.e. 100% launch/tail latency; 8 launches/forward ≈ 40us of a 1,866us forward. gn_stats: 0.5 waves/SM, 46.5% achieved occupancy, only 65.1% DRAM while long_scoreboard = 94.9% ⇒ latency-starved, more blocks will help. Round-7 classification: (a) — its predicted metric DID move (gn_silu_apply DRAM 84.0→62.5%, duration 14.1→18.1us, i.e. real conv/GN contention/overlap) yet the score fell 2.9%, so conv-vs-GN overlap is a dead end; the useful move is removing epilogue launches/latency, which composes with L2 chunking, streams and graph capture. Refutation of the alternative 'conv is the target': the steady-state conv (cutlass_tensorop_s1688fprop, 392us/launch x4 per forward ≈ 1.57ms) already runs at ~94% of 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak; the 178ms conv2d_grouped_direct entry is warm-up autotune, not steady state.

Expected metric change:
(1) gn_final_kernel disappears from the profile; forward kernel launches drop by 8 per forward (nsys total ~382 → ~350) and graph node count falls correspondingly. (2) gn_stats_kernel: waves_per_multiprocessor 0.50 → ≥0.9, sm__warps_active 46.5% → >65%, gpu__dram_throughput 65% → 78-88%, duration per launch ≤ its current 15.5us. (3) Wall time: mid shape 1.866 → ≤1.83ms; small shapes gain most (launch-latency dominated). Anti-regression: gn_silu_apply and gn_silu_res_t durations must not rise >3% (their L2 chunk reuse must be preserved); CUDA-graph capture must still succeed (a capture failure shows as launch count and CPU time rising); the cuDNN autotuned engine must remain the cutlass tensorop TF32 kernel (conv duration within 2%); max abs error ≤2.8e-3 on all four shapes, especially 1x256x131x131 where HW=17161 is not divisible by P and empty-range blocks must still write zeros AND increment the counter.
pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM-bandwidth-bound epilogue] gn_silu_res_t (31.1us/launch, 201MB/forward) plus gn_silu_apply/gn_stats. All sit at 82-87% DRAM SOL with only 12-19% SM throughput, and lts__t_sector_hit_rate is 1.99-2.39%: the conv-output chunk gn_stats reads is re-read by the apply kernel microseconds later yet comes entirely from DRAM. Bytes moved, not latency, set the epilogue wall time.

Optimisation method:
L2 eviction-policy hints on the non-reused streams: issue the residual-x load, the final NCHW output store, the transpose's x load and the apply's last-use y load as streaming/evict-first (__ldcs/__stcs), while the gn_stats read of the conv-output chunk uses __ldcg (L2-resident, L1-bypass). This stops the ~34MB/chunk of write-once/read-once traffic from evicting the 16.8MB chunk that must survive from gn_stats to gn_silu_apply/gn_silu_res_t, converting a second DRAM read into an L2 hit. Composes with existing chunking, streams, graph capture.

Method name:
l2_evict_policy_hints

Modification plan:
Checklist (numbered; each item is a focused edit inside _CUDA_SRC; no host-side structural change).
1. gn_silu_res_t (hottest kernel) — mark its three zero-reuse arrays evict-first: (a) in the load phase replace `const float v = base[(long long)hw * CTOT];` with `const float v = __ldcs(&base[(long long)hw * CTOT]);`; (b) in the store phase replace `out[o] = sm[lh*65+cl] + res[o];` with `const float r0 = __ldcs(&res[o]); __stcs(&out[o], sm[lh*65+cl] + r0);`. Rationale: y2 is dead after this read, res(x) is never read again, out is never re-read — all three must not occupy L2 at evict-normal priority.
2. gn_stats_kernel — make the chunk L2-resident: replace `float v = base[(long long)i * CTOT];` with `float v = __ldcg(&base[(long long)i * CTOT]);` (cache in L2, bypass L1; L1 hit rate is 1.35% so nothing is lost). This is the read whose lines must survive until the matching apply kernel.
3. gn_silu_apply — last-use read: replace `const float4 v = y[o];` with `const float4 v = __ldcs(y + o);`. Keep `out[o] = o4;` at default (that buffer is immediately re-read by conv2, so it must stay evict-normal). Keep w/b loads default (64 float4, broadcast).
4. nchw2nhwc_kernel — replace `sm[lh*65+cl] = src[nbaseS + (long long)(c0+cl)*HW + hw];` with `__ldcs(&src[...])`. x is not touched again for ~600MB of traffic. Leave the dst store default (conv1 consumes xl immediately).
5. Portability guard: if any `__ldcs`/`__stcs` overload is unavailable for the type, fall back to inline PTX helpers defined once at the top of _CUDA_SRC: `__device__ __forceinline__ float ld_cs(const float* p){float v; asm volatile("ld.global.cs.f32 %0,[%1];":"=f"(v):"l"(p):"memory"); return v;}` and `st_cs` using `st.global.cs.f32`; float4 via `ld.global.cs.v4.f32`. Use the helpers uniformly so the diff is mechanical.
6. Do NOT change: grids, block sizes, chunk_imgs()/pick_P() values, the stats->final->apply sequence, the two-stream fork/join with evStage, the CUDA-graph capture/replay cache, or the cuDNN exhaustive autotune. Launch count must stay ~382 and the graph node list must be byte-identical in shape; the base's multistream_pipeline, cuda_graph_capture, cudnn_conv_engine_autotune and l2_cache_blocking all remain operational — this method strengthens l2_cache_blocking rather than replacing it (its hit rate is currently ~2%).
7. Bounds/semantics: cache hints are value-neutral; keep every `if (hw < HW)` guard and the empty-chunk psum/psq writes exactly as-is so the awkward shape 1x256x131x131 (HW=17161, odd, P may exceed HW) still writes every partial slot. Reductions stay float/double as today.
8. Build: no flag changes (no fast-math); recompile with the same -gencode=arch=compute_120,code=sm_120.
9. Verification order: (i) correctness on all four shapes, max abs err <= 2.8e-3; (ii) NCU re-run checking lts__t_sector_hit_rate on gn_silu_apply and gn_silu_res_t; (iii) nsys check that launch count and conv kernel identity/duration are unchanged.
10. If the hit rate does not move on the 4x256x256x256 shape (one image = 67MB, chunking cannot help there), leave it — the hints are still neutral for that shape; do not add a second mechanism in this round.

Evidence:
Numeric: gn_silu_apply lts__t_sector_hit_rate = 1.99%, gn_silu_res_t = 2.02%, gn_stats = 2.39%, while gpu__dram_throughput = 83.7% / 82.6% / 72.6% and sm__throughput = 19.0% / 12.7% / 6.0% — bytes-bound with zero realised reuse. Per forward the epilogue moves ~603MB (transpose 134, stats 134, apply 134, res+transpose 201) = ~336us at 1792 GB/s, i.e. ~18% of the 1.866ms forward; the two convs already run ~95% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak, so only byte reduction is available. Root cause: gn_stats reads the exact 16.8MB chunk that the apply kernel re-reads a few microseconds later, but the concurrently-live zero-reuse streams (residual x 16.8MB/chunk, output 16.8MB/chunk, transpose 33.5MB) share L2 at evict-normal priority and flush it. Refutation of the alternative 'gn_stats is latency-bound (0.5 waves/SM, 92.7% long-scoreboard, 72.6% DRAM) so vectorize/fuse it': NCU serialises kernels, so that headroom is an artefact — in production both streams' GN kernels run in phase and jointly saturate DRAM; round 8 acted on exactly that latency reading and regressed 4.94%. Round 8 classification: (b) — its predicted gn_stats improvement did not occur (DRAM 72.6%->40.25%, duration 13.76->27.5us, 9 divergent branch targets/warp), so the fusion engaged but wrecked the load loop; I am nonetheless switching to an independent mechanism that composes with, instead of restructuring, the base's chunking.

Expected metric change:
(1) lts__t_sector_hit_rate: gn_silu_apply 1.99% -> >20%, gn_silu_res_t 2.02% -> >15% (mid and small shapes; the 4x256x256x256 shape may stay flat since one image is 67MB). (2) gn_silu_res_t duration 31.1us -> <=27us and its gpu__dram_throughput FALLS from 82.6% (bytes served from L2, not DRAM) — a duration drop with a DRAM-% drop is the success signature, not a regression. (3) Anti-regression constraints: total forward launch count must stay ~382 and CUDA-graph replay must still be used (a capture failure shows as launch count and CPU time rising); the autotuned conv must remain the cutlass tensorop TF32 NHWC kernel with duration within 2%; nchw2nhwc duration must not rise >3% (its __ldcs must not degrade its 87% DRAM SOL); gn_stats duration must not rise (>__ldcg is L1-bypass only); max abs error <= 2.8e-3 on all four shapes including 1x256x131x131; no individual shape may regress more than 1%.

pairs.a_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[latency/occupancy-exposure, not per-kernel bound] Hottest non-removable segment is the cuDNN TF32 NHWC conv pair (~90% of forward work, ~417us per half-batch launch ≈ 93 TFLOPS ≈ 89% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak, so nearly SOL). The residual loss is our ~404us of DRAM-bound GN/transpose kernels (72–88% DRAM, 6–19% SM) that only partly overlap the convs: 1668us conv + 404us GN = 2072us work but 1855us wall ⇒ ~187us still exposed.

Optimisation method:
Compute/memory stream phase-staggering: keep the two-stream batch pipeline but offset stream B by a full conv stage (wait on an event recorded AFTER stream A's conv1, not after its transpose) and use 4 finer batch chunks round-robined over the 2 streams, plus lower the multistream threshold to B>=2. Metrics justify it: GN kernels are 72–88% DRAM / <19% SM while convs are ~89% TF32-SOL / low DRAM — complementary units, so co-residency hides the 187us exposed memory time instead of running GN||GN and conv||conv in lockstep.

Method name:
compute_mem_stream_stagger

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST (exact code actions, Python side only; CUDA source unchanged)
1. In `_run_pipeline` (and mirrored in `_forward_eager`), replace the fixed 2-way split `s0=B//2` with a chunk list: `K = 4 if B>=4 else (B if B>=2 else 1)`; build `bounds = [round(i*B/K) for i in range(K+1)]`, dropping empty chunks. Chunk i is assigned to stream `sA if (i%2)==0 else sB`. This keeps per-sample independence (GroupNorm is per (n,group)), so numerics are unchanged.
2. Move the stagger marker: today `evStage.record(sA)` fires right after chunk0's `nchw2nhwc` and stream B starts immediately, so both streams execute the SAME stage type at the same time (conv||conv, GN||GN) and never overlap compute with memory. Instead record `evStage` on sA immediately AFTER `ya = F.conv2d(xla, w1c, ...)` of chunk 0, and have every stream-B chunk's first op wait on it (`sB.wait_event(evStage)`). Result: stream B's transpose+conv1 run while stream A executes its memory-bound gn_stats/gn_final/gn_silu_apply, and vice-versa.
3. Keep exactly one event per stream per chunk to preserve graph-capturability: allocate `self._evs = [torch.cuda.Event() for _ in range(8)]` lazily (same lazy/try-except fallback style as `_get_streams`), and use `self._evs[i]` for chunk i. All events are created once in `__init__`/lazy path, never inside capture.
4. Loop body per chunk i (unchanged op order, so all existing mechanisms survive): `xi = x[b0:b1]`; `xli = ext.nchw_to_nhwc(xi)`; `yi = F.conv2d(xli, w1c, None,1,1)`; if i==0: `evStage.record(sA)`; `yi = ext.gn_silu_nhwc(yi, nw1, nb1, eps)`; `yi = F.conv2d(yi, w2c, None,1,1)`; `ext.gn_silu_res_nchw_out(yi, xi, nw2, nb2, eps, out[b0:b1])`; `ev[i].record(stream_i)`.
5. Join: `cur.wait_event(ev[i])` for every chunk i. Output tensor is one `torch.empty_like(x)` written through the existing out-parameter kernel — no extra allocation, no extra traffic.
6. Lower the fallback threshold from `B < 4` to `B < 2`, so the 2x256x64x64 shape (currently fully serial, only 1.126x) also gets conv/GN overlap. B==1 (131x131 shape) keeps the single-stream path verbatim.
7. Guard against too-small convs: if `B//K < 1` or `B*H*W/K < 65536` elements per chunk, fall back to K=2. This prevents cuDNN plan degradation on the small shape.
8. Preservation audit (no listed mechanism removed): multistream_pipeline (round 3) is EXTENDED, not removed — same 2 streams, deeper phase offset and finer chunking; cuda_graph_capture still captures the whole DAG (event record/wait across streams is legal in capture and already used); cudnn_conv_engine_autotune still runs once per (shape,dtype,layout) key during warm-up — note K changes the per-conv batch, so autotune must run on the SAME chunked pipeline (it already calls `_run_pipeline`, so the tuned plans match the captured shapes); l2_cache_blocking and l2_evict_policy_hints are untouched inside the extension (per-call chunk loop and PTX hints unchanged).
9. Keep `record_stream` bookkeeping in the eager path for every chunk slice on both streams (x, out, weights) to avoid caching-allocator reuse hazards.
10. Validate all 4 shapes; if the small or awkward shape regresses, keep K=2 for B<4 while retaining the conv-stage offset of item 2 (that offset alone is the primary win).

Evidence:
Numeric: conv ≈417us/launch for a half-batch (7517us/18) = 3.87e10 FLOP/417us ≈ 93 TFLOPS ≈ 89% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak; our five kernels sum 404us/forward (res_t 36us x4, stats 13.2 x8, apply 14.6 x4, transpose 29 x2, final 4.7 x8) while measured wall is 1855us against ~1668us of conv work ⇒ ~187us (10%) of memory work is NOT hidden. Root cause: both streams were forked with only a transpose-length offset, so identical-duration stages drift into lockstep (conv||conv, GN||GN), leaving no compute/memory pairing; GN kernels show sm__throughput 6.2–19.2% with gpu__dram_throughput 72–88%, convs the inverse. Refutation of 'DRAM-bound epilogue is the bottleneck': even driving all five kernels to 100% DRAM SOL saves <60us, and refutation of 'suboptimal conv plan': the autotuned engine already sits at ~89% of TF32 SOL, so <11% is reachable there and only via vendor-internal changes.

Expected metric change:
(1) Wall time per forward down 5–10% at the mid/large shapes and up to ~8% at 2x256x64x64 (threshold lowered to B>=2); (2) during conv kernels gpu__dram_throughput rises (GN traffic now co-resident) while per-launch conv duration stays within +3% — if conv duration inflates >5% the offset is causing SM contention and K must drop to 2; (3) sum of gn_* kernel durations must stay flat (±2%) — these kernels are untouched, only their placement changes. Anti-regression guards: kernel launch count per forward may rise (4 chunks) but must remain inside a single captured graph (graph replay count per forward stays 1; if `_graphs[key] is False` appears, capture broke and the change must be reverted); cuDNN autotune must still fire once per shape (watch that conv2d_grouped_direct_kernel trial launches do not reappear in steady state); no change in output tolerance (bitwise-identical kernels, per-sample-independent chunking).
pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[latency/launch-overhead-bound sub-segment inside a DRAM-bound epilogue] The vendor TF32 NHWC convs (~1668us/forward, ~89% of TF32 SOL) are default-keep mainloops. The hottest segment we control is the GroupNorm chain gn_stats -> gn_final -> apply/res_t (396us/forward). gn_final is 8 launches x 5.2us = 41.6us/forward doing only ~1.3us of work (0.03 waves/SM, 5.4% achieved occupancy, 1.84% DRAM): pure launch/drain latency sitting on each stream's critical path.

Optimisation method:
Reduction-kernel fusion: delete gn_final by folding its final reduction into gn_stats_kernel with a deadlock-free 'last-arriving block' pattern (__threadfence + atomicAdd on a self-resetting arrival counter). Justified by E1+E2: gn_final shows 12543 elapsed vs 3131 active cycles, 0.03 waves, 1.84% DRAM — 75% of its time is launch/drain, not work; the work it does (nb*32 groups x P partials, 88.9% L2 hit) is re-executed inside the single last gn_stats block essentially for free, removing 8 launches and 8 stream dependencies per forward.

Method name:
reduction_kernel_fusion

Modification plan:
1. gn_stats_kernel: after the existing `psum[o]=s; psq[o]=q;` writes add `__threadfence();` then a single arrival vote: `__shared__ int last; if(threadIdx.x==0){int old=atomicAdd(&cnt[slot],1); last=(old==gridDim.x*gridDim.y-1);} __syncthreads(); if(!last) return;`. Non-last blocks EXIT (no spin-wait) => no residency requirement, no deadlock, multistream concurrency untouched.
2. In the surviving last block run gn_final's exact math for all nb*NGRP groups, then self-reset: set `tpg = max(1, blockDim.x/(nb*NGRP))` lanes per group (nb*32 in {32,64,128} => tpg in {8,4,2}, power of two, lanes contiguous in a warp); thread t owns gid=t/tpg, l=t%tpg and accumulates `double s,q` over p=l, l+tpg, ... from psum/psq (consecutive threads read consecutive g at fixed p => 128B-coalesced, all L2 hits); reduce the tpg lanes with __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, ...); lane l==0 computes cnt=(double)HW*CPG, m=ts/cnt, v=max(0,tq/cnt-m*m), writes mean[gid]=(float)m, rstd[gid]=(float)(1.0/sqrt(v+eps)); finally `if(threadIdx.x==0) cnt[slot]=0;` so the counter is 0 for the next launch/replay.
3. Kernel signature: gn_stats_kernel(y, HW, P, psum, psq, mean, rstd, eps, nb, cnt+slot). Keep grid=(P,nb), block=256, keep ld_cg on the chunk read, keep the reverse-traversal apply, keep every existing evict-policy hint verbatim.
4. Delete gn_final_kernel and its launch from stats_chunk(); stats_chunk now issues exactly ONE kernel. All three host wrappers (gn_silu_nhwc, gn_silu_res_nchw, gn_silu_res_nchw_out) keep their identical chunk loops, so l2_cache_blocking is preserved bit-for-bit.
5. Counter storage (graph-safe): a file-static pool `static int* g_cnt` of NSLOT=64 ints, allocated once by a `std::call_once` helper doing cudaMalloc + cudaMemset(0). Host side keeps `static int slot_rr` and each stats_chunk call takes `int s = slot_rr++ % NSLOT`. Allocation therefore happens on the first eager/warm-up call (the model always runs >=3 warm-up iterations plus autotune before capture), never inside a capture region; during capture the pointer and slot index are baked into the node, and the last-block reset keeps the slot at 0 across replays. Two concurrent streams get different slots because they are different call sites in capture order.
6. Numerics: psum/psq are still WRITTEN (not accumulated), so no zero-init is needed and no atomics touch float data; the only change is the intra-block summation order of the double accumulation (tpg-strided instead of blockDim-strided), giving ~1e-15 relative drift on mean/rstd vs atol 2.8e-3. No dtype changes anywhere.
7. Guard generality: if nb*NGRP > blockDim.x use a `for(idx=threadIdx.x; idx<nb*NGRP; idx+=blockDim.x)` fallback with tpg=1; if P==0 or the grid is 1 block the same path still runs (old==0==gridDim-1).
8. Mechanism accounting: nothing is removed. multistream_pipeline (per-call slots, no grid-wide sync), cuda_graph_capture (static pointers, fixed node list, node count DROPS by 8), cudnn_conv_engine_autotune (host path untouched), l2_cache_blocking (chunk loop identical), l2_evict_policy_hints (ld_cs/ld_cg/st_cs untouched) all stay operational.
9. Verify: per-forward launch count drops 22 -> 14 on the mid shape; nsys must show gn_final_kernel gone and gn_stats_kernel launch count unchanged at 32.

Evidence:
Prior-attempt verdict: (ii) — the profiled 1.2028 attempt's per-kernel predictions did NOT move (gn_silu_apply 14112->15488ns WORSE, nchw2nhwc 27552->28416ns WORSE, res_t 34720->34880ns flat, lts__t_sector_hit_rate still 1.85->1.88%), so its +0.40% is unattributable to its mechanism; I therefore pick an independent target with its own evidence. Numeric evidence for this target: gn_final gpu__time_duration.avg=5248ns but sm__cycles_active.avg=3131 vs sm__cycles_elapsed.avg=12543 and launch__waves_per_multiprocessor=0.03, achieved occupancy 5.40%, gpu__dram_throughput=2.13% — i.e. ~75% of its 5.2us is launch/drain latency, and lts__t_sector_hit_rate=88.91% proves its input is already L2-resident so re-doing the work inside gn_stats costs ~1-2us on one SM. 8 such launches per forward = 41.6us of a 1855us wall. Root cause: an artificially split two-phase reduction adds a full kernel boundary per chunk per GroupNorm. Alternative bottleneck refuted: 'the conv is the lever' — 3.87e10 FLOP/417us = 93 TFLOPS = 89% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak and it is already engine-autotuned, so <11% is reachable and only inside the vendor library; 'L2 reuse of the conv output' is refuted as reachable here because under two concurrent streams the live set is ~16.8MB(read)+16.8MB(write)+~67MB(other stream's conv) > L2, which is exactly why the round-11 persisting attempt could not hold the chunk.

Expected metric change:
(1) gn_final_kernel disappears entirely from both NCU and nsys (launch count 32 -> 0 over 4 forwards; total forward launches 382 -> ~350). Method name:
compute_mem_stream_stagger

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST (exact code actions, Python side only; CUDA source unchanged)
1. In `_run_pipeline` (and mirrored in `_forward_eager`), replace the fixed 2-way split `s0=B//2` with a chunk list: `K = 4 if B>=4 else (B if B>=2 else 1)`; build `bounds = [round(i*B/K) for i in range(K+1)]`, dropping empty chunks. Chunk i is assigned to stream `sA if (i%2)==0 else sB`. This keeps per-sample independence (GroupNorm is per (n,group)), so numerics are unchanged.
2. Move the stagger marker: today `evStage.record(sA)` fires right after chunk0's `nchw2nhwc` and stream B starts immediately, so both streams execute the SAME stage type at the same time (conv||conv, GN||GN) and never overlap compute with memory. Instead record `evStage` on sA immediately AFTER `ya = F.conv2d(xla, w1c, ...)` of chunk 0, and have every stream-B chunk's first op wait on it (`sB.wait_event(evStage)`). Result: stream B's transpose+conv1 run while stream A executes its memory-bound gn_stats/gn_final/gn_silu_apply, and vice-versa.
3. Keep exactly one event per stream per chunk to preserve graph-capturability: allocate `self._evs = [torch.cuda.Event() for _ in range(8)]` lazily (same lazy/try-except fallback style as `_get_streams`), and use `self._evs[i]` for chunk i. All events are created once in `__init__`/lazy path, never inside capture.
4. Loop body per chunk i (unchanged op order, so all existing mechanisms survive): `xi = x[b0:b1]`; `xli = ext.nchw_to_nhwc(xi)`; `yi = F.conv2d(xli, w1c, None,1,1)`; if i==0: `evStage.record(sA)`; `yi = ext.gn_silu_nhwc(yi, nw1, nb1, eps)`; `yi = F.conv2d(yi, w2c, None,1,1)`; `ext.gn_silu_res_nchw_out(yi, xi, nw2, nb2, eps, out[b0:b1])`; `ev[i].record(stream_i)`.

7. Guard against too-small convs: if `B//K < 1` or `B*H*W/K < 65536` elements per chunk, fall back to K=2. This prevents cuDNN plan degradation on the small shape.
8. 9. Keep `record_stream` bookkeeping in the eager path for every chunk slice on both streams (x, out, weights) to avoid caching-allocator reuse hazards.
10. Validate all 4 shapes; if the small or awkward shape regresses, keep K=2 for B<4 while retaining the conv-stage offset of item 2 (that offset alone is the primary win).

Numeric: conv ≈417us/launch for a half-batch (7517us/18) = 3.87e10 FLOP/417us ≈ 93 TFLOPS ≈ 89% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak; our five kernels sum 404us/forward (res_t 36us x4, stats 13.2 x8, apply 14.6 x4, transpose 29 x2, final 4.7 x8) while measured wall is 1855us against ~1668us of conv work ⇒ ~187us (10%) of memory work is NOT hidden. Root cause: both streams were forked with only a transpose-length offset, so identical-duration stages drift into lockstep (conv||conv, GN||GN), leaving no compute/memory pairing; GN kernels show sm__throughput 6.2–19.2% with gpu__dram_throughput 72–88%, convs the inverse. Expected metric change:
(1) Wall time per forward down 5–10% at the mid/large shapes and up to ~8% at 2x256x64x64 (threshold lowered to B>=2); (2) during conv kernels gpu__dram_throughput rises (GN traffic now co-resident) while per-launch conv duration stays within +3% — if conv duration inflates >5% the offset is causing SM contention and K must drop to 2; (3) sum of gn_* kernel durations must stay flat (±2%) — these kernels are untouched, only their placement changes. Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM/memory-latency bound, insufficient bytes-in-flight] Hottest kernel we control after the default-keep cuDNN TF32 convs is gn_stats_kernel (8 launches x 13.57us = 109us/forward). It reads 16.8MB per launch with 4-byte scalar loads, hitting only 76.8% DRAM SOL vs 85% for the float4 gn_silu_apply, with 97.5% long-scoreboard stalls and 49% achieved occupancy (0.5 waves/SM).

Optimisation method:
mem_vectorize: replace the scalar per-channel ld.global.cg loads in gn_stats_kernel with 16B float4 (ld.global.cg.v4.f32) loads along the contiguous NHWC channel axis. Because C=256 and 8 channels/group, every float4 lies wholly inside one group, so the four components can be folded into one (sum, sumsq) accumulator — bit-legal, no dtype change. This cuts load instructions 4x and quadruples in-flight bytes per thread, which is exactly what a 97.5% long-scoreboard / 0.5-wave / 76.8%-DRAM kernel needs; grid, launch count, chunking, streams and graph capture are untouched.

Method name:
mem_vectorize

Modification plan:
Only gn_stats_kernel changes. Everything else (host chunk loop, pick_P, grids, launch counts, streams, graph capture, cuDNN autotune, evict hints) is byte-identical.

1. Add a vector cache-hint helper next to ld_cg:
   __device__ __forceinline__ float4 ld_cg4(const float4* p){ float4 v; asm("ld.global.cg.v4.f32 {%0,%1,%2,%3}, [%4];" : "=f"(v.x),"=f"(v.y),"=f"(v.z),"=f"(v.w) : "l"(p)); return v; }
   This preserves the already-accepted l2_evict_policy_hints mechanism (chunk stays L2-resident, L1 bypassed) in vectorized form.

2. Replace the 4 scalar strided loads per thread with one float4 row load: in gn_stats_kernel remap threads as c4 = threadIdx.x & 63 (float4 index over the 256 channels), row = threadIdx.x >> 6 (0..3). Keep grid (P, nb), block 256, same chunk math (chunk=(HW+P-1)/P, hw0=p*chunk, hw1=min(hw0+chunk,HW)). Loop `for (int i = row; i < cnt; i += 4)` loading
   float4 v = ld_cg4(reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(y) + ((long long)n*HW + hw0 + i)*64 + c4);
   and accumulate s += v.x+v.y+v.z+v.w;  q += v.x*v.x+v.y*v.y+v.z*v.z+v.w*v.w;  (float accumulators, unchanged precision contract). Keep `#pragma unroll 4` on the loop for MLP.

3. Group-correctness argument (why folding 4 channels into one accumulator is legal): channel = 4*c4 + {0,1,2,3}; group = channel>>3 = c4>>1, identical for all four components because 4 divides 8. So each float4 contributes entirely to group g = c4>>1.

4. Reduction rewrite (replaces the old 8-lane shfl):
   a. Warp step: lanes within a warp hold consecutive c4, so pairs (even,odd) share a group -> s += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffffu, s, 1); same for q.
   b. Cross-row step: __shared__ float ss[4][32], sq[4][32] (1024B total, same as today's shared usage, so occupancy limits are unchanged). If ((c4 & 1) == 0) { ss[row][c4>>1] = s; sq[row][c4>>1] = q; } __syncthreads();
   c. Final: threads 0..31 (g = threadIdx.x) do float S = ss[0][g]+ss[1][g]+ss[2][g]+ss[3][g] (same for Q) and store psum[((n*P+p)*NGRP)+g] = S, psq[...] = Q. Every one of the nb*P*NGRP slots is written unconditionally, including empty chunks (cnt<=0 leaves accumulators at 0) — this is the tail-safety invariant the awkward 131x131 shape depends on.

5. Alignment check: y is channels_last contiguous, row stride = 256 floats = 1024B, torch allocations are >=512B aligned, and hw offsets multiply the 1024B row stride, so every float4 address is 16B aligned for all four scored shapes (including HW=17161).

6. Register/occupancy guard: keep the kernel free of extra state (no extra pointers/flags); target launch__registers_per_thread <= 24 so launch__occupancy_limit_registers stays >= 10 and the warp limit (6 blocks) remains the binding constraint, as today.

7. Leave gn_final_kernel, gn_silu_apply, gn_silu_res_t, nchw2nhwc_kernel, the L2 chunk loop, the two-stream fork/join, _try_capture and the _Autotune context manager completely unmodified — no listed mechanism is removed or bypassed by this diff.

8. Verify after the change: nsys launch counts stay at gn_stats 32 / gn_final 32 / apply 16 / res_t 16 / transpose 8 over 4 forwards, and _graphs[key] never becomes False (one replay per forward).

Evidence:
Previous attempt #3 classification: (a) — the mechanism DID engage (gn_final_kernel vanished from the profile, 32 launches -> 0) yet the predicted 'gn_stats <= 14.5us' failed catastrophically: gn_stats went 13.57us -> 34.46us, gpu__dram_throughput 76.81% -> 31.07%, registers 21 -> 42 (occupancy_limit_registers 10 -> 5), so the launch-latency model was wrong and that direction is abandoned. Independent evidence for the new target: gn_stats gpu__dram_throughput 76.81% vs 85.00% on the already-float4 gn_silu_apply moving comparable bytes; long_scoreboard 97.50%; l1tex__throughput 11.96%; waves_per_multiprocessor 0.50 with achieved occupancy 49.02% -> only half the SM slots resident, so per-thread in-flight bytes (currently 4B x unroll 4) is the limiter. Root cause: 4-byte scalar loads with 1KB stride give too few outstanding sectors per warp to cover DRAM latency. Alternative bottleneck refuted: 'the convs are the lever' — 1.546e11 FLOP / 1668us = 92.7 TFLOPS = 88% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak, already engine-autotuned, so <12% is reachable and only inside the vendor library; 'occupancy of gn_stats' is refuted as the primary knob because raising P would inflate gn_final's reduction length and add partial-buffer traffic, whereas vectorizing raises bytes-in-flight 4x with zero structural change.

Expected metric change:
(1) gn_stats_kernel gpu__dram_throughput 76.81% -> >=84%, and gpu__time_duration.avg 13.57us -> <=11.8us (8 launches/forward => ~14us off the critical path). (2) gn_stats l1tex__throughput 11.96% -> ~6% and smsp__warp_issue_stalled_long_scoreboard 97.5% -> <92% (fewer, wider requests); registers_per_thread must stay <=24 (if it exceeds 26, occupancy_limit_registers drops below the warp limit and the change must be reverted). Anti-regression constraints: gn_silu_apply (15.6us), gn_silu_res_t (34.7us), nchw2nhwc (30.1us) and gn_final (4.8us) durations must stay within +-2% (untouched); launch counts per 4 forwards must remain exactly 32/16/16/8/32 and graph capture must still yield one replay per forward (_graphs[key] never False, node count unchanged); mean/rstd must agree with the current values to <1e-5 relative (gn_final still accumulates in double); the awkward 1x256x131x131 shape must not regress (>= -0.5%) — its P=537 chunking with partial/empty tails must still write every psum/psq slot.

pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[latency/exposure-bound schedule, not per-kernel bound] Hottest non-removable segment is the cuDNN TF32 NHWC conv pair (~1668us/forward, ~88% of TF32 peak) plus our DRAM-bound epilogue (gn_stats 126us, gn_silu_res_t 137us, apply 55us, transpose 56us = 412us/forward at 68-88% DRAM but only 4-19% SM throughput). The two symmetric half-batch streams phase-lock, so 1668+412us of work takes 1855us wall: ~187us of memory time is exposed with tensor cores idle.

Optimisation method:
Stream specialization (producer/consumer software pipeline): one CUDA stream runs ONLY the two cuDNN convs, a second runs ONLY the memory-bound kernels (transpose, GN stats/final/apply/res+transpose), chained by per-chunk events over 2-4 batch chunks with one-chunk lookahead. Because the streams hold disjoint kernel classes, conv (88% tensor-core, low DRAM) is structurally concurrent with GN (77-88% DRAM, <19% SM) instead of accidentally; the symmetric dual pipeline degenerates to conv||conv then GN||GN because both halves have identical stage durations.

Method name:
stream_specialize_pipeline

Modification plan:
1. Replace `_run_pipeline`'s two symmetric half-batch pipelines with a role-specialized 2-stream pipeline; keep the existing single-stream body verbatim as fallback for B<2 or non-fp32/non-4D/non-CUDA input. 2. Chunking: n=min(4,B); starts[i]=(i*B)//n so B=8->4x2, B=4->4x1, B=2->2x1, B=1->fallback; chunks are per-sample independent (GN is per-image) so output is bitwise identical. 3. Lazily create and cache streams sC (conv) and sM (memory) plus event arrays eT/eA/eB/eD of length 4 in `_get_streams` (created once, reused, capture-safe). Fork with ev0.record(cur); sC.wait_event(ev0); sM.wait_event(ev0); allocate out=torch.empty_like(x) before the fork. 4. Prologue on sM: for k in range(n): xl[k]=ext.nchw_to_nhwc(x[starts[k]:starts[k+1]]); eT[k].record(sM). Hold xl/y1/z/y2 in Python lists so in-flight chunks stay alive (no aliasing, no reuse hazard). 5. One-chunk-lookahead interleave, issued in exactly this order for k=0..n-1: (a) sC: wait_event(eT[k]); y1[k]=F.conv2d(xl[k],w1c,None,1,1); eA[k].record(sC). (b) sM: wait_event(eA[k]); z[k]=ext.gn_silu_nhwc(y1[k],nw1,nb1,eps); eB[k].record(sM). (c) if k>=1 sC: wait_event(eB[k-1]); y2[k-1]=F.conv2d(z[k-1],w2c,None,1,1); eD[k-1].record(sC). (d) if k>=1 sM: wait_event(eD[k-1]); ext.gn_silu_res_nchw_out(y2[k-1], x[starts[k-1]:starts[k]], nw2, nb2, eps, out[starts[k-1]:starts[k]]). This gives sC=A0,A1,D0,A2,D1,A3,D2 and sM=T*,B0,B1,E0,B2,E1,B3,E2, so every GN kernel runs while a conv of another chunk holds the tensor cores. 6. Tail: after the loop issue D(n-1) on sC then E(n-1) on sM; join with evC/evM recorded on each stream and cur.wait_event on both; return out. 7. Mirror the identical schedule in `_forward_eager`, adding record_stream(sC)/record_stream(sM) for x, out and all weight tensors as the current code does. 8. Leave the CUDA source untouched: all five kernels, the ld.cs/ld.cg/st.cs eviction hints, and the per-call L2 chunk loop inside gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw_out (now invoked on 1-2 image chunks); pick_P and chunk_imgs unchanged. 9. Graph capture unchanged: the schedule is static per shape, so `_try_capture` still warms up under `_Autotune`, captures `_run_pipeline` into the shared pool, and caches per key. 10. Accounting: this REPLACES the base's multistream_pipeline (symmetric half-batch dual pipeline). It is not dropped — same 2 streams + events — but the two streams now carry disjoint kernel classes so conv‖GN overlap is structural. Verify in nsys that a cutlass conv kernel is resident while gn_* kernels execute; if not, revert.

Evidence:
Previous attempt (mem_vectorize, round 14) classification (a): the predicted metric DID move — gn_stats_kernel 15.81us -> 13.18us (-17%) with gpu__dram_throughput 68.2% -> 74.6% — yet the score fell 0.66% (8x shape -2.7%). Per-kernel bandwidth efficiency is therefore a dead end; the wall is set by how kernels share the GPU. Root cause here: our five kernels sum 412us/forward (res_t 34.3x4, stats 15.8x8, apply 13.8x4, transpose 28x2, final 4.8x8) at gpu__dram_throughput 68-88% but sm__throughput 5-20%, while the convs sit at 1.546e11 FLOP/1668us = 92.7 TFLOPS = 88% of TF32 peak with low DRAM; wall is 1855us vs 1668us of conv, so ~187us of memory time is exposed against idle tensor cores. Alternative bottleneck refuted: 'the conv is the lever' — it is already engine-autotuned at 88% of TF32 SOL, so <12% is reachable and only inside the vendor library; 'occupancy' refuted because gn_silu_res_t already achieves 96.1% occupancy with 101.6% long-scoreboard stalls (pure DRAM latency). This mechanism composes with every carried optimisation (graph capture, L2 chunk blocking, eviction hints, cuDNN autotune) and only reorders stream ownership.

Expected metric change:
(1) Per-forward wall time down 4-8% on B>=2 shapes (8x256x64x128 1855us -> <=1780us), while the SUM of all kernel durations stays flat (±3%) — this is a scheduling win, not a work win. (2) Per-launch cutlass conv duration should roughly HALVE (417us -> ~210us) because convs no longer run two-at-a-time, with total conv time unchanged: if summed conv time rises >3% above 1668us, serializing the convs is hurting engine efficiency and the change must be reverted. The residual loss is our ~404us of DRAM-bound GN/transpose kernels (72–88% DRAM, 6–19% SM) that only partly overlap the convs: 1668us conv + 404us GN = 2072us work but 1855us wall ⇒ ~187us still exposed.

Optimisation method:
Compute/memory stream phase-staggering: keep the two-stream batch pipeline but offset stream B by a full conv stage (wait on an event recorded AFTER stream A's conv1, not after its transpose) and use 4 finer batch chunks round-robined over the 2 streams, plus lower the multistream threshold to B>=2. Metrics justify it: GN kernels are 72–88% DRAM / <19% SM while convs are ~89% TF32-SOL / low DRAM — complementary units, so co-residency hides the 187us exposed memory time instead of running GN||GN and conv||conv in lockstep.

Method name:
compute_mem_stream_stagger

Modification plan:
CHECKLIST (exact code actions, Python side only; CUDA source unchanged)
1. In `_run_pipeline` (and mirrored in `_forward_eager`), replace the fixed 2-way split `s0=B//2` with a chunk list: `K = 4 if B>=4 else (B if B>=2 else 1)`; build `bounds = [round(i*B/K) for i in range(K+1)]`, dropping empty chunks. Chunk i is assigned to stream `sA if (i%2)==0 else sB`. This keeps per-sample independence (GroupNorm is per (n,group)), so numerics are unchanged.
2. Move the stagger marker: today `evStage.record(sA)` fires right after chunk0's `nchw2nhwc` and stream B starts immediately, so both streams execute the SAME stage type at the same time (conv||conv, GN||GN) and never overlap compute with memory. Instead record `evStage` on sA immediately AFTER `ya = F.conv2d(xla, w1c, ...)` of chunk 0, and have every stream-B chunk's first op wait on it (`sB.wait_event(evStage)`). Result: stream B's transpose+conv1 run while stream A executes its memory-bound gn_stats/gn_final/gn_silu_apply, and vice-versa.
3. Keep exactly one event per stream per chunk to preserve graph-capturability: allocate `self._evs = [torch.cuda.Event() for _ in range(8)]` lazily (same lazy/try-except fallback style as `_get_streams`), and use `self._evs[i]` for chunk i. All events are created once in `__init__`/lazy path, never inside capture.
4. Loop body per chunk i (unchanged op order, so all existing mechanisms survive): `xi = x[b0:b1]`; `xli = ext.nchw_to_nhwc(xi)`; `yi = F.conv2d(xli, w1c, None,1,1)`; if i==0: `evStage.record(sA)`; `yi = ext.gn_silu_nhwc(yi, nw1, nb1, eps)`; `yi = F.conv2d(yi, w2c, None,1,1)`; `ext.gn_silu_res_nchw_out(yi, xi, nw2, nb2, eps, out[b0:b1])`; `ev[i].record(stream_i)`.
5. Join: `cur.wait_event(ev[i])` for every chunk i. Output tensor is one `torch.empty_like(x)` written through the existing out-parameter kernel — no extra allocation, no extra traffic.
6. Lower the fallback threshold from `B < 4` to `B < 2`, so the 2x256x64x64 shape (currently fully serial, only 1.126x) also gets conv/GN overlap. B==1 (131x131 shape) keeps the single-stream path verbatim.
7. Guard against too-small convs: if `B//K < 1` or `B*H*W/K < 65536` elements per chunk, fall back to K=2. This prevents cuDNN plan degradation on the small shape.
8. Preservation audit (no listed mechanism removed): multistream_pipeline (round 3) is EXTENDED, not removed — same 2 streams, deeper phase offset and finer chunking; cuda_graph_capture still captures the whole DAG (event record/wait across streams is legal in capture and already used); cudnn_conv_engine_autotune still runs once per (shape,dtype,layout) key during warm-up — note K changes the per-conv batch, so autotune must run on the SAME chunked pipeline (it already calls `_run_pipeline`, so the tuned plans match the captured shapes); l2_cache_blocking and l2_evict_policy_hints are untouched inside the extension (per-call chunk loop and PTX hints unchanged).
9. Keep `record_stream` bookkeeping in the eager path for every chunk slice on both streams (x, out, weights) to avoid caching-allocator reuse hazards.
10. Validate all 4 shapes; if the small or awkward shape regresses, keep K=2 for B<4 while retaining the conv-stage offset of item 2 (that offset alone is the primary win).

Evidence:
Numeric: conv ≈417us/launch for a half-batch (7517us/18) = 3.87e10 FLOP/417us ≈ 93 TFLOPS ≈ 89% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak; our five kernels sum 404us/forward (res_t 36us x4, stats 13.2 x8, apply 14.6 x4, transpose 29 x2, final 4.7 x8) while measured wall is 1855us against ~1668us of conv work ⇒ ~187us (10%) of memory work is NOT hidden. Root cause: both streams were forked with only a transpose-length offset, so identical-duration stages drift into lockstep (conv||conv, GN||GN), leaving no compute/memory pairing; GN kernels show sm__throughput 6.2–19.2% with gpu__dram_throughput 72–88%, convs the inverse. Refutation of 'DRAM-bound epilogue is the bottleneck': even driving all five kernels to 100% DRAM SOL saves <60us, and refutation of 'suboptimal conv plan': the autotuned engine already sits at ~89% of TF32 SOL, so <11% is reachable there and only via vendor-internal changes.

Expected metric change:
(1) Wall time per forward down 5–10% at the mid/large shapes and up to ~8% at 2x256x64x64 (threshold lowered to B>=2); (2) during conv kernels gpu__dram_throughput rises (GN traffic now co-resident) while per-launch conv duration stays within +3% — if conv duration inflates >5% the offset is causing SM contention and K must drop to 2; (3) sum of gn_* kernel durations must stay flat (±2%) — these kernels are untouched, only their placement changes. Anti-regression guards: kernel launch count per forward may rise (4 chunks) but must remain inside a single captured graph (graph replay count per forward stays 1; if `_graphs[key] is False` appears, capture broke and the change must be reverted); cuDNN autotune must still fire once per shape (watch that conv2d_grouped_direct_kernel trial launches do not reappear in steady state); no change in output tolerance (bitwise-identical kernels, per-sample-independent chunking).
