Bottleneck identified:
[latency/exposure-bound schedule] For B<4 the whole pipeline runs on ONE stream, so the DRAM-bound epilogue (transpose 87.7%, gn_silu_apply 83.1%, gn_silu_res_t 74.0%, gn_stats 75.1% DRAM SOL but only 6–19% SM throughput) is fully serialized behind the cuDNN TF32 convs (~88% of TF32 peak, low DRAM). The 2x256x64x64 shape therefore scores worst (1.1259 vs 1.2668 for the two-stream mid shape).

Optimisation method:
Re-gate the existing multistream fork/join pipeline so B==2 (threshold B<4 → B<2) is split into two per-image streams staggered by evStage, letting one stream's tensor-core conv overlap the other's 75–88%-DRAM/6–19%-SM GroupNorm+transpose kernels. Batch splitting is exactly value-equivalent (GN stats are per (image,group); residual is elementwise). B>=4 and B==1 code paths are left bit-identical, so the -4.4% large-shape regression of round 10 (caused by its separate 4-chunk restructure, not by the gate) cannot recur.

Method name:
smallB_multistream_gate

Modification plan:
Checklist (host-side Python only; no CUDA kernel edits, no change to chunking constants):
1. In `ModelNew._run_pipeline`, change the fallback condition `if (st is None) or (B < 4):` to `if (st is None) or (B < 2):` so B==2 (and 3) take the two-stream fork/join branch; B==1 still takes the single-stream branch (cannot be split by batch).
2. In `ModelNew._forward_eager`, make the identical change in `if (st is None) or (B < 4) or (x.dim() != 4) ...` → `... or (B < 2) or ...`; keep every `record_stream` call exactly as-is so cross-stream allocator reuse stays safe on the eager path.
3. Keep `s0 = B // 2` unchanged: B==2 → streams of 1 image each; B==3 → 1 and 2 images (correct, merely imbalanced). Assert nothing else: s0>=1 is guaranteed because B==1 never forks.
4. Verify the C++ helpers are already nb==1-safe and leave them untouched: `chunk_imgs(1,HW)` returns 1 (single chunk), `pick_P(1,HW)=min(ceil(HW/32),1024)`, `stats_chunk` launches grid (P, nb=1) and `gn_final` launches nb*NGRP=32 blocks reading exactly the P*NGRP slots gn_stats wrote — empty tail partitions still write zeros, so no unwritten-tail hazard for HW=4096 (P=128) or the awkward HW=17161 (P=537).
5. Graph capture: `_try_capture` calls `_run_pipeline`, which now forks for B==2; the fork/join capture pattern (ev0 record on the capturing stream, sA/sB wait, evA/evB join) is already exercised for B>=4, so reuse it verbatim — no new capture code, no allocation inside capture (
all buffers come from the graph pool as today).
6. Autotune: `_autotune_once` / `_try_capture` warm-up now runs the B==1-per-stream conv shapes under `_Autotune()`, so cuDNN selects and caches plans for (1,256,H,W) convs before capture; keep `_MAX_TUNED`/`_MAX_GRAPHS` unchanged.
7. Do NOT touch: kernel sources (eviction hints ld_cs/ld_cg/st_cs, float4 apply, shared-mem transposes), `chunk_imgs`/`pick_P`, the L2 chunk loop inside each ext call, graph cache keying, or the B>=4 branch — the mid/large shapes must produce a byte-identical launch sequence.
8. Correctness argument to record in a comment: conv2d, GroupNorm(32 groups over C,H,W of ONE image) and the residual add are all per-image independent, so `cat(f(x[0:1]), f(x[1:2])) == f(x)` bitwise; only kernel grid z-extent changes.
9. Fallback safety: if stream/event creation fails (`_get_streams()` returns None) the single-stream path is still taken for every B, and if capture throws, `_forward_eager` reproduces the same result.
10. Post-check with nsys on 2x256x64x64: confirm a cutlass conv kernel is time-overlapped with gn_stats/gn_silu_apply/gn_silu_res_t of the other stream, and that exactly one graph replay per forward remains.

Evidence:
Latest rejected attempt classification: (a) — its predicted metric DID move (gn_stats_kernel 13.18us→12.67us, -3.9%, DRAM SOL 75.09%→75.84%, registers 21→20) yet the score fell 1.1980→1.1854, so per-kernel bandwidth micro-optimisation of an already 75–88%-DRAM-SOL kernel is a dead end; the wall is set by how work is placed, and the only shape with NO placement at all is the single-stream one. Numeric evidence for the new target: 2x256x64x64 is the worst shape at 1.1259x while the two-stream 8x256x64x128 reaches 1.2668x; on B=2 every epilogue kernel (74.0–87.7% DRAM SOL, 6.3–19.6% sm__throughput) is serialized behind convs running at ~92.7 TFLOPS ≈ 88% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak (low DRAM), i.e. two complementary resources are used one after the other. Round 10 measured +5.3% on exactly this shape when the multistream threshold was lowered; its -4.4% on 4x256x256x256 came from the separately-introduced 4-chunk stagger, which this plan does not adopt. Alternative bottleneck refuted: 'the conv is the lever' — it is already exhaustively engine-autotuned at 88% of TF32 SOL, so <12% is reachable and only inside the vendor library. This composes with all carried mechanisms: it re-uses (does not remove) multistream_pipeline, keeps cuda_graph_capture (same fork/join pattern already captured for B>=4), keeps cudnn_conv_engine_autotune (warm-up still runs under _Autotune), keeps l2_cache_blocking (chunk loop untouched inside each ext call) and keeps l2_evict_policy_hints (kernel code untouched).

Expected metric change:
(1) 2x256x64x64 wall 272us → <=258us (-5%) and its per-shape speedup 1.1259 → >=1.18; geomean 1.1980 → ~1.211. (2) In nsys for that shape, cutlass/xmma conv kernels must appear time-overlapped with gn_stats/gn_silu_apply/gn_silu_res_t (currently zero overlap), and per-forward kernel count for B=2 doubles (9 → 18) while graph replays per forward stay exactly 1 (`_graphs[key]` must never become False). (3) Per-kernel durations must stay flat: gn_stats, gn_silu_apply, gn_silu_res_t, nchw2nhwc, gn_final within ±3% at equal nb (kernel code untouched), only their grid z-extent halves. Anti-regression constraints: 8x256x64x128, 4x256x256x256 and 1x256x131x131 take an unchanged code path and must stay within ±0.5% — if any of them moves, the gate leaked; cuDNN autotune must still fire once per new (B=1-per-stream) conv shape (no conv2d_grouped_direct_kernel in steady state); outputs must remain bitwise-equal to the current kernel for B!=2 and within tolerance for B=2 (per-image independence makes the split exact); peak memory rises only by the second half-batch's in-flight chunk (~8.4MB at the mid shape) and must not trigger allocator churn; if 2x256x64x64 does not improve by >=2%, restore the `B < 4` threshold.

pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM-bandwidth bound] The GroupNorm pair we control — gn_stats_kernel (13.6us x8) then gn_silu_apply (14.3us x4) / gn_silu_res_t (34.5us x4), ~300us of our 402us epilogue — reads the SAME conv-output chunk from DRAM twice: lts__t_sector_hit_rate 2.31% (stats), 1.85% (apply), 1.94% (res_t) at 75–84% DRAM SOL, ~134MB/forward of pure redundant re-read.

Optimisation method:
Tighten l2_cache_blocking from image granularity to (image x 4-group channel-tile) granularity. Today the smallest reuse unit is one whole image (16.8MB mid, 67MB large), which measurably does not survive L2 (1.85% hit). A 32-channel tile is 128B contiguous per pixel in NHWC (full L2 line, no wasted sectors) and shrinks the stats->apply working set to ~1–8MB, so the apply/res_t read becomes an L2 hit instead of a DRAM read.

Method name:
group_tile_l2_blocking

Modification plan:
1) Add CTILE=32 channels (=4 groups; 32*4B=128B contiguous per pixel in NHWC = one full L2 line, so tiling wastes no sectors). Replace the image-only chunk loop in gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw(_out) with a two-level loop `for n0 (nb images) { for c0 in 0,32,...,224 }`, sized so chunk_bytes = nb*CTILE*HW*4 <= 4MB (nb>=1). This GENERALISES l2_cache_blocking (still present), it does not remove it.
2) Replace gn_stats_kernel with gn_stats_tile(y,c0,HW,P,gsum,gsq): grid=(P,nb), block=256 viewed as 32 lanes (channel c0+lane) x 8 rows. Thread (lane,row) accumulates s,q over hw = hw0+row+8k while hw<hw1, loading ld_cg(&y[((n*HW)+hw)*256 + c0+lane]) so each warp issues one 128B request. Reduce the 8 rows in smem[8][32], then reduce 8 channels -> 4 group sums; one lane per group does atomicAdd(&gsum[n*32+g],(double)s) and atomicAdd(&gsq[...],(double)q).
3) DELETE gn_final_kernel (accounting: it is not one of the carried mechanisms; its job — partials -> mean/rstd — is subsumed by the double atomics plus an inline finalize). Keeping it would multiply its 4.9us launch latency by the 8x finer chunking and eat the whole win. Before each GN pass issue one cudaMemsetAsync(gsum/gsq, 0, B*32*8*2) (graph-capturable node) instead of 8–32 gn_final launches.
4) gn_silu_apply_tile: grid over nb*HW*(CTILE/4) float4s; thread decodes i -> (n, hw, c4 in 0..7), local group g = c0/8 + (c4>>1); loads s=gsum[n*32+g], q=gsq[n*32+g], computes cnt=(double)HW*8, m=s/cnt, r=rsqrt(q/cnt-m*m+eps) once per thread; keeps ld_cs4 on y (last use) and default store on out.
5) gn_silu_res_t_tile: tile 64 spatial x 32 channels, smem[64*33]. Phase 1: lc=tid&31 (32 channels, 128B per warp), lh=tid>>5 (8 rows, 8 iters), ld_cs the y value, normalise+SiLU into smem. Phase 2: lh=tid&63 (64 contiguous hw), lc=tid>>6 (4 iters covering 32 channels), residual ld_cs + st_cs to NCHW. This preserves l2_evict_policy_hints exactly (streaming on y/res/out, ld_cg only in stats).
6) P selection: P = clamp(ceil(HW/512), 1, max(1,1024/nb)) so P*nb lands in 256–1024 blocks; empty partitions (hw0>=HW) simply contribute 0 to the atomics, so no unwritten-tail hazard exists any more (this also removes the psum/psq tail-write requirement entirely).
7) All loops bound-check hw<HW and all grids use ceil-division; nothing assumes HW%32==0, so the awkward 1x256x131x131 (HW=17161, odd) shape is exact.
8) Host side untouched otherwise: keep the two-stream fork/join with the evStage stagger, the out-parameter variant, per-(shape,ptr) CUDA-graph capture with the shared pool, and the _Autotune exhaustive cuDNN warm-up. Only the node list inside each ext call changes (more, smaller nodes + 1 memset), which capture handles because sizes are static.
9) Numerics: per-thread float accumulation, block reduction in float, cross-block accumulation in double atomics, finalize in double -> relative error <1e-8, far inside atol 2.8e-3.
10) Keep TORCH_CHECK(C==256) and the channels_last checks; conv calls, weights and layouts are unchanged.

Evidence:
Previous attempt (round 19, smallB_multistream_gate) = case (i): its predicted metric DID move — 2x256x64x64 improved +8.2% exactly as forecast (272us -> ~251us) — so the mechanism works but is shape-limited; I keep that gate untouched and attack an independent, larger target. Numeric evidence here: gn_stats_kernel reads a 16.8MB chunk at lts__t_sector_hit_rate=2.31%, and gn_silu_apply re-reads the identical chunk microseconds later at 1.85% (res_t 1.94%), i.e. ~134MB of the ~603MB epilogue traffic per forward is a redundant DRAM read; DRAM SOL is 75–84% while sm__throughput is only 6–19%, and long_scoreboard is 82–102%, so bytes, not issue, set the time. Root cause: the smallest reuse unit today is one whole image (16.8MB mid, 67MB large) and that working set demonstrably does not survive L2 next to the second stream's conv plus the apply's own 16.8MB write stream. Refutation of 'the conv is the lever': 1.546e11 FLOP / 1668us = 92.7 TFLOPS = 88% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak and the engine is already exhaustively autotuned, so <12% is reachable and only inside the vendor library. Refutation of 'scheduling/occupancy': rounds 10/15/16 moved their scheduling metrics and all lost score, so only DRAM bytes remain. Bottleneck identified:
[latency/exposure-bound schedule, not per-kernel bound] Hottest non-removable segment is the cuDNN TF32 NHWC conv pair (~1668us/forward, ~88% of TF32 peak) plus our DRAM-bound epilogue (gn_stats 126us, gn_silu_res_t 137us, apply 55us, transpose 56us = 412us/forward at 68-88% DRAM but only 4-19% SM throughput). The two symmetric half-batch streams phase-lock, so 1668+412us of work takes 1855us wall: ~187us of memory time is exposed with tensor cores idle.

Optimisation method:
Stream specialization (producer/consumer software pipeline): one CUDA stream runs ONLY the two cuDNN convs, a second runs ONLY the memory-bound kernels (transpose, GN stats/final/apply/res+transpose), chained by per-chunk events over 2-4 batch chunks with one-chunk lookahead. Because the streams hold disjoint kernel classes, conv (88% tensor-core, low DRAM) is structurally concurrent with GN (77-88% DRAM, <19% SM) instead of accidentally; the symmetric dual pipeline degenerates to conv||conv then GN||GN because both halves have identical stage durations.

Method name:
stream_specialize_pipeline

Modification plan:
1. Replace `_run_pipeline`'s two symmetric half-batch pipelines with a role-specialized 2-stream pipeline; keep the existing single-stream body verbatim as fallback for B<2 or non-fp32/non-4D/non-CUDA input. 2. Chunking: n=min(4,B); starts[i]=(i*B)//n so B=8->4x2, B=4->4x1, B=2->2x1, B=1->fallback; chunks are per-sample independent (GN is per-image) so output is bitwise identical. 3. Lazily create and cache streams sC (conv) and sM (memory) plus event arrays eT/eA/eB/eD of length 4 in `_get_streams` (created once, reused, capture-safe). Fork with ev0.record(cur); sC.wait_event(ev0); sM.wait_event(ev0); allocate out=torch.empty_like(x) before the fork. 4. Prologue on sM: for k in range(n): xl[k]=ext.nchw_to_nhwc(x[starts[k]:starts[k+1]]); eT[k].record(sM). Hold xl/y1/z/y2 in Python lists so in-flight chunks stay alive (no aliasing, no reuse hazard). 5. One-chunk-lookahead interleave, issued in exactly this order for k=0..n-1: (a) sC: wait_event(eT[k]); y1[k]=F.conv2d(xl[k],w1c,None,1,1); eA[k].record(sC). (b) sM: wait_event(eA[k]); z[k]=ext.gn_silu_nhwc(y1[k],nw1,nb1,eps); eB[k].record(sM). (c) if k>=1 sC: wait_event(eB[k-1]); y2[k-1]=F.conv2d(z[k-1],w2c,None,1,1); eD[k-1].record(sC). (d) if k>=1 sM: wait_event(eD[k-1]); ext.gn_silu_res_nchw_out(y2[k-1], x[starts[k-1]:starts[k]], nw2, nb2, eps, out[starts[k-1]:starts[k]]). This gives sC=A0,A1,D0,A2,D1,A3,D2 and sM=T*,B0,B1,E0,B2,E1,B3,E2, so every GN kernel runs while a conv of another chunk holds the tensor cores. 6. Tail: after the loop issue D(n-1) on sC then E(n-1) on sM; join with evC/evM recorded on each stream and cur.wait_event on both; return out. 7. Mirror the identical schedule in `_forward_eager`, adding record_stream(sC)/record_stream(sM) for x, out and all weight tensors as the current code does. 8. Leave the CUDA source untouched: all five kernels, the ld.cs/ld.cg/st.cs eviction hints, and the per-call L2 chunk loop inside gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw_out (now invoked on 1-2 image chunks); pick_P and chunk_imgs unchanged. 9. Graph capture unchanged: the schedule is static per shape, so `_try_capture` still warms up under `_Autotune`, captures `_run_pipeline` into the shared pool, and caches per key. 10. Accounting: this REPLACES the base's multistream_pipeline (symmetric half-batch dual pipeline). It is not dropped — same 2 streams + events — but the two streams now carry disjoint kernel classes so conv‖GN overlap is structural. Verify in nsys that a cutlass conv kernel is resident while gn_* kernels execute; if not, revert.

Evidence:
Previous attempt (mem_vectorize, round 14) classification (a): the predicted metric DID move — gn_stats_kernel 15.81us -> 13.18us (-17%) with gpu__dram_throughput 68.2% -> 74.6% — yet the score fell 0.66% (8x shape -2.7%). Per-kernel bandwidth efficiency is therefore a dead end; the wall is set by how kernels share the GPU. Root cause here: our five kernels sum 412us/forward (res_t 34.3x4, stats 15.8x8, apply 13.8x4, transpose 28x2, final 4.8x8) at gpu__dram_throughput 68-88% but sm__throughput 5-20%, while the convs sit at 1.546e11 FLOP/1668us = 92.7 TFLOPS = 88% of TF32 peak with low DRAM; wall is 1855us vs 1668us of conv, so ~187us of memory time is exposed against idle tensor cores. Alternative bottleneck refuted: 'the conv is the lever' — it is already engine-autotuned at 88% of TF32 SOL, so <12% is reachable and only inside the vendor library; 'occupancy' refuted because gn_silu_res_t already achieves 96.1% occupancy with 101.6% long-scoreboard stalls (pure DRAM latency). This mechanism composes with every carried optimisation (graph capture, L2 chunk blocking, eviction hints, cuDNN autotune) and only reorders stream ownership.

Expected metric change:
(1) Per-forward wall time down 4-8% on B>=2 shapes (8x256x64x128 1855us -> <=1780us), while the SUM of all kernel durations stays flat (±3%) — this is a scheduling win, not a work win. (2) Per-launch cutlass conv duration should roughly HALVE (417us -> ~210us) because convs no longer run two-at-a-time, with total conv time unchanged: if summed conv time rises >3% above 1668us, serializing the convs is hurting engine efficiency and the change must be reverted. (3) In nsys, gn_stats/gn_silu_apply/gn_silu_res_t must appear concurrent with a cutlass conv kernel; conv-stream idle gaps must be <30us apart from the initial transpose. Anti-regression constraints: gn_* kernel durations unchanged ±5% (kernel code untouched) and their launch counts unchanged (4 chunks vs 2 streams x 2 chunks); graph capture must still succeed with exactly one replay per forward (`_graphs[key]` never False) and no cudaMalloc inside capture; cuDNN autotune must still fire once per shape (no conv2d_grouped_direct_kernel in steady state); B=1 (1x256x131x131) takes the untouched single-stream path and must stay within ±0.5%; peak memory rises by at most 2 extra in-flight chunks (~34MB mid, ~268MB large) which must not trigger allocator churn.

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/occupancy-exposure, SM-slot contention] Hottest non-removable segment we control is the DRAM-bound epilogue (gn_silu_res_t 141us, gn_stats 106us, apply 54us, transpose 55us per forward). Each epilogue kernel launches 2048-4096 blocks and fills every warp slot (sm__warps_active 82-111%) while using only 11-20% of SM issue, so the other stream's tensor-core conv cannot get resident blocks and the 397us epilogue stays exposed on the 1855us wall.

Optimisation method:
Concurrent-kernel SM budgeting: convert nchw2nhwc_kernel, gn_silu_apply and gn_silu_res_t into persistent grid-stride kernels whose grid is capped at ~2 blocks/SM (340 blocks) instead of 2-4 full waves, but only on the multistream path (B>=4). Metrics justify it: gn_stats already reaches 76.99% DRAM SOL at 48.6% warps_active, so half the warp slots saturate DRAM; the remaining slots currently squatted by 11%-SM-throughput epilogue warps are exactly what the co-scheduled cuDNN TF32 conv needs to overlap.

Method name:
sm_budget_grid_cap

Modification plan:
1) Add SM-count query once: `static int g_sm = at::cuda::getCurrentDeviceProperties()->multiProcessorCount;` (cached in a function-local static). Add an `int bpsm` argument (0 = uncapped) to nchw_to_nhwc, gn_silu_nhwc, gn_silu_res_nchw and gn_silu_res_nchw_out; the C++ side computes `cap = (bpsm>0) ? g_sm*bpsm : INT_MAX` and clamps each grid, keeping every other host-side line (chunk loop, pick_P, stats_chunk, allocations) byte-identical so l2_cache_blocking survives.
2) gn_silu_res_t: replace the 3D grid (HWtiles, C/64, nb) by a flat 1D grid. Precompute on host `TH=(HW+31)/32, TC=4, T=TH*TC*nb`, launch `dim3 g(min(T,cap))`, pass TH, TC, T. Inside: `for (int i = blockIdx.x; i < T; i += gridDim.x) { int t = T-1-i; int n = t/(TH*TC); int r = t - n*TH*TC; int cb = r/TH; int bx = r - cb*TH; const int hw0 = bx*32, c0 = cb*64; ... }` — body (shared tile, ld_cs/st_cs hints, `hw<HW` guards) copied verbatim, with `__syncthreads()` before AND after the shared-memory phase so the tile is reusable across iterations. This preserves the reverse traversal order and all l2_evict_policy_hints.
3) nchw2nhwc_kernel: identical flattening (same 32x64 tile, T=TH*TC*B, forward order), grid `min(T,cap)`, same double `__syncthreads()` pattern, same ld_cs load.
4) gn_silu_apply: keep gridDim.y = nb (image), cap x: `gx = min((n4+255)/256, max(1, cap/nb))`; inside replace the single index by `for (int b = gridDim.x-1-blockIdx.x; b < gx_total; b += gridDim.x)` computed as `i = b*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; if (i>=n4perimg) continue;` where gx_total = (n4perimg+255)/256 is passed in — reverse traversal and the float4 ld_cs4 path unchanged.
5) gn_stats_kernel and gn_final_kernel: UNTOUCHED (gn_stats already sits at 3.0 blocks/SM and 48.6% occupancy, i.e. it already leaves half the slots free and still hits 77% DRAM).
6) Python gating (this is the critical anti-regression rule): in `_run_pipeline` and `_forward_eager`, pass `bpsm=2` for every ext call ONLY on the two-stream branch (B>=4); pass `bpsm=0` on the single-stream fallback branch (B<4, i.e. 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131) so those shapes keep today's full-wave grids and cannot regress. The value is a Python int fixed by B, so the captured graph records one static grid per shape -> cuda_graph_capture keeps working; no allocation or shape change, so multistream_pipeline, l2_cache_blocking, cudnn_conv_engine_autotune and l2_evict_policy_hints all remain operational and none is removed.

Bottleneck identified:

Optimisation method:
mem_vectorize: replace the scalar per-channel ld.global.cg loads in gn_stats_kernel with 16B float4 (ld.global.cg.v4.f32) loads along the contiguous NHWC channel axis. Because C=256 and 8 channels/group, every float4 lies wholly inside one group, so the four components can be folded into one (sum, sumsq) accumulator — bit-legal, no dtype change. This cuts load instructions 4x and quadruples in-flight bytes per thread, which is exactly what a 97.5% long-scoreboard / 0.5-wave / 76.8%-DRAM kernel needs; grid, launch count, chunking, streams and graph capture are untouched.

Method name:
mem_vectorize

Modification plan:
Only gn_stats_kernel changes. Everything else (host chunk loop, pick_P, grids, launch counts, streams, graph capture, cuDNN autotune, evict hints) is byte-identical.

1. Add a vector cache-hint helper next to ld_cg:
   __device__ __forceinline__ float4 ld_cg4(const float4* p){ float4 v; asm("ld.global.cg.v4.f32 {%0,%1,%2,%3}, [%4];" : "=f"(v.x),"=f"(v.y),"=f"(v.z),"=f"(v.w) : "l"(p)); return v; }
   This preserves the already-accepted l2_evict_policy_hints mechanism (chunk stays L2-resident, L1 bypassed) in vectorized form.

2. Replace the 4 scalar strided loads per thread with one float4 row load: in gn_stats_kernel remap threads as c4 = threadIdx.x & 63 (float4 index over the 256 channels), row = threadIdx.x >> 6 (0..3). Keep grid (P, nb), block 256, same chunk math (chunk=(HW+P-1)/P, hw0=p*chunk, hw1=min(hw0+chunk,HW)). Loop `for (int i = row; i < cnt; i += 4)` loading
   float4 v = ld_cg4(reinterpret_cast<const float4*>(y) + ((long long)n*HW + hw0 + i)*64 + c4);
   and accumulate s += v.x+v.y+v.z+v.w;  q += v.x*v.x+v.y*v.y+v.z*v.z+v.w*v.w;  (float accumulators, unchanged precision contract). Keep `#pragma unroll 4` on the loop for MLP.

3. Group-correctness argument (why folding 4 channels into one accumulator is legal): channel = 4*c4 + {0,1,2,3}; group = channel>>3 = c4>>1, identical for all four components because 4 divides 8. So each float4 contributes entirely to group g = c4>>1.

4. Reduction rewrite (replaces the old 8-lane shfl):
   a. Warp step: lanes within a warp hold consecutive c4, so pairs (even,odd) share a group -> s += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffffu, s, 1); same for q.
   b. Cross-row step: __shared__ float ss[4][32], sq[4][32] (1024B total, same as today's shared usage, so occupancy limits are unchanged). If ((c4 & 1) == 0) { ss[row][c4>>1] = s; sq[row][c4>>1] = q; } __syncthreads();

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/exposure-bound schedule] For B<4 the whole pipeline runs on ONE stream, so the DRAM-bound epilogue (transpose 87.7%, gn_silu_apply 83.1%, gn_silu_res_t 74.0%, gn_stats 75.1% DRAM SOL but only 6–19% SM throughput) is fully serialized behind the cuDNN TF32 convs (~88% of TF32 peak, low DRAM). The 2x256x64x64 shape therefore scores worst (1.1259 vs 1.2668 for the two-stream mid shape).

Optimisation method:
Re-gate the existing multistream fork/join pipeline so B==2 (threshold B<4 → B<2) is split into two per-image streams staggered by evStage, letting one stream's tensor-core conv overlap the other's 75–88%-DRAM/6–19%-SM GroupNorm+transpose kernels. Batch splitting is exactly value-equivalent (GN stats are per (image,group); residual is elementwise). B>=4 and B==1 code paths are left bit-identical, so the -4.4% large-shape regression of round 10 (caused by its separate 4-chunk restructure, not by the gate) cannot recur.

Method name:
smallB_multistream_gate

Modification plan:
Checklist (host-side Python only; no CUDA kernel edits, no change to chunking constants):
1. In `ModelNew._run_pipeline`, change the fallback condition `if (st is None) or (B < 4):` to `if (st is None) or (B < 2):` so B==2 (and 3) take the two-stream fork/join branch; B==1 still takes the single-stream branch (cannot be split by batch).
2. In `ModelNew._forward_eager`, make the identical change in `if (st is None) or (B < 4) or (x.dim() != 4) ...` → `... or (B < 2) or ...`; keep every `record_stream` call exactly as-is so cross-stream allocator reuse stays safe on the eager path.
3. Keep `s0 = B // 2` unchanged: B==2 → streams of 1 image each; B==3 → 1 and 2 images (correct, merely imbalanced). Assert nothing else: s0>=1 is guaranteed because B==1 never forks.
4. Verify the C++ helpers are already nb==1-safe and leave them untouched: `chunk_imgs(1,HW)` returns 1 (single chunk), `pick_P(1,HW)=min(ceil(HW/32),1024)`, `stats_chunk` launches grid (P, nb=1) and `gn_final` launches nb*NGRP=32 blocks reading exactly the P*NGRP slots gn_stats wrote — empty tail partitions still write zeros, so no unwritten-tail hazard for HW=4096 (P=128) or the awkward HW=17161 (P=537).
5. Graph capture: `_try_capture` calls `_run_pipeline`, which now forks for B==2; the fork/join capture pattern (ev0 record on the capturing stream, sA/sB wait, evA/evB join) is already exercised for B>=4, so reuse it verbatim — no new capture code, no allocation inside capture (
all buffers come from the graph pool as today).
6. Autotune: `_autotune_once` / `_try_capture` warm-up now runs the B==1-per-stream conv shapes under `_Autotune()`, so cuDNN selects and caches plans for (1,256,H,W) convs before capture; keep `_MAX_TUNED`/`_MAX_GRAPHS` unchanged.
7. Do NOT touch: kernel sources (eviction hints ld_cs/ld_cg/st_cs, float4 apply, shared-mem transposes), `chunk_imgs`/`pick_P`, the L2 chunk loop inside each ext call, graph cache keying, or the B>=4 branch — the mid/large shapes must produce a byte-identical launch sequence.
8. Correctness argument to record in a comment: conv2d, GroupNorm(32 groups over C,H,W of ONE image) and the residual add are all per-image independent, so `cat(f(x[0:1]), f(x[1:2])) == f(x)` bitwise; only kernel grid z-extent changes.
9. Fallback safety: if stream/event creation fails (`_get_streams()` returns None) the single-stream path is still taken for every B, and if capture throws, `_forward_eager` reproduces the same result.
10. Post-check with nsys on 2x256x64x64: confirm a cutlass conv kernel is time-overlapped with gn_stats/gn_silu_apply/gn_silu_res_t of the other stream, and that exactly one graph replay per forward remains.

Evidence:
Latest rejected attempt classification: (a) — its predicted metric DID move (gn_stats_kernel 13.18us→12.67us, -3.9%, DRAM SOL 75.09%→75.84%, registers 21→20) yet the score fell 1.1980→1.1854, so per-kernel bandwidth micro-optimisation of an already 75–88%-DRAM-SOL kernel is a dead end; the wall is set by how work is placed, and the only shape with NO placement at all is the single-stream one. Numeric evidence for the new target: 2x256x64x64 is the worst shape at 1.1259x while the two-stream 8x256x64x128 reaches 1.2668x; on B=2 every epilogue kernel (74.0–87.7% DRAM SOL, 6.3–19.6% sm__throughput) is serialized behind convs running at ~92.7 TFLOPS ≈ 88% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak (low DRAM), i.e. two complementary resources are used one after the other. Round 10 measured +5.3% on exactly this shape when the multistream threshold was lowered; its -4.4% on 4x256x256x256 came from the separately-introduced 4-chunk stagger, which this plan does not adopt. Alternative bottleneck refuted: 'the conv is the lever' — it is already exhaustively engine-autotuned at 88% of TF32 SOL, so <12% is reachable and only inside the vendor library. This composes with all carried mechanisms: it re-uses (does not remove) multistream_pipeline, keeps cuda_graph_capture (same fork/join pattern already captured for B>=4), keeps cudnn_conv_engine_autotune (warm-up still runs under _Autotune), keeps l2_cache_blocking (chunk loop untouched inside each ext call) and keeps l2_evict_policy_hints (kernel code untouched).

Expected metric change:
(1) 2x256x64x64 wall 272us → <=258us (-5%) and its per-shape speedup 1.1259 → >=1.18; geomean 1.1980 → ~1.211. (2) In nsys for that shape, cutlass/xmma conv kernels must appear time-overlapped with gn_stats/gn_silu_apply/gn_silu_res_t (currently zero overlap), and per-forward kernel count for B=2 doubles (9 → 18) while graph replays per forward stay exactly 1 (`_graphs[key]` must never become False). (3) Per-kernel durations must stay flat: gn_stats, gn_silu_apply, gn_silu_res_t, nchw2nhwc, gn_final within ±3% at equal nb (kernel code untouched), only their grid z-extent halves. Anti-regression constraints: 8x256x64x128, 4x256x256x256 and 1x256x131x131 take an unchanged code path and must stay within ±0.5% — if any of them moves, the gate leaked; cuDNN autotune must still fire once per new (B=1-per-stream) conv shape (no conv2d_grouped_direct_kernel in steady state); outputs must remain bitwise-equal to the current kernel for B!=2 and within tolerance for B=2 (per-image independence makes the split exact); peak memory rises only by the second half-batch's in-flight chunk (~8.4MB at the mid shape) and must not trigger allocator churn; if 2x256x64x64 does not improve by >=2%, restore the `B < 4` threshold.

pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM-bandwidth bound] The GroupNorm pair we control — gn_stats_kernel (13.6us x8) then gn_silu_apply (14.3us x4) / gn_silu_res_t (34.5us x4), ~300us of our 402us epilogue — reads the SAME conv-output chunk from DRAM twice: lts__t_sector_hit_rate 2.31% (stats), 1.85% (apply), 1.94% (res_t) at 75–84% DRAM SOL, ~134MB/forward of pure redundant re-read.

Optimisation method:
Tighten l2_cache_blocking from image granularity to (image x 4-group channel-tile) granularity. Today the smallest reuse unit is one whole image (16.8MB mid, 67MB large), which measurably does not survive L2 (1.85% hit). A 32-channel tile is 128B contiguous per pixel in NHWC (full L2 line, no wasted sectors) and shrinks the stats->apply working set to ~1–8MB, so the apply/res_t read becomes an L2 hit instead of a DRAM read.

Method name:
group_tile_l2_blocking

Modification plan:
1) Add CTILE=32 channels (=4 groups; 32*4B=128B contiguous per pixel in NHWC = one full L2 line, so tiling wastes no sectors). Replace the image-only chunk loop in gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw(_out) with a two-level loop `for n0 (nb images) { for c0 in 0,32,...,224 }`, sized so chunk_bytes = nb*CTILE*HW*4 <= 4MB (nb>=1). This GENERALISES l2_cache_blocking (still present), it does not remove it.
2) Replace gn_stats_kernel with gn_stats_tile(y,c0,HW,P,gsum,gsq): grid=(P,nb), block=256 viewed as 32 lanes (channel c0+lane) x 8 rows. Thread (lane,row) accumulates s,q over hw = hw0+row+8k while hw<hw1, loading ld_cg(&y[((n*HW)+hw)*256 + c0+lane]) so each warp issues one 128B request. Reduce the 8 rows in smem[8][32], then reduce 8 channels -> 4 group sums; one lane per group does atomicAdd(&gsum[n*32+g],(double)s) and atomicAdd(&gsq[...],(double)q).
3) DELETE gn_final_kernel (accounting: it is not one of the carried mechanisms; its job — partials -> mean/rstd — is subsumed by the double atomics plus an inline finalize). Keeping it would multiply its 4.9us launch latency by the 8x finer chunking and eat the whole win. Before each GN pass issue one cudaMemsetAsync(gsum/gsq, 0, B*32*8*2) (graph-capturable node) instead of 8–32 gn_final launches.
4) gn_silu_apply_tile: grid over nb*HW*(CTILE/4) float4s; thread decodes i -> (n, hw, c4 in 0..7), local group g = c0/8 + (c4>>1); loads s=gsum[n*32+g], q=gsq[n*32+g], computes cnt=(double)HW*8, m=s/cnt, r=rsqrt(q/cnt-m*m+eps) once per thread; keeps ld_cs4 on y (last use) and default store on out.
5) gn_silu_res_t_tile: tile 64 spatial x 32 channels, smem[64*33]. Phase 1: lc=tid&31 (32 channels, 128B per warp), lh=tid>>5 (8 rows, 8 iters), ld_cs the y value, normalise+SiLU into smem. Phase 2: lh=tid&63 (64 contiguous hw), lc=tid>>6 (4 iters covering 32 channels), residual ld_cs + st_cs to NCHW. This preserves l2_evict_policy_hints exactly (streaming on y/res/out, ld_cg only in stats).

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/exposure-bound schedule, not per-kernel bound] Hottest non-removable segment is the cuDNN TF32 NHWC conv pair (~1668us/forward, ~88% of TF32 peak) plus our DRAM-bound epilogue (gn_stats 126us, gn_silu_res_t 137us, apply 55us, transpose 56us = 412us/forward at 68-88% DRAM but only 4-19% SM throughput). The two symmetric half-batch streams phase-lock, so 1668+412us of work takes 1855us wall: ~187us of memory time is exposed with tensor cores idle.

Optimisation method:
Stream specialization (producer/consumer software pipeline): one CUDA stream runs ONLY the two cuDNN convs, a second runs ONLY the memory-bound kernels (transpose, GN stats/final/apply/res+transpose), chained by per-chunk events over 2-4 batch chunks with one-chunk lookahead. Because the streams hold disjoint kernel classes, conv (88% tensor-core, low DRAM) is structurally concurrent with GN (77-88% DRAM, <19% SM) instead of accidentally; the symmetric dual pipeline degenerates to conv||conv then GN||GN because both halves have identical stage durations.

Method name:
stream_specialize_pipeline

Modification plan:
1. Replace `_run_pipeline`'s two symmetric half-batch pipelines with a role-specialized 2-stream pipeline; keep the existing single-stream body verbatim as fallback for B<2 or non-fp32/non-4D/non-CUDA input. 2. Chunking: n=min(4,B); starts[i]=(i*B)//n so B=8->4x2, B=4->4x1, B=2->2x1, B=1->fallback; chunks are per-sample independent (GN is per-image) so output is bitwise identical. 3. Lazily create and cache streams sC (conv) and sM (memory) plus event arrays eT/eA/eB/eD of length 4 in `_get_streams` (created once, reused, capture-safe). Fork with ev0.record(cur); sC.wait_event(ev0); sM.wait_event(ev0); allocate out=torch.empty_like(x) before the fork. 4. Prologue on sM: for k in range(n): xl[k]=ext.nchw_to_nhwc(x[starts[k]:starts[k+1]]); eT[k].record(sM). Hold xl/y1/z/y2 in Python lists so in-flight chunks stay alive (no aliasing, no reuse hazard). 5. One-chunk-lookahead interleave, issued in exactly this order for k=0..n-1: (a) sC: wait_event(eT[k]); y1[k]=F.conv2d(xl[k],w1c,None,1,1); eA[k].record(sC). (b) sM: wait_event(eA[k]); z[k]=ext.gn_silu_nhwc(y1[k],nw1,nb1,eps); eB[k].record(sM). (c) if k>=1 sC: wait_event(eB[k-1]); y2[k-1]=F.conv2d(z[k-1],w2c,None,1,1); eD[k-1].record(sC). (d) if k>=1 sM: wait_event(eD[k-1]); ext.gn_silu_res_nchw_out(y2[k-1], x[starts[k-1]:starts[k]], nw2, nb2, eps, out[starts[k-1]:starts[k]]). This gives sC=A0,A1,D0,A2,D1,A3,D2 and sM=T*,B0,B1,E0,B2,E1,B3,E2, so every GN kernel runs while a conv of another chunk holds the tensor cores. 6. Tail: after the loop issue D(n-1) on sC then E(n-1) on sM; join with evC/evM recorded on each stream and cur.wait_event on both; return out. 7. Mirror the identical schedule in `_forward_eager`, adding record_stream(sC)/record_stream(sM) for x, out and all weight tensors as the current code does. 8. Leave the CUDA source untouched: all five kernels, the ld.cs/ld.cg/st.cs eviction hints, and the per-call L2 chunk loop inside gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw_out (now invoked on 1-2 image chunks); pick_P and chunk_imgs unchanged. 9. Graph capture unchanged: the schedule is static per shape, so `_try_capture` still warms up under `_Autotune`, captures `_run_pipeline` into the shared pool, and caches per key. 10. Accounting: this REPLACES the base's multistream_pipeline (symmetric half-batch dual pipeline). It is not dropped — same 2 streams + events — but the two streams now carry disjoint kernel classes so conv‖GN overlap is structural. Verify in nsys that a cutlass conv kernel is resident while gn_* kernels execute; if not, revert.

Evidence:
Previous attempt (mem_vectorize, round 14) classification (a): the predicted metric DID move — gn_stats_kernel 15.81us -> 13.18us (-17%) with gpu__dram_throughput 68.2% -> 74.6% — yet the score fell 0.66% (8x shape -2.7%). Per-kernel bandwidth efficiency is therefore a dead end; the wall is set by how kernels share the GPU. Root cause here: our five kernels sum 412us/forward (res_t 34.3x4, stats 15.8x8, apply 13.8x4, transpose 28x2, final 4.8x8) at gpu__dram_throughput 68-88% but sm__throughput 5-20%, while the convs sit at 1.546e11 FLOP/1668us = 92.7 TFLOPS = 88% of TF32 peak with low DRAM; wall is 1855us vs 1668us of conv, so ~187us of memory time is exposed against idle tensor cores. This mechanism composes with every carried optimisation (graph capture, L2 chunk blocking, eviction hints, cuDNN autotune) and only reorders stream ownership.

Expected metric change:
(1) Per-forward wall time down 4-8% on B>=2 shapes (8x256x64x128 1855us -> <=1780us), while the SUM of all kernel durations stays flat (±3%) — this is a scheduling win, not a work win. (2) Per-launch cutlass conv duration should roughly HALVE (417us -> ~210us) because convs no longer run two-at-a-time, with total conv time unchanged: if summed conv time rises >3% above 1668us, serializing the convs is hurting engine efficiency and the change must be reverted. (3) In nsys, gn_stats/gn_silu_apply/gn_silu_res_t must appear concurrent with a cutlass conv kernel; conv-stream idle gaps must be <30us apart from the initial transpose. Anti-regression constraints: gn_* kernel durations unchanged ±5% (kernel code untouched) and their launch counts unchanged (4 chunks vs 2 streams x 2 chunks); graph capture must still succeed with exactly one replay per forward (`_graphs[key]` never False) and no cudaMalloc inside capture; cuDNN autotune must still fire once per shape (no conv2d_grouped_direct_kernel in steady state); B=1 (1x256x131x131) takes the untouched single-stream path and must stay within ±0.5%; peak memory rises by at most 2 extra in-flight chunks (~34MB mid, ~268MB large) which must not trigger allocator churn.

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/occupancy-exposure, SM-slot contention] Hottest non-removable segment we control is the DRAM-bound epilogue (gn_silu_res_t 141us, gn_stats 106us, apply 54us, transpose 55us per forward). Each epilogue kernel launches 2048-4096 blocks and fills every warp slot (sm__warps_active 82-111%) while using only 11-20% of SM issue, so the other stream's tensor-core conv cannot get resident blocks and the 397us epilogue stays exposed on the 1855us wall.

Optimisation method:
Concurrent-kernel SM budgeting: convert nchw2nhwc_kernel, gn_silu_apply and gn_silu_res_t into persistent grid-stride kernels whose grid is capped at ~2 blocks/SM (340 blocks) instead of 2-4 full waves, but only on the multistream path (B>=4). Metrics justify it: gn_stats already reaches 76.99% DRAM SOL at 48.6% warps_active, so half the warp slots saturate DRAM; the remaining slots currently squatted by 11%-SM-throughput epilogue warps are exactly what the co-scheduled cuDNN TF32 conv needs to overlap.

Method name:
sm_budget_grid_cap

Modification plan:
1) Add SM-count query once: `static int g_sm = at::cuda::getCurrentDeviceProperties()->multiProcessorCount;` (cached in a function-local static). Add an `int bpsm` argument (0 = uncapped) to nchw_to_nhwc, gn_silu_nhwc, gn_silu_res_nchw and gn_silu_res_nchw_out; the C++ side computes `cap = (bpsm>0) ? g_sm*bpsm : INT_MAX` and clamps each grid, keeping every other host-side line (chunk loop, pick_P, stats_chunk, allocations) byte-identical so l2_cache_blocking survives.
2) gn_silu_res_t: replace the 3D grid (HWtiles, C/64, nb) by a flat 1D grid. Precompute on host `TH=(HW+31)/32, TC=4, T=TH*TC*nb`, launch `dim3 g(min(T,cap))`, pass TH, TC, T. Inside: `for (int i = blockIdx.x; i < T; i += gridDim.x) { int t = T-1-i; int n = t/(TH*TC); int r = t - n*TH*TC; int cb = r/TH; int bx = r - cb*TH; const int hw0 = bx*32, c0 = cb*64; ... }` — body (shared tile, ld_cs/st_cs hints, `hw<HW` guards) copied verbatim, with `__syncthreads()` before AND after the shared-memory phase so the tile is reusable across iterations. This preserves the reverse traversal order and all l2_evict_policy_hints.
3) nchw2nhwc_kernel: identical flattening (same 32x64 tile, T=TH*TC*B, forward order), grid `min(T,cap)`, same double `__syncthreads()` pattern, same ld_cs load.
4) gn_silu_apply: keep gridDim.y = nb (image), cap x: `gx = min((n4+255)/256, max(1, cap/nb))`; inside replace the single index by `for (int b = gridDim.x-1-blockIdx.x; b < gx_total; b += gridDim.x)` computed as `i = b*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; if (i>=n4perimg) continue;` where gx_total = (n4perimg+255)/256 is passed in — reverse traversal and the float4 ld_cs4 path unchanged.
5) gn_stats_kernel and gn_final_kernel: UNTOUCHED (gn_stats already sits at 3.0 blocks/SM and 48.6% occupancy, i.e. it already leaves half the slots free and still hits 77% DRAM).
6) Python gating (this is the critical anti-regression rule): in `_run_pipeline` and `_forward_eager`, pass `bpsm=2` for every ext call ONLY on the two-stream branch (B>=4); pass `bpsm=0` on the single-stream fallback branch (B<4, i.e. 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131) so those shapes keep today's full-wave grids and cannot regress. The value is a Python int fixed by B, so the captured graph records one static grid per shape -> cuda_graph_capture keeps working; no allocation or shape change, so multistream_pipeline, l2_cache_blocking, cudnn_conv_engine_autotune and l2_evict_policy_hints all remain operational and none is removed.
7) Tuning knob: if the profiled shape shows the epilogue kernels ballooning more than 2x standalone (i.e. DRAM SOL of res_t falling below ~55%), raise bpsm to 3; if conv per-launch duration does not fall, revert to bpsm=0 (single-line change).
8) Correctness: grid-stride loops must cover T exactly for non-multiple extents (HW=17161 -> TH=537, T=537*4*nb); every `hw<HW` guard is retained, so partial tiles still write only valid elements and no psum/psq tail is involved (stats path untouched). Output is bit-identical: only block-to-tile assignment changes, and each tile is written by exactly one block.

Evidence:
Prior attempt #5 classification: (a) — its mechanism DID engage (nchw2nhwc per-launch 27.4->13.7us with grid (256,4,2), 4 chunks instead of 2) yet the score fell 2.81%, so re-ordering streams is a dead end; likewise #4 made gn_stats 17% faster and still lost 0.66%. Both failures share one unaddressed cause, measured here: gn_silu_res_t runs 2048 blocks, launch__occupancy_limit_warps=6, sm__warps_active=111.36% of peak while sm__throughput=11.26% and DRAM=77.48% — it holds 100% of the warp slots on all 170 SMs for 35us while doing almost no math, so the other stream's cutlass TF32 conv has zero resident blocks and cannot overlap. That capping is nearly free is proven by gn_stats_kernel: 48.61% warps_active still yields 76.99% DRAM SOL. Alternative bottleneck refuted: 'the conv is the lever' — 1.546e11 FLOP/1668us = 92.7 TFLOPS = 88% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak and it is already exhaustively engine-autotuned, so <12% is reachable and only inside the vendor library; 'per-kernel epilogue bandwidth' is refuted by #4's measured 17% kernel win producing a score loss.

Expected metric change:
(1) gn_silu_res_t launch__grid_size 2048 -> 340 and launch__waves_per_multiprocessor 2.01 -> ~0.33; same for nchw2nhwc (4096->340, 4.02->0.33) and gn_silu_apply (4096->340). (2) In nsys, cutlass_tensorop_s1688fprop/xmma conv kernels must now appear time-overlapped with gn_silu_res_t/apply, and per-forward wall on 8x256x64x128 must drop from 1855us to <=1790us (-3.5% or better); summed conv GPU time must stay within +3% of today's value. (3) Standalone epilogue kernel durations are EXPECTED to rise (res_t 35->up to ~55us, DRAM SOL 77%->~55%) — this is acceptable only if wall time falls; if res_t DRAM SOL drops below 45% or wall does not improve, raise bpsm to 3 or set 0. Anti-regression constraints: 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 take the bpsm=0 single-stream branch and must stay within +/-0.5%; kernel launch counts per forward unchanged (2/8/8/4/4) and graph capture must still yield exactly one replay per forward (`_graphs[key]` never False, node count unchanged); gn_stats/gn_final durations flat +/-2% (untouched); cuDNN autotuned engine must not revert (no conv2d_grouped_direct_kernel in steady state); outputs bit-identical (tile-to-block mapping only).

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/exposure-bound schedule] For B<4 the whole pipeline runs on ONE stream, so the DRAM-bound epilogue (transpose 87.7%, gn_silu_apply 83.1%, gn_silu_res_t 74.0%, gn_stats 75.1% DRAM SOL but only 6–19% SM throughput) is fully serialized behind the cuDNN TF32 convs (~88% of TF32 peak, low DRAM). The 2x256x64x64 shape therefore scores worst (1.1259 vs 1.2668 for the two-stream mid shape).

Optimisation method:
Re-gate the existing multistream fork/join pipeline so B==2 (threshold B<4 → B<2) is split into two per-image streams staggered by evStage, letting one stream's tensor-core conv overlap the other's 75–88%-DRAM/6–19%-SM GroupNorm+transpose kernels. Batch splitting is exactly value-equivalent (GN stats are per (image,group); residual is elementwise). B>=4 and B==1 code paths are left bit-identical, so the -4.4% large-shape regression of round 10 (caused by its separate 4-chunk restructure, not by the gate) cannot recur.

Method name:
smallB_multistream_gate

Modification plan:
Checklist (host-side Python only; no CUDA kernel edits, no change to chunking constants):
1. In `ModelNew._run_pipeline`, change the fallback condition `if (st is None) or (B < 4):` to `if (st is None) or (B < 2):` so B==2 (and 3) take the two-stream fork/join branch; B==1 still takes the single-stream branch (cannot be split by batch).
2. In `ModelNew._forward_eager`, make the identical change in `if (st is None) or (B < 4) or (x.dim() != 4) ...` → `... or (B < 2) or ...`; keep every `record_stream` call exactly as-is so cross-stream allocator reuse stays safe on the eager path.
3. Keep `s0 = B // 2` unchanged: B==2 → streams of 1 image each; B==3 → 1 and 2 images (correct, merely imbalanced). Assert nothing else: s0>=1 is guaranteed because B==1 never forks.
4. Verify the C++ helpers are already nb==1-safe and leave them untouched: `chunk_imgs(1,HW)` returns 1 (single chunk), `pick_P(1,HW)=min(ceil(HW/32),1024)`, `stats_chunk` launches grid (P, nb=1) and `gn_final` launches nb*NGRP=32 blocks reading exactly the P*NGRP slots gn_stats wrote — empty tail partitions still write zeros, so no unwritten-tail hazard for HW=4096 (P=128) or the awkward HW=17161 (P=537).
5. Graph capture: `_try_capture` calls `_run_pipeline`, which now forks for B==2; the fork/join capture pattern (ev0 record on the capturing stream, sA/sB wait, evA/evB join) is already exercised for B>=4, so reuse it verbatim — no new capture code, no allocation inside capture (
all buffers come from the graph pool as today).
6. Autotune: `_autotune_once` / `_try_capture` warm-up now runs the B==1-per-stream conv shapes under `_Autotune()`, so cuDNN selects and caches plans for (1,256,H,W) convs before capture; keep `_MAX_TUNED`/`_MAX_GRAPHS` unchanged.
7. Do NOT touch: kernel sources (eviction hints ld_cs/ld_cg/st_cs, float4 apply, shared-mem transposes), `chunk_imgs`/`pick_P`, the L2 chunk loop inside each ext call, graph cache keying, or the B>=4 branch — the mid/large shapes must produce a byte-identical launch sequence.
8. Correctness argument to record in a comment: conv2d, GroupNorm(32 groups over C,H,W of ONE image) and the residual add are all per-image independent, so `cat(f(x[0:1]), f(x[1:2])) == f(x)` bitwise; only kernel grid z-extent changes.
9. Fallback safety: if stream/event creation fails (`_get_streams()` returns None) the single-stream path is still taken for every B, and if capture throws, `_forward_eager` reproduces the same result.
10. Post-check with nsys on 2x256x64x64: confirm a cutlass conv kernel is time-overlapped with gn_stats/gn_silu_apply/gn_silu_res_t of the other stream, and that exactly one graph replay per forward remains.

Evidence:
Latest rejected attempt classification: (a) — its predicted metric DID move (gn_stats_kernel 13.18us→12.67us, -3.9%, DRAM SOL 75.09%→75.84%, registers 21→20) yet the score fell 1.1980→1.1854, so per-kernel bandwidth micro-optimisation of an already 75–88%-DRAM-SOL kernel is a dead end; the wall is set by how work is placed, and the only shape with NO placement at all is the single-stream one. Numeric evidence for the new target: 2x256x64x64 is the worst shape at 1.1259x while the two-stream 8x256x64x128 reaches 1.2668x; on B=2 every epilogue kernel (74.0–87.7% DRAM SOL, 6.3–19.6% sm__throughput) is serialized behind convs running at ~92.7 TFLOPS ≈ 88% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak (low DRAM), i.e. two complementary resources are used one after the other. Round 10 measured +5.3% on exactly this shape when the multistream threshold was lowered; its -4.4% on 4x256x256x256 came from the separately-introduced 4-chunk stagger, which this plan does not adopt. Alternative bottleneck refuted: 'the conv is the lever' — it is already exhaustively engine-autotuned at 88% of TF32 SOL, so <12% is reachable and only inside the vendor library. This composes with all carried mechanisms: it re-uses (does not remove) multistream_pipeline, keeps cuda_graph_capture (same fork/join pattern already captured for B>=4), keeps cudnn_conv_engine_autotune (warm-up still runs under _Autotune), keeps l2_cache_blocking (chunk loop untouched inside each ext call) and keeps l2_evict_policy_hints (kernel code untouched).

Expected metric change:
(1) 2x256x64x64 wall 272us → <=258us (-5%) and its per-shape speedup 1.1259 → >=1.18; geomean 1.1980 → ~1.211. (2) In nsys for that shape, cutlass/xmma conv kernels must appear time-overlapped with gn_stats/gn_silu_apply/gn_silu_res_t (currently zero overlap), and per-forward kernel count for B=2 doubles (9 → 18) while graph replays per forward stay exactly 1 (`_graphs[key]` must never become False). (3) Per-kernel durations must stay flat: gn_stats, gn_silu_apply, gn_silu_res_t, nchw2nhwc, gn_final within ±3% at equal nb (kernel code untouched), only their grid z-extent halves. Anti-regression constraints: 8x256x64x128, 4x256x256x256 and 1x256x131x131 take an unchanged code path and must stay within ±0.5% — if any of them moves, the gate leaked; cuDNN autotune must still fire once per new (B=1-per-stream) conv shape (no conv2d_grouped_direct_kernel in steady state); outputs must remain bitwise-equal to the current kernel for B!=2 and within tolerance for B=2 (per-image independence makes the split exact); peak memory rises only by the second half-batch's in-flight chunk (~8.4MB at the mid shape) and must not trigger allocator churn; if 2x256x64x64 does not improve by >=2%, restore the `B < 4` threshold.

pairs.a_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[latency/exposure-bound schedule, not per-kernel bound] Hottest non-removable segment is the cuDNN TF32 NHWC conv pair (~1668us/forward, ~88% of TF32 peak) plus our DRAM-bound epilogue (gn_stats 126us, gn_silu_res_t 137us, apply 55us, transpose 56us = 412us/forward at 68-88% DRAM but only 4-19% SM throughput). The two symmetric half-batch streams phase-lock, so 1668+412us of work takes 1855us wall: ~187us of memory time is exposed with tensor cores idle.

Optimisation method:
Stream specialization (producer/consumer software pipeline): one CUDA stream runs ONLY the two cuDNN convs, a second runs ONLY the memory-bound kernels (transpose, GN stats/final/apply/res+transpose), chained by per-chunk events over 2-4 batch chunks with one-chunk lookahead. Because the streams hold disjoint kernel classes, conv (88% tensor-core, low DRAM) is structurally concurrent with GN (77-88% DRAM, <19% SM) instead of accidentally; the symmetric dual pipeline degenerates to conv||conv then GN||GN because both halves have identical stage durations.

Method name:
stream_specialize_pipeline

Modification plan:
1. Replace `_run_pipeline`'s two symmetric half-batch pipelines with a role-specialized 2-stream pipeline; keep the existing single-stream body verbatim as fallback for B<2 or non-fp32/non-4D/non-CUDA input. 2. Chunking: n=min(4,B); starts[i]=(i*B)//n so B=8->4x2, B=4->4x1, B=2->2x1, B=1->fallback; chunks are per-sample independent (GN is per-image) so output is bitwise identical. 3. Lazily create and cache streams sC (conv) and sM (memory) plus event arrays eT/eA/eB/eD of length 4 in `_get_streams` (created once, reused, capture-safe). Fork with ev0.record(cur); sC.wait_event(ev0); sM.wait_event(ev0); allocate out=torch.empty_like(x) before the fork. 4. Prologue on sM: for k in range(n): xl[k]=ext.nchw_to_nhwc(x[starts[k]:starts[k+1]]); eT[k].record(sM). Hold xl/y1/z/y2 in Python lists so in-flight chunks stay alive (no aliasing, no reuse hazard). 5. One-chunk-lookahead interleave, issued in exactly this order for k=0..n-1: (a) sC: wait_event(eT[k]); y1[k]=F.conv2d(xl[k],w1c,None,1,1); eA[k].record(sC). (b) sM: wait_event(eA[k]); z[k]=ext.gn_silu_nhwc(y1[k],nw1,nb1,eps); eB[k].record(sM). (c) if k>=1 sC: wait_event(eB[k-1]); y2[k-1]=F.conv2d(z[k-1],w2c,None,1,1); eD[k-1].record(sC). (d) if k>=1 sM: wait_event(eD[k-1]); ext.gn_silu_res_nchw_out(y2[k-1], x[starts[k-1]:starts[k]], nw2, nb2, eps, out[starts[k-1]:starts[k]]). This gives sC=A0,A1,D0,A2,D1,A3,D2 and sM=T*,B0,B1,E0,B2,E1,B3,E2, so every GN kernel runs while a conv of another chunk holds the tensor cores. 6. Tail: after the loop issue D(n-1) on sC then E(n-1) on sM; join with evC/evM recorded on each stream and cur.wait_event on both; return out. 7. Mirror the identical schedule in `_forward_eager`, adding record_stream(sC)/record_stream(sM) for x, out and all weight tensors as the current code does. 8. Leave the CUDA source untouched: all five kernels, the ld.cs/ld.cg/st.cs eviction hints, and the per-call L2 chunk loop inside gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw_out (now invoked on 1-2 image chunks); pick_P and chunk_imgs unchanged. 9. Graph capture unchanged: the schedule is static per shape, so `_try_capture` still warms up under `_Autotune`, captures `_run_pipeline` into the shared pool, and caches per key. 10. Accounting: this REPLACES the base's multistream_pipeline (symmetric half-batch dual pipeline). It is not dropped — same 2 streams + events — but the two streams now carry disjoint kernel classes so conv‖GN overlap is structural. Verify in nsys that a cutlass conv kernel is resident while gn_* kernels execute; if not, revert.

Evidence:
Previous attempt (mem_vectorize, round 14) classification (a): the predicted metric DID move — gn_stats_kernel 15.81us -> 13.18us (-17%) with gpu__dram_throughput 68.2% -> 74.6% — yet the score fell 0.66% (8x shape -2.7%). Per-kernel bandwidth efficiency is therefore a dead end; the wall is set by how kernels share the GPU. Root cause here: our five kernels sum 412us/forward (res_t 34.3x4, stats 15.8x8, apply 13.8x4, transpose 28x2, final 4.8x8) at gpu__dram_throughput 68-88% but sm__throughput 5-20%, while the convs sit at 1.546e11 FLOP/1668us = 92.7 TFLOPS = 88% of TF32 peak with low DRAM; wall is 1855us vs 1668us of conv, so ~187us of memory time is exposed against idle tensor cores. Alternative bottleneck refuted: 'the conv is the lever' — it is already engine-autotuned at 88% of TF32 SOL, so <12% is reachable and only inside the vendor library; 'occupancy' refuted because gn_silu_res_t already achieves 96.1% occupancy with 101.6% long-scoreboard stalls (pure DRAM latency). This mechanism composes with every carried optimisation (graph capture, L2 chunk blocking, eviction hints, cuDNN autotune) and only reorders stream ownership.

Expected metric change:
(1) Per-forward wall time down 4-8% on B>=2 shapes (8x256x64x128 1855us -> <=1780us), while the SUM of all kernel durations stays flat (±3%) — this is a scheduling win, not a work win. (2) Per-launch cutlass conv duration should roughly HALVE (417us -> ~210us) because convs no longer run two-at-a-time, with total conv time unchanged: if summed conv time rises >3% above 1668us, serializing the convs is hurting engine efficiency and the change must be reverted. (3) In nsys, gn_stats/gn_silu_apply/gn_silu_res_t must appear concurrent with a cutlass conv kernel; conv-stream idle gaps must be <30us apart from the initial transpose. Anti-regression constraints: gn_* kernel durations unchanged ±5% (kernel code untouched) and their launch counts unchanged (4 chunks vs 2 streams x 2 chunks); graph capture must still succeed with exactly one replay per forward (`_graphs[key]` never False) and no cudaMalloc inside capture; cuDNN autotune must still fire once per shape (no conv2d_grouped_direct_kernel in steady state); B=1 (1x256x131x131) takes the untouched single-stream path and must stay within ±0.5%; peak memory rises by at most 2 extra in-flight chunks (~34MB mid, ~268MB large) which must not trigger allocator churn.
pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM-bandwidth bound] The GroupNorm pair we control — gn_stats_kernel (13.6us x8) then gn_silu_apply (14.3us x4) / gn_silu_res_t (34.5us x4), ~300us of our 402us epilogue — reads the SAME conv-output chunk from DRAM twice: lts__t_sector_hit_rate 2.31% (stats), 1.85% (apply), 1.94% (res_t) at 75–84% DRAM SOL, ~134MB/forward of pure redundant re-read.

Optimisation method:
Tighten l2_cache_blocking from image granularity to (image x 4-group channel-tile) granularity. Today the smallest reuse unit is one whole image (16.8MB mid, 67MB large), which measurably does not survive L2 (1.85% hit). A 32-channel tile is 128B contiguous per pixel in NHWC (full L2 line, no wasted sectors) and shrinks the stats->apply working set to ~1–8MB, so the apply/res_t read becomes an L2 hit instead of a DRAM read.

Method name:
group_tile_l2_blocking

Modification plan:
1) Add CTILE=32 channels (=4 groups; 32*4B=128B contiguous per pixel in NHWC = one full L2 line, so tiling wastes no sectors). Replace the image-only chunk loop in gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw(_out) with a two-level loop `for n0 (nb images) { for c0 in 0,32,...,224 }`, sized so chunk_bytes = nb*CTILE*HW*4 <= 4MB (nb>=1). This GENERALISES l2_cache_blocking (still present), it does not remove it.
2) Replace gn_stats_kernel with gn_stats_tile(y,c0,HW,P,gsum,gsq): grid=(P,nb), block=256 viewed as 32 lanes (channel c0+lane) x 8 rows. Thread (lane,row) accumulates s,q over hw = hw0+row+8k while hw<hw1, loading ld_cg(&y[((n*HW)+hw)*256 + c0+lane]) so each warp issues one 128B request. Reduce the 8 rows in smem[8][32], then reduce 8 channels -> 4 group sums; one lane per group does atomicAdd(&gsum[n*32+g],(double)s) and atomicAdd(&gsq[...],(double)q).
3) DELETE gn_final_kernel (accounting: it is not one of the carried mechanisms; its job — partials -> mean/rstd — is subsumed by the double atomics plus an inline finalize). Keeping it would multiply its 4.9us launch latency by the 8x finer chunking and eat the whole win. Before each GN pass issue one cudaMemsetAsync(gsum/gsq, 0, B*32*8*2) (graph-capturable node) instead of 8–32 gn_final launches.
4) gn_silu_apply_tile: grid over nb*HW*(CTILE/4) float4s; thread decodes i -> (n, hw, c4 in 0..7), local group g = c0/8 + (c4>>1); loads s=gsum[n*32+g], q=gsq[n*32+g], computes cnt=(double)HW*8, m=s/cnt, r=rsqrt(q/cnt-m*m+eps) once per thread; keeps ld_cs4 on y (last use) and default store on out.
5) gn_silu_res_t_tile: tile 64 spatial x 32 channels, smem[64*33]. Phase 1: lc=tid&31 (32 channels, 128B per warp), lh=tid>>5 (8 rows, 8 iters), ld_cs the y value, normalise+SiLU into smem. Phase 2: lh=tid&63 (64 contiguous hw), lc=tid>>6 (4 iters covering 32 channels), residual ld_cs + st_cs to NCHW. This preserves l2_evict_policy_hints exactly (streaming on y/res/out, ld_cg only in stats).
6) P selection: P = clamp(ceil(HW/512), 1, max(1,1024/nb)) so P*nb lands in 256–1024 blocks; empty partitions (hw0>=HW) simply contribute 0 to the atomics, so no unwritten-tail hazard exists any more (this also removes the psum/psq tail-write requirement entirely).
7) All loops bound-check hw<HW and all grids use ceil-division; nothing assumes HW%32==0, so the awkward 1x256x131x131 (HW=17161, odd) shape is exact.
8) Host side untouched otherwise: keep the two-stream fork/join with the evStage stagger, the out-parameter variant, per-(shape,ptr) CUDA-graph capture with the shared pool, and the _Autotune exhaustive cuDNN warm-up. Only the node list inside each ext call changes (more, smaller nodes + 1 memset), which capture handles because sizes are static.
9) Numerics: per-thread float accumulation, block reduction in float, cross-block accumulation in double atomics, finalize in double -> relative error <1e-8, far inside atol 2.8e-3.
10) Keep TORCH_CHECK(C==256) and the channels_last checks; conv calls, weights and layouts are unchanged.

Evidence:
Previous attempt (round 19, smallB_multistream_gate) = case (i): its predicted metric DID move — 2x256x64x64 improved +8.2% exactly as forecast (272us -> ~251us) — so the mechanism works but is shape-limited; I keep that gate untouched and attack an independent, larger target. Numeric evidence here: gn_stats_kernel reads a 16.8MB chunk at lts__t_sector_hit_rate=2.31%, and gn_silu_apply re-reads the identical chunk microseconds later at 1.85% (res_t 1.94%), i.e. ~134MB of the ~603MB epilogue traffic per forward is a redundant DRAM read; DRAM SOL is 75–84% while sm__throughput is only 6–19%, and long_scoreboard is 82–102%, so bytes, not issue, set the time. Root cause: the smallest reuse unit today is one whole image (16.8MB mid, 67MB large) and that working set demonstrably does not survive L2 next to the second stream's conv plus the apply's own 16.8MB write stream. Refutation of 'the conv is the lever': 1.546e11 FLOP / 1668us = 92.7 TFLOPS = 88% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak and the engine is already exhaustively autotuned, so <12% is reachable and only inside the vendor library. Refutation of 'scheduling/occupancy': rounds 10/15/16 moved their scheduling metrics and all lost score, so only DRAM bytes remain. Rounds 11/17 targeted the same bytes but never ran (stream access-policy windows are illegal during graph capture); this plan uses no cudaStreamSetAttribute and no device-limit call at all — pure loop restructuring — so it composes with cuda_graph_capture, multistream_pipeline, cudnn autotune and the existing eviction hints.

Expected metric change:
(1) gn_silu_apply lts__t_sector_hit_rate 1.85% -> >=60% and gn_silu_res_t 1.94% -> >=40%; their gpu__dram_throughput must FALL (fewer DRAM bytes) while duration drops: apply 14.3us -> <=10.5us aggregate-equivalent, res_t 34.5us -> <=29us aggregate-equivalent per equal byte volume. (2) gn_final_kernel disappears (32 launches per 4 forwards -> 0), replaced by 4 memset nodes; per-forward wall on 8x256x64x128 1855us -> <=1770us (-4.5%). (3) gn_stats_tile must keep gpu__dram_throughput >=72% and its total time must not exceed the current 109us/forward by more than 10% — a balloon here is the round-13 failure signature (registers 21->42) and means revert; launch__registers_per_thread must stay <=28 for stats and <=32 for apply/res_t. Anti-regression: cutlass_tensorop_s1688fprop per-launch conv time within +3% of 417us; graph capture must still succeed with exactly one replay per forward (`_graphs[key]` never False) and node count may rise but must stay in ONE graph; cuDNN autotuned engine must not revert (no conv2d_grouped_direct_kernel in steady state); the awkward 1x256x131x131 (HW=17161) and small 2x256x64x64 shapes must not regress beyond -0.5% (bounds-checked loops + atomic accumulation remove all tail-write hazards); outputs within atol 2.8e-3 (double cross-block accumulation).

pairs.a_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[latency/occupancy-exposure, SM-slot contention] Hottest non-removable segment we control is the DRAM-bound epilogue (gn_silu_res_t 141us, gn_stats 106us, apply 54us, transpose 55us per forward). Each epilogue kernel launches 2048-4096 blocks and fills every warp slot (sm__warps_active 82-111%) while using only 11-20% of SM issue, so the other stream's tensor-core conv cannot get resident blocks and the 397us epilogue stays exposed on the 1855us wall.

Optimisation method:
Concurrent-kernel SM budgeting: convert nchw2nhwc_kernel, gn_silu_apply and gn_silu_res_t into persistent grid-stride kernels whose grid is capped at ~2 blocks/SM (340 blocks) instead of 2-4 full waves, but only on the multistream path (B>=4). Metrics justify it: gn_stats already reaches 76.99% DRAM SOL at 48.6% warps_active, so half the warp slots saturate DRAM; the remaining slots currently squatted by 11%-SM-throughput epilogue warps are exactly what the co-scheduled cuDNN TF32 conv needs to overlap.

Method name:
sm_budget_grid_cap

Modification plan:
1) Add SM-count query once: `static int g_sm = at::cuda::getCurrentDeviceProperties()->multiProcessorCount;` (cached in a function-local static). Add an `int bpsm` argument (0 = uncapped) to nchw_to_nhwc, gn_silu_nhwc, gn_silu_res_nchw and gn_silu_res_nchw_out; the C++ side computes `cap = (bpsm>0) ? g_sm*bpsm : INT_MAX` and clamps each grid, keeping every other host-side line (chunk loop, pick_P, stats_chunk, allocations) byte-identical so l2_cache_blocking survives.
2) gn_silu_res_t: replace the 3D grid (HWtiles, C/64, nb) by a flat 1D grid. Precompute on host `TH=(HW+31)/32, TC=4, T=TH*TC*nb`, launch `dim3 g(min(T,cap))`, pass TH, TC, T. Inside: `for (int i = blockIdx.x; i < T; i += gridDim.x) { int t = T-1-i; int n = t/(TH*TC); int r = t - n*TH*TC; int cb = r/TH; int bx = r - cb*TH; const int hw0 = bx*32, c0 = cb*64; ... }` — body (shared tile, ld_cs/st_cs hints, `hw<HW` guards) copied verbatim, with `__syncthreads()` before AND after the shared-memory phase so the tile is reusable across iterations. This preserves the reverse traversal order and all l2_evict_policy_hints.
3) nchw2nhwc_kernel: identical flattening (same 32x64 tile, T=TH*TC*B, forward order), grid `min(T,cap)`, same double `__syncthreads()` pattern, same ld_cs load.
4) gn_silu_apply: keep gridDim.y = nb (image), cap x: `gx = min((n4+255)/256, max(1, cap/nb))`; inside replace the single index by `for (int b = gridDim.x-1-blockIdx.x; b < gx_total; b += gridDim.x)` computed as `i = b*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x; if (i>=n4perimg) continue;` where gx_total = (n4perimg+255)/256 is passed in — reverse traversal and the float4 ld_cs4 path unchanged.
5) gn_stats_kernel and gn_final_kernel: UNTOUCHED (gn_stats already sits at 3.0 blocks/SM and 48.6% occupancy, i.e. it already leaves half the slots free and still hits 77% DRAM).
6) Python gating (this is the critical anti-regression rule): in `_run_pipeline` and `_forward_eager`, pass `bpsm=2` for every ext call ONLY on the two-stream branch (B>=4); pass `bpsm=0` on the single-stream fallback branch (B<4, i.e. 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131) so those shapes keep today's full-wave grids and cannot regress. The value is a Python int fixed by B, so the captured graph records one static grid per shape -> cuda_graph_capture keeps working; no allocation or shape change, so multistream_pipeline, l2_cache_blocking, cudnn_conv_engine_autotune and l2_evict_policy_hints all remain operational and none is removed.
7) Tuning knob: if the profiled shape shows the epilogue kernels ballooning more than 2x standalone (i.e. DRAM SOL of res_t falling below ~55%), raise bpsm to 3; if conv per-launch duration does not fall, revert to bpsm=0 (single-line change).
8) Correctness: grid-stride loops must cover T exactly for non-multiple extents (HW=17161 -> TH=537, T=537*4*nb); every `hw<HW` guard is retained, so partial tiles still write only valid elements and no psum/psq tail is involved (stats path untouched). Output is bit-identical: only block-to-tile assignment changes, and each tile is written by exactly one block.

Evidence:
Prior attempt #5 classification: (a) — its mechanism DID engage (nchw2nhwc per-launch 27.4->13.7us with grid (256,4,2), 4 chunks instead of 2) yet the score fell 2.81%, so re-ordering streams is a dead end; likewise #4 made gn_stats 17% faster and still lost 0.66%. Both failures share one unaddressed cause, measured here: gn_silu_res_t runs 2048 blocks, launch__occupancy_limit_warps=6, sm__warps_active=111.36% of peak while sm__throughput=11.26% and DRAM=77.48% — it holds 100% of the warp slots on all 170 SMs for 35us while doing almost no math, so the other stream's cutlass TF32 conv has zero resident blocks and cannot overlap. That capping is nearly free is proven by gn_stats_kernel: 48.61% warps_active still yields 76.99% DRAM SOL. Alternative bottleneck refuted: 'the conv is the lever' — 1.546e11 FLOP/1668us = 92.7 TFLOPS = 88% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak and it is already exhaustively engine-autotuned, so <12% is reachable and only inside the vendor library; 'per-kernel epilogue bandwidth' is refuted by #4's measured 17% kernel win producing a score loss.

Expected metric change:
(1) gn_silu_res_t launch__grid_size 2048 -> 340 and launch__waves_per_multiprocessor 2.01 -> ~0.33; same for nchw2nhwc (4096->340, 4.02->0.33) and gn_silu_apply (4096->340). (2) In nsys, cutlass_tensorop_s1688fprop/xmma conv kernels must now appear time-overlapped with gn_silu_res_t/apply, and per-forward wall on 8x256x64x128 must drop from 1855us to <=1790us (-3.5% or better); summed conv GPU time must stay within +3% of today's value. (3) Standalone epilogue kernel durations are EXPECTED to rise (res_t 35->up to ~55us, DRAM SOL 77%->~55%) — this is acceptable only if wall time falls; if res_t DRAM SOL drops below 45% or wall does not improve, raise bpsm to 3 or set 0. Anti-regression constraints: 2x256x64x64 and 1x256x131x131 take the bpsm=0 single-stream branch and must stay within +/-0.5%; kernel launch counts per forward unchanged (2/8/8/4/4) and graph capture must still yield exactly one replay per forward (`_graphs[key]` never False, node count unchanged); gn_stats/gn_final durations flat +/-2% (untouched); cuDNN autotuned engine must not revert (no conv2d_grouped_direct_kernel in steady state); outputs bit-identical (tile-to-block mapping only).
pairs.b_text:
Bottleneck identified:
[latency/exposure-bound schedule] For B<4 the whole pipeline runs on ONE stream, so the DRAM-bound epilogue (transpose 87.7%, gn_silu_apply 83.1%, gn_silu_res_t 74.0%, gn_stats 75.1% DRAM SOL but only 6–19% SM throughput) is fully serialized behind the cuDNN TF32 convs (~88% of TF32 peak, low DRAM). The 2x256x64x64 shape therefore scores worst (1.1259 vs 1.2668 for the two-stream mid shape).

Optimisation method:
Re-gate the existing multistream fork/join pipeline so B==2 (threshold B<4 → B<2) is split into two per-image streams staggered by evStage, letting one stream's tensor-core conv overlap the other's 75–88%-DRAM/6–19%-SM GroupNorm+transpose kernels. Batch splitting is exactly value-equivalent (GN stats are per (image,group); residual is elementwise). B>=4 and B==1 code paths are left bit-identical, so the -4.4% large-shape regression of round 10 (caused by its separate 4-chunk restructure, not by the gate) cannot recur.

Method name:
smallB_multistream_gate

Modification plan:
Checklist (host-side Python only; no CUDA kernel edits, no change to chunking constants):

Bottleneck identified:
[latency/occupancy-exposure, SM-slot contention] Hottest non-removable segment we control is the DRAM-bound epilogue (gn_silu_res_t 141us, gn_stats 106us, apply 54us, transpose 55us per forward). Optimisation method:
Concurrent-kernel SM budgeting: convert nchw2nhwc_kernel, gn_silu_apply and gn_silu_res_t into persistent grid-stride kernels whose grid is capped at ~2 blocks/SM (340 blocks) instead of 2-4 full waves, but only on the multistream path (B>=4). sm_budget_grid_cap

1) Add SM-count query once: `static int g_sm = at::cuda::getCurrentDeviceProperties()->multiProcessorCount;` (cached in a function-local static). Bottleneck identified:
[DRAM-bandwidth bound] The GroupNorm pair we control — gn_stats_kernel (13.6us x8) then gn_silu_apply (14.3us x4) / gn_silu_res_t (34.5us x4), ~300us of our 402us epilogue — reads the SAME conv-output chunk from DRAM twice: lts__t_sector_hit_rate 2.31% (stats), 1.85% (apply), 1.94% (res_t) at 75–84% DRAM SOL, ~134MB/forward of pure redundant re-read.

Optimisation method:
Tighten l2_cache_blocking from image granularity to (image x 4-group channel-tile) granularity. Today the smallest reuse unit is one whole image (16.8MB mid, 67MB large), which measurably does not survive L2 (1.85% hit). A 32-channel tile is 128B contiguous per pixel in NHWC (full L2 line, no wasted sectors) and shrinks the stats->apply working set to ~1–8MB, so the apply/res_t read becomes an L2 hit instead of a DRAM read.

Method name:
group_tile_l2_blocking

Modification plan:
1) Add CTILE=32 channels (=4 groups; 32*4B=128B contiguous per pixel in NHWC = one full L2 line, so tiling wastes no sectors). Replace the image-only chunk loop in gn_silu_nhwc / gn_silu_res_nchw(_out) with a two-level loop `for n0 (nb images) { for c0 in 0,32,...,224 }`, sized so chunk_bytes = nb*CTILE*HW*4 <= 4MB (nb>=1). This GENERALISES l2_cache_blocking (still present), it does not remove it.
2) Replace gn_stats_kernel with gn_stats_tile(y,c0,HW,P,gsum,gsq): grid=(P,nb), block=256 viewed as 32 lanes (channel c0+lane) x 8 rows. Thread (lane,row) accumulates s,q over hw = hw0+row+8k while hw<hw1, loading ld_cg(&y[((n*HW)+hw)*256 + c0+lane]) so each warp issues one 128B request. Reduce the 8 rows in smem[8][32], then reduce 8 channels -> 4 group sums; one lane per group does atomicAdd(&gsum[n*32+g],(double)s) and atomicAdd(&gsq[...],(double)q).
3) DELETE gn_final_kernel (accounting: it is not one of the carried mechanisms; its job — partials -> mean/rstd — is subsumed by the double atomics plus an inline finalize). Keeping it would multiply its 4.9us launch latency by the 8x finer chunking and eat the whole win. Before each GN pass issue one cudaMemsetAsync(gsum/gsq, 0, B*32*8*2) (graph-capturable node) instead of 8–32 gn_final launches.
4) gn_silu_apply_tile: grid over nb*HW*(CTILE/4) float4s; thread decodes i -> (n, hw, c4 in 0..7), local group g = c0/8 + (c4>>1); loads s=gsum[n*32+g], q=gsq[n*32+g], computes cnt=(double)HW*8, m=s/cnt, r=rsqrt(q/cnt-m*m+eps) once per thread; keeps ld_cs4 on y (last use) and default store on out.
5) gn_silu_res_t_tile: tile 64 spatial x 32 channels, smem[64*33]. Phase 1: lc=tid&31 (32 channels, 128B per warp), lh=tid>>5 (8 rows, 8 iters), ld_cs the y value, normalise+SiLU into smem. Phase 2: lh=tid&63 (64 contiguous hw), lc=tid>>6 (4 iters covering 32 channels), residual ld_cs + st_cs to NCHW. This preserves l2_evict_policy_hints exactly (streaming on y/res/out, ld_cg only in stats).
6) P selection: P = clamp(ceil(HW/512), 1, max(1,1024/nb)) so P*nb lands in 256–1024 blocks; empty partitions (hw0>=HW) simply contribute 0 to the atomics, so no unwritten-tail hazard exists any more (this also removes the psum/psq tail-write requirement entirely).
7) All loops bound-check hw<HW and all grids use ceil-division; nothing assumes HW%32==0, so the awkward 1x256x131x131 (HW=17161, odd) shape is exact.
8) Host side untouched otherwise: keep the two-stream fork/join with the evStage stagger, the out-parameter variant, per-(shape,ptr) CUDA-graph capture with the shared pool, and the _Autotune exhaustive cuDNN warm-up. Only the node list inside each ext call changes (more, smaller nodes + 1 memset), which capture handles because sizes are static.
9) Numerics: per-thread float accumulation, block reduction in float, cross-block accumulation in double atomics, finalize in double -> relative error <1e-8, far inside atol 2.8e-3.
10) Keep TORCH_CHECK(C==256) and the channels_last checks; conv calls, weights and layouts are unchanged.

Evidence:
Previous attempt (round 19, smallB_multistream_gate) = case (i): its predicted metric DID move — 2x256x64x64 improved +8.2% exactly as forecast (272us -> ~251us) — so the mechanism works but is shape-limited; I keep that gate untouched and attack an independent, larger target. Numeric evidence here: gn_stats_kernel reads a 16.8MB chunk at lts__t_sector_hit_rate=2.31%, and gn_silu_apply re-reads the identical chunk microseconds later at 1.85% (res_t 1.94%), i.e. ~134MB of the ~603MB epilogue traffic per forward is a redundant DRAM read; DRAM SOL is 75–84% while sm__throughput is only 6–19%, and long_scoreboard is 82–102%, so bytes, not issue, set the time. Root cause: the smallest reuse unit today is one whole image (16.8MB mid, 67MB large) and that working set demonstrably does not survive L2 next to the second stream's conv plus the apply's own 16.8MB write stream. (1) gn_silu_apply lts__t_sector_hit_rate 1.85% -> >=60% and gn_silu_res_t 1.94% -> >=40%; their gpu__dram_throughput must FALL (fewer DRAM bytes) while duration drops: apply 14.3us -> <=10.5us aggregate-equivalent, res_t 34.5us -> <=29us aggregate-equivalent per equal byte volume. (2) gn_final_kernel disappears (32 launches per 4 forwards -> 0), replaced by 4 memset nodes; per-forward wall on 8x256x64x128 1855us -> <=1770us (-4.5%).
